records.title: A reactivation order and deemed-work remedy can leave payment and later access unobserved
records.source_unit: One adjudicated Fair Work Commission platform-worker case, UDE2025/134
records.geography: Australia; comparative case used to test platform remedy and recovery stages in the US-centered atlas
records.boundary: This is one comparative Australian adjudicated case, not a worker prevalence estimate or a US population result. It distinguishes reactivation, deemed work, procedural lost-pay resolution, quantified payment, receipt, actual access, continued work, and practical exit.

records.title: Regular casual work and a formal unfair-dismissal finding can still leave income restoration unresolved
records.source_unit: Fair Work Commission decision [2025] FWC 561 concerning a regular casual nail technician's dismissal
records.geography: Perth, Western Australia; Fair Work Commission U2024/9845
records.boundary: This record establishes regular-casual work, a dismissal, formal recognition of jurisdiction and procedural unfairness, and a deferred remedy process. It does not establish final remedy receipt, recovered earnings, alternative work, household recovery, health outcome, trust change, recurrence, or exit.

records.title: An injury-related dismissal can produce a reinstatement and lost-pay order while actual compliance remains unverified
records.source_unit: Fair Work Commission decision [2025] FWC 2621 concerning Alam Shah
records.geography: Greenacre, Sydney, Australia; Fair Work Commission case [2025] FWC 2621
records.boundary: This record establishes one adjudicated worker case with observed injury, return, dismissal, language/cultural access, tribunal response, reinstatement, continuity, and lost-pay order. It does not establish post-order compliance, payment receipt, restored livelihood, trust, recurrence, collective action, or exit.

records.title: Back pay and continuity can be implemented while actual workplace return remains unresolved
records.source_unit: Fair Work Commission Full Bench decision [2015] FWCFB 1523 concerning Sportsmed SA and Cartisano
records.geography: South Australia; Fair Work Commission Sportsmed SA appeal
records.boundary: This record establishes a same-case boundary in which reported back-pay payment and continuity coexist with no actual return, and the tribunal distinguishes legal payment from real and practical reinstatement. It does not establish final remedy, causality of non-return, later compensation, household recovery, trust, or exit.

records.title: Pregnancy-linked work interruption can produce a quantified reinstatement order while durable restoration remains unverified
records.source_unit: Fair Work Commission decision [2025] FWC 3646 concerning Kaur v Adecco Industrial Australia Pty Ltd
records.geography: Australia; Amazon-site labour-supply employment and Fair Work Commission proceeding
records.boundary: This record establishes one adjudicated case from pregnancy-linked work interruption through bounded alternative employment, worker action, and quantified institutional remedy. It does not establish post-order implementation, payment receipt, restored work, discrimination prevalence, household recovery, trust, or exit.

records.title: A platform can reactivate a worker after one complaint and later deactivate again before an adjudicated access remedy
records.source_unit: Fair Work Commission Uber Eats platform reactivation and repeat-deactivation case [2026] FWC 48
records.geography: Australia; Uber Eats delivery platform, FWC UDE2025/185
records.boundary: This record establishes repeated platform-access interruption, procedural adjudication, and a reactivation/lost-pay order. It does not establish final payment, durable access, recovered earnings, alternative work, trust, or exit.

records.title: An Australian platform worker resumed work after voluntary reactivation and later received a formal access-restoration order
records.source_unit: One Australian platform worker and Fair Work Commission proceeding; adjudicated same-case remedy follow-up, not a population estimate
records.geography: Australia
records.boundary: This comparative Australian case closes voluntary access restoration, subsequent observed work activity, and ordinary payment for post-reactivation work before and alongside a formal access-restoration order. It does not close lost-remuneration payment, net recovery, alternative work, durable protection, trust, collective action, or practical exit.

records.title: Process deficiencies can coexist with a valid platform reason and no restoration remedy
records.source_unit: One adjudicated Fair Work Commission platform-worker case, UDE2025/105
records.geography: Australia; comparative case used to test procedural fairness, remedy, and recovery stages in the US-centered atlas
records.boundary: This is one comparative Australian adjudicated case, not a worker prevalence estimate or a US population result. It distinguishes filing continuation, process deficiency, substantive valid reason, unfairness finding, restoration, payment, later access, alternatives, trust, and exit.

records.title: A platform worker can show substitute earnings and a formal remedy while receipt and durable access remain open
records.source_unit: One adjudicated Fair Work Commission platform-worker case, UDE2025/141 / PR792727
records.geography: Australia; comparative case used to test the platform-remedy stage of the US-centered atlas
records.boundary: This is one comparative Australian adjudicated case, not a worker prevalence estimate or a US population result. It closes an observed substitute-earnings stage and a formal remedy-order stage for one worker, but not freely chosen alternatives, payment receipt, actual account restoration, durable protection, household recovery, trust, political action, or practical exit.

records.title: An Australian platform worker received formal access-restoration and lost-remuneration orders after deactivation
records.source_unit: One employee-like platform worker and adjudicated Fair Work Commission case; comparative institutional remedy record, not a population estimate
records.geography: Australia
records.boundary: This comparative Australian case closes a remedy-stage arrow from platform exclusion through worker application to access restoration and ordered lost remuneration. It does not establish payment receipt, net recovery, alternative choice, durable protection, trust change, political action, or practical exit.

records.title: A conditional interim-payment obligation is a distinct stage between platform remedy and worker recovery
records.source_unit: One adjudicated Fair Work Commission platform-worker case, UDE2025/160 and appeal C2026/7842
records.geography: Australia; comparative case used to test remedy implementation in the US-centered atlas
records.boundary: This is one comparative Australian adjudicated case, not a worker prevalence estimate or a US population result. It distinguishes unfairness, reactivation order, conditional interim payment obligation, payment receipt, actual access, final quantum, appeal outcome, continued work, and durable recovery.

records.title: NHS legitimacy is increasingly an access-time problem: care quality remains more trusted than the ability to reach it
records.source_unit: National Centre for Social Research, British Social Attitudes 43, Waiting for treatment
records.geography: Great Britain; BSA adult respondents, with service-performance comparisons primarily for England and historical NHS series
records.boundary: This record adds an NHS legitimacy route in which waiting time, service reachability, quality judgments, productivity, demographics, migration, and public feedback interact. It does not establish individual patient outcomes, causal policy effects, actual time lost, clinical quality, or a single Britain-wide administrative trend; historical definitions and geographies vary.

records.title: Welfare opinion is not one bloc: disability support remains resilient while deservingness and political identity polarize the boundary
records.source_unit: National Centre for Social Research, British Social Attitudes 43, Attitudes to welfare
records.geography: Great Britain; adult BSA respondents, excluding Northern Ireland and respondents under 18 in the chapter's analyses
records.boundary: This record identifies welfare deservingness as a cultural-political boundary: abstract anti-welfare sentiment can coexist with strong support for disability benefits, while claimant prototypes, fiscal context, political identity, media framing, and reform salience shape which forms of care remain legitimate. It does not measure policy effectiveness, claimant outcomes, disability prevalence, benefit adequacy, or causality.

records.title: Culture functions as everyday social infrastructure, but cost, time and accessibility still shape who can participate
records.source_unit: 4Culture and Wilkening Consulting, Doors Open Culture and Communities Study
records.geography: King County, Washington; representative resident sample and supplementary cultural-audience sample
records.boundary: This record adds a local cultural-infrastructure layer: culture is widely experienced and valued as connection, identity, learning, wellbeing and community quality of life, while cost, time, competing priorities and accessibility shape depth and equity of participation. It is a King County survey and program-baseline study with self-reported outcomes, not a national cultural census, attendance register, causal impact evaluation or economic-impact estimate.

records.title: Diary-based time use shows care and disability as hidden conversion costs for free time and social life
records.source_unit: Australian Bureau of Statistics, How Australians use their time, 2024; supplementary disability, carer, and time-pressure tables released August 5, 2026
records.geography: Australia; people aged 15 years and over in in-scope private households
records.boundary: This record adds diary-based time allocation as a conversion layer between disability, caring, free time, and social participation. It is descriptive 2024 Australian Time Use Survey evidence, not a longitudinal or causal estimate, not a complete prevalence measure for carers or volunteers, and not proof that a specific care responsibility caused a cultural or social outcome.

records.title: Cultural and social reconnection coexists with worsening household financial pressure in Australia
records.source_unit: Australian Bureau of Statistics General Social Survey: Summary Results, Australia, 2025
records.geography: Australia; people aged 15 years and over for cultural participation and people aged 18 years and over for social experiences, with all-household financial-stress measures
records.boundary: This record adds a same-instrument Australian bridge between cultural engagement, social contact, and household financial stress. It does not establish causal relationships, individual longitudinal change, affordability, cultural quality, belonging, mental-health outcomes, or the mechanisms behind cycle differences.

records.title: Australia's older migrant cultural-attendance baseline shows large country-of-birth and arrival-cohort differences
records.source_unit: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Arts and Culture in Australia: A Statistical Overview, 2008, Feature Article 4
records.geography: Australia; people aged 15 years and over in the 2005-06 Multipurpose Household Survey cultural-attendance module
records.boundary: This record adds a historical direct migrant-cultural-attendance baseline beneath the current Australian settlement and General Social Survey layers. It does not establish current participation, causal integration, equal access, digital cultural behavior, or trend continuity across the 2005-06 to 2025 measurement gap.

records.title: Australian migrant settlement outcomes diverge by visa stream across income, rent pressure, language, and service access
records.source_unit: Australian Bureau of Statistics, Migrant Settlement Outcomes, 2026
records.geography: Australia; permanent migrants with linked administrative, Census, and settlement-outcome data
records.boundary: This record adds migration-linked household-room, housing-pressure, language, and service-contact evidence beneath cultural and consumer conversion. It does not establish cultural participation, discretionary spending, causal visa-stream effects, equal service quality, or a single universal integration trajectory.

records.title: Australian household spending held up in August through transport while recreation and culture reversed its July rise
records.source_unit: Australian Bureau of Statistics Monthly Household Spending Indicator, August 2026
records.geography: Australia; national and state/territory household-spending estimates
records.boundary: This record follows the ABS transaction-based household-spending series one month forward. It does not establish individual cultural attendance, household welfare, affordability, unique consumers, causal substitution, or equal access.

records.title: Australian household spending rose in July while recreation and culture outpaced total volume, but nominal growth still mixes prices and quantities
records.source_unit: Australian Bureau of Statistics Monthly Household Spending Indicator, July 2026
records.geography: Australia; national and state/territory household-spending estimates
records.boundary: This record adds observed Australian household-spending and real-volume evidence beneath cultural-participation and financial-stress surveys. It does not establish individual cultural attendance, household welfare, affordability, unique consumers, causal category substitution, or equal access.

records.title: Professionals are adopting AI while demanding human judgment, hybrid flexibility and credible organizational purpose
records.source_unit: Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA), Global Talent Trends 2026
records.geography: Global accountancy and finance professionals, employers and leaders covered by the ACCA survey and report evidence
records.boundary: This record adds a professional and workplace layer to the broader trend stream: AI adoption is advancing alongside demands for human judgment, skill access, hybrid flexibility, meaningful work and credible support. It is an aggregate ACCA accountancy and finance survey/report, not a representative general workforce panel, respondent-level dataset, observed employment register, causal evaluation or proof of improved job quality.

records.title: Consumers are beginning to delegate shopping labor to AI agents while retaining control over purchases carrying identity, emotion, risk, or personal meaning
records.source_unit: Accenture Consumer Pulse Research 2026
records.geography: Consumers in 16 countries: Australia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, China, France, Germany, India, Italy, Japan, Mexico, Spain, Sweden, United Arab Emirates, United Kingdom, and United States
records.boundary: This record adds a cross-national consumer-AI signal on delegation, trust, safeguards, meaning, and shifting control points in commerce. It is based on Accenture's 2026 survey and strategic interpretation; it is not observed autonomous purchasing, a causal evaluation, a public-use respondent dataset, proof of equal access or recourse, or evidence that agentic commerce improves consumer welfare.

records.title: Conflict systems are broadening beyond battlefield violence into economic pressure, hybrid disorder, cultural disruption, alliances, and material bottlenecks
records.source_unit: ACLED, Raleigh Report: September 2026
records.geography: Global conflict systems, including Ukraine, the Middle East, Iran, India-China relations, China-linked materials, hybrid disorder, and conflict-affected societies
records.boundary: This record adds a conflict-system route from event intensity through economic pressure, hybrid disorder, cultural coordination, alliances, defense materials, and local-global strategic shifts. It is an interpretive ACLED publication, not a complete event dataset, causal conflict forecast, household-impact estimate, or proof that every described geopolitical intention will be realized.

records.title: Household-level poverty can conceal unequal access to health, internet, property, and decision power within the same family
records.source_unit: Asian Development Bank, Key Indicators for Asia and the Pacific 2026
records.geography: Asia and the Pacific; theme analysis of 23 developing economies and statistical indicators for 50 ADB regional member economies
records.boundary: This record adds an Asia-Pacific measurement-to-capability route from household poverty classification through individual deprivation, gender and rural inequality, health insurance, internet access, property ownership, decision power, and targeted policy. It uses ADB comparative indicators and a thematic deprivation framework; it is not a causal evaluation, a universal household survey, or proof that targeting produces realized agency or wellbeing.

records.title: Africa’s development gains are broad but infrastructure quality, financing, and delivery gaps keep access uneven
records.source_unit: African Union Commission, African Development Bank, UNDP, and UN Economic Commission for Africa, 2026 Africa Sustainable Development Report
records.geography: African countries and subregions, with comparisons across urban-rural settings and the 2030 Agenda and Agenda 2063 implementation system
records.boundary: This record adds a regional implementation route linking water, sanitation, energy, clean cooking, mobile connectivity, infrastructure, cities, financing, trade, regional integration, and SDG delivery. It is an aggregate publication-level assessment, not household service histories, respondent-level data, a country forecast, or proof that coverage equals reliable or affordable access.

records.title: Africa's development gains remain real but insufficient as water, energy, infrastructure, cities, finance, climate, and demographic pressures converge
records.source_unit: African Union Commission, UNECA, African Development Bank, and UNDP, 2026 Africa Sustainable Development Report
records.geography: African countries and subregions; implementation of the 2030 Agenda and African Union Agenda 2063, focused on SDGs 6, 7, 9, 11, and 17
records.boundary: This record adds a regional African development layer linking water, energy, infrastructure, cities, youth, finance, climate, conflict, and partnerships. It uses aggregate SDG and Agenda 2063 monitoring, not household-level service records, causal project evaluation, individual migration or consumption histories, or proof that regional priorities have been implemented.

records.title: African publics seek integration and multi-partner agency while separating openness from practical exposure
records.source_unit: Afrobarometer, African Insights 2026: Beyond borders: Citizen perspectives on a shifting global order
records.geography: 38 African countries surveyed in Afrobarometer Round 10, 2024–2025
records.boundary: This record adds African public-opinion evidence on trade integration, mobility, migration, external powers, global voice, and climate justice. It preserves attitudes, reported exposure, and intentions as distinct from realized trade, migration, geopolitical leverage, climate damage, policy implementation, or household welfare; country comparisons and associations are not causal estimates.

records.title: Support for women’s reproductive autonomy is broad, but access and abortion legitimacy remain conditional on age, marriage, and circumstance
records.source_unit: Afrobarometer, East Africa sexual and reproductive health and rights news release, Round 10
records.geography: Comoros, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Mauritius, Madagascar, and Seychelles; 2024–2025 surveys
records.boundary: This record adds East African public-attitude evidence on marital autonomy, childbearing decisions, sexuality education, contraceptive access, and abortion justification. It preserves the distinction between cultural norm, policy preference, law, service availability, and lived reproductive agency; it does not measure behavior, clinical outcomes, legal compliance, or institutional delivery.

records.title: African social cohesion combines broad tolerance with steep trust gradients, restrictive immigration attitudes, and weak institutional fairness
records.source_unit: Afrobarometer Dispatch AD1227, Social cohesion in Africa: Bonds, belonging, and the common good
records.geography: 38 African countries; Afrobarometer Round 10 interviews conducted in 2024/2025
records.boundary: This record adds a pan-African social-cohesion layer connecting trust distance, tolerance, immigration, identity, perceived institutional fairness, informal solidarity, and civic action. It is a cross-sectional public-opinion profile, not respondent-level ingestion, a causal model of cohesion, a continent-wide uniform estimate, or proof that tolerance becomes equal treatment or collective political action.

records.title: Democratic support is recovering modestly across the Americas as material security improves, but weak governance and representation keep legitimacy fragile
records.source_unit: Vanderbilt Center for Global Democracy and Notre Dame Kellogg Institute, 2026 Pulse of Democracy / AmericasBarometer
records.geography: Americas; 21 countries including the United States and Canada, Latin America and Cuba
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative democratic-legitimacy mechanism: improvements in economic security, food security and neighborhood safety coincide with a modest recovery in democratic support, while corruption, weak public services and doubts about government honesty and responsiveness keep that recovery fragile. It is a repeated cross-national public-opinion program, not a causal panel, administrative security dataset, direct measure of democratic durability or proof that material improvement alone restores institutional trust.

records.title: Household financial pessimism can deepen even when purchase timing barely moves
records.source_unit: ANZ and Roy Morgan, Australian Consumer Confidence, 29 September 2026
records.geography: Australia; weekly national consumer-confidence survey, with state-level movement reported
records.boundary: This record identifies a weekly consumer-sentiment, household-room and purchase-timing subtheme. It does not establish changes in income, expenditure, debt, employment, inflation, interest rates, household welfare, political attribution or consumer behavior; those require linked panel, transaction, price, labor-market and household-budget episodes.

records.title: Acute short-term financial hardship can reduce turnout among poor German voters
records.source_unit: German individual survey respondents and elections observed under long-month-after-short bank-calendar timing
records.geography: Germany; comparative mechanism, not a United States estimate
records.boundary: This is a Germany-specific comparative causal mechanism: short-term bank-calendar-induced income scarcity reduced turnout intentions and election turnout, especially among poor respondents. It is not a United States estimate, does not measure trust change or a specific responsible actor, and does not observe remedy, recovery, switching, non-use, or durable political realignment.

records.title: Moving children out of high-poverty neighborhoods did not increase later turnout and reduced teen participation
records.source_unit: Low-income U.S. households and children randomly offered housing vouchers through the Moving to Opportunity experiment, linked to later voter-file outcomes
records.geography: United States; Baltimore, Boston, Chicago, Los Angeles, and New York City
records.boundary: This is a U.S. randomized housing/place-to-voting result, not a universal neighborhood effect or a proof that poverty reduction, income, education, or mobility automatically produces political participation.

records.title: Northern Irish 16-year-olds combine strong place belonging with divided community confidence, heavy social-media exposure, and selective political agency
records.source_unit: ARK, Northern Ireland Young Life and Times Survey 2026
records.geography: Northern Ireland; 16-year-olds invited from across the region
records.boundary: This record adds a public youth-survey route from place belonging and community tension through social-media exposure, online harm, safety, political agency, and environmental meaning. It is a Northern Ireland 16-year-old survey with a split instrument and self-reported measures; it does not establish causal effects, population-wide prevalence beyond the survey frame, future voting, platform telemetry, independently verified harm, or durable social cohesion.

records.title: ASEAN scam prevention is not converting into resolution, recovery, or durable digital trust
records.source_unit: GSMA ASEAN Consumer Scam Report 2026, covering Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam
records.geography: Six ASEAN countries; consumer survey estimates reported by the GSM Association
records.boundary: This record adds an ASEAN digital-consumer trust, scam-harm, resolution, recovery, and switching layer. It does not establish independently verified fraud prevalence, administrative case outcomes, causal trust loss, provider liability, or representative market-level switching.

records.title: Connected technology is becoming essential infrastructure, but consumer value now depends on reliability, support, trust, and total ownership cost
records.source_unit: Assurant, 2026 Global Connected Consumer Trends Report
records.geography: Global online consumer sentiment survey across connected-device users, with market snapshots including the United States, United Kingdom, Germany, Japan, India, Mexico, and Australia
records.boundary: This record adds a consumer-technology, ownership, support, trust, AI, and market-infrastructure route. It uses a company-sponsored aggregate survey and report synthesis, not respondent-level ingestion, observed transaction or claims data, a causal estimate of protection or support effects, an independent audit of AI trust, or proof that connected technology produces equal welfare across markets.

records.title: National pride can remain strong while everyday cohesion and institutional legitimacy weaken
records.source_unit: AthenaLab, National Identity and Social Cohesion: Chile in Perspective
records.geography: Chile; nationally representative adult survey fielded 30 July-16 August 2025 across 70 municipalities, plus qualitative interviews and grounded-theory analysis
records.boundary: This record adds a nation-state cohesion mechanism: emotional national belonging can persist while interpersonal trust, representative-institution legitimacy, and everyday cooperation weaken; migration and crisis solidarity expose the boundary. It does not establish causal effects, actual integration outcomes, violence, service burden, or generalize beyond the Chilean study design.

records.title: Data portability creates consumer choice only when shared data is accurate, comparable, timely, and usable
records.source_unit: Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, Data quality in the Consumer Data Right: Observations from the 2026 Data Quality Survey, September 2026
records.geography: Australia; Consumer Data Right ecosystem across banking, energy, and newly designated non-bank lending sectors
records.boundary: This record adds an Australia-specific data-quality-to-choice-and-recourse route. It is a small stakeholder survey and regulatory observation, not a representative consumer study, platform telemetry, incident census, causal estimate, or proof that data portability improves household financial outcomes; the next test is whether repeated data-quality and resolution measures predict actual switching, savings, fraud exposure, small-business productivity, and distributional access.

records.title: Australian cinema ticketing shows physical cultural access can be distorted by late mandatory fees
records.source_unit: Australian Competition and Consumer Commission Dendy Cinema drip-pricing infringement notice
records.geography: Australia; Dendy cinemas in New South Wales, Queensland, and the Australian Capital Territory
records.boundary: This record adds an Australian physical-culture enforcement episode linking cinema access to mandatory booking fees, late price disclosure, consumer decision time, and sector monitoring. The ACCC source was browser-readable but returned a 403 to shell retrieval in this pass; the retrieval hash therefore identifies the blocked response, while the reported facts are transcribed from the official ACCC publication. It does not estimate consumer harm, refund completion, attendance exclusion, or industry-wide prevalence.

records.title: Employer liquidation can leave lower-paid replacement work and a compensation order without verified recovery
records.source_unit: Primary Fair Work Commission decision [2024] FWC 2775, Adam Smith v Adcon Admin Pty Ltd
records.geography: Victoria, Australia
records.boundary: This record adds one employment-shutdown episode with lower-paid alternative work, quantified earnings trade-off, reported family and financial stress, liquidation, FEG advice, and an ordered remedy. It does not establish FEG eligibility or payment, compensation receipt, durable employment, household recovery, trust, recurrence, collective action, or exit.

records.title: A documented non-return decision can follow job search and alternative employment without proving durable distrust or recovery
records.source_unit: Primary Fair Work Commission decision [2023] FWC 2485 and order PR766604
records.geography: Melbourne, Australia
records.boundary: This record adds one primary case with observed job-search effort, alternative employment, an explicit non-return decision tied to a workplace mechanism, and an ordered compensation remedy. It does not establish payment receipt, full trust measurement, household recovery, recurrence, collective action, switching, or exit.

records.title: Compensation payment can be reported while reinstatement and durable recovery fail
records.source_unit: Official Fair Work Commission case-example summary of Meadley v Sort Worx Pty Ltd [2013] FCA 1012
records.geography: Australia
records.boundary: This record demonstrates a dated, publicly reported compensation payment without reinstatement, followed by additional court relief and penalty. It does not establish independent receipt verification, restored opportunity, adequate recovery, general enforcement performance, recurrence, trust change, collective action, or exit.

records.title: A forced employment exit can reach partial payment and compensation order while trust and full recovery remain open
records.source_unit: Primary Fair Work Commission decision [2025] FWC 1570 and order PR788459, Mudiyanselage case
records.geography: Melbourne, Australia
records.boundary: This record establishes one same-worker public case chain from persistent wage failure through complaint, forced exit, new employment, partial payment, compensation order, and reported broken trust. It does not establish full remedy receipt, adequate recovery, durable employment, recurrence, collective action, or general prevalence.

records.title: An unsuccessful alternative-employment search can coexist with an ordered remedy and no restored work
records.source_unit: Primary Fair Work Commission decision [2024] FWC 3523, IAA work-from-home employment case
records.geography: Australia
records.boundary: This record adds one primary adjudicated case with unsuccessful alternative-employment search, assessed income loss, non-reinstatement, and an ordered remedy. It does not establish payment receipt, household recovery, durable work, prevalence, trust, recurrence, collective action, switching, or exit.

records.title: Alternative employment can preserve work while transferring lower pay and travel costs after site-clearance loss
records.source_unit: Fair Work Commission Bulletin Volume 4/25, item 3, summarizing a mining employment unfair-dismissal and compensation decision
records.geography: Australia; drive-in/drive-out mining employment case
records.boundary: This record adds one public case in which alternative employment is observed alongside lower pay, travel burden, and a compensation order after site-clearance loss. It does not establish payment receipt, full recovery, prevalence, durable work, trust, action, recurrence, switching, or exit.

records.title: Alternative employment can coexist with an unfair-dismissal remedy and an unresolved payment boundary
records.source_unit: Primary Fair Work Commission decision [2023] FWC 2632, Westrip dismissal case
records.geography: Sydney, Australia
records.boundary: This record adds one primary adjudicated case with observed dismissal, alternative employment, a five-week transition, an assessed interim income gap, non-return through compensation in lieu of reinstatement, and an ordered remedy. It does not establish payment receipt, household recovery, durable trust, recurrence, collective action, switching, or exit.

records.title: Court-held funds can reach every worker in a small enforcement case while adequacy and durable recovery remain unknown
records.source_unit: Official Fair Work Ombudsman enforcement follow-up for Atkins Freight Services truck drivers
records.geography: Adelaide, Australia
records.boundary: This record closes a reported payment-receipt endpoint for ten workers after court enforcement and appeal. It does not establish independent receipt verification, adequacy, durable recovery, prevalence, or general enforcement performance.

records.title: Reported full back-pay can follow deliberate cashback exploitation while migrant-worker safety and recovery remain open
records.source_unit: Official Fair Work Ombudsman penalty follow-up release for Innovative Associates and owner
records.geography: Sydney, Australia; temporary graduate visa worker
records.boundary: This record closes a reported full-back-pay endpoint for one vulnerable migrant worker after deliberate cashback exploitation and public enforcement. It does not establish independent receipt verification, adequacy, durable recovery, prevalence, general enforcement performance, recurrence, collective action, or exit.

records.title: Reported full back-pay can follow worker exit and alternative-employment search without proving durable recovery
records.source_unit: Official Fair Work Ombudsman release and Federal Circuit Court reasons, Fair Work Ombudsman v Longridge Group Pty Ltd [2015] FCCA 129
records.geography: Adelaide, South Australia
records.boundary: This record contains two separate public worker episodes from commission-only underpayment through resignation, alternative-employment pursuit, complaint, enforcement, and institutionally reported full back-pay. It does not establish independent receipt verification, adequacy, durable livelihood, prevalence, recurrence, trust change, collective action, or exit.

records.title: A worker question can trigger large back-pay correction while individual reachability remains unresolved
records.source_unit: Official Fair Work Ombudsman release and enforceable undertaking for Southern Cross Care NSW and ACT
records.geography: New South Wales and Australian Capital Territory, Australia
records.boundary: This record closes a worker-triggered institutional-response and reported aggregate correction segment. It does not establish complete worker reachability, independent receipt, adequacy, durable payroll compliance, household recovery, prevalence, or general enforcement success.

records.title: Intergenerational politics is becoming a contest over who receives, finances, and governs simultaneous AI, energy, geopolitical, demographic, and care transitions
records.source_unit: Australian Treasury, 2026 Intergenerational Report, released 21 September 2026
records.geography: Australia; 40-year macroeconomic, demographic, fiscal, and policy projection to 2065-66
records.boundary: This record adds a long-horizon intergenerational-politics route from simultaneous AI, geopolitical, energy, demographic, care, and industrial transitions through housing, work, public finance, household security, and distributional judgment. It does not treat Treasury projections as realized outcomes, establish causal effects of reforms, or infer that aggregate growth will produce shared intergenerational benefit.

records.title: Mental-health awareness is rising while lived wellbeing deteriorates, especially for young adults, amid cost, work, access and digital pressures
records.source_unit: AXA and Ipsos, Mind Health Report 2026
records.geography: 18-country survey with longitudinal comparisons across countries surveyed in every wave
records.boundary: This record adds a health-and-social-pressure mechanism: rising mental-health awareness is not translating into improved lived wellbeing, with younger adults exposed to disproportionate distress and AI emerging as both an access layer and a trust/isolation risk. It is a cross-national public-opinion and wellbeing index source, not a clinical prevalence study, causal evaluation, provider-capacity audit or treatment recommendation.

records.title: Consumer choice is shifting from price alone toward perceived value, solo-life fit, concentrated trust, longevity, and AI-guided discovery
records.source_unit: Boston Consulting Group Center for Customer Insight, Five Consumer Behavior Shifts Reshaping Growth in 2026
records.geography: Consumers in 12 markets: Brazil, China, France, Germany, India, Italy, Japan, South Korea, Sweden, Turkey, the United Kingdom, and the United States
records.boundary: This record adds a publication-level consumer route across perceived value, price, time and convenience, solo living, longevity, trust, information overload, and AI-guided purchase discovery. It uses BCG's aggregate survey, interviews, and proprietary brand analysis, not individual purchase histories, household budgets, respondent-level psychological profiles, causal AI effects, welfare estimates, or proof that these themes apply uniformly across consumers or markets.

records.title: Citizens are increasingly open to AI-enabled government services, but legitimacy depends on visible human oversight, appeals, and public reporting
records.source_unit: Boston Consulting Group, 2026 Digital Government Citizen Survey
records.geography: 44 countries and 48,500 respondents; regional comparisons include the Americas, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and the Middle East and Africa
records.boundary: This record adds a public-sector AI legitimacy route across digital-service use, AI proficiency, agentic delegation, human oversight, appeals, public reporting, regional variation, and operational trust. It uses BCG’s public survey summary, not administrative service logs, representative country microdata, observed appeals, algorithmic error rates, causal implementation evidence, or proof that citizen openness equals safe or equitable deployment.

records.title: Post-pandemic social connection was broadly stable in Belgium, but young people and those living alone show specific functional losses
records.source_unit: Verhaegen et al., Social connection before and after the COVID-19 pandemic: results of the Belgian Health Interview Survey, BMC Public Health 2026
records.geography: Belgium, national population aged 15 years and older, with stratified analyses by age, household situation, sex, and education
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative social-connection route from pandemic-era disruption through national recovery, youth support, living alone, education, social satisfaction, and policy targeting. It is nationally sampled repeated cross-sectional evidence from Belgium, not a longitudinal causal estimate, global trend, qualitative relationship assessment, or proof that pandemic policy caused subgroup changes.

records.title: Belonging is becoming a practical test of whether everyday systems, places and institutions feel workable and fair
records.source_unit: Belonging Forum, 2026 Belonging Barometer
records.geography: United Kingdom adults aged 18 and over; nationally and politically representative weighted survey across all four nations
records.boundary: This record adds a UK belonging, place, participation and institutional-performance layer linking social connection to relationships, local spaces, housing, services, economic pressure, time, health and political representation. It is a nationally weighted cross-sectional survey and descriptive trend comparison, not a longitudinal panel, causal evaluation, behavioral observation or proof that any single factor produces belonging.

records.title: AI-led resilience is colliding with inflation, public-debt, non-bank, and digital-money risks that test financial stability and trust
records.source_unit: Bank for International Settlements, Annual Economic Report 2026
records.geography: Global monetary, financial, fiscal, AI-investment, supply-shock, non-bank, and digital-money systems
records.boundary: This record adds a global central-bank and financial-stability route across AI investment, inflation, public debt, non-bank finance, supply shocks, digital money, and trust. It uses aggregate policy analysis and system-level evidence, not household financial diaries, individual portfolio behavior, causal AI employment estimates, or a forecast of a particular crisis.

records.title: Consumer confidence rebounds on income hopes while living standards remain flat and housing, inflation, and rates keep shaping perceived room
records.source_unit: Bank of Korea, Consumer Survey Index for September 2026; official release indexed by Korea Development Institute Economic Information and Education Center
records.geography: South Korea; urban household consumer survey
records.boundary: This record adds a non-U.S. consumer-expectations route: composite sentiment, household living-standard perceptions, inflation expectations, housing-price expectations, and interest-rate concern can move on different margins. It does not establish realized consumption, affordability, household debt stress, housing transactions, or causal effects of policy or markets.

records.title: Brazil’s Pix transition is rapid but incomplete: actual cash displacement coexists with knowledge and connectivity barriers
records.source_unit: Banco Central do Brasil, second edition of O brasileiro e os hábitos de uso de meios de pagamento, data collected October–November 2023
records.geography: Brazil; national adult consumer survey, merchant survey, and one-week payment diaries, with payment-method, preference, income-receipt, and barrier dimensions
records.boundary: This record adds a Brazil payment-diary, preference, merchant, and digital-barrier layer to the cultural, social, and consumer atlas. It does not establish causal Pix effects, financial welfare, merchant profitability, fraud reduction, cultural consumption, or universal cash displacement.

records.title: Brazil’s cultural reach is broad digitally but physical participation remains sharply stratified by education and economic class
records.source_unit: Observatório Fundação Itaú, Hábitos Culturais 6ª edição, with technical support from Datafolha
records.geography: Brazil; people aged 16 to 65, with national socioeconomic and education comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a current Brazilian demand-side hybrid-access and socioeconomic-gap layer. It does not establish causal class effects, venue supply, household spending, device or data affordability, cultural quality, or durable participation trajectories.

records.title: Brazil’s cultural economy is large and regionally uneven, with employment growth alongside informality and a weak education-to-cultural-work conversion
records.source_unit: IBGE Sistema de Informações e Indicadores Culturais 2013-2024, seventh edition
records.geography: Brazil; national, state, capital-municipality, sector, occupation, education, and cultural-trade comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a Brazil cultural-production, labor, entrepreneurship, education, trade, and regional-inequality layer beneath cultural participation and consumer-demand findings. It does not establish cultural welfare, audience access, job quality, causal policy effects, or household-level spending and participation.

records.title: Brazilian retail volume contracts monthly while essential, technology, cultural-goods, and regional paths diverge
records.source_unit: IBGE Monthly Survey of Trade, July 2026
records.geography: Brazil
records.boundary: This record adds a Brazil retail-volume, category, and regional layer to the cross-country consumer comparison. It does not measure online commerce, unique consumers, household affordability, cultural attendance, causal substitution, or merchant margins. Books and stationery are treated as a retail category rather than a proxy for cultural meaning.

records.title: Brazil's cultural life is digitally domestic, while cultural policy has high approval despite low public awareness
records.source_unit: Brazil Ministry of Culture, Hábitos e Consumo de Cultura / Percepções sobre as Políticas Culturais
records.geography: Brazil; all 27 federative units; adults aged 16 and above
records.boundary: This record adds Brazilian evidence on cultural reach, access constraints, intended venue return, and perceived legitimacy of cultural policy. It is a commissioned self-report survey with qualitative context, not transaction data, causal policy evaluation, or a direct measure of durable institutional trust.

records.title: Young people experience social and cultural infrastructure as an access-and-activation system, not simply a stock of available places
records.source_unit: British Academy / London Development Trust, Investigating Young People's Views and Experiences of Social and Cultural Infrastructure in England, Scotland and Wales
records.geography: England, Scotland, and Wales; national phase across seven sites plus an initial London phase
records.boundary: This record adds a youth social-infrastructure layer: safety, affordability, transport, relational support, identity, cultural access, and co-creation jointly determine whether nominally available places become usable sources of wellbeing, belonging, and civic capacity. It is purposive qualitative focus-group evidence, not a representative prevalence estimate, causal evaluation, attendance dataset, or proof that consultation transfers decision power.

records.title: Democratic and market institutions are eroding across many countries while civic resistance and selective reform remain active counterforces
records.source_unit: Bertelsmann Stiftung, Bertelsmann Transformation Index 2026 Global Trends: Repression meets resistance
records.geography: 137 developing and transition countries assessed across political transformation, economic transformation, and governance
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative political-institutional route from elections, participation rights, rule of law, governance capacity, market competition, and civic resistance through legitimacy, economic opportunity, public problem-solving, and geopolitical resilience. It uses expert-coded country comparisons and review-period synthesis, not respondent-level data, a causal regime model, a prediction of democratic transition, or proof that any one protest produces durable reform.

records.title: Cultural-sector AI adoption is being negotiated through creator rights, cultural sovereignty, trust, co-design and institutional readiness
records.source_unit: Government of Canada, What We Heard at The National Summit on Artificial Intelligence and Culture
records.geography: Canadian cultural and creative sector, including creators, cultural organizations, technology companies, Indigenous organizations, labour, civil society and governments
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural-AI governance signal linking adoption to trust, copyright, creator livelihoods, cultural and Indigenous sovereignty, co-design, infrastructure, literacy, training and institutional readiness. It is an organizer-produced synthesis of a 314-person summit, not representative public opinion, formal consensus, sector-wide adoption measurement or a causal evaluation.

records.title: Arts and culture operate as social infrastructure, but cost and welcome determine who can convert participation into belonging
records.source_unit: Canadian Heritage and Canada Council for the Arts, Arts and Heritage Access and Availability Survey 2025-26, conducted by Leger
records.geography: Canada; national survey of residents ages 16 and older, including a telephone sample from the territories
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative cultural-infrastructure route from arts access through socializing, local and national belonging, perceived community value, and organizational contribution while preserving cost and welcome as access conditions. It is a national survey summary, not a causal evaluation, a measure of actual cohesion, a longitudinal participation panel, or proof that cultural institutions distribute belonging equally.

records.title: Economic immigration selection is being evaluated as a prediction-and-matching system whose scores shape occupational mobility and migrant household security
records.source_unit: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada, Express Entry and Labour Market Outcomes of Economic Immigrants, September 2026
records.geography: Canada; economic immigrants admitted through Express Entry and comparison non-Express Entry streams, linked administrative and census outcomes
records.boundary: This record adds a migration-selection-to-work-mobility route from ranking factors through employment, wages, occupational matching, household security, and the governance of immigrant selection. It does not establish causal effects of Express Entry, measure social belonging or family outcomes, or imply that predictive validity alone makes a selection factor normatively fair.

records.title: Canadian cost pressure, social connection, and care exit form a linked but non-causal consumer-social pressure pattern
records.source_unit: Mental Health Research Canada, Understanding the Mental Health of Canadians Poll 29: Economic pressures, social connections and care
records.geography: Canada; national online survey of people aged 16 and older
records.boundary: This record adds a Canadian material-pressure, social-connection, and care-continuity layer. It does not establish clinical prevalence, causal effects of cost or connection, verified household hardship, cultural participation, or treatment quality.

records.title: Consumers are redefining value as a hybrid bargain: fair prices, reliable quality, controlled AI and meaningful human support
records.source_unit: Capgemini Research Institute, What matters to today's consumer 2026
records.geography: Consumers aged 18 and over across Australia, Canada, France, Germany, India, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands, Spain, Sweden, the United Kingdom and the United States
records.boundary: This record adds a consumer-value and AI-commerce layer linking inflation fatigue to fairness, quality, switching, emotional indulgence, controlled automation, data concern, human support and social commerce. It is a 12-country survey with executive interviews, not respondent-level ingestion, transaction telemetry, a causal evaluation, a complete global consumer census or proof that stated preferences become realized loyalty.

records.title: Unpaid care is becoming an employment-continuity fault line: workers cut hours, absorb stress, or leave depending on the support around them
records.source_unit: Carers UK, Balancing work and unpaid care: a critical issue
records.geography: United Kingdom; adults and workers with current or past unpaid-care experience
records.boundary: This record adds a UK employment-continuity route to the atlas: unpaid care becomes a material work and time constraint, with graded consequences from stress and reduced hours to employment exit. It does not establish causality, validate population counts administratively, measure care intensity, or show that paid leave would produce the proposed outcomes. The report is an advocacy publication and includes Standard Life sponsorship context.

records.title: Election legitimacy is conditional on an information environment voters can authenticate, correct, and locally explain
records.source_unit: Catawba College Center for North Carolina Politics & Public Service, Catawba College-YouGov National Survey: The Ballots & Bots
records.geography: United States; adults 18 and older
records.boundary: This record adds an election-specific legitimacy route: commitment to fair elections can coexist with weaker confidence when voters perceive that political content is synthetic, difficult to authenticate, fast to spread, and hard for officials to correct. It does not establish actual synthetic-content exposure, detection accuracy, persuasion, post-election behavior, causal effects of safeguards, or the quality of interpersonal information. The survey was commissioned for a conference and the linked crosstabs/methodology resources were access-gated during review.

records.title: Chile’s cultural participation is high in aggregate but sharply constrained by age, socioeconomic status, disability, and time
records.source_unit: Instituto Nacional de Estadísticas de Chile and Ministry of Cultures, Arts and Heritage, National Survey of Cultural Participation and Reading Behavior 2024
records.geography: Chile; urban residents aged 15 and over, with age, socioeconomic, education, disability, sex, and household-composition dimensions
records.boundary: This record adds a Chilean cultural-participation, unmet-demand, time constraint, socioeconomic, disability, and reading layer. It does not establish causal barriers, national rural participation, cultural quality, household spending, or individual-level reasons beyond self-reported survey categories.

records.title: A licensing control can contract early critical-mineral shipments and raise price uncertainty without proving durable geopolitical leverage
records.source_unit: China export-control announcement, MOFCOM licensing update, and USITC March 2024 critical-mineral briefing
records.geography: China and international gallium/germanium supply chain with U.S. import exposure
records.boundary: This record establishes a dated export-control, early shipment-contraction, and price-response sequence. It does not establish a sustained cutoff, U.S. shortage, firm-level production loss, household effect, or realized geopolitical concession.

records.title: China's cultural-consumption growth is real but remains stratified by household place and room
records.source_unit: National Bureau of Statistics of China 2025 household income and consumption expenditure release
records.geography: China; nationwide, urban, and rural resident aggregates
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative household-budget and cultural-consumption layer for China. It supports a place-stratified spending signal, not equal cultural access, attendance, digital use, quality, cultural meaning, or causal welfare; the education-culture-recreation category is broader than culture alone.

records.title: China’s August 2026 consumer basket shows weak aggregate retail growth alongside online, category, and price divergence
records.source_unit: National Bureau of Statistics of China August 2026 Consumer Price Index and Total Retail Sales of Consumer Goods releases
records.geography: China, national urban and rural consumer-price and retail-sales indicators
records.boundary: This record adds a high-frequency Chinese consumer-price and retail-composition layer. It does not establish household-specific affordability, quantities, cultural participation, consumer sentiment, durable preference change, or causal welfare effects.

records.title: China's cultural sector grew in H1 2026 while communication channels contracted and creative-information services expanded
records.source_unit: National Bureau of Statistics of China, Business Revenue of Enterprises above the Designated Size Engaged in Culture and Related Industries, First Half of 2026
records.geography: China; nationwide cultural and related-industry enterprises above designated size
records.boundary: This record adds a supply-side cultural-economy layer to the household and participation corpus. It measures reported revenue among above-designated-size enterprises, not consumer spending, audience behavior, employment quality, profit distribution, platform power, or cultural meaning; the category definitions are broader than culture alone.

records.title: China’s rural consumption is growing faster than urban consumption while the cultural-spending level gap remains large
records.source_unit: National Bureau of Statistics of China, Households’ Income and Consumption Expenditure in the First Half of 2026
records.geography: China; national, urban, and rural resident household income and consumption expenditure
records.boundary: This record adds a current Chinese household-consumption and urban-rural budget layer. It does not identify cultural activity participation, frequency, taste, consumer confidence, affordability, causal urban-rural effects, or the composition of education/culture/recreation spending.

records.title: Eating is becoming an occasion-and-channel system shaped by budget, convenience, identity and where food is consumed
records.source_unit: Circana, Eating Patterns in America 2026
records.geography: United States food, beverage, retail and foodservice consumption
records.boundary: This record adds an everyday food-culture and consumption-system layer. It treats Circana's public page as a commercial report overview: the page establishes the measurement scope and analytical frame, but does not disclose the full findings, sampling, weighting, category tables, household distribution, causal mechanisms or food-security outcomes.

records.title: Community is being repositioned from attention and audience growth toward belonging, trust, retention and intentionally designed human connection
records.source_unit: Circle, The 2026 Community Trends Report
records.geography: Community builders, creators, brands and online communities; report scope is not fully disclosed in the public summary
records.boundary: This record adds a commercial community-culture signal linking AI-generated content and algorithmic noise to perceived human connection, belonging, creator and brand strategy, intentional design and platform economics. It is based on Circle’s public summary and self-described research, not a representative population study, independent behavioral audit or causal evaluation.

records.title: Civil society is responding to democratic, technological, geopolitical, climate, migration, and gender-rights pressure through organized resistance and accountability work
records.source_unit: CIVICUS, 2026 State of Civil Society Report, March 2026
records.geography: Around 100 countries and territories, with civil-society action across democracy, technology, global governance, conflict, climate, migration, gender rights, and youth protest
records.boundary: This record adds a civil-society route from democratic and geopolitical pressure through technology, rights exposure, collective resistance, youth mobilization, and accountability. It is a curated global publication, not a representative public-opinion survey, causal evaluation of activism, country ranking, or proof that documented resistance produces durable institutional change.

records.title: Civil society is shifting toward distributed resistance as geopolitical impunity, technology power and civic-space contraction reinforce one another
records.source_unit: CIVICUS, 2026 State of Civil Society Report
records.geography: Global civil society, civic space, democracy, technology, geopolitics, conflict, climate, migration, gender rights and Gen Z mobilization
records.boundary: This record adds a global civic and geopolitical layer to the atlas: the source connects democratic retreat, impunity, technology power, civic-space contraction, funding pressure and distributed resistance. It is a CIVICUS advocacy and analytical synthesis using selected cases, not a respondent survey, representative movement census, democracy index or causal evaluation.

records.title: Shrinking civic space and contested global rules are shifting the cost of dissent toward civil society while resistance adapts
records.source_unit: CIVICUS, 2026 State of Civil Society Report
records.geography: Global civil-society, civic-space, technology-governance, conflict, climate, migration, and gender-rights analysis
records.boundary: This record adds an advocacy-informed geopolitical and state-consequences route linking civic space, technology governance, multilateral rules, repression, resistance, and external accountability. It is not a neutral country index, incident census, respondent political-attitudes dataset, or causal estimate of civic action or state behavior.

records.title: Colombia's cultural and creative economy expands overall while cultural industries contract and employment composition shifts
records.source_unit: DANE Cuenta Satélite de Economía Cultural y Creativa, 2023 definitive–2025 preliminary
records.geography: Colombia
records.boundary: This record adds a Colombia supply-side cultural-economy and labor layer to the Mexico household-budget and participation findings. It does not measure consumer attendance, household cultural spending, subjective cultural meaning, firm profitability, earnings distribution, or causal effects. 2025 values are preliminary and 2024 values provisional where marked by DANE.

records.title: Colombia’s unpaid-care time remains a large gendered constraint on household and cultural room
records.source_unit: DANE Colombia, National Time Use Survey (ENUT), preliminary results for October 2024–March 2025
records.geography: Colombia; civilian non-institutional population aged 10 years and older, with national, urban-headquarters, rural-dispersed, regional, sex, and place-of-birth dimensions
records.boundary: This record adds a Colombian time-and-care layer to the cultural, social, and consumer atlas. It does not measure cultural attendance directly, establish causal gender or migration effects, value unpaid work monetarily, or identify household bargaining, wellbeing, or consumer outcomes.

records.title: Consumer value pressure is being expressed through scale-versus-value retailer choice
records.source_unit: Coresight Research, Consumers Reward Scale as Amazon Gains: US Consumer Survey Insights, September 29, 2026 public report preview
records.geography: United States; consumer sentiment and retailer/category shopping tracked weekly and described by income group
records.boundary: This record captures only the public preview of a proprietary Coresight report. It does not establish sample composition, retailer market share, causal substitution, price pass-through, household welfare, durable loyalty or general consumer behavior; full report access or independent transaction and household evidence is required.

records.title: European democratic resilience is being reframed as a whole-society security problem spanning rights, trust, participation, and technology
records.source_unit: Council of Europe, Report of the Secretary General 2026: The New Democratic Pact for Europe in Times of Rupture
records.geography: Council of Europe member states and broader European democratic-security context, with a focus on institutional, civic, social-rights, information, election, and technology resilience
records.boundary: This record adds a European democratic-security and institutional-trust route linking war and geopolitical rupture, information manipulation, social rights, civic space, elections, inclusion, digital technology, AI, and democratic participation. It is a strategic report and consultation synthesis, not a representative public-opinion survey, democracy score, causal security model, or proof that proposed Pact actions have been implemented.

records.title: Diaspora communities are being reframed as democratic and social-cohesion infrastructure rather than only integration populations
records.source_unit: Council of Europe Parliamentary Assembly, The role of diasporas and migrants in developing social cohesion and democratic engagement, Doc. 16476
records.geography: Council of Europe member states and European diaspora communities; report and draft recommendations for national and European institutions
records.boundary: This record adds a diaspora-to-democratic-legitimacy route from multilingual and multicultural social capacity through consultation, civic education, formal and deliberative participation, organizational funding, and institutional feedback. It does not establish representative diaspora voice, implementation, causal cohesion effects, or electoral outcomes.

records.title: Australian arts participation is culturally connective but increasingly cost-constrained
records.source_unit: Creative Australia, Creative Transformations: Results of the National Arts Participation Survey 2025
records.geography: Australia; nationally representative survey of people aged 15 years and over
records.boundary: This record adds a current Australian arts-participation, cultural-connection, cost-barrier, and arts-education layer. It does not provide migrant-specific attendance cross-tabs, causal education effects, verified spending, or equal cultural access across household groups.

records.title: Crises affect social cohesion through changing dependence, power asymmetries, interests, and the perceived legitimacy of cooperation
records.source_unit: Koster, Lang, and Van Lange, Interdependence explains how and when crises impact social cohesion, Communications Psychology 2026
records.geography: Theory-guided review drawing on evidence across natural hazards, pandemics, economic crises, and wars in multiple national and community contexts
records.boundary: This record adds a crisis-mechanism route from changing mutual dependence, unequal vulnerability, conflicting interests, and coordination mode through horizontal and vertical social cohesion. It is a theory-guided review and hypothesis framework, not a pooled causal estimate, crisis forecast, or claim that any crisis has one uniform social effect.

records.title: Consumer culture is increasingly polycultural, with identity, trusted voices and AI reshaping discovery and choice
records.source_unit: Culturati Research & Consulting, Cultural Mosaic 5.0 syndicated report public overview
records.geography: United States consumer segments identified in the public overview as Hispanic, Black, Asian and General Market; public sample frame N=5,050
records.boundary: This record adds a public cultural-intelligence layer linking identity, polycultural segmentation, creators, trusted voices and AI-mediated discovery to consumer decision-making. It is deliberately limited to the public overview of a syndicated report: detailed results, weighting, field dates, full questionnaire, causal mechanisms and subgroup outcome estimates are not publicly available on the source page.

records.title: Sustained organizational performance is framed as a collective culture system linking engagement, confidence, leadership, voice, energy, and resource alignment rather than individual heroics
records.source_unit: Culture Amp, Find your 47% advantage: Turning culture into strategy in the age of AI
records.geography: Global organizations represented in Culture Amp benchmark and research data; organization size and industry comparisons reported
records.boundary: This record adds an organizational-culture route from engagement, confidence, leadership, voice, energy, and resource alignment through retention, performance, strategic execution, and AI-enabled people management. It relies on sponsor-produced benchmark and proxy analysis, with incomplete public methodology and no causal identification; the stock-price comparison is not proof that culture causes market performance.

records.title: Digital life is becoming a layered utility: connectivity, sociality and AI are expanding together but unevenly
records.source_unit: DataReportal, Digital 2026 Mid-Year Global Update Report
records.geography: Global digital users, with GWI survey comparisons across 54 economies and platform, connectivity and web-traffic evidence from multiple data partners
records.boundary: This record adds a global digital-connectivity, platform-attention and AI-use layer linking access to sociality, information, advice, learning, entertainment and uneven technological dependence. It synthesizes publisher and partner estimates plus surveys, not respondent-level ingestion, a direct global census, unique-person counts, behavioral telemetry, causal effects or evidence that digital access produces equal welfare.

records.title: The digital economy is shifting from access expansion toward capability, agency, resilience, and strategic fragmentation
records.source_unit: Digital Cooperation Organization, Digital Economy Trends 2026, third edition
records.geography: Global digital economy, regional readiness comparisons, and expert survey perspectives across public, private, and societal stakeholders
records.boundary: This record adds a global digital-economy foresight and readiness route linking AI, automation, energy, data, cybersecurity, trade, sovereignty, work, digital well-being, and social agency. It is an expert-informed publication and survey synthesis, not a technology forecast, firm census, individual employment panel, causal employment estimate, or proof that preparedness produces equitable outcomes.

records.title: Media consumption is reorganizing around persistent fandom, fragmented platforms, creator connection, and AI-enabled continuity between releases
records.source_unit: Deloitte Center for Technology, Media & Telecommunications, 2026 Digital Media Trends: Capturing always-on fandom between releases and seasons, 25 March 2026
records.geography: United States consumer media and entertainment behavior across streaming, social media, music, gaming, live events, creators, and fandom communities
records.boundary: This record adds a Deloitte consumer-media signal about fandom, streaming fragmentation, creator-mediated discovery, and labeled generative-AI engagement. It is aggregate survey and industry analysis, not respondent-level ingestion, a causal panel, a global cultural census, a measure of creator welfare, or proof that platform aggregation benefits audiences.

records.title: India's consumer economy is moving toward AI-assisted, transparent, connected commerce where governance and resilient supply chains become part of competitive advantage
records.source_unit: Deloitte India and FICCI, Consumer trends IGNITEing growth and governance
records.geography: India FMCG, retail, and e-commerce sectors
records.boundary: This record adds an India consumer-economy signal on AI-assisted discovery, transparency-led choice, connected commerce, resilient supply chains, governance, sustainability, and globalizing Indian brands. It uses the official Deloitte press-release summary of a Deloitte India-FICCI report; it is not a representative national survey, a complete market census, a causal evaluation, or proof that stated consumer preferences become realized purchasing power or improved welfare.

records.title: Gen Z and millennials are sequencing ambition around stability, sustainable work, purpose and AI readiness rather than rejecting advancement
records.source_unit: Deloitte Global 2026 Gen Z and Millennial Survey, Progress on Their Own Terms
records.geography: 44 countries; global survey of Gen Z and millennial adults with supplementary qualitative insights from business leaders
records.boundary: This record adds a global work-and-life sequencing layer: financial and housing constraints are changing the timing and conditions of ambition, while AI adoption is outpacing organizational readiness and purpose remains central to job satisfaction. It is a Deloitte-sponsored cross-sectional survey with qualitative leader insight, not a representative longitudinal labor panel, causal evaluation, clinical assessment, employer performance audit or proof of actual AI productivity or displacement.

records.title: Younger adults are sequencing ambition around financial security, sustainable work, purpose, and practical AI capability
records.source_unit: Deloitte Global, 2026 Gen Z and Millennial Survey: Progress on Their Own Terms
records.geography: 44 countries; more than 22,500 Gen Z and millennial respondents, with qualitative business-leader interviews
records.boundary: This record adds a generational work-and-life sequencing route connecting cost of living, housing, major life decisions, sustainable workload, AI adoption, mental health, digital fatigue, purpose and leadership. It is not a causal labor-market model, a representative estimate of all young adults, an employer audit, or respondent-level raw-data ingestion.

records.title: Organizations are moving from balancing AI tensions to making deliberate choices about human–machine work, adaptation and trust
records.source_unit: Deloitte and Oxford Economics, 2026 Global Human Capital Trends
records.geography: Global organizations, business and HR leaders, workers, managers and executives across 89 countries and multiple industries
records.boundary: This record adds an organizational AI-and-work layer: leaders describe agility, human–machine redesign, human advantage, cultural debt and trust as strategic choices. It relies on Deloitte/Oxford Economics surveys, supplementary executive research and interviews; it is not a representative worker panel, observed productivity study, causal evaluation, or proof of improved job quality, autonomy or worker power.

records.title: Generative technology is accelerating cultural production while consumers seek craft, friction, grounding, and reconnection
records.source_unit: Dentsu Creative, Generative Realities Trends Report 2026
records.geography: Consumer and cultural trend synthesis informed by research across the United States, United Kingdom, India, Spain, Brazil, China, and Japan
records.boundary: This record adds a commercial-cultural route across generative technology, cultural production, craft, fandom, connectivity ambivalence, grounding, and reconnection. It uses published aggregate survey and strategist synthesis, not raw respondent-level data, individual consumer histories, clinical mental-health measures, causal technology effects, or a universal forecast of consumer behavior.

records.title: India's next screen era is framed around relevance, cultural afterlife, and plural mainstreams across languages, places, and communities
records.source_unit: Dentsu IWMBuzz, Stream Culture 2026
records.geography: India's screen and streaming culture, as framed by a public industry field guide
records.boundary: This record adds an India-focused screen-culture signal on relevance over abundance, meaning, cultural afterlife, and plural mainstreams across languages, places, and communities. It is based on the official public summary of an industry field guide, not respondent-level data, a representative national survey, a complete streaming-market census, causal evidence, or the full gated report.

records.title: Fashion culture is moving from algorithmic novelty toward edited identity, repeatable staples, nostalgia, everyday ritual, and circular self-expression
records.source_unit: Depop, The Edited Self: 2026 Trends Report, public newsroom summary supported by platform search, sales, and cultural research
records.geography: Depop global peer-to-peer fashion community and 2026 fashion-culture forecast
records.boundary: This record adds a fashion and resale-culture signal about intentional editing, repetition, nostalgia, everyday ritual, sport, circularity, and public belonging. It is a platform-owned trend forecast using aggregate search and sales interpretation, not respondent-level data, an independent market estimate, a causal sustainability evaluation, or proof that all consumers are moving away from novelty and volume.

records.title: Planned educational routes are confident but unevenly informed: pathway usability depends on awareness, finance, place, and support
records.source_unit: UK Department for Education, Parent, Pupil and Learner Voice: May 2026
records.geography: England; parents, secondary pupils, and 16-19 pupils and learners
records.boundary: This record adds a learner-voice route from planned education choices through route visibility, confidence, finance anxiety, attendance, and mental-health support conversion. It does not establish confirmed enrollment, completion, debt, service adequacy, or later labor-market outcomes. The source is an official DfE panel survey with multiple subgroup bases, rounded self-reports, and limited comparability across survey years.

records.title: Streaming is becoming cultural discovery infrastructure, but platform value and local cultural benefits remain jointly contested
records.source_unit: Digital Media Association 2026 Annual Report, using MusicWatch consumer research
records.geography: United States plus Canada, Brazil, Chile, and Mexico; comparative consumer streaming and music-culture findings
records.boundary: This record adds a platform-to-culture and platform-to-consumption route across engagement, spending, discovery, back-catalogue use, local culture, AI-generated music, and regulation. It does not treat industry-sponsored satisfaction as independent welfare evidence, infer artist-level distribution, or establish that streaming causes cultural diversity, local-artist success, or consumer surplus.

records.title: Opportunity is a readiness ecology, not an exam result: educators connect young people’s pathways to skills, place, support, and confidence
records.source_unit: UK Department for Work and Pensions / YouGov, Survey of Education Professionals: Young People and Work Report, August 27, 2026
records.geography: Great Britain; teachers and education professionals surveyed through the YouGov panel
records.boundary: This record adds an education-to-work opportunity route: professionals describe employability as a readiness ecology shaped by work-readiness, confidence, local opportunity, transport, health, SEND support, family context, and work experience, alongside academic attainment. It does not establish young people’s actual transitions, causal curriculum effects, pathway quality, or employer outcomes. The source is a DWP-commissioned YouGov online panel of professional perceptions.

records.title: European audiovisual culture is expanding as a market while creator security, public media, and cultural control remain uneven
records.source_unit: European Audiovisual Observatory, Key Trends 2026: Television, Cinema, Video and On-Demand Audiovisual Services
records.geography: Pan-European audiovisual sector, covering EU and wider Council of Europe markets with comparisons across creators, producers, broadcasters, platforms, audiences, and public media
records.boundary: This record adds a European audiovisual cultural-economy route from creator work and social protection through streaming investment, market concentration, public media funding, and cultural access.
