It uses sectoral and market data, not individual creator panels, causal platform evaluations, audience-level welfare measures, or proof that market scale produces cultural diversity.

records.title: Public demand for economic-system change is broad, but the social contract is weakened by distrust that governments can deliver long-term benefits
records.source_unit: Earth4All, Rebuild Trust: Rigged economies, fractured societies and the case for change, Earth for All Survey 2026, conducted by Ipsos
records.geography: 17 countries representing 58% of global GDP, 38% of world population, and 37% of fossil-fuel and industrial CO2 emissions; G20 countries surveyed except China, Russia, and Saudi Arabia, plus Sweden
records.boundary: This record adds a social-contract route from perceived inequality and demand for economic-system change through long-term government trust, perceived social division, democratic legitimacy, and consent for climate transformation. It is a weighted cross-national public-opinion study, not an objective inequality estimate, causal test of trust, forecast of political regime change, or respondent-level life-history dataset.

records.title: Euro-area household expectations remain stable in aggregate while income and credit exposure diverge sharply by position
records.source_unit: European Central Bank, Consumer Expectations Survey results – August 2026
records.geography: Euro area; adults in Belgium, Germany, Ireland, Greece, Spain, France, Italy, the Netherlands, Austria, Portugal and Finland
records.boundary: This record adds a distributional expectations route: lower-income euro-area consumers report higher inflation, unemployment and mortgage-rate expectations while aggregate income, spending and credit-access expectations remain comparatively stable. The monthly online survey is broad and repeated but self-reported; it does not measure realized prices, borrowing, spending, employment, housing transactions, or causal household outcomes.

records.title: Euro-area households expect spending to outpace income while inflation and credit expectations remain unequal by income
records.source_unit: European Central Bank Consumer Expectations Survey results, August 2026
records.geography: Euro area; adults aged 18 and over in 11 countries, with income-quintile, inflation, income, spending, unemployment, housing, and credit-expectation dimensions
records.boundary: This record adds euro-area household expectations and distributional outlook evidence. It does not establish realized inflation, spending, unemployment, credit access, housing transactions, cultural behavior, or causal effects of monetary policy.

records.title: Trust is retreating toward familiar circles as economic anxiety, geopolitical tension, and technological disruption widen social distance
records.source_unit: Edelman Trust Institute, 2026 Edelman Trust Barometer
records.geography: Published global trust survey covering 28 countries, with cross-country and socioeconomic comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a cross-cultural trust, insularity, optimism, class-divergence, and social-media-brokering route. It uses published aggregate survey results and report synthesis, not raw respondent-level records, reweighted microdata, causal attitude models, individual political histories, or proof that trust brokering resolves polarization.

records.title: Unpaid care is a gendered time-and-work infrastructure whose effects depend on formal services, household position, and digital support
records.source_unit: European Institute for Gender Equality, CARE Survey second-wave technical report
records.geography: All 27 EU Member States; population aged 16–74; fieldwork October–December 2024
records.boundary: This record adds a European care-and-time infrastructure route across unpaid long-term care, childcare, housework, leisure, volunteering, formal services, employment, transport, digital tools, migration, and work–life balance. It uses EIGE’s published survey design and scope, not respondent-level results, a probability sample, time-use diaries, causal estimates, observed service quality, wage histories, or proof that care responsibility produces one universal gender or labor-market outcome.

records.title: European consumers report growing confidence in their own food choices while trust in the surrounding information environment remains fragile
records.source_unit: EIT Food Consumer Observatory, Trust Report 2026: Who do consumers believe?
records.geography: Consumers across 18 European countries; nearly 20,000 respondents in the TrustTracker study
records.boundary: This record adds a European food-information and consumer-trust layer. It uses self-reported, cross-national TrustTracker survey findings summarized on the EIT Food report page; it does not provide a public respondent-level file, objective accuracy test, causal model, realized diet or sustainability outcomes, or intervention evaluation. The report is produced by an agrifood consumer-observatory organization and should be read with its sponsorship and disclosure context.

records.title: England’s loneliness rate is broadly stable nationally but sharply stratified by disability, deprivation, and place
records.source_unit: Department for Culture, Media and Sport / Community and Engagement Survey 2025/26 loneliness report
records.geography: England; representative estimates for people aged 16 and over, with local-authority and subgroup breakdowns
records.boundary: This record adds an England social-connection and unequal-exposure layer. It does not establish causal loneliness mechanisms, mental-health outcomes, cultural participation, service effectiveness, or individual trajectories.

records.title: England’s cultural participation is shifting by mode and institution while community action rises modestly
records.source_unit: Department for Culture, Media and Sport Community and Engagement Survey 2025/26 Quarter 2 statistical release and data tables
records.geography: England; adults aged 16 and over, with national, ITL2, and Combined Authority coverage
records.boundary: This record adds a current England cultural-and-community participation layer that separates physical and digital cultural modes, sector-specific change, volunteering, local-official contact, and loneliness. It does not establish causal substitution, cultural welfare, institutional responsiveness, attendance frequency, or durable social cohesion.

records.title: Museum and gallery engagement varies sharply by English local area, with physical and digital access following different geographies
records.source_unit: Department for Culture, Media and Sport, Community and Engagement Survey 2025/26: museums and galleries
records.geography: England; adults aged 16 and over, national and local-authority estimates
records.boundary: This record adds an England local-area, museum/galleries, physical/digital engagement layer. It does not establish venue supply, travel time, affordability, cultural belonging, service quality, causal local-authority effects, or that digital access substitutes for physical attendance.

records.title: England’s arts participation remains physical-first while digital access is thinner among disadvantaged groups
records.source_unit: UK Department for Culture, Media and Sport and Department for Science, Innovation and Technology, Participation Survey 2024–25
records.geography: England; adults aged 16 and over, with arts participation, physical/digital mode, disability, socioeconomic classification, and deprivation dimensions
records.boundary: This record adds a national England arts-participation and physical/digital optionality layer. It does not establish transport causality, venue access, consumer spending, cultural quality, or causal effects of deprivation, disability, occupation, or digital use.

records.title: Unpaid carers face a durable time-and-work conversion constraint while service involvement remains limited
records.source_unit: Department of Health and Social Care, Survey of Adult Carers in England 2025 to 2026
records.geography: England; unpaid adult carers aged 18 and over known to local authorities
records.boundary: This record adds a current England unpaid-care route from time and care intensity through work, household financial pressure, social contact, health, information access, and service voice. It does not estimate all-carer prevalence, causal employment loss, household welfare, care-recipient outcomes, or equal local-authority service quality.

records.title: Child safety online is becoming a developmental social contract: platforms, families, regulators, and offline institutions share responsibility for digital autonomy
records.source_unit: European Commission Special Panel report Child Safety Online: Protecting and Empowering Minors in a Digital World, published July 2026
records.geography: European Union, with comparative references to Australia, Brazil, Canada, the United Kingdom, and other national approaches
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural and political subtheme in which online childhood is treated as shared social infrastructure: developmental autonomy, safety by design, privacy-preserving age assurance, platform accountability, child voice, complaint remedy, digital literacy, and offline alternatives. The report is an independent co-chair policy synthesis and explicitly should not be treated as the European Commission's official position; it does not establish causal effects, platform compliance, prevalence of harm, developmental outcomes, or the effectiveness and equity of age restrictions.

records.title: EU online consumer adoption is expanding faster than protection, trust, and sustainable-choice capacity
records.source_unit: European Commission Consumer Conditions Scoreboard 2025 and November 2024 Consumer Conditions Survey
records.geography: EU27 plus Iceland and Norway; representative consumer survey across the Single Market
records.boundary: This record adds EU-wide consumer-conditions evidence connecting e-commerce growth to purchase problems, scams, fake reviews, targeted-ad concerns, cost-of-living pressure, repair barriers, sustainable-choice decline, and institutional trust. It does not provide verified fraud loss, household welfare, causal effects, platform-level attribution, or a single common denominator for all conditional indicators.

records.title: EU consumer authorities converted ticket-resale concerns into platform commitments on identity, price, pressure, ranking, and remedy
records.source_unit: European Commission Consumer Protection Cooperation Network dialogue with Viagogo
records.geography: European Union and European Economic Area consumer-facing Viagogo websites
records.boundary: This record adds an EU/EEA ticket-resale platform-governance episode linking seller identity, price clarity, ranking, scarcity pressure, fraud/cancellation, legal jurisdiction, and remedy routes. It does not quantify affected consumers, verify implementation or compliance, estimate ticket affordability, or prove that the commitments changed cultural participation.

records.title: EU Vinted action shows a second-hand marketplace converting complaint pressure into implemented price, refund, identity, and review controls
records.source_unit: European Commission Consumer Protection Cooperation Network dialogue with Vinted
records.geography: European Union and European Economic Area consumer-facing Vinted websites and mobile apps
records.boundary: This record adds an EU/EEA second-hand marketplace implementation episode linking automatic fees, total-price disclosure, refund routes, counterfeit handling, seller identity, review transparency, and an unresolved delivery-fee gap. It does not quantify consumer harm, verify refund completion, estimate affordability or resale-market welfare, or prove that the controls changed behavior.

records.title: Cultural availability no longer guarantees cultural visibility: platforms, metadata, language, and AI shape who gets discovered
records.source_unit: European Commission, Study on the Discoverability of Diverse European Cultural Content Online, commissioned under the EU Work Plan for Culture 2023-2026
records.geography: European Union cultural and linguistic markets, with comparative analysis of music and book sectors and implications for digital cultural policy
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural-discoverability route from digital abundance through platform ranking, recommendation, metadata, language, skills, AI-generated content, creator visibility, and cultural pluralism. It is a European policy and sector study with mixed evidence and a small consumer survey, not a population-level causal estimate of exposure, platform impact, or cultural participation.

records.title: Europeans want digital sovereignty and infrastructure while demanding stronger AI governance, child protection, and democratic safeguards
records.source_unit: European Commission, Digital Decade 2026: Special Eurobarometer, survey conducted February-March 2026 and published 17 June 2026
records.geography: European Union citizens across the 27 Member States
records.boundary: This record adds EU public-opinion evidence on digital sovereignty, AI use and regulation, digital rights, child online safety, democratic manipulation, and willingness to pay for EU-based services. It is aggregate survey evidence, not respondent-level ingestion, a technical dependency inventory, an AI safety evaluation, a child-harm estimate, or proof that sovereignty policies improve outcomes.

records.title: Digital platform governance is becoming a correction system, but reversal rates do not yet show durable user remedy
records.source_unit: European Commission DSA impact overview, current 2026 page summarizing platform supervision and Article 21 out-of-court dispute settlement
records.geography: European Union; users and very large online platforms including Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat, and other designated services
records.boundary: This record establishes an EU-level platform-remedy and supervision layer: certified dispute bodies reviewed more than 1,800 disputes and reversed 52% of closed decisions in the Commission's summary, while the Commission describes DSA rules and proceedings across platforms. It does not establish platform-wide moderation error rates, user-level remedy success, compliance after reversal, child safety, age-assurance accuracy, targeted-ad exposure, or durable trust. The aggregate Commission figures are not merged with Snapchat's platform telemetry or the Dutch youth-panel evidence.

records.title: Civic participation is becoming an AI-mediated public-service layer, shifting legitimacy toward listening, translation, moderation, and feedback capacity
records.source_unit: European Commission Reform and Investment Task Force, Improving Civic Participation with Emerging Technologies, published 3 September 2026, with OECD companion analysis
records.geography: European Union project involving Portugal, Spain, and the Netherlands; ecosystem evidence involving 21 EU member states
records.boundary: This record adds a civic-participation infrastructure route from AI-mediated listening and input processing through public-sector capacity, inclusion, transparency, contestability, feedback, and democratic legitimacy. It does not establish that the prototypes improve participation, trust, policy quality, representation, or outcomes; reported actor and prototype counts are project outputs, not population-level adoption.

records.title: Europeans treat culture as community infrastructure and democratic expression while questioning artist livelihoods and AI’s creative-economic effects
records.source_unit: European Commission, Special Eurobarometer on Europeans' attitudes towards culture, fielded February-April 2025 and published 8 May 2025
records.geography: European Union citizens across all 27 Member States
records.boundary: This record adds EU-wide public-opinion evidence on culture as community and democratic infrastructure, artistic freedom, generative AI concerns, artist remuneration, and cultural participation. It is aggregate survey evidence, not respondent-level ingestion, a causal culture-and-democracy estimate, a cultural labor-market panel, or proof that stated importance translates into equal access.

records.title: EU physical activity rises modestly while active commuting, fitness use, and country gaps reshape social participation
records.source_unit: European Commission Special Eurobarometer on sport and physical activity, 2026 release
records.geography: European Union; cross-national population survey with Member State comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds an EU physical-activity, active-commuting, fitness, and social-meaning layer. It does not establish cultural participation, household spending, facility affordability, health outcomes, causal post-pandemic change, or community cohesion in practice.

records.title: Adolescent screen use is a negotiated household and platform-governance problem, not only an individual time problem
records.source_unit: European Commission Flash Eurobarometer 579, Impact of excessive screen time and social media on young people’s mental health
records.geography: European Union, all 27 Member States; adolescents aged 13–18 and their parents
records.boundary: This record adds a large cross-national paired survey on adolescent screen use, social-media experience, harmful content, parent perception, and support demand. It does not establish that screen duration causes mental illness, identify platform-level causal effects, validate parent–teen discrepancies as measurement error, or evaluate age limits, design changes, or mental-health interventions.

records.title: Migration policy is being rebuilt as cross-domain infrastructure linking labor, demography, AI, climate, data, and social cohesion
records.source_unit: European Commission Directorate-General for Research and Innovation, Future research on migration, human mobility and integration: Opportunities and Needs
records.geography: European Union research and policy ecosystem, with relevance to migration, mobility, integration, labor markets, technology, climate, and social cohesion across Europe
records.boundary: This record adds a migration-policy research-capacity and systems-framing route. It is not a migrant survey, labor-market outcome study, integration evaluation, causal policy test, or proof that research coordination changes public attitudes or lived conditions.

records.title: Demographic change is reorganizing labor, care, housing, migration, regional cohesion, and public finance at the same time
records.source_unit: European Commission Joint Research Centre, Demographic transformation in the EU: challenges and opportunities, July 14, 2026
records.geography: European Union; population, labor-market, care, housing, migration, and regional-policy synthesis
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative EU route from population decline, aging, and longevity through labor participation, care demand, housing, skills, migration, regional cohesion, and multilevel policy response. It uses official projections and policy synthesis, not a causal evaluation of the Demography Toolbox, a household panel, or evidence that announced measures have produced durable care, work, housing, or demographic outcomes.

records.title: EU proceedings turn child-safety concern into a named platform-control episode, while user protection and remedy remain unverified
records.source_unit: European Commission formal proceedings against Snapchat under the Digital Services Act, published March 26, 2026
records.geography: European Union; Snapchat users and minors exposed to the service
records.boundary: This record establishes a named Commission proceeding and its five control surfaces: age assurance, harmful contact, defaults, illegal-product information, and reporting/redress. It also records Snap's adjacent public position on voluntary CSAM detection after the ePrivacy derogation expired, the Dutch ACM's incorporation of a vaping-related investigation into the Commission-led case, a small advocacy-originated youth-panel observation about dealer discoverability, claimant-reported collective litigation and cross-border recruitment, a Dutch judiciary-hosted SOMI summons extract, a separate SMC summons with proposed platform remedies and evidence preservation, Snapchat's published Article 21 DSA dispute route, and Snap's H2 2025 platform-produced transparency telemetry. The youth-panel observation is not a prevalence estimate or independent platform audit; the litigation observations and summons categories are allegations, requests, and proposed group definitions, not court findings, proof of harm, proof of compensation eligibility, or issued preservation orders; the support page is a published process description, not evidence of user uptake or remedy success; the transparency metrics are not an independent audit, unique-user exposure measure, remedy measure, or child-outcome measure. None of these observations establishes a final violation, prevalence or severity of child harm, platform response to the DSA proceeding, user-level exposure, complaint resolution, correction, safety improvement, trust repair, or exit.

records.title: Democratic participation in the EU is constrained by unfamiliarity with participatory tools and an information environment where distrust and AI opacity are central concerns
records.source_unit: European Commission, Special Eurobarometer 568: Protecting and Promoting Democracy, fielded November 2025 and catalogued in 2026
records.geography: European Union citizens across the 27 Member States
records.boundary: This record adds EU public-opinion evidence on familiarity with participatory democracy, distrust, foreign information manipulation, AI transparency, election information quality, cyberattacks, and foreign influence. It is aggregate survey evidence, not respondent-level ingestion, an incident dataset, an election forecast, a platform audit, or proof that transparency alone restores trust.

records.title: EU public confidence combines institutional support and security alignment with persistent cost-of-living pressure and uneven democratic satisfaction
records.source_unit: European Commission, Standard Eurobarometer 105: Spring 2026, fieldwork March-April 2026 and publication May 2026
records.geography: European Union citizens across the 27 Member States, with country factsheets and wider coverage in the Eurobarometer dataset
records.boundary: This record adds current EU public-opinion evidence on democratic satisfaction, trust, EU membership, security, Ukraine, cost of living, economic expectations, euro support, and future optimism. It is aggregate cross-national survey evidence, not respondent-level ingestion, a causal trust model, a security forecast, or proof that EU support is evenly distributed across countries and social groups.

records.title: Consumer trust is institutionally produced, but consumer-protection gains reach the economically vulnerable less reliably
records.source_unit: Kanitsar and Nessel, Trust in Consumer Markets: The Role of Consumer Policy and Market Norms Across 30 European Countries, Journal of Sociology, 2026
records.geography: 30 European countries; pooled European Union consumer-attitudes surveys from 2016-2020
records.boundary: This record adds an open-access comparative institutional layer connecting consumer policy, market norms, consumer trust, economic vulnerability, and recourse reachability. It is an observational multilevel analysis of pooled European survey waves, not respondent-level ingestion, a causal policy evaluation, a dispute-resolution audit, proof of equal protection, or a U.S. consumer estimate.

records.title: Citizen participation can build administrative capacity and legitimacy, but only when institutions commit, communicate, and show what changed
records.source_unit: European Commission Joint Research Centre, Citizen Engagement Impact: Making a difference to policy, institutions and society
records.geography: European Union Member State public administrations and citizen-engagement processes, with cross-EU synthesis
records.boundary: This record adds an institutional participation route across policy quality, administrative culture, civic networks, legitimacy, trust, capacity, follow-up, and accountability. It uses EU public-administration survey responses, qualitative interviews, and report synthesis, not raw participant-level data, representative public opinion, a causal evaluation of any single deliberative process, a complete inventory of all European exercises, or proof that participation is equitable or effective when outputs are ignored.

records.title: European energy policy is converging household affordability, clean-energy investment, geopolitical dependence and consumer agency into one state-capacity agenda
records.source_unit: European Commission, Citizens' Energy Package and initiatives to boost EU energy independence and lower costs
records.geography: European Union energy, consumer, industrial and geopolitical policy
records.boundary: This record adds an institutional-response layer to the EU energy-consumer and global transition findings. It captures policy commitments and stated rationales, not implemented outcomes, causal bill effects, local consent, project delivery, or proof that strategic autonomy reduces all forms of dependence.

records.title: European consumer confidence and employment expectations turned away from a four-month recovery as household outlooks remained below long-term norms
records.source_unit: European Commission Directorate-General for Economic and Financial Affairs harmonised business and consumer surveys, September 2026 release
records.geography: European Union and euro area; harmonised sentiment indicators with sectoral and employment-expectation components
records.boundary: This record adds a sentiment-to-room conversion route: economic and employment expectations can shape purchase timing, precaution, household narratives, and political attribution, but the September 2026 indicators do not establish realized income, employment, consumption, debt, cultural participation, or welfare. The aggregate EU and euro-area movement must not be treated as a uniform household experience or causal forecast.

records.title: EU consumer confidence reversed its recovery in September as uncertainty and inflation expectations rose
records.source_unit: European Commission Directorate-General for Economic and Financial Affairs, Joint Harmonised EU Programme of Business and Consumer Surveys, September 2026
records.geography: European Union and euro area; harmonised monthly consumer and business surveys with composite confidence, sentiment, employment, and uncertainty indicators
records.boundary: This record adds EU-wide consumer sentiment, major-purchase intention, inflation-expectation, and uncertainty evidence. It does not establish realized consumption, income, cultural behavior, household inequality, causal effects, or a country-specific demand shock.

records.title: European energy-transition legitimacy is being organized around affordable bills, consumer protection and practical control over energy use—not climate ambition alone
records.source_unit: European Commission Directorate-General for Energy, Special Eurobarometer 555 Europeans' attitudes towards energy policy and Flash Eurobarometer 566 Consumer behaviour in the energy transition
records.geography: European Union citizens and consumers across all 27 EU Member States
records.boundary: This record adds an EU household-control and consumer-protection route to the energy-transition atlas. It is public-attitudes and reported-behaviour evidence, not household meter data, a bill audit, a causal policy evaluation, or proof that stated support produces durable consumption change.

records.title: Europe’s cultural economy employs 8.9 million people but remains a highly educated and place-concentrated production system
records.source_unit: Eurostat, EU cultural sector employment in 2025 and Guide to Eurostat culture statistics
records.geography: European Union; cultural employment across EU Member States
records.boundary: This record adds EU evidence on the size, demographic, education, and country distribution of cultural employment. It does not measure cultural output, wages, job quality, precarity, consumer access, participation, cultural meaning, or causal effects of cultural-sector employment.

records.title: Cultural participation is strongly age- and disability-stratified across Europe
records.source_unit: Eurostat, ilc_scp37 cultural or sport participation dataset, 2022 EU-SILC quality-of-life module; 2026 culture-statistics refresh
records.geography: European countries in the Eurostat dataset; selected comparative cells and Sweden subgroup cells
records.boundary: This record adds harmonized cultural-participation evidence connecting country context, disability limitation, and age to reported participation in cinema, live performances, or cultural sites. It is a 2022 cross-sectional percentage dataset refreshed and documented in 2026, not a causal accessibility estimate, a longitudinal participation record, a spending measure, or proof of cultural belonging or wellbeing.

records.title: Cultural participation is measurable as a social-distribution problem, but the evidence is periodic, multidimensional, and bounded by what official surveys can ask
records.source_unit: Eurostat, Guide to Eurostat culture statistics: 2026 edition
records.geography: European Union, most EFTA countries, and selected enlargement countries, using EU-SILC, ICT, household-budget, labor-force, business, and government-finance statistical systems
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural-participation measurement, access-barrier, household-resource, digital-consumption, and public-finance route. It uses an official methodological guide, not respondent-level ingestion, current participation estimates, a causal cultural-participation effect, a complete cultural ecosystem census, or proof that one reported barrier is the binding constraint.

records.title: Enterprise social-media participation is broad but strongly stratified by firm size and country
records.source_unit: Eurostat 2025 EU survey on ICT usage and e-commerce in enterprises, published 12 June 2026
records.geography: European Union; enterprises with 10 or more employees or self-employed persons in covered NACE sections
records.boundary: This record adds a harmonized enterprise-side platform-discovery and digital-market participation layer. It does not establish consumer exposure, sales conversion, firm survival, labor effects, platform dependence, causal productivity, or cultural influence.

records.title: Generative-AI use is widespread among younger EU internet users but much less common among older adults and remains purpose-specific
records.source_unit: Eurostat Digitalisation in Europe 2026 interactive publication, 2025 EU ICT usage by individuals
records.geography: European Union; individuals aged 16-74 who used the internet in the previous three months
records.boundary: This record adds a harmonized EU population-level AI-adoption, age-gradient, purpose, and country-comparison layer. It does not establish trust, capability, productivity, displacement, cultural influence, educational outcomes, consumer welfare, or causal social change.

records.title: Exposure to hostile or degrading online content is concentrated among younger EU users and differs by gender and target
records.source_unit: Eurostat 2025 EU survey on ICT usage by households and individuals, published 18 June 2026
records.geography: European Union; internet users aged 16-74
records.boundary: This record adds an official EU digital-exposure and identity-safety layer. It does not establish direct victimization, severity, platform causality, moderation effectiveness, mental-health outcomes, political behavior, cultural belonging, or consumer welfare.

records.title: EU household budgets remain concentrated in essentials while cultural, hospitality, education, transport, and communication spending move differently
records.source_unit: Eurostat, What are the main expenses in EU households?, Key figures on Europe 2026, September 2, 2026
records.geography: European Union aggregate household consumption expenditure, January 2026 compared with January 2025
records.boundary: This record adds an EU aggregate consumption route from essential household expenditure through relative movement in cultural, hospitality, education, transport, and information/communication shares. It is a macro expenditure and price synthesis, not household-level consumption behavior, welfare, affordability, cultural participation, or causal substitution evidence.

records.title: Cultural and leisure supply remains materially out of reach for many European households despite long-run improvement
records.source_unit: Eurostat, EU Statistics on Income and Living Conditions: inability to afford holidays and regular leisure activity in 2025
records.geography: European Union; population aged 16 years and older and EU-SILC respondents across Member States
records.boundary: This record adds EU evidence on leisure affordability, holiday exclusion, country inequality, and the distinction between internet access and regular leisure capacity. It does not measure cultural desire, actual travel, attendance, time scarcity, disability access, household-level causal pathways, or cultural meaning.

records.title: Online ticketing is becoming a cultural-access gateway in Europe, but digital purchase rates remain sharply place-stratified
records.source_unit: Eurostat, EU survey on the use of ICT in households and by individuals: online event-ticket purchases in 2025
records.geography: European Union; individuals across EU Member States purchasing tickets online for cultural or other events
records.boundary: This record adds EU evidence on online event-ticket purchasing, growth, country variation, and the pre-attendance conversion stage in cultural consumption. It does not measure attendance, event quality, ticket prices, household affordability, cultural meaning, payment exclusion, or causal effects of digital ticketing.

records.title: Online event-ticket buying is becoming a cultural-consumer gateway, with wide national access gaps
records.source_unit: Eurostat, ICT usage by households and individuals dataset isoc_ec_ibgs; 2025 online event-ticket purchase release published August 4, 2026
records.geography: European Union and member countries; individuals aged 16 to 74 in the ICT survey universe
records.boundary: This record adds an online transaction gateway between digital commerce and cultural participation. It is official Eurostat repeated cross-sectional survey evidence, not a ticketing ledger, attendance measure, household-spending estimate, causal platform-power evaluation, or proof that online access expanded cultural belonging or consumer welfare.

records.title: Paid streaming is the dominant online cultural subscription, but access remains geographically uneven
records.source_unit: Eurostat, ICT usage by households and individuals dataset isoc_ec_ibgs; 2025 online cultural-subscription release published August 27, 2026
records.geography: European Union and member countries; internet users aged 16 to 74 who used the internet in the previous 3 months
records.boundary: This record adds recurring paid digital-cultural consumption as a platform and household-room layer. It is official Eurostat repeated cross-sectional survey evidence, not a usage, billing, affordability, content-quality, creator-income, market-concentration, or causal wellbeing estimate.

records.title: EU retail volume softened in July as non-food demand fell while food sales rose
records.source_unit: Eurostat Euro indicators, Volume of retail trade, July 2026
records.geography: European Union and euro area; seasonally adjusted retail-trade volume and calendar-adjusted annual comparisons by sector and Member State
records.boundary: This record adds observed EU retail-volume behavior to the confidence and household-expectations layers. It does not establish household-level substitution, discretionary cultural spending, affordability, causal sentiment effects, or durable consumer welfare.

records.title: Social-network use is near-universal among young Europeans, but the age and country gaps reveal different digital social worlds
records.source_unit: Eurostat, EU survey on the use of ICT in households and by individuals: online social-network use in 2025
records.geography: European Union; people aged 16-29 and general population aged 16-74 across EU Member States

records.title: Youth cultural and consumer room is constrained by sharply unequal overcrowding across age and place
records.source_unit: Eurostat 2025 EU-SILC housing conditions, published 29 September 2026

records.title: Youth household autonomy arrives at very different ages across Europe and tracks employment conditions
records.source_unit: Eurostat 2025 European Union Labour Force Survey and youth-demography indicators, published 15 September 2026

records.title: Migration, social trust, and frontier resources are becoming coupled infrastructure questions as demographic and technological pressure rises
records.source_unit: EY, Futures Reimagined: EY Megatrends 2026 and beyond, chapters on migration infrastructure and the global resource rush
records.geography: Global strategic-foresight framing spanning migration, labor markets, technology investment, trust, critical resources, the Arctic, deep earth and sea, and orbit
records.boundary: This record adds a publisher-foresight signal about migration as infrastructure, labor and technology constraints, trust as social and organizational infrastructure, and competition across frontier resources. It is not a respondent-level survey, migration-flow estimate, causal evaluation of integration policy, mineral-reserve assessment, conflict forecast, or neutral consensus forecast.

records.title: Food-trade integration expands access and efficiency while making geopolitical, climate, and financial shocks transmit through more connected commodity networks
records.source_unit: FAO, The State of Agricultural Commodity Markets 2026: Trade, resilience and food security
records.geography: Global food and agricultural trade networks, with emphasis on low- and middle-income countries and country vulnerability
records.boundary: This record adds a geopolitical and climate shock-to-trade-network-to-domestic-price route. It is not a country-specific price forecast, does not estimate household food insecurity or firm losses, and does not establish causal effects of any trade policy on nutrition, consumption, migration, or political stability.

records.title: Agrifood climate finance is being reframed from a volume problem into a quality, access, governance, and local-ownership problem
records.source_unit: FAO and CIRAD, Exploring the quality of climate finance for agrifood systems
records.geography: Global agrifood systems, with attention to climate-vulnerable countries, communities, farmers, women, and local institutions
records.boundary: This record captures an official FAO-CIRAD systems-level signal that climate finance for agrifood systems must be evaluated by quality, access, cost, governance, equity, and local ownership as well as volume. It is not respondent-level evidence, a causal evaluation of finance projects, or proof that the proposed reforms will be implemented.

records.title: Food markets remain well supplied in aggregate while weather, conflict, fertilizer, shipping, and import-cost risks make access more fragile
records.source_unit: FAO Food Outlook, June 2026: Global food commodity market trends face rising geopolitical and weather risks
records.geography: Global food commodity markets, with commodity, income-group, and trade-route analysis
records.boundary: This record adds a global food-system route across commodity production, stocks, fertilizer, shipping, energy, weather, conflict, trade, food import bills, and consumer access. It uses FAO aggregate market assessments and forecasts, not household food diaries, respondent-level nutrition histories, farm-level causal estimates, retailer pass-through estimates, or proof that aggregate supply conditions translate equally into affordability or diet quality.

records.title: Food-price pressure is being rebuilt by weather, conflict, trade logistics, and input risk even when global supply remains historically large
records.source_unit: FAO Food Price Monitoring and Analysis Bulletin #7, 14 September 2026
records.geography: Global food commodity markets and domestic staple-food prices, with emphasis on developing-country early warning
records.boundary: This record adds a current food-price and early-warning route linking household food costs to weather, El Niño, conflict, trade logistics, supply expectations, stocks, production, and market resilience. It uses aggregate market indicators and forecasts, not household purchase histories, diet records, local retail pass-through, causal welfare estimates, or proof that food security improved or worsened for every group.

records.title: Forest loss is slowing but land, commodity, conservation, and community-use pressures remain unevenly distributed
records.source_unit: FAO, Global Forest Resources Assessment 2025
records.geography: 236 countries and areas, with forest extent, change, condition, management, ownership, use, disturbance, and carbon estimates for 1990-2025
records.boundary: This record adds a forest-land-use-to-livelihoods, commodity, public-ownership, conservation, cultural-use, and climate-capacity route. It is not local property or benefit-incidence data, does not establish household dependence or community consent, and does not equate forest area with ecological or social well-being.

records.title: Healthy eating is constrained by food-system costs and household affordability, not only by food supply
records.source_unit: FAO, IFAD, UNICEF, WFP and WHO, The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World 2026
records.geography: Global food systems, with country and regional affordability variation
records.boundary: This record adds global food affordability, food-system value-chain, nutrition, and consumption-pressure evidence. It is not respondent-level diet data, does not estimate household purchasing decisions or causal health effects, and does not equate diet cost with hunger or individual malnutrition.

records.title: Food-system risk is being reframed as a governance problem spanning affordability, power, technology, health, and agency
records.source_unit: FAO Committee on World Food Security HLPE-FSN Note on Critical, Emerging and Enduring Issues for Food Security and Nutrition, launched 14 September 2026
records.geography: Global food-security and nutrition system foresight for the CFS strategic and multiyear policy agenda
records.boundary: This record adds a food-governance and agency route linking healthy-diet affordability, power, corporate concentration, trade, geopolitical uncertainty, digital and AI change, One Health, and participation. It uses a global foresight issue map, not household purchase histories, dietary intake records, market-concentration estimates for every commodity, causal nutrition effects, representative agency measures, or proof of policy implementation.

records.title: Food trade is more interconnected and often resilient to shocks, but conflict, weather, export restrictions, and price spikes transmit instability into food security
records.source_unit: FAO, The State of Agricultural Commodity Markets 2026: Trade, resilience and food security
records.geography: Global food and agricultural trade networks, commodity markets, and food-security consequences of shocks
records.boundary: This record adds a global food-trade and shock-transmission layer linking markets, geopolitics, climate, infrastructure, prices, and social protection. It uses aggregate trade-network and policy evidence, not household food diaries, individual nutrition, causal welfare estimates, or proof that trade connectivity guarantees food security.

records.title: Modest global food-security gains coexist with high healthy-diet costs, regional disparities, and unequal nutrition exposure
records.source_unit: FAO, IFAD, UNICEF, WFP, and WHO, The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World 2026
records.geography: Global and regional food insecurity, diet quality, nutrition, and healthy-diet affordability estimates
records.boundary: This record adds a global hunger, food-insecurity, healthy-diet affordability, nutrition-disparity, and public-response route. It uses aggregate UN estimates and report synthesis, not respondent-level nutrition data, household food diaries, individual medical histories, causal food-price estimates, or proof that global hunger improvement means secure or healthy diets for every subgroup.

records.title: Aquatic food production and trade reach new highs while resource health, equity, livelihoods, and value-chain resilience remain contested
records.source_unit: Food and Agriculture Organization, The State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture 2026: Blue Transformation, Turning Vision into Impact
records.geography: Global marine and inland fisheries, aquaculture, aquatic-food trade, resources, livelihoods, and regional food systems
records.boundary: This record adds an aquatic-food, fisheries, aquaculture, nutrition, trade, livelihoods, ecological-resource, and community-governance route. It uses FAO aggregate sector statistics and report synthesis, not respondent-level data, individual fisher histories, household seafood diaries, causal price estimates, or proof that production and trade growth are automatically sustainable or equitable.

records.title: Soil degradation is worsening while adoption of proven management practices lags, turning food security and climate resilience into an implementation problem
records.source_unit: FAO Global Soil Partnership and Intergovernmental Technical Panel on Soils, Status of the World's Soil Resources 2026
records.geography: Global soils, agricultural land, agrifood systems, and seven FAO Global Soil Partnership regions
records.boundary: This record adds a soil-to-food-security and climate-resilience route from land degradation through sustainable-management adoption, ecosystem functions, agrifood productivity, and implementation governance. It is not farm-level data, a causal yield estimate, a food-price forecast, or proof that restoration policies produce equitable outcomes.

records.title: Cities are becoming governing sites for food access, health, livelihoods, and environmental transition across the rural–urban continuum
records.source_unit: FAO, Framework for Transforming Urban Agrifood Systems: Local action, national impact, global goals, 2026
records.geography: Urban and peri-urban agrifood systems, rural–urban continuums, cities, local governments, and food-system actors
records.boundary: This record adds an urban-to-rural agrifood governance route linking food access, health, livelihoods, environmental sustainability, markets, investment, and multi-level implementation. It is a policy framework, not a city-level outcome study, household diet dataset, food-price estimate, or proof of equitable transformation.

records.title: Acute food crises are concentrating where conflict, displacement, climate shocks, and response-financing gaps compound
records.source_unit: FAO, WFP, Global Network Against Food Crises, Global Report on Food Crises 2026
records.geography: 47 countries and territories analyzed for acute food insecurity in 2025, with global food-crisis, displacement, conflict, climate, and humanitarian-response comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds acute food-crisis, conflict, displacement, climate-shock, famine-risk, data-access, and response-financing evidence. It is not the same indicator as SOFI chronic hunger or healthy-diet affordability, does not estimate individual consumption, and does not use respondent-level microdata.

records.title: Persistent public pessimism is converting institutional distrust into demand for disruption, visible results, and affordability
records.source_unit: FGS Global Radar 2026 public-pessimism report and public findings overview
records.geography: 27 countries described as major democracies; polling of 20,000 people plus 175 in-depth interviews with global leaders
records.boundary: This record adds a global public-pessimism and legitimacy layer connecting institutional distrust to disruption, political impatience, affordability, fairness, and consumer behavior. It is a publisher-produced polling and interview synthesis, not respondent-level ingestion, a representative global census, a causal model of populism, proof that institutions are objectively failing, or evidence that rule-breaking leadership improves outcomes.

records.title: Consumer culture is reframing care, attention, and surprise: postpartum support, phone-free time, and whimsy become responses to optimized everyday life
records.source_unit: Foresight Factory, September 2026 cultural and consumer trends brief
records.geography: Global trend-intelligence framing with examples from the United States, United Kingdom, Australia, India, China, Southeast Asia, and cross-market consumer data
records.boundary: This record adds a commercial cultural-intelligence layer linking care recognition, attention governance, analog sociality, repair, surprise, and consumer meaning. It is not a representative population survey, clinical evaluation, education-policy evaluation, transaction dataset, or proof that brands, phone bans, or mystery products produce durable wellbeing, connection, affordability, or agency.

records.title: France's household cultural and leisure spending has shifted toward services while books and durable goods lose share
records.source_unit: INSEE, Cultural, sports and leisure expenditure, annual national accounts data 2000-2025
records.geography: France; household cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure
records.boundary: This record adds French national-accounts evidence on the composition of household cultural, sports, and leisure expenditure. It measures expenditure shares rather than participation, reach, frequency, quality, prices by category, income distribution, or cultural meaning; 2025 figures are provisional and the aggregate category is broader than culture alone.

records.title: France's cultural recovery returned to pre-pandemic levels while education, income, age, and place still stratify access
records.source_unit: France Ministry of Culture DEPS and CREDOC Conditions de vie et aspirations cultural outings barometer 2024
records.geography: France; population aged 15 years and above
records.boundary: This record adds France's official 2024 cultural-recovery evidence with persistent education, income, age, gender, and territorial gradients. It does not estimate causal price or time effects, online participation, individual welfare, or equal recovery across all groups; the underlying survey is an online self-report of 3,000 people.

records.title: France's cultural outings remain near pre-pandemic levels, but place, education, income, and mobility still sort access
records.source_unit: French Ministry of Culture, Baromètre des sorties culturelles 2025, DEPS and Crédoc
records.geography: France; residents aged 15 and above, France-wide
records.boundary: This record adds French evidence on physical cultural attendance, socioeconomic and settlement stratification, cultural-tourism mobility, and barriers. It is a commissioned online self-report survey and does not establish causal recovery, actual spending, venue supply effects, or individual-level cultural trajectories.

records.title: Online civic space is narrowing through censorship, repression, shutdowns, and information manipulation across a majority of assessed countries
records.source_unit: Freedom House, Freedom on the Net 2025: An Uncertain Future for the Global Internet
records.geography: 72 countries assessed using country-level expert-coded internet-freedom indicators, covering the majority of the world's internet users
records.boundary: This record adds an online-control-to-civic-space, information-manipulation, infrastructure, privacy, and political-capacity route. It is not respondent-level media-use data, does not establish individual persuasion or voting effects, and does not treat an expert-coded country score as direct proof of personal experience.

records.title: Global freedom declines continue as conflict, coups, institutional erosion, and repression narrow political and civil space
records.source_unit: Freedom House, Freedom in the World 2026: The Growing Shadow of Autocracy
records.geography: 195 countries and 13 territories assessed for calendar year 2025
records.boundary: This record adds an independent political-rights and civil-liberties route linking freedom decline, conflict, coups, institutional erosion, media and expression, due process, and reform resilience. It uses an expert-coded country and territory index, not respondent-level political attitudes, individual rights histories, causal repression estimates, or a replacement for the International IDEA assessment.

records.title: Diaspora cultural identity is reproduced through media exposure and direct cultural contact, but national context changes the pathway
records.source_unit: Frontiers in Psychology, Factors influencing Chinese cultural identity among new generations of ethnic Chinese in Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand
records.geography: Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand; second-generation or beyond ethnic Chinese respondents
records.boundary: This record adds a diaspora cultural-reproduction route: media content exposure and direct heritage contact are consistently associated with cultural identity, while language and device preference vary by national context. It does not establish causal effects, representative prevalence for all ethnic Chinese populations, political allegiance to China, or a universal diaspora identity model.

records.title: AI-mediated information and fragmented institutional responsibility are turning uncertainty itself into a democratic risk
records.source_unit: Full Fact, Full Fact Report 2026: A system under strain—strengthening the UK's democratic information environment
records.geography: United Kingdom, with international comparisons and lessons for democratic information resilience
records.boundary: This record adds a UK democratic-information route connecting platform design, AI mediation, synthetic media, institutional coordination, media literacy, trust and participation. It is a policy and advocacy report with cited polling and cases, not a representative global prevalence estimate, an algorithm audit, a causal electoral study, or respondent-level raw-data ingestion.

records.title: Economic progress is being reframed through work engagement, access to real jobs, and perceived life trajectory alongside GDP
records.source_unit: Gallup Economics 2026, Annual Report: leading indicators of economic growth
records.geography: Global Gallup World Poll adult population, with 2025 data and additional U.S. working-population samples
records.boundary: This record adds a measurement and lived-progress route from GDP and work access through engagement, full-time employer-based employment, life trajectory, and economic inclusion. It uses Gallup's aggregate survey and proprietary framework, not respondent-level records, national-account validation, bargaining-power measures, causal growth estimates, or proof that the three indicators predict future welfare equally across countries.

records.title: Current financial confidence is age-stratified while future security remains broadly uncertain across generations
records.source_unit: Edward Jones-Gallup, Money and Meaning: Understanding Financial Fulfillment, September 15, 2026
records.geography: United States and Canada; adults aged 21 and older, with generation and life-stage comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a life-course household-security mechanism: current financial confidence is strongly age-stratified, while confidence in the future remains comparatively low across generations; younger adults absorb pressure through stress, extra work and delayed wealth-building, and Gen X faces a retirement-control gap. The study does not establish causal cohort effects, financial adequacy, realized retirement outcomes, asset distributions or policy impact.

records.title: Global institutional confidence is not in universal decline; trust is diverging by institution, regime type and political position
records.source_unit: Gallup, Global Confidence in Institutions: A 20-Year Review
records.geography: Global World Poll countries, with 2025 comparisons across liberal democracies, electoral democracies and closed or electoral autocracies, plus European party-support analysis
records.boundary: This record adds a countertrend to simple institutional-decline narratives: confidence varies by institution, regime type, country and political position. It relies on Gallup World Poll country medians and subgroup associations, not a causal experiment, a universal trust index, direct behavioral legitimacy or proof that reported confidence reflects unconstrained opinion in every political system.

records.title: Perceived safety is reaching a global high even as conflict rises, but gendered insecurity and local institutional trust remain the dividing lines
records.source_unit: Gallup, Global Safety Report 2025 / Gallup World Poll
records.geography: 144 countries and territories; global and country comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a lived-security mechanism: global perceptions of everyday safety can improve even amid historically high conflict, while gendered insecurity and local institutional trust remain persistent divides. It is a repeated global public-opinion program, not a crime registry, conflict dataset, causal estimate of policing, or proof that perceived safety equals objective safety.

records.title: Global AI optimism is widespread while adoption, trust, and worry remain unevenly distributed
records.source_unit: Gallup, AI Optimism Globally Widespread Despite Uneven Use, reporting ongoing Gallup research with Microsoft, 22 September 2026
records.geography: Adults in the first 37 countries completing 2026 fieldwork in an ongoing global study intended to cover 140 countries
records.boundary: This record adds a global AI diffusion route from awareness through use frequency, expected impact, trust in accuracy, emotions, and unequal access. It is a published cross-country survey summary, not a pooled causal panel, usage telemetry, model-accuracy audit, employment study, or proof that trust causes adoption.

records.title: Global work remains low-engagement and emotionally costly, while work location and regional context redistribute both agency and wellbeing
records.source_unit: Gallup, State of the Global Workplace 2026, global employee survey and regional comparisons
records.geography: Global; Gallup regional groupings and employee subgroups
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative work-and-wellbeing mechanism: global engagement remains low after a 2022–23 peak, emotional strain remains elevated, and work location and region correspond with markedly different engagement and wellbeing profiles. It is a repeated global survey and descriptive subgroup comparison, not a causal evaluation of remote or hybrid work, a respondent-level panel, a job-quality audit or proof that one work arrangement generalizes across occupations and countries.

records.title: Public attention converges on economic security but diverges toward work, governance, or safety according to place and stability
records.source_unit: Gallup and World Governments Summit, The World's Most Important Problem: What People Need Leaders to Hear in 2026
records.geography: 107 countries and territories; regional, World Bank income-group, and conflict/stability comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds an aggregate public-attention route from household economic security, work, service performance, institutional trust, and conflict exposure through perceived national problems and political judgment. It uses country-level survey aggregates and contextual comparisons, not respondent-level records, individual panel histories, causal effects, or a claim that perceived priority equals objective severity.

records.title: AI-generated content is weakening default trust in influencers and brands while increasing demand for human credibility and demonstrated expertise
records.source_unit: Gartner Marketing survey and September 2026 public Q&A on AI-generated marketing content
records.geography: United States consumers aged 18+
records.boundary: This record adds a platform-and-marketing trust route linking AI-generated content, influencer reliance, brand credibility, human expertise, provenance, and information burden. It uses a Gartner U.S. consumer survey and analyst interpretation, not platform telemetry, a representative global sample, a causal experiment, or proof that skepticism leads to better decisions.

records.title: Government AI adoption is becoming an organizational-capacity problem: agentic systems, adaptive cyber defense, and workforce redesign must move together
records.source_unit: Gartner, Top Technology Trends in Government, September 2026
records.geography: Global government and public-sector technology outlook; supporting CIO survey of 1,219 government respondents conducted January 2026
records.boundary: This record adds a public-sector operating-capacity and legitimacy route linking agentic AI, cyber resilience, digital identity, workforce readiness, service redesign, and accountability. It uses Gartner’s public analyst outlook and a summarized CIO survey, not administrative deployment data, observed cyber incidents, service-user outcomes, causal evidence, representative global public opinion, or proof that modernization produces equitable public value.

records.title: Wealth, inheritance, housing, debt, and tax measurement require harmonized evidence before mobility and power can be compared across countries
records.source_unit: Longmuir et al., Scientific Data 2026, Wealth Composition, Distribution, and Transmission: The Graduate Center Wealth Project Data Warehouse
records.geography: Multiple countries and time periods; international wealth, household-balance-sheet, inequality, and wealth-transfer-tax evidence
records.boundary: This record adds a measurement and policy-infrastructure layer for wealth composition, distribution, inheritance, and tax transmission. It does not ingest respondent-level microdata, estimate causal mobility effects, provide a single global wealth truth, or make every underlying source comparable; it is a documented aggregate data warehouse and data descriptor.

records.title: Urban residents value downtowns but underuse them, making belonging, cultural draw, mobility, and street-level comfort the next city-centre battleground
records.source_unit: Gensler Research Institute, City Pulse 2026: The Downtown Report
records.geography: Residents across 75 cities and 30 countries, with longitudinal comparison of urban experience since the pandemic
records.boundary: This record adds an aggregate, multi-city urban-experience signal linking downtown belonging, visit frequency, mixed-use expectations, cultural draw, mobility friction, and public-space vibrancy. It uses published survey summaries and is not respondent-level data, a causal evaluation, a city ranking, or proof that design investment alone produces inclusion, safety, or economic recovery.

records.title: Energy-price anxiety is shifting German consumer sentiment toward precautionary saving while macroeconomic expectations remain comparatively stable
records.source_unit: Nuremberg Institute for Market Decisions, NIM Consumer Climate powered by GfK, September 2026
records.geography: Germany; approximately 2,000 consumer interviews conducted 3-14 September 2026
records.boundary: This record adds an energy-price-to-consumer-precaution route from perceived purchasing-power loss through saving propensity, large-purchase hesitation, household/macro expectation divergence, and potential political attribution. It does not establish realized spending or saving changes, causal energy-price effects, or uniform household exposure.

records.title: Ghana’s mobile-money system is scaling rapidly while active-agent capacity and oversight remain critical constraints
records.source_unit: Bank of Ghana, Payment Systems Oversight Annual Report 2024
records.geography: Ghana; national payment-system and fintech administrative indicators, with mobile-money, banking-channel, agent, licensing, financial-inclusion, and oversight dimensions
records.boundary: This record adds a Ghana administrative payment-system, agent-integrity, fintech-oversight, and financial-inclusion layer to the cultural, social, and consumer atlas. It does not establish unique-person use, household welfare, causal inclusion, consumer harm, cultural consumption, or the effect of sanctions and licensing on outcomes.

records.title: Ghana's mobile data reach is expanding faster than voice intensity, while fixed broadband remains a small layer
records.source_unit: Ghana National Communications Authority, Telecom Industry Trends Dashboard, Q2 2026
records.geography: Ghana; national telecommunications subscriptions and usage indicators
records.boundary: This record adds Ghana administrative telecommunications evidence on mobile data reach, voice intensity, and fixed broadband structure. Subscription counts are not unique-person access, household connectivity, consumer spending, cultural participation, or proof of data-mediated substitution.

records.title: Adult relationship quality is associated with childhood family belonging, health, financial security, and adversity across countries, but the strength of pathways varies by context
records.source_unit: Wilkinson et al., Life course insights into social relationship quality: a cross-national analysis of 22 countries, Scientific Reports 2025
records.geography: 22 countries in Wave 1 of the Global Flourishing Study, including the United States, United Kingdom, and diverse non-Western contexts
records.boundary: This record adds a life-course mechanism from childhood family relationships, abuse, belonging, health, and financial security through adult relationship quality and cross-national heterogeneity. It is exploratory retrospective cross-sectional evidence, not longitudinal causal proof, an intervention evaluation, or a claim that national culture alone determines adult relationships.

records.title: Relationship quality varies across cultures and life situations, with age, religious participation, partnership status, and employment shaping social well-being differently across countries
records.source_unit: Wilkinson et al., Strangers, Friends, and Everything Between: Sociodemographic Variation in Social Relationship Quality Across 22 Countries, Social Indicators Research 2026
records.geography: 22 countries in Wave 1 of the Global Flourishing Study, including non-Western and Western national contexts
records.boundary: This record adds a global relationship-quality route from culture and life situation through age, religious participation, partnership, employment, social resources, and targeted social infrastructure. It is cross-sectional subjective survey evidence with country-comparative and meta-analytic estimates, not longitudinal causal evidence, an objective social-network measure, or a universal cultural typology.

records.title: AI governance is expanding faster than public accountability, labor protection, and rights-respecting implementation
records.source_unit: Global Center on AI Governance, Global Index on Responsible AI 2026, second edition
records.geography: 135 countries and jurisdictions across seven global regions
records.boundary: This record adds a global institutional route from AI diffusion through public-sector disclosure, procurement, labor protection, cultural and linguistic inclusion, environmental accountability, civil-society participation, and redress. It uses comparative public evidence and index indicators, not respondent-level data, individual case histories, causal impact estimates, or proof that a framework changes lived outcomes.

records.title: Loneliness is becoming a policy category, but national recognition has not yet become evaluated social infrastructure
records.source_unit: Goldman et al., National policy responses to address loneliness: A global scoping review of 194 WHO member states, Health Policy 165 (2026), 105553
records.geography: Global review of national policies across 194 WHO Member States; included policy documents from selected high-income countries
records.boundary: This record adds a global policy-capacity route from loneliness recognition through national strategies, community infrastructure, cross-sector collaboration, funding, and evaluation. It is a scoping review of publicly available policy documents, not a prevalence estimate, intervention evaluation, causal health study, or proof that dedicated national policy improves social connection.

records.title: Nutrition is becoming a converging climate, health, and financing problem as healthy diets remain unaffordable and delivery systems stay fragmented
records.source_unit: 2026 Global Nutrition Report: Integrating food and health systems for climate-resilient nutrition, Global Nutrition Report
records.geography: Global nutrition, food-system, health-system, climate, financing, and equity evidence, with particular attention to low- and middle-income countries
records.boundary: This record adds a global nutrition, climate-resilience, food-health systems, social protection, financing, gender-equity, and accountability route. It uses public report-level evidence, not respondent-level ingestion, household microdata, a causal estimate of climate effects, a forecast of future nutrition outcomes, or proof that integrated policy will succeed in every setting.

records.title: Wellness forecasting is moving from quantified self-optimization toward embodied connection, collective ritual, and preparedness for human and environmental crises
records.source_unit: Global Wellness Summit, The Future of Wellness: 2026 Trends, public trend summaries and annual industry forecast
records.geography: Global wellness economy and consumer-culture forecast
records.boundary: This record adds a commercial wellness-industry forecast as a cultural and consumer signal: quantified-self fatigue, embodied and social wellness, neurowellness, healthspan environments, and crisis preparedness. It is not respondent-level data, clinical evidence, a representative consumer forecast, or proof that the predicted offerings will scale or improve health.

records.title: Generative AI is becoming a cultural-representation problem: identity, sacred meaning, and local red lines shape acceptable use
records.source_unit: Google Research preprint, Cultural Perspectives and Expectations for Generative AI: A Global Survey Approach
records.geography: Brazil, Cameroon, France, Germany, India, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, Mexico, Nigeria, South Korea, United Arab Emirates, and United States
records.boundary: This record adds a global cultural-governance layer for generative AI: identity, sacred meaning, historical memory, representation, participation, and redress. It is a cross-sectional preprint survey and qualitative synthesis, not respondent-level ingestion, a representative global census, an audit of model outputs, a legal rule, a causal study of cultural harm, or proof that any proposed safeguard works.

records.title: Civic engagement has recovered nationally but remains sharply place- and status-dependent
records.source_unit: UK Department for Culture, Media and Sport / Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, Community and Engagement Survey 2025/26: Civic Engagement
records.geography: England; people aged 16 and over
records.boundary: This record adds an official civic-action route from local experience and social position through participation, consultation, and activism. It does not measure whether institutions responded, whether participants changed decisions, the quality of deliberation, or durable civic power; all estimates are descriptive and self-reported.

records.title: People value local influence more strongly than they feel able to exercise it
records.source_unit: UK Department for Culture, Media and Sport / Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, Community and Engagement Survey 2025/26: Influencing Local Decisions
records.geography: England; people aged 16 and over
records.boundary: This record adds a perceived-efficacy and practical-access layer between civic participation and institutional legitimacy. It does not measure council response, decision change, policy influence, deliberative quality, or durable trust; estimates are self-reported, descriptive, and subject to the survey's pathway and local-estimate caveats.

records.title: Local cohesion is broad but uneven: everyday contact and willingness to pull together coexist with weak trust and place-specific decline
records.source_unit: UK Department for Culture, Media and Sport / Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, Community and Engagement Survey 2025/26: Neighbourhood and Community
records.geography: England; people aged 16 and over
records.boundary: This record adds an official place-and-cohesion route: routine contact and willingness to pull together coexist with lower reported trust, negative local trajectory judgments, and sharp age, disability, deprivation, and local-authority variation. It does not establish which local intervention causes belonging, actual mutual aid, service quality, or durable institutional trust. The survey is representative at the England population level, but local and subgroup estimates remain descriptive and self-reported.

records.title: By late 2026, food-crisis risk is being compounded by conflict, climate variability, high input prices, and shrinking humanitarian finance while the evidence system itself is under strain
records.source_unit: Global Report on Food Crises 2026 Mid-year Update, summarized by the European Commission Joint Research Centre
records.geography: Global food-crisis settings assessed through IPC, Cadre Harmonisé, FEWS NET, WFP CARI, HNRP and partner systems; famine-risk focus on Somalia, South Sudan, and Sudan
records.boundary: This record is a September 2026 mid-year update to the existing GRFC 2026 signal. It adds late-year conflict, climate, price, funding, famine-risk, and food-security data-system developments; it is not a household food-consumption survey, a complete global census, a causal attribution of each driver, or proof that projected funding declines will produce identical outcomes in every crisis.

records.title: Mobile internet access is expanding for women in LMICs, but affordability, skills, and safety preserve a large gendered usage gap
records.source_unit: GSMA Mobile Gender Gap Report 2026, based on GSMA Consumer Survey 2025 and modelling
records.geography: Low- and middle-income countries; regional estimates for Sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, East Asia and Pacific, Middle East and North Africa, Europe and Central Asia, and Latin America and Caribbean
records.boundary: This record adds an LMIC digital-access and gender layer to the platform and infrastructure themes. It does not establish internet quality, financial or cultural outcomes, platform causation, safety incidence, household welfare, or equal effective agency.

records.title: Public support for state-funded care coexists with weak system understanding and unresolved funding trade-offs
records.source_unit: Health Foundation, We need to talk: Public attitudes to social care and the NHS, with Ipsos
records.geography: United Kingdom; detailed funding and service-organisation questions include England
records.boundary: This record adds UK public-opinion evidence on social-care performance, funding knowledge, household preparation, provider ownership, NHS principles, and access priorities. It keeps current and prior survey waves distinct and does not establish actual care quality, future affordability, causal effects of ownership, or public consent for a specific reform package.

records.title: Belonging remains widespread but local cohesion slips as financial stress, housing, isolation, and unequal safety sort social connection
records.source_unit: Helen Clark Foundation, Social Cohesion in New Zealand 2026
records.geography: New Zealand; population-weighted 2025 survey of adults, with Māori, Pacific, and Asian booster samples
records.boundary: This record adds a belonging-and-material-stress route: national belonging can remain high while local cohesion, trust, safety, and hope weaken; financial stress, housing tenure, cross-cultural friendship, age, gender, and media habits sort exposure. It does not establish causal effects, clinical loneliness, actual civic behavior, or policy impact.

records.title: Belonging is produced through relationships with communities, places, and histories, and inclusive cultural practice depends on shared institutional power
records.source_unit: Humanities in the European Research Area, En/counter/points: (re)negotiating belonging through culture and contact in public space and place, a Public Spaces: Culture and Integration in Europe project impact story
records.geography: Europe, with research led in the United Kingdom and collaboration involving Poland, Germany, and the Netherlands; cultural institutions and public-space cases
records.boundary: This record adds a culture-to-place-to-belonging route from community, historical, and spatial connection through collaborative cultural practice, museum decision-making, public-space design, participation, and social inclusion. It is a comparative case-study and research-impact account, not a population trend, representative public-opinion estimate, causal intervention evaluation, or proof that toolkit adoption changes belonging.

records.title: Australian household security is being stretched across housing, food, work fit, and life-course timing while intimate relationships remain a resilient resource
records.source_unit: Melbourne Institute of Applied Economic and Social Research, University of Melbourne, 2026 HILDA Annual Statistical Report
records.geography: Australia; nationally representative HILDA household panel, Waves 1–24 with selected 2024 outcomes
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative longitudinal household-security route: life-course timing, job fit, food insecurity, housing and financial stress, intimate relationships, fatigue and age-linked wellbeing should be read together without assuming that employment or relationship strength automatically produces security. It is an official report synthesis of HILDA panel evidence, not a new respondent-level extraction or causal evaluation.

records.title: Travel is being recalibrated around flexibility, trusted human guidance, wellbeing and shorter meaningful escapes
records.source_unit: Hilton, The Great Rebalance: Hilton's 2027 Trends Report, September 29, 2026; Morning Consult survey commissioned by Hilton
