records.geography: Travelers ages 18 and older in 14 countries: United States, Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, United Kingdom, Germany, Türkiye, United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, Australia, China, India, Japan and Korea
records.boundary: This record identifies a commissioned travel-culture and consumer subtheme around flexibility, human trust, wellness, personal growth and shorter travel. It does not establish representative global travel demand, booking behavior, affordability, wellbeing outcomes, local cultural effects, emissions, causal AI-human trust differences or durable trend persistence.

records.title: Hong Kong retail growth masks a split between online and luxury-linked demand and everyday mobility categories
records.source_unit: Hong Kong Census and Statistics Department retail sales release reported by the Hong Kong Government Information Services, July 2026
records.geography: Hong Kong
records.boundary: This record adds a Hong Kong category and channel divergence layer to South African real retail growth, Japanese household contraction, and Great Britain online adaptation. It does not measure household welfare, tourism attribution, cultural attendance, or causal demand polarization.

records.title: U.S. consumers remain willing to spend while shifting toward value, selectivity, and financial-risk management as job-security anxiety rises
records.source_unit: International Council of Shopping Centers, Consumer Economy Report, September 2026
records.geography: United States households, consumers, workers, retailers, brands, and the consumer economy
records.boundary: This record adds a U.S. consumer-economy route from job security and household financial margin through value-seeking, brand switching, discretionary spending, and selective resilience. It uses a commercial survey and economic context, not respondent-level records in the corpus, causal household-budget analysis, observed transactions, or proof of welfare improvement.

records.title: Latin America’s digital-trade growth is constrained less by online demand than by regional interoperability and capability gaps
records.source_unit: IDB, World Bank, and WTO, Digital Trade in Latin America and the Caribbean: Connecting Markets, Powering Growth
records.geography: Latin America and the Caribbean, with regional and subregional digital-trade comparisons and country-level policy analysis
records.boundary: This record adds a digital-trade-to-regional-integration mechanism linking online commerce to payment, regulation, privacy, cybersecurity, skills, finance, logistics, and consumer-protection infrastructure. It is descriptive and scenario-based evidence, not proof that any one reform causes exports, that digital growth is inclusive, or that regional platforms will capture the value of regional demand.

records.title: Democratic performance is weakening across rights and institutional checks while participation and migrant political inclusion remain uneven
records.source_unit: International IDEA Global State of Democracy 2025: Democracy on the Move and Global State of Democracy Indices v9
records.geography: 173 countries with 2024 country data in the report; the full index release covers 174 countries and 1975-2024 country-years
records.boundary: This record adds a global institutional-performance and migrant-political-inclusion route. It does not infer individual political attitudes, prove democratic backsliding from one indicator, estimate diaspora causal effects, or treat participation, press freedom, rights, and rule of law as interchangeable outcomes.

records.title: Democratic stagnation and declining rights are increasingly linked to conflict conditions and weakened institutional checks
records.source_unit: International IDEA, The Global State of Democracy 2026: Democracy in an Age of Conflict
records.geography: 173 countries assessed through the Global State of Democracy Indices, with regional comparisons and conflict analysis
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative democracy-to-conflict route linking representation, rights, rule of law, participation, institutional checks, and violent conflict conditions. It uses country-level indices and report analysis, not respondent-level political attitudes, individual voting histories, causal conflict forecasts, or a single overall democracy score.

records.title: Internal displacement is becoming a structural crisis as conflict, disasters, repeated movements, and weak data systems compound
records.source_unit: Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre, 2026 Global Report on Internal Displacement
records.geography: Global, with regional overviews covering 104 countries and territories
records.boundary: This record adds a global conflict, disaster, mobility, durable-solutions, and displacement-data route using IDMC aggregate estimates and publication analysis. It does not contain respondent-level displacement histories, individual location trajectories, household files, causal conflict forecasts, person-level service needs, or proof that every displaced population follows the same path.

records.title: Energy, digital, and defence transitions are intensifying mineral demand while refining and trade controls concentrate supply-chain risk
records.source_unit: International Energy Agency, Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026
records.geography: Global critical-mineral markets, refining and investment, energy and technology value chains, and Latin America and the Caribbean
records.boundary: This record adds a mineral-demand-to-refining-concentration-to-export-control-to-downstream-production and regional-value-capture route. It is not mine-level incidence, respondent data, proof of completed projects, realized shortages, consumer-price effects, local consent, or evidence that mineral dependence automatically creates geopolitical leverage.

records.title: Clean-energy transition capacity is becoming a supply-chain, manufacturing, trade, affordability, and industrial-policy problem as much as a deployment problem
records.source_unit: International Energy Agency, Energy Technology Perspectives 2026
records.geography: Global clean-energy technology deployment, manufacturing, investment, trade, supply chains, and industrial competitiveness
records.boundary: This record adds an infrastructure and geopolitical-economy signal on clean-energy technology deployment, manufacturing, trade, supply-chain vulnerability, cost, industrial competitiveness, and evidence infrastructure. It is based on the official IEA report description and model documentation, not a causal forecast, a project-level delivery audit, a household affordability study, or proof that modeled transition pathways will be equitable or realized.

records.title: Energy affordability is a household-cost, infrastructure, health, and policy-targeting problem rather than only a price problem
records.source_unit: International Energy Agency Household Energy Affordability report and Household Energy Affordability: Data and Indicators framework
records.geography: Global; advanced economies, emerging markets and developing economies, sub-Saharan Africa, and IEA member/association-country comparison
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative household-energy affordability route connecting geopolitical price shocks, retail bill design, housing and appliance efficiency, energy access, health, clean cooking, and policy targeting. It does not infer individual hardship, energy deprivation, causal health effects, policy effectiveness, or household welfare from modeled averages and policy counts.

records.title: AI is becoming an electricity-system and affordability issue: efficiency gains are being overtaken by scale, intensive use cases, grid bottlenecks and concentrated infrastructure
records.source_unit: International Energy Agency, Key Questions on Energy and AI
records.geography: Global data-centre and energy-system analysis with regional and United States case evidence on electricity demand, prices, grids and policy
records.boundary: This record adds an AI-to-energy-system route: data-centre investment, electricity demand, efficiency, intensive AI use, grid timing, affordability, emissions, energy security and public policy are analyzed together. It is an IEA global energy and infrastructure synthesis, not household electricity microdata, a full life-cycle AI emissions audit, a local rate case, a causal productivity evaluation or proof that AI benefits are evenly distributed.

records.title: Energy shocks are widening the policy response from transition deployment to reserves, affordability, access, and supply-chain resilience
records.source_unit: International Energy Agency, State of Energy Policy 2026
records.geography: Global energy-policy landscape across 84 countries, with policy, affordability, access, regulatory, and supply-chain examples across regions
records.boundary: This record adds a policy-adoption and implementation route linking geopolitical shocks to reserves, demand restraint, affordability support, regulation, energy access, transition deployment, and supply-chain resilience. It is not respondent-level data, household survey evidence, proof of implementation quality, realized consumer benefit, or a forecast of emissions or energy-system outcomes.

records.title: Energy investment is shifting toward electricity and AI, but grids, finance, and geography determine who can absorb the transition
records.source_unit: International Energy Agency, World Energy Investment 2026
records.geography: Global energy investment, electricity systems, clean-energy supply chains, emerging and developing economies, and regional investment patterns
records.boundary: This record adds an investment-to-grid-bottleneck-to-industrial-geography-to-development-finance route. It is publication-level aggregate evidence, not respondent-level data, household incidence, completed-project evidence, causal welfare effects, or proof that investment concentration automatically produces geopolitical leverage.

records.title: Global peacefulness is deteriorating as conflicts diffuse across borders, militarization rises, and a fragmented power system weakens the conditions for peace
records.source_unit: Institute for Economics & Peace, Global Peace Index 2026: Measuring Peace in a Complex World
records.geography: 163 independent states and territories covering 99.7 percent of the world population, with comparisons across regions and three peace domains
records.boundary: This record adds a geopolitical peace route across peacefulness, conflict diffusion, conflict deaths, militarisation, power fragmentation, economic costs, and Positive Peace. It uses an aggregate IEP composite index and report synthesis, not respondent-level safety histories, event-level conflict microdata, individual victim records, causal geopolitical forecasts, or proof that index movement directly describes every community.

records.title: Terrorism declined globally in 2025 but became more concentrated in conflict zones, borderlands, and youth radicalisation pathways
records.source_unit: Institute for Economics & Peace, Global Terrorism Index 2026
records.geography: 163 countries covering 99.7 percent of the world population, with global, regional, borderland, conflict, and youth-radicalisation comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a terrorism route across global decline, regional concentration, conflict linkage, borderlands, youth radicalisation, online pathways, governance, and employment conditions. It uses aggregate IEP index measures and report synthesis, not respondent-level radicalisation histories, individual victim files, raw case-management records, causal platform effects, or proof that any correlate is a universal cause of terrorism.

records.title: Agrifood futures are being modeled as an interconnected system where population, income, technology, climate, demand, production, nutrition, livelihoods, and natural resources co-determine long-term outcomes
records.source_unit: IFPRI/CGIAR, Global Agrifood Systems Outlook to 2050
records.geography: Global and regional agrifood systems, with particular attention to low- and middle-income countries
records.boundary: This record adds a long-horizon agrifood-systems signal linking population, income, technology, climate, food production, consumption, markets, nutrition, livelihoods, and natural resources. It is based on the official CGIAR summary of a peer-reviewed scenario volume, not a prediction, a realized-outcome evaluation, a household food-consumption dataset, or proof that projected progress will be equitable or climate-resilient.

records.title: In crises, harmful information is becoming an operational hazard that can determine aid access, safety, dignity, trust, and recovery
records.source_unit: IFRC World Disasters Report 2026: Truth, Trust and Humanitarian Action in the Age of Harmful Information
records.geography: Global humanitarian operations and communities affected by disasters, public-health emergencies, migration, and conflict
records.boundary: This record adds a humanitarian information-resilience signal linking misinformation, disinformation, dehumanizing narratives, trust, aid access, safety, social cohesion, local participation, and data systems. It is a sector synthesis and operational roadmap, not a global prevalence study, a causal estimate of information effects, a representative community survey, or proof that the recommended pillars are implemented or effective everywhere.

records.title: Shared religious practice and value alignment appear as relationship infrastructure, not only private belief
records.source_unit: Institute for Family Studies, Churchgoing husbands and wives are happier, September 25, 2026 insight
records.geography: United States; married adults ages 20–54
records.boundary: This record identifies a communal-practice, shared-values and relationship-infrastructure subtheme. It does not establish causality, sample representativeness, effect sizes, temporal ordering, fertility or household-consumption effects, civic participation, institutional inclusion or superiority of religious over nonreligious forms of social connection.

records.title: Religious practice functions as relational infrastructure for some married couples even as religious participation declines
records.source_unit: Institute for Family Studies, The Devout Difference: Religion, Marital Quality, and Sex Among Americans, September 25, 2026
records.geography: United States; married adults ages 20-54, with General Social Survey trend comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a relational-social-infrastructure route: regular religious practice and shared marital norms are associated with higher reported marital quality and sexual satisfaction among the groups studied even as participation declines. It does not establish a causal faith effect, universal religious advantage, or that sexual frequency equals relationship wellbeing. Public report materials do not provide the full 2026 survey sample and model documentation.

records.title: Justice capacity depends on infrastructure, management, geography, and adjacent services as much as headline spending
records.source_unit: Institute for Fiscal Studies, Transforming Justice programme, Resources and the justice system
records.geography: England and Wales justice system, with local-authority and service-distribution analysis
records.boundary: This record adds justice as public capacity and household-access infrastructure. It covers England and Wales and combines budget, administrative, geographic, and linked-service evidence; it does not produce one causal spending estimate, measure all unmet legal need, equate case volume with justice quality, or generalize UK justice findings to other jurisdictions.

records.title: Households are turning home into a resilience buffer, but security, comfort, and control remain need–experience gaps
records.source_unit: IKEA Life at Home Report 2026, based on YouGov, Crowd DNA, and GlobeScan research
records.geography: Global; quantitative life-at-home survey in 31 countries, with qualitative ethnographies in India, Spain, and the United States
records.boundary: This record adds consumer-perception evidence about home as a resilience, comfort, control, security and climate-action setting. It is a commercially commissioned online survey and qualitative research programme, not objective housing, income, welfare, emissions, mental-health, or longitudinal behavioral evidence; reported associations do not establish causal effects.

records.title: Home is becoming resilience infrastructure: people seek security, comfort, and control as outside uncertainty enters everyday life
records.source_unit: Ingka Group/IKEA, Life at Home Report 2026
records.geography: Global; adults in 31 countries for the Life at Home quantitative study, with qualitative work in India, Spain, and the United States
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural-consumer home-resilience route: external uncertainty is managed through the household as a space of security, comfort, control, future optimism, and sustainability practice. It does not establish that home happiness causes optimism, that reported climate action changes emissions, or that IKEA interventions close the security/comfort/control gap. The source is retailer-commissioned mixed-method consumer research based largely on 2025 fieldwork and online panels.

records.title: Home is becoming a resilience and control infrastructure as financial, health, climate, and technological pressures enter everyday life
records.source_unit: IKEA Life at Home Report 2026, with quantitative research by YouGov
records.geography: Adults aged 18+ in 31 countries; global results weight each country equally
records.boundary: This record adds a consumer-and-household route linking financial and health pressure, climate concern, technology stress, life-stage differences, security, comfort, control, and the practical conversion of sustainability motivation. It uses a commissioned YouGov survey and IKEA interpretive framing, not observed household behavior, objective housing conditions, representative global-population inference, causal wellbeing evidence, or proof that products or services close the reported gaps.

records.title: Household mess is a coordination and meaning system: clutter converts domestic labor into conflict, time loss, and identity work
records.source_unit: Ingka Group/IKEA, Store & Organise Report 2026: Finding Meaning in the Mess
records.geography: Global; adults in 31 markets
records.boundary: This record adds a household coordination and meaning route: mess can expose indirect negotiation over domestic labor, impose hidden search-time costs, and preserve identity through sentimental objects. It does not establish unequal labor allocation, intentional protest in every case, causal conflict effects, or that storage products resolve these tensions. The source is retailer-commissioned consumer research based on online self-reports.

records.title: Migration systems built around return are confronting ageing, multigenerational settlement, and cross-border social-protection gaps
records.source_unit: ILO STREAM, Old-age security in the South Asia–Gulf migration corridor: policy challenges and opportunities, and accompanying ILO article
records.geography: South Asia–Gulf Cooperation Council migration corridor, focused on lower- and middle-income Indian migrant families with long residence in the United Arab Emirates
records.boundary: This record adds a migration life-course and social-protection portability route: temporary labour migration can become long-term residence and multigenerational family life, exposing gaps in retirement income, healthcare, housing, residency and cross-border benefit continuity. It is a focused qualitative research and policy synthesis centred on Indian families in the UAE, not representative Gulf-wide prevalence, causal evidence, a complete pension account, or proof that proposed reforms have been adopted or would work.

records.title: AI-enabled management is turning surveillance, work intensity, autonomy and data use into psychosocial work conditions requiring integrated rights and health governance
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, AI systems @ work: a changing psychosocial work environment, ILO Working Paper 170
records.geography: Global policy and occupational-safety analysis of AI and digitalization across employment settings
records.boundary: This record adds an AI-to-psychosocial-work route: surveillance, work intensification, reduced autonomy, dignity, data use and transparency are treated as work conditions and governance issues. It is an ILO working-paper synthesis, not worker-level mental-health data, a workplace audit, a prevalence estimate, a legal determination or a causal evaluation of AI deployment.

records.title: AI labour governance in Asia is being negotiated as a South-South employment, skills, and digital-inclusion project rather than only a firm technology decision
records.source_unit: ILO report on Regional Policy Dialogue 2026: Harnessing AI to Build Employment-Friendly Labour Markets in ASEAN and China, published September 8, 2026
records.geography: ASEAN and China; regional policy dialogue held in Bangkok, Thailand, August 26-27, 2026
records.boundary: This record captures the policy-dialogue and regional-cooperation framing of AI labour governance in ASEAN and China. It does not establish AI job loss, productivity, worker outcomes, adopted standards, implementation, or causal effects of social dialogue.

records.title: Labour rights are becoming a condition of trade and supply-chain competitiveness in ASEAN, but market requirements still have to reach workplace remedy
records.source_unit: ILO report on the ASEAN regional seminar on trade, labour rights, and sustainable competitiveness, including the ASEAN Regional Study on labour provisions in free trade agreements
records.geography: ASEAN member-state governments, workers’ and employers’ organizations, and export-oriented sectors across South-East Asia
records.boundary: This record adds a trade-to-work conversion route: labour rights, FTA provisions, due diligence, ESG requirements, and tripartite dialogue are becoming part of sustainable supply-chain competitiveness in ASEAN. It documents regional policy architecture and planned evidence-building, not worker-level implementation, firm performance, export gains, improved safety, wage change, or effective remedy.

records.title: Bangladesh’s gender pay gap is reinforced by labor-market sorting, unpaid care, informality, and weak enforcement
records.source_unit: ILO, The gender pay gap in Bangladesh: Trends, causes and policy options
records.geography: Bangladesh, using the 2023 Labour Force Survey with stakeholder consultations and policy analysis
records.boundary: This record adds a national labor-market and institutional-enforcement layer to the child-penalty finding. It is descriptive and decomposition-based evidence from Bangladesh’s 2023 survey, not causal proof that discrimination, unpaid care, informality, or a specific legal weakness independently causes the measured gap; it does not establish household welfare, lifetime earnings, or universal cross-country magnitudes.

records.title: Platform work is expanding opportunity while shifting income volatility, safety risk, and bargaining power onto workers
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, Diagnostic review of working conditions and social security coverage of digital platform workers in Cambodia
records.geography: Phnom Penh, Cambodia, with national legal and platform-market context
records.boundary: This record adds a platform-work signal linking digital convenience and employment access to unpaid waiting, operating costs, algorithmic management, injury exposure, legal classification, social protection and worker voice. It is a Phnom Penh diagnostic and not a national labor-market estimate, causal evaluation, or basis for generalizing all platform workers globally.

records.title: AI adoption is an organizational bargain, not an automation switch
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, Artificial Intelligence Adoption in Chinese Enterprises: Productivity Effects, Workforce Implications, and Policy Challenges, September 2026
records.geography: China; enterprises across manufacturing, finance, business services, construction, education, media and travel, plus a survey of Chinese professionals
records.boundary: This record adds an enterprise-level AI transition route from organizational adoption model through measured productivity, task redesign, worker expectations, skills, governance and distributional legitimacy. The qualitative enterprise sample is purposive, firm productivity figures are self-reported, the professional survey is descriptive, and the publication does not establish causal effects on employment, wages, hours, job quality, inequality, innovation or social trust.

records.title: Climate risk becomes an occupational bargain: heat exposure is distributed by work, place and protection
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization Working Paper 178, Climate-Related Heat Stress and Occupational Mortality in Colombia, August 2026
records.geography: Colombia; occupational mortality, temperature exposure and worker-protection systems across covered municipalities
records.boundary: This record adds an occupational-climate route from temperature exposure through mortality, gendered and occupational vulnerability, work-rest and prevention conditions, social-protection coverage, informality and worker voice. It is observational Colombian evidence and policy analysis, not causal proof of heat mortality, future climate effects, protection effectiveness, coverage adequacy or household welfare consequences.

records.title: Disability-inclusive employment is shifting from job placement to a supported pathway of accommodation, retention, progression, and digital access
records.source_unit: ILO report on the Disability Employment Package Mutual Learning Seminar and digital employment pathways, published 9 September 2026
records.geography: European employment-service examples with wider ILO and PROSPECTS implications for disability-inclusive and refugee-host employment pathways
records.boundary: This record adds a disability-inclusive employment-service route linking placement, accommodation, retention, progression, employer adaptation, assistive technology, public services, and digital accessibility. It is a practice-exchange report and mapping of examples, not causal evidence of employment gains, algorithmic fairness, sustained retention, wage equality, or universal service access.

records.title: Public investment can be a formalization gateway only if the project outlives itself
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, Promoting formalization outcomes in Employment-Intensive Investment Programme, ILO Brief, August 2026
records.geography: Employment-Intensive Investment Programme contexts in low- and middle-income countries, with illustrative cases from the Philippines and Central African Republic
records.boundary: This record adds a project-afterlife and public-investment gateway layer to the formalization atlas. The brief is practice guidance and evidence synthesis, not a causal evaluation of EIIP, a universal reversion rate, or proof that social-protection linkage, cooperative organization, procurement access or indicators produce durable formal employment, wages, business growth, poverty reduction or worker wellbeing.

records.title: Global employment is stable at the headline level while job quality, income security and convergence remain under strain
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, Employment and Social Trends 2026
records.geography: Global labour markets, with comparisons across country income groups and attention to women, young people, informal workers and trade-linked employment
records.boundary: This record adds a global labour-market layer: the ILO separates stable unemployment from job quality, informality, working poverty, income recovery, unequal productivity and access to work. It uses ILO modelled estimates and comparative synthesis, not respondent-level microdata, a household panel, transaction data or a causal evaluation of policy effects.

records.title: Stable headline employment is masking a global deficit of job quality, security, and productive convergence
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, Employment and Social Trends 2026
records.geography: Global, with comparisons across country income groups, regions, women, youth, informal workers, and workers linked to foreign demand
records.boundary: This record adds a global labor-market route from headline employment through unmet labor demand, job quality, informality, income recovery, demographic and gender inequality, trade and technology exposure, and domestic institutional buffering. It is an ILO global synthesis with projections and modeled indicators, not a respondent-level panel, a U.S.-specific estimate, or a causal evaluation of any policy.

records.title: AI is shifting the value of work toward judgment, oversight, hybrid capability and broad AI literacy rather than eliminating the need for human agency
records.source_unit: European Training Foundation, Changing Landscape of Skills in the Age of AI, prepared through the Inter-Agency TVET Working Group with Cedefop, Eurofound, European Commission, ILO and UNESCO
records.geography: Cross-sector and international synthesis of AI-related changes in workplace skills and skills policy
records.boundary: This record adds an AI-to-capability route: workplace AI changes the value of judgment, oversight, hybrid expertise, socio-emotional skill and broad AI literacy, while technical AI work remains concentrated. It is an inter-agency synthesis and policy framework, not worker-level task data, an adoption measurement, a causal employment evaluation or a guarantee that AI produces more autonomy.

records.title: Ethiopia’s social-protection expansion is uneven: school meals and health coverage grow while cash security remains thin
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, Social Protection Coverage in Ethiopia: A Fact-Finding Report Based on the ILO-Social Security Inquiry (SSI) Data Collection Tool, 2025/2026
records.geography: Ethiopia nationally, with rural, urban, gender, age, disability, informal-economy, and programme-level coverage distinctions
records.boundary: This record adds a cash-versus-in-kind-and-health protection composition mechanism with life-course, gender, disability, informality, local-delivery, and data-governance implications. It is a national fact-finding baseline, not a causal evaluation, benefit-adequacy study, or complete household-welfare account; the next test is whether expanded cash protection, integrated registries, domestic financing, and locally owned programmes improve realized resilience and equitable access without sacrificing privacy or excluding people poorly represented in administrative data.

records.title: ILO evidence review finds GenAI time savings are real but have not yet become broad output, pay, or employment gains
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, The impact of GenAI on jobs, productivity and work organization: a review of the empirical evidence, Research Brief, June 2026
records.geography: Comparative evidence from Australia, Denmark, Germany, Korea, Kuwait, the United Kingdom, and the United States
records.boundary: This record adds an empirical AI-to-work-organization route. It is a comparative evidence synthesis, not respondent-level data from this program, a causal estimate of one deployment, a forecast of mass unemployment, or proof that time savings become household income, reduced workload, bargaining power, or better job quality.

records.title: The global gender-pay gap is narrowing too slowly because pay is embedded in care, occupational segregation, career progression, undervaluation, and bargaining institutions
records.source_unit: ILO new global gender-pay-gap estimates and Equal Pay International Coalition policy release, published 21 September 2026
records.geography: Global, with comparisons across country income groups and labour-market contexts
records.boundary: This record adds a gendered distribution and bargaining route: the global pay gap is changing slowly, while care, segregation, progression, undervaluation, transparency, collective bargaining, care systems, and social protection shape the conversion of formal equality into household economic power. It is an ILO estimate summary and policy statement, not a country-level causal decomposition, worker panel, employer audit, or proof that proposed measures close gaps.

records.title: Youth labor-market recovery is stalling as unemployment, NEET status, informality, and technology transitions narrow routes into decent work
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, Global Employment Trends for Youth 2026: Back to the future
records.geography: Global and regional youth labor-market trends for people aged 15-24, with country data and comparisons by gender, income, education, and technology exposure
records.boundary: This record adds current youth labor-market conditions and policy pressures linking unemployment, NEET, informality, gender, care, skills, AI, employment services, and social protection. It uses publication-level aggregate estimates, not individual school-to-work histories, respondent-level aspirations, household care diaries, or causal estimates of a specific technology or policy.

records.title: Stable global unemployment is masking a large jobs gap, persistent informality, and uneven job quality
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization Employment and Social Trends 2026
records.geography: Global labour markets, with comparisons across income groups, gender, and youth
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative labour-market route connecting unemployment, unmet labour demand, informality, working poverty, productivity, gender and youth inequalities, trade-linked employment, and AI risk. It does not infer individual job quality, household welfare, employer causality, or worker-level transitions from global modelled indicators.

records.title: Governance quality is persistent but vulnerable, and intermediary organizational capacity determines whether reform becomes durable social dialogue
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, Governance: hard to build, easy to erode: Global trends, business implications and the role of employer and business membership organizations
records.geography: 208 economies over 1996-2024, with a 2025 organizational-governance sample of employer and business membership organizations
records.boundary: This record adds an institutional transmission route from national governance quality through employer and business membership organizations, social dialogue, investment conditions, decent work, and reform durability. It uses ILO aggregate country trajectories, index classifications, regression evidence, and organizational analysis, not individual worker experiences, firm-level causal investment histories, political-event forecasting, respondent-level trust measures, or proof that institutional capacity produces inclusive outcomes everywhere.

records.title: Work inequality is organized through sector, formality, own-account status, and circumstances beyond individual control rather than only headline wage gaps
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, Inequalities in the World of Work, published June 2026
records.geography: Global labor markets with comparative analysis across Sub-Saharan Africa, Latin America, demographic groups, sectors, employment forms, and formal/informal work
records.boundary: This record adds a published structural work-inequality route linking earnings dispersion, sector, formality, own-account work, inequality of opportunity, policy, and decent-work access. It is not new respondent-level analysis, an individual wage estimate, a causal decomposition for every country, or proof that formalization or policy reform improves household outcomes.

records.title: Jordan’s cooperative reforms show how shared ownership can connect refugee livelihoods, women’s agency, food production, and social cohesion—without removing legal or financial fragility
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, Cooperatives as pathways to advancing decent work and economic inclusion: Lessons learned from the PROSPECTS Jordan experience, 2026
records.geography: Jordan, with refugees and vulnerable host-community members in displacement-affected agricultural and cooperative settings
records.boundary: This record adds a concrete cooperative-development intervention route connecting displacement, labor-market access, shared ownership, gender and youth participation, food and water capability, and social cohesion. It is a programme lessons-learned case, not a randomized evaluation, representative refugee survey, verified household-income panel, or proof that legal reform and cooperative outputs produced durable security after programme support.

records.title: Formalization is a trust-and-implementation bargain: digital awareness cannot cross process friction alone
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, Impact evaluation of behaviourally informed awareness campaigns to expand social security coverage in Jordan: Findings from firm-level data, 2026 publication of preliminary RCT findings
records.geography: Jordan; small firms with up to nine registered employees, using Social Security Corporation administrative data and firm-level surveys
records.boundary: This record extends the Jordan social-security experiment with firm-level heterogeneity, administrative-interface friction, data freshness, perceived inspection, and implementation integrity. It is preliminary evidence from firms already connected to SSC, not a causal estimate of long-run formalization, benefit adequacy, trust, job quality, household welfare, or outcomes among firms and workers entirely outside the administrative system.

records.title: Social-protection formalization requires affordability and human navigation, not information alone
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, What Drives Social Security Registration? Experimental Evidence from Behavioural Interventions in Jordan’s Estidama++ Programme, 2026
records.geography: Jordan; small firms with 1–9 registered workers and eligible Jordanian and non-Jordanian workers in the Estidama++ programme
records.boundary: This record adds randomized evidence that in-person outreach plus temporary contribution subsidies increased social-security registration among eligible Jordanian small firms, while SMS alone did not increase worker registration. It does not establish benefit adequacy, durable post-subsidy coverage, job quality, household welfare, or generalizability beyond the Jordanian small-firm and Estidama++ context.

records.title: Permanent tripartite dialogue turns worker and employer voice into a labour-governance institution, but ownership determines whether it becomes operative
records.source_unit: ILO report on the Kurdistan Region of Iraq Social Dialogue Forum, published September 3, 2026
records.geography: Kurdistan Region of Iraq, with exchange links to Federal Iraq and wider Arab States social-dialogue practice
records.boundary: This record captures the institutional design and stated durability conditions of a new tripartite labour-governance forum. It does not establish effective representation, policy influence, enforcement, worker outcomes, social-security access, or institutional survival.

records.title: Cooperative livelihoods become governable when public data, digital administration, and market access are rebuilt together in Lebanon
records.source_unit: ILO news report on the Lebanon cooperative-sector data and digital-modernization partnership, published 23 September 2026
records.geography: Lebanon, especially agricultural cooperatives and rural livelihoods involving Lebanese and Syrian workers and refugee-host communities
records.boundary: This record adds a cooperative-institution route linking data visibility, digital public administration, rural livelihoods, refugee-host economies, finance, market access, decent work, and international development standards. It is an official partnership announcement with reported associated outputs, not evidence of cooperative survival, representative job quality, causal finance effects, or implemented digital-service outcomes.

records.title: Lebanon is trying to make trade and investment policy answerable to employment through evidence, sector selection, and tripartite coordination
records.source_unit: ILO report on the launch of the Mainstreaming Employment into Trade and Investment (METI) project in Lebanon, published 27 August 2026
records.geography: Lebanon, with regional Southern Mediterranean METI II connections across Algeria, Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Morocco, Palestine, Syria, and Tunisia
records.boundary: This record adds a policy-design route linking trade and investment, employment measurement, tripartite coordination, export-oriented value chains, MSMEs, skills, gender, formalization, regional integration, and inclusive recovery. It records a project launch and planned mechanisms, not actual trade growth, job creation, wage change, firm performance, worker outcomes, or implemented policy effects.

records.title: Access to recognized learning is becoming a distributional condition of adapting to digital, green, and demographic change
records.source_unit: ILO, Lifelong learning and skills for the future
records.geography: Global; cross-country institutional, labour-market, training, and online-vacancy evidence synthesized by the ILO
records.boundary: This record adds an education-to-work-adaptation and institutional-delivery route. It is not respondent-level longitudinal data, does not estimate an individual training return, and does not establish that skills policy alone causes better wages, mobility, care quality, political participation, or geopolitical capacity.

records.title: Living-wage policy is moving from voluntary corporate promise toward shared public-private wage infrastructure
records.source_unit: ILO news report on the first public-private partnerships under the Living Wage Programme, published 24 September 2026
records.geography: ILO member states and global supply chains; partnerships involve the Responsible Business Alliance, Unilever, and amfori across multiple countries and sourcing markets
records.boundary: This record adds a wage-governance route linking household living costs, worker and family needs, national data, tripartite institutions, multinational supply chains, consumer-facing firms, and public-private standards. It is an announcement of agreements and intended mechanisms, not evidence of wage increases, worker welfare, bargaining power, price effects, or supply-chain compliance.

records.title: A geopolitical energy shock can reach workers, firms, households, migration, and remittances through a delayed labor-market transmission chain
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, Employment and Social Trends: May 2026 Update: Growing labour market risks from the Middle East crisis
records.geography: Global labor markets with focused exposure analysis for Arab States and Asia and the Pacific, including energy, supply chains, tourism, migration, and remittance channels
records.boundary: This record adds a geopolitical-shock-to-labor-to-household-transmission route linking energy prices, transport, supply chains, tourism, investment, work hours, labor income, unemployment, migration, remittances, and social protection. It is not individual worker or household respondent data, a realized loss estimate, a completed crisis forecast, or proof that the modeled scenario occurred.

records.title: Migrant-worker protection is being reframed as a lifecycle rights pathway rather than a border or recruitment issue
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, International labour standards and migrant workers’ rights: A Guide for policymakers and practitioners, 2025/2026
records.geography: Comparative international labour-migration framework with illustrative regional and national examples across origin, transit, and destination contexts
records.boundary: This record adds a transnational migrant-rights-lifecycle mechanism linking recruitment, work, social protection, residence, family, return, enforcement, and justice. It is a standards-based practical guide, not a prevalence dataset, causal evaluation, or country-compliance audit; the next test is whether rights pathways produce accessible information, lower recruitment debt, safer work, portable protection, worker voice, and effective remedy without creating new status-based exclusions.

records.title: Enterprise registration is not worker formalization: construction exposes the portability gap
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, Informality in Nepal's Construction Sector: Promoting enterprise formalization and extending social protection to construction workers, 2026
records.geography: Nepal construction sector, with national labor-market, enterprise and stakeholder evidence
records.boundary: This record identifies construction as a high-informality social-protection and portability problem: enterprise registration, worker formalization, safety, skills, gender equity and procurement are coupled but distinct. It is a diagnostic policy brief, not causal evidence that any individual recommendation improves registration, earnings, safety, poverty, gender equity or social trust.

records.title: Sector skills institutions are being redesigned as system integrators for AI, green transition, and decent work
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, Next generation sector skills bodies: Driving productivity, innovation, decent work and social justice, 2026
records.geography: Comparative guide drawing on Sector Skills Body models across 18 countries, including Australia, South Africa, New Zealand, Singapore, Ghana, Jordan, Nigeria, Ethiopia, Kenya, and Zambia
records.boundary: This record adds a skills-governance-to-worker-voice, enterprise-adaptation, and Just Transition mechanism. It is a comparative practical guide, not causal evidence that Sector Skills Bodies improve wages, employment, productivity, inclusion, or environmental outcomes; the next test is whether specific bodies convert structured social dialogue, labor-market intelligence, and hybrid financing into measurable improvements in job quality, mobility, skills use, and transition security without employer capture.

records.title: Pacific labour governance is becoming a regional institutional layer linking mobility, skills, social protection, workforce resilience, and economic strategy
records.source_unit: ILO report on Pacific leaders endorsing a regional Labour Ministers Meeting within the Pacific Islands Forum governance architecture, published 11 September 2026
records.geography: Pacific Islands Forum region, with regional labour governance linked to the Blue Pacific 2050 Strategy
records.boundary: This record adds a geopolitical and institutional labour-governance route: Pacific regional cooperation is creating a possible ministerial layer connecting labour mobility, skills, social protection, workforce resilience, economic strategy, and tripartite dialogue. It is an announcement-stage institutional account, not evidence of operational performance, worker outcomes, policy harmonization, labour-rights enforcement, or durable regional power.

records.title: Forced-labour prevention is becoming a cross-border trade and remedy chain linking worker protection, institutions, firms, and import-market accountability
records.source_unit: ILO and Canada launch of Promoting responsive institutions and mechanisms to eliminate forced labour in the Philippines (PRIME PH), published 15 September 2026
records.geography: Philippines, with trade and supply-chain links to Canada and ASEAN markets; agriculture, manufacturing, and mining are targeted sectors
records.boundary: This record adds a forced-labour, trade, and remedy route linking hidden exploitation risk, informality, labour institutions, worker voice, access to justice, responsible business conduct, import controls, and geopolitical economic partnership. It is an announcement-stage project account, not prevalence evidence, a forced-labour case audit, causal impact evaluation, proof of enforcement, or evidence that trade rules improve worker conditions.

records.title: The first global platform-work convention turns algorithmic management, classification, pay, data, deactivation, and remedy into international labor-governance questions
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, Convention concerning decent work in the platform economy, 2026 (No. 193), adopted 12 June 2026
records.geography: ILO Member States, digital labour platforms, platform workers, intermediaries, and cross-border platform arrangements
records.boundary: This record adds an international normative layer to the platform-work control and remedy map. It records an adopted Convention, not ratification, domestic implementation, platform compliance, worker-level outcomes, causal effects, or proof that formal rights produce restored earnings, durable bargaining power, or practical exit.

records.title: Displacement response is shifting from short-term relief toward work, enterprise, social protection, and national-system inclusion
records.source_unit: ILO PROSPECTS: Results at a glance, September 2026, published 24 September 2026
records.geography: PROSPECTS partnership work with forcibly displaced persons and host communities across participating country programmes
records.boundary: This record adds an implementation and labour-market route linking forced displacement, host communities, decent work, skills, employment, enterprise, social protection, national systems, and inclusive-society goals. It uses a public programme results brief, not respondent-level employment histories, a complete beneficiary census, job-quality or earnings estimates, causal programme evaluation, representative host-community attitudes, or proof of durable inclusion.

records.title: Work organization is becoming a population health, productivity, and governance problem, not only an individual wellbeing issue
records.source_unit: ILO, The psychosocial working environment: Global developments and pathways for action
records.geography: Global; international, regional, and national policy evidence synthesized by the ILO
records.boundary: This record adds a global work-organization-to-health, productivity, and governance route. It is not respondent-level data, does not estimate individual mental-health outcomes, and does not establish causal effects of a specific employer, schedule, platform, or policy on worker wellbeing, household security, trust, or exit.

records.title: Responsible fisheries governance is expanding from fish-stock legality to crew welfare, labour exploitation, and decent-work supply-chain conditions
records.source_unit: RPOA-IUU and ILO regional workshop on decent working conditions in the fisheries sector, published 15 September 2026
records.geography: South-East Asia and the Regional Plan of Action to Promote Responsible Fishing Practices including Combating Illegal, Unreported, and Unregulated Fishing
records.boundary: This record adds a fisheries-governance route linking IUU fishing, labour exploitation, crew welfare, decent-work standards, regional enforcement, safe migration, and sustainable seafood supply chains. It is a workshop and programme announcement, not a prevalence study, vessel audit, causal evaluation, worker-outcome dataset, or proof that standards are implemented or that better work conditions prevent IUU fishing.

records.title: Social insurance must adapt to the self-employed worker’s income, status and life-course volatility
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization Working Paper 176, Inclusive social insurance: Exploring real solutions to reach the self-employed, July 2026
records.geography: Comparative evidence from ten country case-study settings, with eight detailed country examples spanning Algeria, Brazil, Cabo Verde, Costa Rica, Mongolia, Portugal, Tunisia, Uruguay and Zambia pilots, plus Thailand
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative design and usability layer to the formalization and portability theme: self-employed workers face status ambiguity, irregular earnings, administrative burden, affordability constraints, benefit-fit problems and weak voice. The selected cases are not globally representative, evidence on beneficiary outcomes is sparse, and the paper does not establish causal effects of voluntary versus mandatory participation, subsidies, one-stop shops, scheme integration, formalization, income, wellbeing or durable coverage.

records.title: Lifelong-learning systems face an institutionalization gap between policy ambition and everyday implementation
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, Independent High-Level Evaluation of the ILO’s strategies and actions under the ILO strategy on skills and lifelong learning, 2022–2026, 2026
records.geography: Comparative evaluation covering six country case studies: Colombia, Panama, Kenya, Ethiopia, Republic of Moldova, and Bangladesh; broader ILO portfolio evidence
records.boundary: This record identifies an institutionalization gap in lifelong-learning systems: policy and governance reforms are advancing faster than routine implementation, domestic financing, worker influence, and scale. It is an independent strategy-level evaluation, not causal proof that skills reforms improve wages, employment, productivity, or inclusion; the next test is whether national systems convert policy frameworks into durable, accessible, worker-legitimate learning and transition institutions.

records.title: Climate policy and climate shocks are being linked to social-protection design, insurance coverage, livelihood security, and the conditions of a just transition
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization and Agence Française de Développement, Social Protection and Climate Change: The Role of Social Insurance
records.geography: Global social-protection systems, workers, households, and states facing climate impacts and low-emissions transitions
records.boundary: This record adds a climate-social-protection and just-transition signal linking climate shocks and policies to lifecycle risk, work, household security, social insurance, coverage gaps, and institutional capacity. It is an ILO-AFD literature review and analytical report whose underlying work was conducted in 2022 and not updated, not a current coverage census, household panel, causal evaluation, or proof that contributory social insurance protects excluded workers.

records.title: Social-protection coverage is being converted through laws, data, automatic enrolment, contribution systems, and worker organization for people outside standard employment
records.source_unit: ILO final results account for the multi-donor project supporting the second phase of the Global Flagship Programme on Building Social Protection Floors for All, published 25 September 2026
records.geography: Six countries across Southeast Asia, West Africa, and Central Africa, with regional learning and Asia-Pacific cooperation context
records.boundary: This record adds a coverage-conversion route: social-protection rights become usable protection through law, data, coordination, worker organization, automatic enrolment, contribution systems, health insurance, and durable public administration, especially for informal workers. It relies on ILO programme reporting and selected country examples, not representative population data, causal evaluation, independently verified reach, benefit adequacy, or proof of post-project sustainability.

records.title: Social-protection reform shows a measurable gap between legal entitlement and effective access
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, ILO Global Flagship Programme on Building Social Protection Floors for All: Report of the second phase (2021-25), 2026
records.geography: 50 priority countries across Africa, the Americas, Arab States, Asia and the Pacific, and Europe and Central Asia, with programme-level global results
records.boundary: This record adds a legal-entitlement-to-effective-access and institutional-sequencing mechanism to the social-protection findings. It is a programme retrospective, not a population-wide causal evaluation or independent verification of every attributed result; the next test is whether country reforms sustain domestic financing, registration, delivery, adequacy, inclusion, and crisis responsiveness after external programme support changes.

records.title: Formalization, worker voice, social protection, and child-labour prevention are being built as one connected governance system in South Asia
records.source_unit: ILO news report on Japan-supported PRS Phase 2 and PPLL initiatives in South Asia, published 21 September 2026
records.geography: India, Nepal, and Pakistan, with regional South Asia and Japan-ILO partnership implications
records.boundary: This record identifies a connected governance route from informality and child-labour risk to formalization, social protection, worker voice, gender equality, community action, and international partnership. It uses an official programme closeout account, not an independent causal evaluation, representative survey, complete beneficiary census, or proof of durable post-project outcomes.

records.title: Social justice gains coexist with persistent informality, unequal power, weak bargaining rights, and transition risks
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, The State of Social Justice 2025: A Work in Progress
records.geography: Global comparison of social-justice indicators, with qualitative findings from 17 countries
records.boundary: This record adds a social-justice route linking poverty, informality, distribution, labour rights, institutional trust, and climate, technological, and demographic transitions. It uses aggregate indicators and a report-level qualitative synthesis, not respondent-level interview analysis, individual worker histories, causal institutional estimates, or claims that legal protection guarantees lived justice.

records.title: A heritage crop becomes a global value-chain test: market access must be built with farmer voice and decent work
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, Development of the Timor-Leste vanilla value chain roadmap including associated skills needs and stocktaking of working conditions, September 2026
records.geography: Timor-Leste, with the vanilla value chain spanning rural farms, collectors, processors, traders, domestic markets and export links to Indonesia
records.boundary: This record identifies a value-chain, bargaining-power, skills, consumer-positioning and decent-work theme. It does not establish that the roadmap will increase farmer income, create durable jobs, improve safety, produce an export premium, strengthen women’s or youth economic power, or distribute value fairly; those require follow-up data on prices, contracts, processing, certification, work conditions, household outcomes and buyer concentration.

records.title: Trade and investment do not automatically produce decent work; policy alignment and social dialogue shape who benefits
records.source_unit: ILO, Trade, Investment and Decent Work in Africa: Evidence and Stakeholder Perspectives
records.geography: Ghana, Kenya, Mozambique, South Africa, and Uganda, with implications for African regional integration and the African Continental Free Trade Area
records.boundary: This record adds a trade-to-work and governance route linking African regional integration, investment, employment policy, informality, labor standards, social protection, skills, supply chains, and social dialogue. It uses an aggregate publication and stakeholder-perspective frame, not individual worker histories, a causal trade-impact estimate, or proof that consultation becomes implementation.

records.title: Platform-work governance and worker financial health are converging as tests of whether economic transformation produces usable security
records.source_unit: ILO account of its priorities at the 81st United Nations General Assembly, including platform-work governance and a workplace financial-health event
records.geography: Global policy agenda at UNGA81, with platform workers, employers, governments, labour institutions, financial-service providers, and international partners in scope
records.boundary: This record adds a transformation-to-security route linking platform-work governance, international labour standards, workplace financial health, fair transitions, and household room. It is an ILO agenda and convening account, not evidence of platform-worker outcomes, financial-health improvement, domestic implementation, or causal effects of Convention No. 193.

records.title: Labour-market change is making social-protection coverage, adequacy, and financing a central resilience question
records.source_unit: ILO, Universal social protection in changing labour markets: Protecting workers in all types of employment
records.geography: Global labour markets and country experiences used by the ILO policy paper
records.boundary: This record adds institutional coverage, adequacy, financing, transition, and resilience mechanisms. It is not respondent-level data, does not estimate benefit take-up or household effects, and does not establish causal effects of social protection on work, consumption, health, or political behavior.

records.title: Informal volunteering is a major but undercounted layer of social infrastructure, shaped by care, resources, and place
records.source_unit: ILO-UNV, Informal volunteering: Trends and characteristics
records.geography: Comparative country contexts covered by the ILO-UNV global analysis of informal volunteering
records.boundary: This record adds an informal-volunteering, civic-capacity, unpaid-care, and social-infrastructure route. It uses comparative published evidence, not respondent-level volunteering histories, causal estimates of care or volunteering, individual service outcomes, or proof that formal recognition improves community wellbeing.

records.title: Youth employment programmes improve labor-market outcomes on average, with effects shaped by design, context, and disadvantage
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization and World Bank, The Impact of Active Labour Market Programmes on Youth: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Impact Evaluations, 1990-2022
records.geography: Comparative systematic review of youth active labour-market programmes across 62 countries and low-, middle-, and high-income settings
records.boundary: This record adds a youth-transition route linking active labor-market programmes to employment, earnings, skills, entrepreneurship, certification, gender, disadvantage, local delivery, partnerships, and cost-effectiveness. It summarizes evaluation evidence rather than respondent-level histories; it does not establish universal programme effects, job quality, household welfare, durable mobility, or causal effects outside the evaluated interventions.

records.title: Social protection expands globally while climate-vulnerable populations remain least protected and just-transition capacity stays uneven
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, World Social Protection Report 2024-26: Universal social protection for climate action and a just transition
records.geography: Global and regional social-protection coverage, expenditure, climate vulnerability, life-course benefits, and just-transition policy indicators
records.boundary: This record adds a global public-system route linking social-protection coverage, climate vulnerability, life-course and gender gaps, fiscal capacity, and just-transition policy. It uses publication-level aggregate indicators, not respondent-level histories, individual benefit records, household panels, or causal estimates of climate or welfare-policy effects.

records.title: Social protection is becoming the political infrastructure of climate adaptation, but coverage gaps leave children, workers and informal livelihoods exposed
records.source_unit: International Labour Organization, World Social Protection Report 2024–2026: Universal Social Protection for Climate Action and a Just Transition
records.geography: Global coverage and financing estimates with regional and income-group comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a protection-to-legitimacy mechanism: social protection is not only a poverty instrument but infrastructure for household resilience, labor-market transitions and politically sustainable climate action. It is an ILO global statistical and policy report, not a household panel, causal evaluation of benefits or country-specific implementation audit.

records.title: Trade resilience is becoming a geopolitical bargain between efficiency, diversification, fiscal room, and household price stability
records.source_unit: International Monetary Fund, Annual Report 2026, In Focus: Trade and Growth: Strained Resilience
records.geography: IMF member economies and global trade, with discussion of US trade policy, Asia, China, ASEAN, the European Union, energy routes, and supply chains
records.boundary: This record adds a geopolitical trade-and-supply-chain layer connecting US policy shifts, regional reorientation, energy-route disruption, diversification, imbalances, and policy predictability. It is an IMF annual-report synthesis, not a causal trade evaluation, household-incidence study, or forecast of a specific future energy or food price path.

records.title: Widening global current-account imbalances raise adjustment and financial risks while coordinated rebalancing offers the least disruptive path
records.source_unit: International Monetary Fund, External Sector Report 2026: Amid Rising Imbalances, the Case for Rebalancing
records.geography: Global external sector with assessments of 30 of the world's largest economies based on 2025 data
records.boundary: This record adds a geoeconomic route across current-account divergence, external positions, trade and exchange-rate adjustment, financial risk, domestic policy, and household-room transmission. It uses IMF model-based external assessments and macro synthesis, not respondent-level data, household expenditure diaries, firm microdata, causal political-behavior estimates, or proof that any surplus or deficit is inherently good or bad.

records.title: High debt is forcing governments to arbitrate among security, aging, climate, investment, and social-protection claims
records.source_unit: International Monetary Fund, Fiscal Monitor April 2026: Fiscal Policy under Pressure: High Debt, Rising Risks
records.geography: Global fiscal outlook with country and regional examples covering debt, defense, aging, climate, aid, public services, and fiscal adjustment
records.boundary: This record adds a fiscal-political route linking debt, interest burdens, defense, aging, climate transition, public investment, aid, social protection, service cuts, revenue mobilization, digital targeting, and political feasibility. It uses aggregate publication evidence and cited cross-country estimates, not household tax records, individual benefit histories, respondent-level political attitudes, or a causal estimate of any single fiscal reform.

records.title: War, inflation, leverage, and nonbank finance create multiple channels through which market stress can become broader instability
records.source_unit: International Monetary Fund, Global Financial Stability Report April 2026: Global Financial Markets Confront the War in the Middle East and Amplification Risks
records.geography: Global financial system, emerging markets, commodity-importing and vulnerable economies, nonbank intermediaries, and major capital markets
records.boundary: This record adds a financial-stability route across war, energy, inflation, market repricing, sovereign rollover, nonbank leverage, capital flows, AI concentration, and public oversight. It uses IMF market surveillance and systemic-risk synthesis, not respondent-level data, household financial diaries, individual portfolio histories, causal market predictions, or proof that a listed vulnerability becomes a crisis.

records.title: Japan’s household debt and leverage amplify consumption responses to fiscal tightening
records.source_unit: International Monetary Fund, Japan 2026 Article IV Consultation, Annex IX: Japan’s Household Consumption Behavior
records.geography: Japan; household-panel and Family Income and Expenditure Survey evidence with income, age, debt, loan-to-value, employment, and consumption dimensions
records.boundary: This record adds panel-based balance-sheet and consumption-response evidence to the consumer trend atlas. It does not establish current Japanese retail behavior, cultural spending, household distress prevalence, or transferability to other countries.

records.title: Low-income economies face divergent growth with aid, remittance, debt, and institutional constraints shaping resilience
records.source_unit: International Monetary Fund, Macroeconomic Developments and Prospects in Low-Income Countries—2026
records.geography: Low-income countries, with emphasis on growth, debt, aid, remittances, commodity prices, fiscal institutions, governance, and private-sector development
records.boundary: This record adds a low-income-country macro route linking aggregate growth to per-capita welfare, aid, remittances, debt, reserves, commodity prices, energy and food costs, governance, public financial management, and job creation. It is publication-level comparative evidence, not household remittance histories, individual income records, respondent-level political data, or causal proof of any particular reform effect.

records.title: Digital public infrastructure can expand fiscal capacity and social assistance, but only when inclusion, trust, and institutional reach travel with it
records.source_unit: IMF Note 2026/009, Digitalization for Stronger Revenue and Social Assistance in the Middle East and Central Asia
records.geography: Middle East and Central Asia comparative evidence, with country cases across Gulf Cooperation Council, Caucasus and Central Asia, non-GCC Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan, and Pakistan
records.boundary: This record adds a digital-public-infrastructure route linking identity, connectivity, financial inclusion, interoperable registries, tax administration, revenue, social-assistance targeting, poverty, inequality, trust, exclusion, privacy, and enforcement costs. It is not a country-level causal evaluation, a guarantee that digitization improves equity, a measure of individual benefit receipt, or evidence that digital systems can substitute for adequate benefits, accountable institutions, or human remedy.

records.title: Social protection spending has different distributional returns across countries, making targeting, coverage, and fiscal capacity part of the inequality outcome
records.source_unit: IMF Working Paper 2026/078, Lean and Just? Social Protection Spending and Inequality Outcomes across Europe
records.geography: European countries with comparable Eurostat EU-SILC and social-protection spending data; country coverage varies by analysis
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative fiscal-capacity route from social-protection spending through targeting, coverage, inequality reduction, poverty, efficiency, and political tradeoffs. It summarizes a working paper using harmonized EU-SILC microdata and model-based benchmarks; it is not a causal evaluation, a respondent-level reanalysis, a complete welfare measure, or a recommendation to cut benefits solely on the basis of the reported efficiency metric.

records.title: Technology momentum offsets part of the war drag while growth, inflation, and fiscal room remain uneven across economies
records.source_unit: International Monetary Fund, World Economic Outlook Update July 2026: Global Economy in Crosscurrents of War and Technology
records.geography: Global economy with advanced, emerging-market, developing, energy-importing, and technology-integrated economy comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a global macro route across war, energy, technology demand, growth, inflation, fiscal space, and unequal exposure. It uses IMF forecasts and report-level risk synthesis, not respondent-level data, household price diaries, firm microdata, causal AI productivity estimates, or proof that aggregate growth improves welfare evenly.

records.title: India’s consumption room is expanding, but cultural and discretionary access remains sharply stratified
records.source_unit: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Household Consumption Expenditure Survey 2023–24 press note and report
records.geography: India; 261,953 sampled households across States and Union Territories, with rural/urban, State/UT, and MPCE-fractile dimensions
records.boundary: This record adds an India-wide household-consumption and distribution layer beneath cultural and consumer trends. It does not isolate entertainment spending, measure cultural attendance, establish causal welfare effects, or treat MPCE as disposable income or equal opportunity.

records.title: India's cultural and leisure time is widespread, but gendered unpaid work changes who can actually use it
records.source_unit: National Statistics Office India Time Use Survey 2024
records.geography: India; persons aged 6 years and above, with national, gender, age, and rural-urban estimates
records.boundary: This record adds observed time-allocation evidence linking cultural/leisure/media time to unpaid domestic work, caregiving, gender, age, and rural-urban context. The category is broad and combines culture, leisure, mass media, and sports; the one-day diary does not establish habitual cultural consumption, quality, preference, or causality.

records.title: India's UPI becomes dominant payment infrastructure while transaction throughput remains distinct from consumer capability
records.source_unit: Government of India Press Information Bureau release marking ten years of UPI, using NPCI statistics for FY2025-26
records.geography: India
records.boundary: This record adds India's payment-rail infrastructure layer to South Korea's online commerce and the Africa/Asia retail signals. It does not measure unique users, household welfare, merchant economics, cultural consumption, fraud, affordability, or effective consumer remedy.

records.title: Indonesia shows broad neighborhood social participation but thin formal organizational reach
records.source_unit: BPS-Statistics Indonesia, Statistics of Socio Culture 2025, sourced from Susenas September 2025
records.geography: Indonesia; population aged 5 years and older for cultural measures and aged 10 years and older for social-interaction measures, with sex, age, expenditure, and urban/rural dimensions
records.boundary: This record adds an Indonesia-wide socio-cultural participation layer distinguishing broad neighborhood activity from formal meetings and standing organization membership. It does not establish causality, social trust, political participation, household spending, cultural meaning, organizational effectiveness, or within-country causal mechanisms.

records.title: Indonesia's internet use is widespread, but the device ecology remains mobile-first with low computer and fixed-line ownership
records.source_unit: BPS-Statistics Indonesia, Telecommunication Statistics in Indonesia 2024
records.geography: Indonesia; national population, households, and internet users represented by Susenas 2024
records.boundary: This record adds Indonesian evidence on internet penetration, mobile/computer/fixed-line device ecology, and access locations. It does not measure cultural participation, platform behavior, digital quality, data affordability, household inequality, or causal consumer effects.

records.title: French household confidence remains depressed while precautionary saving stays elevated and major-purchase room remains weak
records.source_unit: INSEE, Monthly consumer confidence survey, September 2026
records.geography: France; approximately 2,000 households surveyed by telephone during August 26–September 17, 2026
records.boundary: This record adds a consumer-room route from price salience and confidence through precautionary saving, major-purchase restraint, future living-standard judgments and household expectations. It is a monthly repeated cross-sectional opinion survey with synthetic indexes, not realized spending, saving, debt, income distribution or causal household behavior.

records.title: AI capability gains are becoming a societal risk-management problem as misuse, malfunction, systemic dependence, and governance capacity move on different clocks
records.source_unit: International AI Safety Report 2026, chaired by Yoshua Bengio and written with guidance from more than 100 independent experts
records.geography: Global general-purpose AI capability, risk, and risk-management evidence with expert guidance from more than 30 countries and international organisations
records.boundary: This record adds a scientific risk-and-resilience route across general-purpose AI capability, malicious use, malfunctions, systemic dependence, labor, human autonomy, AI companions, safeguards, governance, and societal resilience. It uses an international scientific review and evidence synthesis, not respondent-level ingestion, a probability forecast of catastrophic outcomes, a complete incident or misuse census, a causal evaluation of any safeguard, or proof that one risk-management regime is sufficient.

records.title: Democratic stagnation and declining rights are being linked to conflict risk, especially where procedures exist without real competition or enforceable rights
records.source_unit: International IDEA, The Global State of Democracy 2026: Democracy in an Age of Conflict, 15 September 2026
records.geography: Countries assessed through the Global State of Democracy Indices, across regions and levels of democratic performance
records.boundary: This record adds a democracy-to-conflict route from institutional credibility, competition, rights, expression, and justice through legitimacy and peace. It uses comparative index and report analysis, not individual political histories, causal conflict attribution, public-opinion representativeness, or proof that any ranking determines future outcomes.

records.title: Democratic stagnation is becoming a conflict and public-voice problem as rule of law, expression, and participation weaken
records.source_unit: International IDEA, The Global State of Democracy 2026: Democracy in an Age of Conflict
records.geography: Global assessment of democratic performance, covering the International IDEA Global State of Democracy Indices through 2025 and conflict analysis with country and regional comparisons
