records.boundary: This record adds a political-institutional route from democratic stagnation and rights erosion through participation, rule of law, state capacity, public accountability, and conflict risk. It uses an international index, event tracker, and comparative conflict synthesis; it is not respondent-level public opinion, a causal evaluation of any government, or proof that one institutional reform will produce peace.

records.title: Migration remains a development asset under pressure from disruption, displacement, climate mobility, and constrained pathways
records.source_unit: International Organization for Migration, World Migration Report 2026
records.geography: Global migration, mobility, displacement, migrant development contributions, climate mobility, regular pathways, and community response
records.boundary: This record adds a global migration, displacement, development, climate-mobility, pathway, disability, and local-response route. It uses aggregate stocks, report synthesis, and thematic policy analysis, not individual migration histories, respondent-level attitudes, causal remittance or pathway estimates, or a claim that climate stress mechanically causes migration.

records.title: International mobility is widespread but still selective, while climate disruption and pathway design redistribute migration risk
records.source_unit: IOM World Migration Report 2026, chapters on global migration, regular pathways, climate mobility, and internal displacement
records.geography: Global international migration, climate mobility, regular migration pathways, and internal displacement
records.boundary: This record adds international-migrant stocks, pathway governance, climate mobility, local action, and internal-displacement framing. It is not respondent-level migration data, does not infer individual motives or route choices, and does not establish causal effects of climate or migration policy on displacement, welfare, or political behavior.

records.title: Information abundance is separating access from trust while platform accountability and AI-mediated search reshape the conditions for shared reality
records.source_unit: International Panel on the Information Environment, Trends in the Information Environment: 2026 Expert Survey Results
records.geography: 71 countries of expertise, including developed and developing economies and a separately reported United States comparison
records.boundary: This record adds an information-environment route from platform accountability, source trust, AI-mediated search, viewpoint diversity, research capacity, and political pressure through shared reality and civic participation. It uses expert survey judgments and report synthesis, not a public prevalence estimate, observed platform traffic, direct misinformation exposure, causal political effects, or proof that AI summaries will narrow viewpoints everywhere.

records.title: The information environment is becoming a platform-accountability, trust, and research-capacity problem
records.source_unit: International Panel on the Information Environment, Trends in the Information Environment: 2026 Expert Survey Results
records.geography: Global expert survey covering 71 countries, with separate USA, developing-economy, and other-developed-economy comparisons
records.boundary: This record is expert-assessment evidence about the global information environment and the capacity to study it. It does not establish public-level exposure, platform causality, observed news traffic, actual censorship rates, public trust trends, or the effects of AI summaries on civic participation.

records.title: Healthcare AI is moving into routine diagnostic work faster than trust is generalizing across clinical tasks
records.source_unit: Ipsos, The AI Trust Deficit in Healthcare 2026
records.geography: Healthcare professionals and patients; public report summary with geography and full sample details not disclosed
records.boundary: This record adds a clinical-trust mechanism: healthcare AI adoption and patient awareness can advance while confidence remains task-specific, with higher acceptance in lower-friction analytic applications and lower acceptance where judgment, vulnerability and consequence are harder to separate from the human relationship. It is a public summary of a healthcare opinion study, not a clinical validation, safety assessment, implementation evaluation or patient-outcome dataset.

records.title: Healthcare AI adoption is outpacing shared trust, with confidence varying by diagnostic task and perceived clinical friction
records.source_unit: Ipsos, The AI Trust Deficit in Healthcare, September 2026
records.geography: Healthcare professionals and patients; public summary does not disclose the full country frame or sample sizes
records.boundary: This record adds a health-AI adoption route linking clinician use, patient awareness, task-specific trust, clinical friction, explanation, oversight, and accountability. The public Ipsos summary provides only selected findings from a gated report, so this is not a full representative dataset, diagnostic accuracy evaluation, clinical outcomes study, or proof of safe adoption.

records.title: Economic fatigue, cultural anchoring, AI-mediated choice, and delayed life stages are reorganizing Irish consumer identity and everyday adaptation
records.source_unit: Ipsos B&A Ireland, Sign of the Times 2026
records.geography: Ireland; national survey of adults aged 16 and over, supplemented by focus groups, interviews, digital ethnography, and consumer-confidence research
records.boundary: This record adds a deep Irish cultural-consumer route across economic fatigue, emergency liquidity, cultural identity, geopolitical alignment, AI-mediated search, human meaning, trust circles, performance pressure, housing, delayed life stages, and intergenerational support. It uses a public Ipsos B&A mixed-method overview, not raw respondent microdata, a longitudinal household panel, verified search or attendance causality, clinical mental-health evidence, or proof that Ireland’s pattern generalizes to the United States or globally.

records.title: Tariffs are becoming a lived consumer signal through visible price increases, product-value judgments, safety trust, and political attribution
records.source_unit: Ipsos Consumer Tracker wave released 28 September 2026, including tariff perceptions, clothing-value judgments, food-inspection trust, community safety, and consumer technology use
records.geography: United States adults age 18 and older; recurring Ipsos online Consumer Tracker with current wave focused on tariff and consumer perceptions
records.boundary: This record adds a tariff-to-consumer-politics route: trade policy becomes socially legible through perceived price increases, product value, public safety, institutional trust, and household substitution. It uses Ipsos’s public tracker summary, not product-level price data, causal tariff incidence, observed purchasing, administrative inspection outcomes, or proof of political behavior.

records.title: Education retains mobility legitimacy while publics separate harmful social media from potentially useful AI and confront a youth mental-health crisis
records.source_unit: Ipsos, Education Monitor 2026
records.geography: 31-country cross-national public-opinion survey on youth, education, social media and AI
records.boundary: This record adds an education-legitimacy mechanism: publics still treat university as the default route to opportunity, even as they question its value and differentiate between harmful social media and potentially useful AI. Youth mental health is the dominant perceived pressure, while future confidence varies sharply by geography. This is a cross-national attitude study, not an enrollment, learning-outcome, mental-health prevalence or technology-impact dataset.

records.title: Energy-transition legitimacy is being renegotiated through affordability, geopolitical dependence and confidence in the grid
records.source_unit: Ipsos, Energy Transition Barometer 2026 / Global Advisor study
records.geography: 31 countries; global, regional and country comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a geopolitical-energy legitimacy mechanism: a conflict shock makes foreign dependence more salient, while affordability pressure, household cutbacks, grid reliability and AI load concerns condition support for the energy transition. It is a cross-national public-opinion study with a before-and-after comparison, not a causal conflict experiment, engineering reliability assessment, household billing panel or proof that broad transition support translates into local project consent.

records.title: Generational differences are often life-stage effects: work moves from optimism through pressure toward selective stability while housing and care reshape milestones
records.source_unit: Ipsos Generations Report 2026
records.geography: Global; Ipsos Global Advisor survey across 30 countries and Ipsos Global Employee Experience Benchmark Database across industries, roles and regions
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative life-stage mechanism: generational behavior should not be read only as cohort difference because care responsibilities, housing constraints, career stage, workplace friction and institutional communication evolve across the life course. The report combines a 30-country attitude survey, secondary demographic sources and a very large employee-experience benchmark; it is not a single probability sample, person-level panel, causal aging study, caregiver prevalence estimate or verified workplace outcome dataset.

records.title: AI adoption is becoming a negotiated bargain: time savings and future usefulness coexist with labor, environmental and commercial-trust concerns
records.source_unit: Ipsos, Global Attitudes on AI 2026 / fifth annual AI Monitor
records.geography: 32 countries; global, regional, income and generational comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a negotiated-adoption mechanism: people see AI as increasingly consequential and often time-saving, while income gaps, environmental trade-offs, regional affect and advertiser influence shape whether that usefulness is trusted and legitimate. It is a cross-national attitude study, not a causal productivity evaluation, AI-use trace, labor-market forecast, environmental lifecycle assessment or proof of actual consumer switching.

records.title: Consumer sentiment has stabilized globally without fully recovering from geopolitical shock, leaving current economic room below future expectations
records.source_unit: Ipsos Global Consumer Confidence Index, September 2026
records.geography: 30 countries; more than 21,000 adults under 75 surveyed 21 August-4 September 2026
records.boundary: This record adds a recurring consumer-confidence route linking current household purchasing room, investment, jobs, future expectations, geopolitical shock recovery, and country divergence. It uses Ipsos perception indices, not realized consumption, income, employment, investment, poverty, or causal welfare outcomes.

records.title: Stable global consumer confidence masks a present-purchase and investment shortfall beneath stronger expectations and job sentiment
records.source_unit: Ipsos Global Consumer Confidence Index, September 2026 monthly survey
records.geography: 30 countries; more than 21,000 adults under age 75 surveyed August 21-September 4, 2026
records.boundary: This record identifies a cross-country consumer-sentiment and sub-index asymmetry. It does not establish realized spending, investment, jobs, household welfare, causal geopolitical effects, or a population-weighted global confidence level.

records.title: Citizens want essential infrastructure investment and see economic and climate benefits, but a delivery deficit makes them pragmatic about public–private funding
records.source_unit: Ipsos and Global Infrastructure Investor Association, Global Infrastructure Index 2026
records.geography: 29 countries; global country-average and country comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds an infrastructure-legitimacy mechanism: citizens prioritize essential and visible infrastructure, believe investment can improve jobs and climate resilience, but report a delivery deficit and condition openness to private capital on results. It is a cross-national public-opinion survey, not a project-delivery audit, infrastructure asset inventory, fiscal willingness-to-pay study or causal test of public–private financing.

records.title: Global publics are retreating toward local trust, personal control and present-focused coping as technology, institutions and climate feel less governable
records.source_unit: Ipsos, Global Trends 10th Edition 2026
records.geography: 38-market cross-national survey; market-average comparisons and global thematic synthesis
records.boundary: This record adds a cross-market cultural mechanism: when institutions, technology and the future feel less controllable, publics combine nostalgia, personal autonomy, local/value-based trust and present-focused consumption, while demanding practical adaptation from organisations. It is a weighted online-attitude survey and thematic interpretation, not a population-weighted world estimate, causal model, behavioral transaction dataset or forecast.

records.title: Technology unease, social fracture, nostalgia, individualism, and uncertainty are reshaping cultural and consumer meaning
records.source_unit: Ipsos, Global Trends 10th Edition 2026: In Search of a New Consensus
records.geography: Global social, technology, cultural, and consumer trend synthesis based on 38-market survey and macro-force analysis
records.boundary: This record adds a commercial-cultural route across technology sentiment, social fragmentation, nostalgia, individualism, uncertainty, and meaning. It uses Ipsos published aggregate survey and macro-force synthesis, not raw respondent-level records, individual purchase histories, causal attitude models, clinical outcomes, or a universal forecast of consumer behavior.

records.title: Trust remains concentrated in competence-bearing professions and ordinary people while politicians, influencers, and AI chatbots face a credibility deficit
records.source_unit: Ipsos Global Trustworthiness Index 2026, 31-Country Global Advisor Survey
records.geography: 31 countries; 23,537 online adults under age 75 surveyed 19 June-3 July 2026
records.boundary: This record adds a profession, AI, intermediary, ordinary-person, and country-trust route. It uses Ipsos perception data, not verified competence, institutional performance, chatbot accuracy, interpersonal behavior, or causal explanation of regional trust differences.

records.title: Short-term happiness is improving across most countries while longer-run gains remain uneven, with relationships supporting happiness and finances driving unhappiness
records.source_unit: Ipsos, Happiness Index 2026 / Global Advisor
records.geography: 29 countries; global, income and country comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a wellbeing-mechanism distinction: short-term happiness can improve while longer-run levels decline, relationships are perceived as the strongest happiness supports, and financial and housing pressures dominate unhappiness. It is a cross-national self-report survey, not a clinical mental-health measure, causal wellbeing model, longitudinal panel or population-weighted global happiness estimate.

records.title: Football club heritage converts place-based identity into organized fan voice when institutional survival is threatened
records.source_unit: Ipsos Public Affairs for the Independent Football Regulator, club heritage and fan-response polling, September 2026 release
records.geography: England and Wales; adults aged 16+ and supporters of men's clubs in the top five divisions
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural-institutional route: football clubs operate as place-based identity and community infrastructure, and perceived existential threat can convert attachment into prospective fan voice. The Ipsos survey is representative of adults in England and Wales with a weighted supporter subsample, but its dissolution scenario and action items are hypothetical. The record does not establish actual mobilization, financial rescue, attendance, spending, regulator effectiveness, or causal effects of heritage protection.

records.title: Young people still want stable work and homes, but the widening cultural shift is confidence in access rather than abandonment of traditional milestones
records.source_unit: Ipsos, Life Aspirations 2026 / Global Advisor
records.geography: 30 countries; global, generational, income and Western-country comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a life-course and consumer-culture mechanism: stable work and housing remain widely shared definitions of success, while income and access shape confidence, emotional stakes and the timing or substitution of family and care milestones. It is a cross-national public-opinion study, not a fertility forecast, housing-demand model, longitudinal life-course panel or proof that pet ownership replaces parenthood.

records.title: Mobility remains car-dependent and safety-constrained even as people support shared, active and lower-carbon alternatives
records.source_unit: Ipsos, Mobility Report 2026 / Global Advisor
records.geography: 31 countries and markets; global, regional and country comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a mobility-dependency mechanism: people remain attached to cars because access, time and daily destinations are structured around them, while broad support exists for safer streets, cycle lanes, public transport and lower-carbon vehicles. It is a cross-national public-attitude survey, not a travel diary, service-quality audit, crash dataset, engineering assessment or proof that stated support produces modal shift.

records.title: Institutional skepticism is redirecting trust toward familiar, local, and values-aligned actors
records.source_unit: Ipsos, Global Trends 10th Edition 2026: The Power of Trust, 21 September 2026
records.geography: Adults across 38 markets in the Ipsos Global Trends 2026 comparative framework
records.boundary: This record adds a distinct Ipsos publication route from institutional skepticism and perceived economic unfairness through local, familiar, values-aligned trust and AI-era consumption. It is aggregate comparative trend evidence, not respondent-level data, causal proof of local-trust effects, or a claim that formal institutions are becoming irrelevant.

records.title: Broad LGBT acceptance is holding while support for brand advocacy, media visibility and contested policy issues diverges
records.source_unit: Ipsos, LGBT+ Pride Report 2026 / Global Advisor
records.geography: 26 countries and markets; 23-country trend comparisons for selected questions
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural-legitimacy mechanism: broad legal recognition remains supported while corporate advocacy, media visibility and contested gender-policy questions show weaker or more polarized support. It is a cross-national public-opinion survey, not a behavioral purchase dataset, legal implementation audit, population-weighted global estimate or measure of lived safety and discrimination.

records.title: Targeted winter kindness meets older residents at the intersection of energy hardship, food trade-offs, loneliness and information access
records.source_unit: Ipsos for Small Acts of Kindness, Warm in Winter and Bags of Kindness recipient feedback, September 2026 release
records.geography: Hertfordshire and Bedfordshire, England; nominated older and vulnerable residents receiving charity gift bags
records.boundary: This record adds an intervention-encounter route: targeted material warmth, printed information and recognition meet energy hardship, food trade-offs, isolation and mediated companionship among nominated older and vulnerable residents. It is an opt-in recipient feedback sample from Hertfordshire and Bedfordshire, not population prevalence, a randomized evaluation, a matched panel, or evidence that the bags caused changes in bills, food security, health, loneliness or service take-up.

records.title: Climate concern is being filtered through affordability, health and credibility, making sustainability an everyday-value problem rather than a duty-only problem
records.source_unit: Ipsos, The Sustainability Reality Check / Market Essentials Sustainability Report 2026
records.geography: 15-market comparative consumer research; public analysis synthesizes the Market Essentials Sustainability Report 2026
records.boundary: This record adds a climate-to-household translation mechanism: concern remains high, but action is filtered through affordability, health relevance, convenience, organizational responsibility and trust. It is a public synthesis of comparative consumer research, not a transaction dataset, emissions inventory, product lifecycle assessment or causal evaluation of sustainability interventions.

records.title: Thai consumers retain routine spending resilience while corruption, safety, unemployment and affordability weaken political-economic legitimacy
records.source_unit: Ipsos Thailand, What Worries Thailand? September 2026, combining What Worries the World and consumer-sentiment findings
records.geography: Thailand; Thai consumers and public-opinion respondents as defined by the Ipsos release
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative consumer-legitimacy route: routine purchasing confidence can remain resilient while corruption, crime, unemployment, inequality, economic pessimism and national-direction judgments deteriorate. The Ipsos public release combines concern and consumer-sentiment indicators without publishing one pooled denominator on the country page; it does not measure objective conditions, realized purchasing, subsidy incidence, causal attribution or durable political trust.

records.title: Support for refugee protection remains broad while confidence depends on eligibility, integration, permanence and responsibility-sharing
records.source_unit: Ipsos and UNHCR, Global Attitudes Towards Refugees 2026
records.geography: Global multi-country survey; country, generation and crisis-scenario comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a migration-legitimacy mechanism: support for the right to seek refuge remains broad, but public confidence is conditional on credible eligibility, integration, permanence and responsibility-sharing arrangements. It is a cross-national public-opinion survey, not an asylum adjudication dataset, refugee-integration outcome study, public-service capacity audit or forecast of migration behavior.

records.title: Public concern remains materially grounded while country optimism can move ahead of lived economic satisfaction
records.source_unit: Ipsos What Worries the World, September 2026
records.geography: 30-country monthly public-opinion survey, around 20,000 adults
records.boundary: This record adds a recurring public-attention route linking healthcare, unemployment, crime, inequality, corruption, economic sentiment, political direction, and the gap between optimism and lived conditions. It uses selected highlights from a monthly Ipsos opinion survey, not administrative outcomes, causal political analysis, full country microdata, or a single globally representative estimate.

records.title: Women’s political representation is edging forward while executive power, parliamentary leadership, and safety remain sharply unequal
records.source_unit: Inter-Parliamentary Union and UN Women, Women in Politics: 2026 and Women in Parliament 2025 reporting
records.geography: Global national parliaments, cabinets, heads of state or government, parliamentary speakers, women parliamentarians, and countries holding elections or parliamentary renewals in 2025
records.boundary: This record adds a political-voice route linking formal representation, executive and parliamentary leadership, electoral rules, quotas, public hostility, safety, and participation. It is not a survey of general citizens, a causal estimate of women’s policy influence, proof of equal power, or a respondent-level microdata analysis.

records.title: Renewable deployment is creating a large but geographically concentrated workforce, while automation, supply-chain frictions and grid constraints weaken the simple promise that more capacity means proportionally more jobs
records.source_unit: International Renewable Energy Agency and International Labour Organization, Renewable Energy and Jobs – Annual Review 2025
records.geography: Global renewable-energy employment and supply-chain analysis, with attention to geographic concentration, workforce inclusion and public policy
records.boundary: This record treats renewable employment as a transition-distribution and geopolitical supply-chain signal. It is not respondent-level labor microdata, a causal evaluation of renewable policy, a complete accounting of job quality, or evidence that every new megawatt produces a fixed number of jobs.

records.title: Renewable deployment is accelerating, but technology and regional concentration shape who gains energy security
records.source_unit: International Renewable Energy Agency, Renewable Capacity Statistics 2026
records.geography: Global renewable power generation capacity, with regional and technology comparisons for 2016-2025 and detailed 2025 additions
records.boundary: This record adds a renewable-deployment route across capacity growth, technology concentration, regional inequality, off-grid systems, and energy security. It uses aggregate IRENA capacity statistics, not respondent-level energy histories, individual utility bills, plant-level operating records, causal forecasts, or proof that capacity growth produces equal affordability or security for every place.

records.title: Americans are using AI as a practical life infrastructure while fearing losses of purpose, agency and human connection
records.source_unit: Imagining the Digital Future Center at Elon University, Human Purpose in Peril national public-opinion poll
records.geography: United States adults, including large language model users and demographic subgroups
records.boundary: This record adds a public meaning-and-agency layer to the broader AI trend stream: Americans are adopting LLMs for learning, shopping, health, work, finance, housing and social rehearsal while worrying about purpose, connection, critical thinking, dependence and institutional guidance. It is a nationally representative U.S. adult survey with an LLM-user oversample, not a longitudinal behavioral study, clinical or economic outcome evaluation, or proof that AI causes social fragmentation.

records.title: AI and ageing are being framed as an inclusion and agency problem across health, economic security, participation and connectivity
records.source_unit: ITU, Artificial intelligence and ageing: Inclusive pathways for older persons in a digital world
records.geography: Older persons globally, with attention to age, gender, regional, affordability, skills, trust and connectivity differences
records.boundary: This record adds an ageing and digital-inclusion route linking AI to health, economic security, participation, connectivity, age and gender inequality, affordability, skills, trust, human support and institutional design. It is a global policy publication and practice synthesis, not a representative older-person survey, clinical or financial outcome study, causal AI evaluation, implementation inventory or proof that AI improves later-life wellbeing.

records.title: Basic internet access is expanding while quality, affordability, skills, and location continue to stratify meaningful digital participation
records.source_unit: ITU, Measuring digital development: Facts and Figures 2025
records.geography: Global, with income-group, gender, age, and urban-rural comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a global connectivity-to-digital-participation and unequal-optionality route. It is not respondent-level data, does not estimate individual online behavior or welfare, and does not establish that connectivity caused cultural, political, consumer, work, or trust outcomes.

records.title: Digital expansion is creating a material-recovery and environmental-health gap: e-waste grows faster than formal collection, while regulation strongly differentiates outcomes
records.source_unit: Global E-waste Monitor 2024, summarized by the International Telecommunication Union backgrounder on electronic waste and the circular economy
records.geography: Global e-waste generation, collection, recycling, materials and policy comparison
records.boundary: This record adds a digital-consumption-to-materials-and-health route: device expansion, e-waste, recovery, critical materials, emissions, regulation, worker safety and circularity are connected. It is a global aggregate monitor and policy synthesis, not device-level replacement behavior, household disposal data, a worker-health study, a causal regulatory evaluation or proof that formal recycling is environmentally sound in every case.

records.title: Connectivity is progressing globally, but affordability, usage, and network quality continue to divide digital participation
records.source_unit: International Telecommunication Union, Measuring Digital Development: The ICT Development Index 2026
records.geography: 159 economies compared on universal and meaningful connectivity, affordability, Internet use, and quality of connectivity
records.boundary: This record adds a global digital-infrastructure, affordability, quality, platform-participation, and institutional-capacity route. It uses an economy-level composite index and report synthesis, not respondent-level Internet diaries, individual transaction data, causal welfare estimates, or proof that connectivity automatically creates agency.

records.title: Child online protection is shifting from blocking risk toward building accessible reporting, help-seeking and referral pathways
records.source_unit: ITU and Office of the Special Representative of the Secretary-General on Violence against Children, Protection through Online Participation (PoP) Principles
records.geography: Global child online protection systems involving governments, industry, civil society, child helplines, academia and international organizations
records.boundary: This record adds a child-protection and digital-participation route linking online risk, child agency, reporting, help-seeking, support, referral, platform responsibility and public protection systems. It is global policy guidance, not an implementation inventory, incident prevalence estimate, child-level dataset, platform audit, service-quality evaluation or proof that online reporting produces safer outcomes.

records.title: Digital-system failure is being reframed as a cross-border cascade risk requiring analogue fallback, shared warning, and coordinated resilience
records.source_unit: International Telecommunication Union, United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction, and Sciences Po Paris School of International Affairs, When digital systems fail: An expert report on the hidden risks of our digital world
records.geography: Global digital infrastructure and the cross-border systems that depend on communications, energy, finance, transport, healthcare, emergency response, and government services
records.boundary: This record adds a digital-infrastructure and public-systems trend linking interdependence, cascade risk, service continuity, analogue fallback, unequal redundancy, early warning, trust, and international coordination. It is an expert report and scenario-based preparedness framework, not a forecast, incident census, respondent-level dataset, household impact estimate, causal evaluation, or proof that the proposed priorities produce equitable resilience.

records.title: Digital companies are expanding connectivity and AI capacity while emissions, electricity demand, and climate-accountability gaps remain material
records.source_unit: International Telecommunication Union and World Benchmarking Alliance, Greening Digital Companies 2026: Monitoring Emissions and Climate Commitments
records.geography: 200 digital companies worldwide assessed on greenhouse-gas emissions, energy consumption, climate commitments, and transition plans
records.boundary: This record adds a digital-company climate, energy, emissions, transition-plan, and public-accountability route. It uses company comparisons and disclosed aggregates, not user-level behavior, causal AI climate effects, complete lifecycle accounting, or proof that renewable procurement eliminates local environmental burdens.

records.title: Job flexibility changed intrahousehold work and care tradeoffs without uniformly improving child well-being
records.source_unit: 464 Dutch couples with children in combined LISS and Bilendi samples
records.geography: Netherlands; representative survey samples of couples with children
records.boundary: This comparative record adds a work-control-to-household-care route: parent-specific job flexibility can change market work, childcare, chores, household resources, and modeled child well-being, with different implications by parent and wage scenario. It does not establish a U.S. causal effect, durable worker autonomy, long-run child development, or universal welfare gains.

records.title: Biodiversity awareness rises faster than everyday conservation action, creating an intention–capability gap
records.source_unit: Japan Cabinet Office, Public Opinion Survey on Biodiversity, July 2026 survey; preliminary report published 25 September 2026
records.geography: Japan; national public-opinion survey of people aged 18 and over with 3,000 sampled Japanese citizens; preliminary results
records.boundary: This record adds an environmental-culture route from biodiversity awareness and willingness through consumer choice, learning, action barriers, and public-policy translation. It does not establish realized ecological outcomes, causal campaign effects, durable behavior, or that individual consumer action is sufficient for biodiversity conservation.

records.title: Japan's household confidence recovered modestly in August while durable-purchase timing improved beneath persistent price expectations
records.source_unit: Japan Cabinet Office Economic and Social Research Institute, monthly Consumer Confidence Survey, August 2026
records.geography: Japan; national household consumer-confidence survey
records.boundary: This record adds a Japan-specific household-perception and purchase-timing surface to the comparative consumer atlas. It does not establish realized purchases, household income or employment change, price-index inflation, financial stress, cultural preference, or causal effects.

records.title: Japan turns loneliness and isolation into a statutory, cross-government policy system, while delivery and lived outcomes remain open
records.source_unit: Japan Cabinet Office, Priority Plan to Facilitate the Promotion of Policies Regarding Measures to Address Loneliness and Isolation
records.geography: Japan; national and local government measures addressing loneliness and social isolation
records.boundary: This record adds a named national policy and legal route for loneliness and social isolation in Japan. It establishes statutory and planning architecture plus an open implementation pathway; it does not establish budget, local coverage, service quality, participant experience, reduced loneliness, improved health, work, belonging, or civic outcomes.

records.title: Rechargeable battery products are normalized consumer infrastructure while safety and end-of-life systems remain unevenly understood
records.source_unit: Japan Consumer Affairs Agency, FY2026 Consumer Awareness Survey No. 1: products using lithium-ion batteries, released 17 September 2026
records.geography: Japan; internet survey of 5,000 people aged 15 and over, quota-allocated by sex, age, and region to population composition, conducted 30 July–3 August 2026
records.boundary: This record adds a consumer-technology route from rechargeable-product adoption through age-stratified risk knowledge, price/safety tradeoffs, usage practices, disposal uncertainty, and municipal or take-back infrastructure. It does not establish actual accident rates, unsafe products, causal age effects, disposal compliance, or recycling outcomes.

records.title: Japan’s modeled household consumption falls in real terms while category and household-type exposure diverge
records.source_unit: Statistics Bureau of Japan Consumer Trend Index (CTI), July 2026, 2025-base revision
records.geography: Japan; all households, single-person households, two-or-more-person households, and ten major expenditure categories
records.boundary: This record adds a Japanese modeled consumption, price-pressure, category, and household-type layer. It does not establish household-specific spending, quantities, affordability, debt, income, cultural preference, or causal welfare effects; July 2026 values are revision-sensitive.

records.title: Japanese household consumption and worker income contract in real terms despite nominal stability
records.source_unit: Japan Statistics Bureau Family Income and Expenditure Survey, July 2026, two-or-more-person households
records.geography: Japan
records.boundary: This record adds a household-account layer beneath aggregate national spending and establishment sales. It does not isolate cultural or leisure categories in July, identify individual households, establish causality, measure one-person households, or prove that real consumption contraction equals reduced wellbeing.

records.title: Japanese online-shopping reach and ticket spending soften alongside household contraction
records.source_unit: Japan Statistics Bureau Survey of Household Economy, July 2026 expenditure-related results
records.geography: Japan
records.boundary: This record adds an observed household internet-shopping and ticket-channel layer to Japan's broader consumption and income contraction. It does not measure cultural attendance, household welfare, real expenditure, platform causality, or whether online substitution preserved access for households that stopped shopping online.

records.title: Israeli election salience fuses security, judicial relations, unity and identity while social confidence deteriorates
records.source_unit: Jewish People Policy Institute, Israeli Society Index, September 2026
records.geography: Israel; Jewish-sector and Arab-sector adult respondents as described by JPPI
records.boundary: This record adds a geopolitical-cultural legitimacy route: security, judicial relations, unity, identity, conflict attribution and education are interpreted together as election stakes, while Jewish-Arab, ideological and religiosity differences remain central. It uses a weighted monthly panel and mixed Jewish/Arab survey frames, not a probability sample with fully disclosed uncertainty; it does not establish objective conditions, causality, turnout, policy delivery, conflict outcomes or durable cohesion.

records.title: Climate pressure becomes a displacement and conflict risk through existing vulnerabilities, while mobility and social protection can also build resilience
records.source_unit: European Commission Joint Research Centre, Climate security, migration and fragility, 2026
records.geography: Global climate security, migration, displacement and fragility pathways, with policy implications for vulnerable places and communities
records.boundary: This record adds a climate-security and mobility mechanism: climate stress is treated as a risk multiplier whose effects depend on political, economic and social vulnerabilities, while mobility, remittances, shock-responsive social protection, safe pathways and inclusive urbanization can support resilience under effective institutions. It is a policy brief, not a global causal event study or evaluation of a specific program.

records.title: Citizen-authored futures connect resilience to agency, institutional capacity, and unresolved social trade-offs
records.source_unit: European Commission Joint Research Centre, Resilience: The future of Europe as seen by EU citizens, analyzed through the Our Futures initiative
records.geography: European Union; citizen-authored future narratives in all 24 official languages
records.boundary: This record is citizen-authored narrative and foresight evidence, not a representative public-opinion survey, forecast, or causal evaluation. It is useful for mapping perceived futures, cross-domain tensions, and agency; it does not establish population prevalence, policy preferences, realized resilience, or institutional performance.

records.title: Consumers are seeking more agency over algorithms, institutions, leisure, health, and local culture while adopting AI on their own terms
records.source_unit: Kantar MONITOR, Caught by the tides: the 2026 Consumer Trends and the desire to opt out
records.geography: Kantar consumer-trends synthesis across contemporary consumer, institutional, cultural, health, and technology contexts
records.boundary: This record adds a commercial consumer-culture signal about agency, opting out, active leisure, transparency, self-directed health, local cultural identity, and conditional generative-AI adoption. It is a public trend synthesis, not respondent-level data, a representative global survey, a causal study, or proof that consumers can equally exercise the agency described.

records.title: Wellbeing is becoming a consumer-led negotiation over affordability, trust, time, and control
records.source_unit: Kantar MONITOR, The Pursuit of Wellbeing: understanding the rise of consumer-led wellbeing
records.geography: Kantar MONITOR consumer-wellbeing synthesis with emphasis on contemporary consumer choices and institutional contexts
records.boundary: This record adds a consumer-wellbeing route across affordability, health behavior, institutional reliability, guidance, navigation burden, personalization, and AI agency. It is a commercial foresight synthesis, not a representative population-health survey, clinical evidence, causal study, or proof that consumer-led wellbeing reduces inequity or improves outcomes.

records.title: Migration becomes a projection surface for urban insecurity when weak state capacity leaves jobs, housing, services, and belonging politically unresolved
records.source_unit: Konrad-Adenauer-Stiftung Occasional Paper Series No. 2/2026, Migration, Rule of Law, and Social Cohesion in Urban South Africa: Xenophobic Mobilisation as a Challenge to State Capacity
records.geography: Urban South Africa, focused on Gauteng/Johannesburg/Pretoria with Cape Town as a comparative context
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative urban-cohesion route from unemployment, inequality, housing, services, migration, and institutional distrust through political attribution, xenophobic mobilisation, rule-of-law erosion, private claims to authority, and social fragmentation. It is a qualitative case analysis with cited statistics and event series, not a representative public-opinion study, a causal migration-impact estimate, or a general claim about South Africa or migrants.

records.title: Consumer life is becoming a verification and attention-management problem as choice, convenience, personalization, and AI compound
records.source_unit: Kearney Consumer Institute, The Tyranny of Too Much: Global Future Consumer Study 2026
records.geography: Consumers across 20 countries spanning the Americas, Europe, Middle East and Africa, and Asia Pacific
records.boundary: This record adds a forward-looking consumer route linking choice overload, verification work, performance-based trust, AI-mediated time, attention, and synthetic social connection. It is a Kearney commercial survey and foresight scenario, not a causal experiment, longitudinal time-use study, representative age distribution, clinical assessment, or realized 2036 forecast.

records.title: Kenya’s mobile-finance adoption is deepening while exclusion, debt distress, and consumer-protection risks remain
records.source_unit: Kenya National Bureau of Statistics, 2024 FinAccess Household Survey, with Central Bank of Kenya and Financial Sector Deepening Kenya
records.geography: Kenya; adults aged 18 years and older in conventional households, nationally and across rural/urban areas and all 47 counties, with sex, age, education, wealth, disability, and provider dimensions
records.boundary: This record adds a Kenya financial-consumer and digital-recourse layer to the cultural, social, and consumer atlas. It does not establish causal effects of mobile money, digital credit, regulation, poverty, product quality, or consumer welfare, and its outcomes use different conditional denominators.

records.title: Kenya’s mobile reach exceeds internet and household connectivity, with sharp rural and county gaps
records.source_unit: Kenya National Bureau of Statistics, Analytical Report on ICT based on the 2023/24 Kenya Housing Survey
records.geography: Kenya; individuals and households across all 47 counties, with rural/urban, sex, age, education, income, employment, disability, and county dimensions
records.boundary: This record adds a Kenya digital-access and household-connectivity layer to the cultural, social, and consumer atlas. It does not establish cultural use, online purchasing, platform effects, digital welfare, quality of service, or causal explanations for county and residence gaps.

records.title: Global health capacity is shaped by overlapping institutions, misaligned funding cycles, governance voice, and the burdens of transition—not only by available money
records.source_unit: KFF, Mapping the Global Health Landscape: Analysis of Fourteen International Organizations, September 2026
records.geography: Fourteen international organizations operating in or financing health work in low- and middle-income countries
records.boundary: This record adds a global-health institutional-capacity route linking governance voice, civil-society inclusion, overlapping mandates, technical assistance, financing cycles, eligibility, graduation, co-financing, and country sustainability. It is a descriptive institutional mapping, not an organizational performance evaluation, country-level outcome study, causal financing analysis, exhaustive global-health census, or proof that alignment alone improves health equity.

records.title: Ukrainians separate infrastructure endurance from leader trust: wartime resilience remains broad but legitimacy is conditional
records.source_unit: Kyiv International Institute of Sociology, August–September 2026 public-opinion releases
records.geography: Ukraine; adults living in government-controlled territory
records.boundary: This record adds a wartime geopolitical-state mechanism: civilians distinguish infrastructure endurance and national resistance from trust in the current leader, while direct exposure and institutional conduct condition the legitimacy of sacrifice. KIIS covers adults in government-controlled territory by mobile CATI during wartime; occupied territories and citizens abroad are excluded, and the scenario is hypothetical. The results do not measure outage behavior, military capacity, corruption itself, or causal effects.

records.title: Post-crisis adaptation is reorganizing AI expectations, practical consumption, identity, wellness, and cultural belonging
records.source_unit: Republic of Korea Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism, Korea’s Social and Cultural Trends in 2026: From Recovery to Adaptation
records.geography: South Korea; online discourse from Korean news, social media, online communities, and video platforms
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative cultural-consumer route from post-crisis adaptation through AI governance attention, individualized identity, practical consumption, wellness, K-culture, fandom, and emotional coexistence. It is a government trend forecast derived from online keyword analysis, not a representative public-opinion survey, behavioral panel, causal cultural evaluation, or proof of population-wide change.

records.title: South Korean leisure and group participation rebound while generalized social trust declines
records.source_unit: Statistics Korea, 2025 Social Survey: welfare, social participation, leisure, income and consumption, and labor
records.geography: South Korea; residents aged 13 or 19 and over depending on the module, with two-year comparisons to 2023
records.boundary: This record adds a South Korean leisure, cultural-participation, social-organization, trust, and loneliness layer. It does not establish causal recovery, spending, affordability, institutional legitimacy, group quality, cultural belonging, or a contradiction between participation and trust at the individual level.

records.title: Financial caution is reallocating discretionary life rather than stopping consumption: households cut everyday room and large purchases while preserving selected food, leisure, culture, and resale occasions
records.source_unit: KPMG UK, Consumer Pulse Q3 2026: Consumer confidence marginally improves, heading toward final quarter of 2026
records.geography: United Kingdom consumer households, with quarterly comparison and September 2026 outlook
records.boundary: This record adds a current UK consumer-behavior route from financial security and perceived economic decline through precautionary spending, job stickiness, social and cultural occasions, resale, channels, and big-ticket optionality. It is a sponsor-commissioned online survey and descriptive pulse, not verified transaction data, household-budget microdata, a causal consumption model, or a universal consumer trend.

records.title: Delivered mobile radars turn allied air-surveillance procurement into an integrated capability stage
records.source_unit: Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence account of AN/TPS-77 MRR radar delivery and integration
records.geography: Lithuania and NATO integrated air and missile defence system
records.boundary: This record establishes reported delivery and integration of AN/TPS-77 MRR radars into Lithuanian/NATO air-surveillance arrangements, plus a stated follow-on procurement plan. It does not establish acceptance, sustained availability, actual detections, response outcomes, deterrence, reduced civilian risk, or public consent.

records.title: Lithuania converts a Bolide/RBS-70 contract into reported air-defence delivery before firing readiness or protection is visible
records.source_unit: Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence account of Bolide missile delivery for the RBS-70 system
records.geography: Lithuania; Lithuanian Air Defence Battalion and RBS-70 short-range air-defence system
records.boundary: This record establishes a reported Bolide missile delivery for Lithuania's RBS-70 system, a €7 million delivery value, Saab Dynamics as manufacturer, and a broader supply contract. It does not establish quantity, acceptance, training, firing readiness, operational use, replenishment, interception, deterrence, civilian protection, or public legitimacy.

records.title: A Lithuania–Ukraine ammunition-factory investment creates an industrial option before construction, output, or jobs are visible
records.source_unit: Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence account of the DEMZ ammunition-factory investment contract
records.geography: Alytus and Prienai district, Lithuania; Lithuania–Ukraine defence-industrial partnership
records.boundary: This record establishes a reported Lithuania–Ukraine DEMZ investment contract to build an ammunition factory and a projected maximum of 450 jobs in Alytus and Prienai district. It does not establish contract value, construction, production, deliveries, actual jobs, supply substitution, readiness, local burden, or public legitimacy.

records.title: Lithuania turns Leopard 2A8 industrial strategy into named facility construction before output or readiness is visible
records.source_unit: Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence account of the Leopard 2A8 assembly and repair facility at Kaunas Free Economic Zone
records.geography: Kaunas Free Economic Zone, Lithuania; Lithuanian and German defense-industrial relationship
records.boundary: This record establishes a reported construction start for a named Leopard 2A8 assembly and repair facility, with stated investment and job targets. It does not establish completion, production, repair throughput, delivery, readiness, realized jobs, reduced external dependence, local effects, or public legitimacy.

records.title: Lithuania joins a multilateral surveillance procurement before national delivery and contribution are visible
records.source_unit: Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence account of Lithuania joining collective procurement of NATO next-generation surveillance aircraft
records.geography: Lithuania and participating NATO Allies; Alliance surveillance and early-warning architecture
records.boundary: This record establishes reported Lithuanian participation in a planned NATO GlobalEye collective procurement, the stated overall quantity/value and expected delivery window, and described surveillance functions. It does not establish a binding final contract, Lithuania-specific cost or quantity, aircraft delivery, acceptance, operation, industrial participation, deterrence, or public/civilian effects.

records.title: Lithuania and Norway turn a naval capability need into non-binding industrial cooperation before procurement is visible
records.source_unit: Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence account of the Lithuania–Norway standardized multirole warship cooperation memorandum
records.geography: Lithuania and Norway; Lithuanian Navy, Norwegian standardized vessel programme, and Lithuanian maritime/defence industry
records.boundary: This record establishes a reported Lithuania–Norway maritime-capability MOU, a four-ship requirement, a planned Lithuanian industrial share, and modular capability intent. It does not establish a binding procurement contract, financing, construction, delivery, acceptance, operational use, realized local content or jobs, reduced dependence, deterrence, maritime safety, or public legitimacy.

records.title: Defense-industrial funding creates a regional production option before output or readiness is visible
records.source_unit: Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence account of an EU-selected RSI Europe and Odin Defence project
records.geography: Panevėžys district, Lithuania; Estonia and European defense-industrial supply chains
records.boundary: This record establishes a reported EU funding selection, named industrial partners, planned Panevėžys expansion, and stated supply-chain and regional-capacity rationale. It does not establish grant disbursement, facility operation, jobs, production, delivery, accepted capability, readiness, deterrence, civilian protection, or realized regional benefit.

records.title: Lithuania moves SkyFortress from Ukrainian test-system adoption into planned deployment before detection performance is known
records.source_unit: Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence account of SkyFortress test-system deployment
records.geography: Lithuania; national airspace-surveillance and counter-drone system
records.boundary: This record establishes a reported plan to install and test a named Ukrainian SkyFortress airspace-surveillance system in Lithuania. It does not establish installation completion, validated performance, operational integration, warning or interception, civilian protection, deterrence, or public legitimacy.

records.title: Lithuania converts a Spike LR2 contract into reported warehouse receipt before stockpile readiness or deterrence is visible
records.source_unit: Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence account of Spike LR2 missile receipt
records.geography: Lithuania; Lithuanian Armed Forces warehouses and Vilkas Infantry Fighting Vehicle force
records.boundary: This record establishes a reported July 2026 Spike LR2 warehouse receipt, an implemented contract valued above €3 million, and a platform link to Vilkas vehicles. It does not establish quantity, acceptance, training, maintenance, readiness, use, replenishment, deterrence, civilian protection, or public legitimacy.

records.title: Lithuania moves Switchblade 600 capability from procurement into reported warehouse receipt before use or deterrence is visible
records.source_unit: Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence account of the first Switchblade 600 shipment
records.geography: Lithuania; Lithuanian Armed Forces warehouses; United States–Lithuania defense-supply relationship
records.boundary: This record establishes a reported first shipment of Switchblade 600 systems and associated support equipment reaching Lithuanian Armed Forces warehouses. It does not establish quantity, acceptance, training, deployment, operational use, deterrence, adversary response, civilian protection, or public legitimacy.

records.title: Lithuania and Ukraine turn drone and electronic-warfare cooperation into a planned joint venture before production is visible
records.source_unit: Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence account of Pekkla UAB and December One RND UAV/EW cooperation
records.geography: Lithuania and Ukraine; Pekkla UAB and December One RND Ltd; planned Lithuanian joint venture
records.boundary: This record establishes a reported Letter of Intent between Pekkla UAB and December One RND, a planned Lithuanian joint venture, and a stated 2027 production aim for UAV components and electronic-warfare systems. It does not establish binding formation, technology transfer, testing, production, delivery, operational use, realized resilience, jobs, or public legitimacy.

records.title: Health misinformation creates an unequal practical-judgment gap between information exposure, confidence, and safe care decisions
records.source_unit: London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, Health Misinformation: Public Perceptions of Threat to the UK, based on Survation survey
records.geography: United Kingdom adults aged 18+; national online-panel survey conducted 9–10 September 2026
records.boundary: This record adds a health-information, practical-judgment, and institutional-trust layer. It uses an online-panel survey of 2,110 UK adults and self-reported exposure, confidence, regret, and known harms; it does not verify misinformation, clinically confirm outcomes, establish causality, estimate population prevalence beyond the sample design, or evaluate an intervention.

records.title: Malaysia approaches universal mobile and internet access while device and place gaps remain
records.source_unit: Department of Statistics Malaysia, ICT Use and Access by Individuals and Households Survey Report 2025
records.geography: Malaysia; household ICT access and individual ICT use, including urban-rural and sex comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a Malaysian digital-access and device-configuration layer. It does not establish online shopping, content preferences, digital skills, service quality, affordability, frequency, or causal urban-rural, sex, or device effects.

records.title: AI-informed audience development converted surrounding footfall into modestly higher cultural visitation at a Maltese arts centre
records.source_unit: Peer-reviewed study of AI-powered footfall monitoring, non-visitor surveys, and audience-development intervention at Spazju Kreattiv, Malta's National Centre for Creativity
records.geography: Valletta, Malta; Spazju Kreattiv and surrounding public spaces
records.boundary: This record adds a named cultural-venue episode connecting AI-assisted measurement of non-visitors to human outreach and a venue-level visitation change. It does not establish causal algorithmic impact, equitable participation, revenue, repeat engagement, belonging, or generalizability beyond Spazju Kreattiv.

records.title: AI is shifting work from a replacement debate toward job redesign, rapid relearning, trust, and a weaker traditional employment bargain
records.source_unit: ManpowerGroup, The Human Edge: Global Future of Work Trends 2026
records.geography: Workers and employers across 41 countries, with global future-of-work trend synthesis
records.boundary: This record adds a commercial future-of-work route across AI job redesign, hybrid teams, skills, training access, burnout, trust, contingent work, workforce aging, degrees, and mentorship. It uses ManpowerGroup surveys, cited external evidence, and vendor trend interpretation, not raw respondent-level ingestion, a complete global labor-market census, causal AI displacement or productivity estimates, an independent audit of employer claims, or proof that the recommended workforce strategies improve worker welfare.

records.title: Conscious consumption is moving from stated intention toward circular commerce when affordability, durability, trust, and access make the lower-impact choice practical
records.source_unit: Mastercard Economics Institute, The Next Era of Conscious Consumption, 2026, with Global Financial Sentiment Study and GlobeScan Healthy and Sustainable Living inputs
records.geography: Global consumer and spending frame, with comparisons across markets, generations, categories, and the United States
records.boundary: This record adds a consumer-culture and circular-commerce route across affordability, durability, trust, values, resale, rental, repair, reuse, digital access, and spending behavior. It combines Mastercard aggregated and anonymized spending analysis with partner survey and sustainability research, not respondent-level ingestion, a representative global consumer panel, a causal sustainability estimate, a complete lifecycle analysis, or proof that circular adoption improves welfare or environmental outcomes uniformly.

records.title: Small-business growth is being redefined as controlled momentum under cost, uncertainty, and digital-fragmentation pressure
records.source_unit: Mastercard-sponsored Hypothesis survey of more than 6,000 small and medium-sized businesses across 18 countries, with regional comparisons and report synthesis
records.geography: United States, Latin America, Europe, Middle East and Africa, and Asia Pacific; small and medium-sized businesses across 18 countries
records.boundary: This record adds a global firm-side and business-infrastructure pathway linking uncertainty, controlled growth, digital fragmentation, cybersecurity, and regional variation. It does not measure audited SME performance, survival, employment, household incidence, or causal effects of Mastercard or any specific tool.

records.title: Youth culture is shifting from audience consumption toward co-creation, micro-communities, and AI-mediated agency
records.source_unit: Mastercard, The Next Growth Generation: Winning with Gen Z and Gen Alpha
records.geography: 18 global markets across Europe, the Americas, Africa, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific; Gen Z and Gen Alpha-family perspectives
records.boundary: This record adds a youth-culture route across identity, fandom, creators, micro-communities, AI-mediated agency, household influence, and projected economic power. It is a sponsor-produced strategic research report, not a representative longitudinal youth panel, a causal estimate of platform or AI effects, proof of universal Gen Z or Gen Alpha behavior, or evidence that cultural co-creation is equally accessible.

records.title: Consumer value is being recalculated through AI-mediated discovery, measurable wellness, experiences, and resourceful low-waste spending
records.source_unit: McKinsey & Company, State of the Consumer 2026: When tech acceleration and cost pressures collide, 22 June 2026
records.geography: Consumer trends in Brazil, France, Germany, the United Kingdom, and the United States, with global market and category context
records.boundary: This record adds a publisher consumer-research signal about AI-mediated discovery, health and wellness measurement, experience spending, and resourceful consumption under cost pressure. It uses aggregate survey and market synthesis, not respondent-level ingestion, a representative global consumer panel, causal health evidence, household budget diaries, or proof that any business response will work.

records.title: Most people feel connected, but global loneliness is uneven and cannot be inferred from connection alone
records.source_unit: Meta-Gallup, The Global State of Social Connections
records.geography: 142 countries and areas, with national, age and gender comparisons; fieldwork June 2022-February 2023 and report published 2023
records.boundary: This record adds a social-connection and public-health infrastructure layer: most people report feeling connected, but loneliness is substantial, uneven and partly distinct from social contact, with young adults reporting more loneliness than older adults. The evidence is representative survey data collected in 2022-2023 and published in 2023, not current 2026 monitoring, a social-network trace, longitudinal causal analysis or proof of health or resilience effects.

records.title: Indian retail journeys are becoming social, creator-led, conversational, and omnichannel, with platform data connecting discovery to offline purchase
records.source_unit: Meta and Retailers Association of India, India omnichannel shopping whitepaper findings
records.geography: India retail consumers, brands, creators, and online/offline commerce journeys
records.boundary: This record adds an India retail signal on social discovery, short-form video, creators, WhatsApp, online/offline research, and platform-linked omnichannel measurement. It is based on a Meta newsroom summary of a Meta-RAI whitepaper and contains company-reported platform and campaign measures; it is not an independent national survey, a causal evaluation, a complete retail-market census, or proof that platform-attributed conversion reflects durable consumer welfare.

records.title: Mexico’s internet access is expanding and rural gaps are narrowing, but device, age, and territorial inequalities remain
records.source_unit: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Geografía (INEGI), ENDUTIH 2025
records.geography: Mexico; people aged 6 and over and private households, with national, urban-rural, state, age, and Indigenous self-identification dimensions
records.boundary: This record adds a Mexican digital-access, device, age, minority-identification, and state-variation layer. It does not establish digital skills, online consumer behavior, service quality, affordability, causal rural or state effects, or Indigenous group access rates.

records.title: Mexican household spending recovers in aggregate while education, culture, and recreation remain distributionally constrained
records.source_unit: INEGI Encuesta Nacional de Ingresos y Gastos de los Hogares, ENIGH 2024
records.geography: Mexico
records.boundary: This record adds a direct household-budget and distributional layer to the Mexico and Latin America consumer-culture comparison. It does not measure real-time 2026 behavior, unique cultural attendance, platform use, causal preference formation, or whether spending increases produced greater subjective well-being. The broad education-and-recreation and specific education/esparcimiento measures use different reference periods and should remain separate.

records.title: Mexico's cultural participation is broad but sharply stratified by age, education, disability, and Indigenous-language status
records.source_unit: INEGI MODECULT 2025 Module on Selected Cultural Events
records.geography: Mexico; national population aged 12 years and above, with urban comparison for selected events
records.boundary: This record adds Mexican cultural-participation evidence with explicit disability, Indigenous-language, age, education, event-type, and active-creation gradients. It does not identify causal barriers, final individual-level trajectories, price or transport mechanisms, or direct comparison with pre-2025 waves because the 2025 instrument expanded coverage and concepts. Source-dependence audit 2026-09-30: the companion MODECULT 2025 record uses the same survey wave; overlapping estimates are not independent corroboration.

records.title: Mexican cultural participation rebounds but remains stratified by age, education, identity, time, cost, and digital form
records.source_unit: INEGI Módulo sobre Eventos Culturales Seleccionados, MODECULT 2025
records.geography: Mexico
records.boundary: This record adds direct cultural participation, barrier, artistic-agency, organizer, and online-consumption evidence to the Mexico household-spending and Brazil/Canada retail layers. The comparable 2016-2025 adult series covers 32 large urban areas, while the redesigned 2025 indicators cover people aged 12+ nationally; these universes must not be merged. The record does not measure cultural quality, identity formation, causal access barriers, spending amounts, or long-run social outcomes. Source-dependence audit 2026-09-30: the companion MODECULT 2025 record uses the same survey wave; overlapping estimates are not independent corroboration.

records.title: Snacking is becoming a flexible food, social, and emotional infrastructure balancing convenience, health, indulgence, and connection
records.source_unit: Mondelēz International, 2026 State of Snacking, developed with Mintel and Black Swan Data
records.geography: Selected global markets across North America, Latin America, Europe, Asia, and Australia; market-specific survey bases vary
records.boundary: This record adds a food-culture and consumer route linking snacking to social connection, meal substitution, time pressure, health intentions, sensory novelty, nostalgia, and emotional reward. It uses a branded commercial trend study with market-specific surveys and social listening, not nationally pooled dietary surveillance, nutritional assessment, causal health evidence, food-insecurity measurement, or a globally representative estimate.

records.title: A distant conflict is reorganizing domestic safety judgments, identity boundaries, speech restraint, and interfaith cohesion even as most Britons reject a simple partisan side
records.source_unit: More in Common, Caught between sides: Britons' shifting attitudes to the Israel-Palestine conflict and its consequences at home
records.geography: United Kingdom, with polling and focus-group evidence on conflict attitudes, Jewish and Muslim safety, media exposure, identity, and community cohesion
records.boundary: This record adds a geopolitical-to-domestic-cultural route: international conflict salience can shape identity judgment, perceived safety, media exposure, speech restraint, platform accountability, and interfaith-cohesion expectations. It does not establish direct causation, a complete hate-crime count, actual platform behavior, migration or exit, household economic effects, or durable community breakdown.

records.title: Britons want open disagreement but lack trusted spaces and confidence to practice it
records.source_unit: More in Common and University College London, Disagreeing Well research
records.geography: Britain, with polling and focus-group evidence on political disagreement, identity conflict and civic forums
records.boundary: This record adds a civic-culture layer: people may value disagreement and understanding while withholding views, avoiding difficult topics and lacking trusted spaces in which to practice political conversation. It is a Britain-focused polling and focus-group synthesis with incomplete public sample details, not a representative longitudinal panel, behavioral trace, causal polarization study or proof that new forums would improve democratic outcomes.

records.title: Nature becomes a cross-party source of pride, place attachment, and electoral accountability
records.source_unit: More in Common with the National Trust, RSPB, WWF, Woodland Trust, and Wildlife Trusts, Strong Roots: the role of nature in uniting voter coalitions
records.geography: Great Britain; national survey and swing-voter focus groups
records.boundary: This is commissioned survey and focus-group evidence about political meaning, place attachment, and environmental attitudes. It does not establish realized conservation, willingness to pay, project-level local acceptance, household affordability, emissions behavior, vote change, or policy implementation.

records.title: Migration control signalling can improve the appearance of state control while weakening integration, service capacity, and public trust
records.source_unit: Migration Policy Institute Europe, Beyond Control Signalling: Designing integration policies for better outcomes and public trust, July 2026
records.geography: High-income immigrant-destination countries, with European examples and comparative evidence on migration, integration, housing, education, labor markets, and public trust
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative migration-governance route from public anxiety and control signalling through housing, language, family, labor, service capacity, community voice, integration, and trust. It is a policy synthesis using heterogeneous country cases and cited studies, not a pooled causal estimate, a representative global opinion survey, an implementation evaluation, or proof that any recommended policy improves outcomes.

records.title: Browser choice screens can weaken defaults, with effects depending on platform rollout
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35112; browser market-share data around the European Union Digital Markets Act choice-screen mandate
records.geography: European Union digital-market regulation; iOS and Android browser markets
records.boundary: This record adds an observed regulation-to-default-switching pathway in a comparative digital market. It does not establish U.S. generalization, privacy or security improvement, informed consent, durable consumer welfare, or broader platform exit. Choice-screen exposure, browser use, actual switching, understanding, and downstream data outcomes remain separate stages.

records.title: Better information about loan prices can change search, negotiation, and borrowing decisions
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35605, randomized consumer-credit trial conducted with Chile's financial regulator using administrative loan data
records.geography: Chile consumer-credit market; 112,063 loan seekers in the regulator-linked randomized trial
records.boundary: This comparative record measures belief updating, search, negotiation, interest rates, and loan take-up in Chile. It does not establish a U.S. effect, lower total borrowing cost, improved repayment, or better household financial security.

records.title: Cookie-consent interface friction changes data-sharing choices and time cost
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34025; field experiment randomizing cookie-consent banners plus structural analysis of site-specific and browser-level consent
records.geography: Comparative online consumer and website setting; policy and interface experiment
records.boundary: This record adds an interface-friction and repeated-attention-cost mechanism to the platform/data lane. It does not establish informed consent, actual privacy protection, U.S. population generalization, downstream fraud or welfare, or durable platform exit.

records.title: Household preferences about women's employment can shift after direct work experience
records.source_unit: Comparative NBER Working Paper 34969, randomized household job-assignment experiment in Bangladesh
records.geography: Bangladesh; rural households in the randomized employment experiment, retained as comparative cultural evidence rather than a U.S. estimate
records.boundary: This comparative record tests the malleability of household preferences about women's employment in Bangladesh. It does not establish U.S. gender norms, a universal cultural mechanism, long-run employment, household safety, political mobilization, or causal transferability across labor and institutional settings.

records.title: Beliefs about crashes can push some investors out of markets and concentrate risk among those who remain
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35708, more than two decades of respondent-level investor surveys linked to option-implied market benchmarks
records.geography: Investor survey respondents and financial markets; the public abstract does not fully specify the geographic frame
records.boundary: This comparative market-participation record measures beliefs, participation proxies, and asset-price relationships. It does not establish a U.S.-household wealth effect, individual causality, retirement adequacy, or a universal reason why people enter or leave financial markets.

records.title: Elite club membership can open a route to political office when personal networks matter
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35611, historical family-level records on Buenos Aires Jockey Club membership and legislative office
records.geography: Buenos Aires, Argentina; historical elite families and legislative careers
records.boundary: This comparative record measures an association between historical elite social-club membership, network position, and legislative office in Buenos Aires. It does not establish a contemporary U.S. effect, prove a single causal mechanism, measure ordinary club participation, or show whether office produced representative governance, public trust, or durable democratic inclusion.

records.title: Microenterprise credit can create customer surplus beyond the borrowing firm
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35729 randomized evaluation of large loans to microenterprises in Chile, with treated firms, customer surveys, and a market comparison of more than 125,000 non-treated firms
records.geography: Chile; comparative international evidence used to test a firm-credit-to-consumer-welfare mechanism, not a U.S. estimate
records.boundary: This comparative record adds a credit-to-firm-to-customer-welfare pathway. It does not establish a U.S. consumer effect, a universal microenterprise-credit result, worker benefit, durable firm survival, or long-run inequality change.

records.title: Universal childcare can have long-run maternal work and fiscal effects beyond preschool years
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35514; Quebec universal subsidized childcare program and long-run maternal labor, earnings, benefit, and tax outcomes
records.geography: Quebec, Canada; comparative policy evidence for U.S. childcare and work-capacity analysis
records.boundary: This comparative record adds a long-run childcare-to-career-and-fiscal-persistence mechanism. It does not establish a U.S. policy effect, universal access, care quality, child wellbeing, maternal time satisfaction, or a causal cultural or political response.

records.title: Social-media restrictions can erode when compliance is socially costly
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35162; Australian teenagers surveyed after the national under-16 social-media account restriction
records.geography: Australia; comparative mechanism test for U.S. youth-platform policy
records.boundary: This comparative record shows a policy-to-compliance-to-social-norm mechanism in an Australian youth-platform setting. It does not establish U.S. compliance, mental-health benefit, school effect, family burden, privacy improvement, durable exit, or political legitimacy.
