Formal restriction, actual behavior, peer norms, wellbeing, and later action remain separate stages.

records.title: Integrity norms can weaken without continued enforcement even in a low-corruption setting
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35756, universe-level Singapore housing transactions linked to public-official status, planned MRT stations, enforcement changes, and survey measures
records.geography: Singapore public officials, their relatives, housing transactions, MRT planning, and anti-corruption enforcement
records.boundary: This comparative record measures information-linked housing transactions, enforcement response, and survey/model evidence about integrity norms in Singapore. It does not establish a contemporary U.S. effect, a universal relationship between norms and corruption, or direct citizen legitimacy and political outcomes.

records.title: Network feasibility may require removing a constrained node rather than relaxing one link
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35757, a theoretical graph model of spectrum repacking, station buyouts, and pairwise engineering waivers
records.geography: Conceptual spectrum-market and network-design mechanism; no observed U.S. auction or station outcome sample
records.boundary: This record adds a network-remedy-design mechanism: local link-by-link relaxation can miss node-level complementarity. It does not establish a realized spectrum remedy, consumer benefit, broadcaster outcome, market concentration effect, or U.S. policy success.

records.title: Rewarding buyer feedback can increase sales and signal seller quality in an online marketplace
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 22584; Taobao reward-for-feedback mechanism and online-marketplace seller outcomes
records.geography: China's Taobao online marketplace; comparative platform evidence for a U.S.-centered mechanism atlas
records.boundary: This record adds comparative platform evidence: buyer-feedback rewards on Taobao were associated with higher sales and higher-quality sellers. It does not establish a U.S. effect, consumer welfare, review accuracy, return recovery, or that rewards improve every marketplace.

records.title: Coffee remains a daily household routine while specialty, app, drive-through, and out-of-home formats diversify the consumption occasion
records.source_unit: National Coffee Association, 2026 National Coffee Data Trends Fall Report media highlights, conducted by Dig Insights
records.geography: United States adult coffee and beverage consumption, June 2026 field period
records.boundary: This record adds an everyday-consumption and consumer-channel signal linking routine, specialty differentiation, at-home and out-of-home occasions, drive-through and app convenience, and retail-channel movement. It is a trade-association summary of a commissioned cross-sectional survey, not respondent-level ingestion, transaction data, a longitudinal trend estimate, a causal model, a measure of household affordability, or proof of durable cultural change.

records.title: Global streaming is making local-language stories, cross-border discovery, recurring franchises, and broad genre choice part of one increasingly connected entertainment system
records.source_unit: Netflix, What We Watched: The First Half of 2026, Netflix Engagement Report
records.geography: Global Netflix viewing from January through June 2026 across Netflix members and available titles
records.boundary: This record adds Netflix's platform-engagement signal on global viewing scale, local-language breakout, franchise reactivation, and genre/format breadth. It uses company-reported aggregate viewing data, not respondent-level data, a quality or satisfaction measure, a complete entertainment-market census, or proof that platform visibility equals cultural influence.

records.title: Consumer protection is shifting from formal legal awareness toward practical rights knowledge, mediated advice, and successful recourse
records.source_unit: New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment and Commerce Commission, New Zealand Consumer Survey 2026
records.geography: New Zealand; nationally weighted adults aged 18 and over, with consumer-protection and dispute-resolution implications
records.boundary: This record adds a consumer-rights-to-recourse route from formal legal awareness through usable knowledge, mediated information, problem action, resolution, and regulator trust. It does not establish legal comprehension, causal AI effects, equal remedy access, or the fairness and durability of reported resolutions.

records.title: New Zealand cultural participation rises while active creation falls and digital tools reshape production
records.source_unit: Manatū Taonga Ministry for Culture and Heritage, New Zealanders’ Cultural Participation in 2025, Verian survey research
records.geography: New Zealand; adults aged 18 years and over, with selected age, ethnicity, creator, and volunteer comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a New Zealand cultural audience/creator/digital/volunteer layer. It does not establish causal access effects, creator earnings, AI productivity, copyright outcomes, cultural quality, wellbeing impact, or representative subgroup trajectories beyond the survey’s weighted online-panel frame.

records.title: New Zealand domestic travel is socially motivated and culturally selective, with cost, health, and weather limiting future trips
records.source_unit: New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment Domestic Visitor Survey, October 2025 wave
records.geography: New Zealand; population-representative domestic visitors and planned domestic travellers, weighted to 2023 Census age, gender, region, and ethnicity
records.boundary: This record adds a New Zealand domestic-mobility, cultural-activity, social-motivation, and travel-cost layer. It does not establish household-level affordability, regional distribution, cultural meaning, Māori community benefit, causal travel effects, or booked/completed future trips.

records.title: New Zealand visitor recovery reaches near-pre-pandemic spend while travel purpose and market composition shift
records.source_unit: New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment International Visitor Survey, year ending June 2026 release
records.geography: New Zealand; international visitors aged 15+ excluding foreign-fee-paying students, with market and travel-purpose breakdowns
records.boundary: This record adds an international mobility, visitor-spend, purpose, and cultural-experience layer. It does not establish household consumer trends, regional distribution of tourism benefits, local cultural-sector income, visitor causality, environmental impact, or Māori community outcomes.

records.title: A fiscally improving recovery can still feel constrained when inflation, energy and fixed budgets redistribute room
records.source_unit: New Zealand Treasury, Pre-election Economic and Fiscal Update 2026, 29 September 2026
records.geography: New Zealand; national household, labor-market, energy-price, tax, public-spending and fiscal forecasts
records.boundary: This record identifies a macro-to-household, energy-inflation, fiscal-capacity and public-service operating-pressure subtheme. It does not establish that New Zealand households will experience a particular welfare change, that forecast surpluses will improve services, that inflation will produce a specific distributional effect, or that geopolitical energy shocks will occur; those require realized price, wage, debt, service, budget, regional and household episodes.

records.title: Citizens’ assemblies are being institutionalized as a way to bring time, information, civic lottery, and deliberation into democratic decisions beyond elections
records.source_unit: newDemocracy Foundation, Democracy Beyond Elections: A Handbook on Citizens' Assemblies, second edition, produced with UNDP and UN Democracy Fund support
records.geography: Global deliberative-democracy practice, with examples of citizens’ assemblies addressing climate change, constitutional reform, and other major public decisions
records.boundary: This record adds a democratic-institution signal linking civic lottery, time, information, deliberation, representation, agency, trust, policymaking, and institutional follow-through. It is a practical handbook and practice synthesis, not a representative public-opinion dataset, respondent-level ingestion, causal evaluation, or proof that citizens’ assemblies produce trusted or equitable outcomes in every setting.

records.title: AI is becoming an entertainment-discovery interface for younger audiences faster than trust in its answers is consolidating
records.source_unit: Nielsen Gracenote, TV Search and Discovery in the AI Era, reported in Nielsen News Center, 8 April 2026
records.geography: United States entertainment search and discovery among AI-chatbot users ages 13-79, with Gen Alpha findings limited to ages 13 and 14
records.boundary: This record adds a Nielsen Gracenote signal about AI-powered entertainment search, Gen Alpha discovery, utility-versus-trust tradeoffs, verification, and metadata infrastructure. It is aggregate survey and publisher systems analysis, not respondent-level ingestion, a representative sample of all Gen Alpha, a recommendation-quality audit, a child-safety assessment, or proof of cultural influence.

records.title: German consumer sentiment improves through income expectations while willingness to buy remains depressed and willingness to save stays high
records.source_unit: Nuremberg Institute for Market Decisions, NIM Consumer Climate powered by GfK, Consumer Climate Improves, August 2026
records.geography: Germany’s private consumers and household economic expectations
records.boundary: This record adds a Germany-specific consumer-sentiment route from income and economic expectations through saving precaution, major-purchase hesitation, and the gap between sentiment and realized consumption. It uses aggregate index evidence, not respondent-level records in the corpus, household budgets, transaction data, or causal welfare estimates.

records.title: Consumer recovery is cautious: households protect essentials, seek income insurance and demand lived value across local and digital commerce
records.source_unit: NIQ, Consumer Outlook: Guide to 2026
records.geography: Global consumers and FMCG markets, with NIQ consumer survey, retail measurement and omnishopper evidence across multiple countries and market groups
records.boundary: This record adds a global consumer-economy layer linking household caution to essential spending, secondary income seeking, inflation, geopolitical concern, category demand, brand trust, cultural localization and omnichannel commerce. It synthesizes NIQ surveys and market measurements, not respondent-level ingestion, a complete household expenditure panel, causal welfare evidence or proof that reported intentions become realized purchases.

records.title: Global consumers are switching between premium and value modes as trust and perceived payoff determine what earns a place in the basket
records.source_unit: NIQ and World Data Lab, A Tale of Two Consumers: The polarized mindsets reshaping global consumption
records.geography: Global FMCG markets with consumer-class, generational, regional, and United States comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a global consumer-culture route from inflation and unequal spending power through situational premiumization, trade-down, trust, identity, convenience, private label, generational influence, and regional divergence. It is a commercial publisher synthesis combining surveys, shopper and market data, and modeled projections; it is not a probability household panel, causal welfare analysis, or proof that reported value perceptions produce realized health, cultural, or financial outcomes.

records.title: Global consumption is polarising between selectively justified upgrades and tightly managed value choices, putting the mainstream middle under pressure
records.source_unit: NIQ and World Data Lab, A Tale of Two Consumers: The Polarized Mindsets Reshaping Global Consumption
records.geography: Global fast-moving consumer-goods markets, with mature Western markets and emerging Asia-Pacific, Latin America, and Africa comparisons; 2021–2026 observations and 2026–2036 projections
records.boundary: This record adds a global consumption and market-structure route across inflation, selective upgrading, trading down, premiumisation, private label, cultural relevance, income mobility, and regional consumer growth. It uses NIQ survey, price, shopper, and consumption analysis plus World Data Lab projections, not individual household budgets, respondent-level purchase histories, causal welfare estimates, nutrition outcomes, or proof that commercial consumer classes map cleanly onto social classes in every country.

records.title: Demographic, labour, economic, and geopolitical transitions are territorially uneven, making place-based capacity more important than national averages
records.source_unit: Nordregio, State of the Nordic Region 2026, Nordic Council of Ministers Report 2026:2
records.geography: The Nordic Region: Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, the Faroe Islands, Greenland, and Åland; analysis at Nordic, national, regional, municipal, and cross-regional levels
records.boundary: This record adds a place-based Nordic capacity route across population change, ageing, migration, urbanisation, labour-market vulnerability, regional economies, critical infrastructure, green innovation, and territorial governance. It uses Nordregio’s comparative regional synthesis, indicators, maps, and projections, not a single causal index, household panel, individual wellbeing measure, service-quality audit, or proof that Nordic regional patterns generalize to the United States.

records.title: Household water behavior is structured by routine, dwelling equipment, and deprivation rather than conservation preference alone
records.source_unit: Northern Ireland Department for Infrastructure / Northern Ireland Statistics and Research Agency, Household Water Usage in Northern Ireland 2025/26
records.geography: Northern Ireland private households and adults, with settlement, local-government-district, and deprivation-quintile comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a place-based household-consumption route from water routines and household equipment through time, infrastructure, deprivation, and environmental adaptation. It does not measure metered volumes, water bills, conservation effectiveness, health, appliance efficiency, causal deprivation effects, or a longitudinal response to drought or policy. Household and individual denominators are kept separate.

records.title: Retreat from moderation shifts information risk toward users and under-resourced local trust networks
records.source_unit: Northwestern University Roberta Buffett Institute and Center for Communication & Public Policy, Global Disinformation in a Post-Moderation World synthesis report, published 10 September 2026
records.geography: Global information ecosystems, with examples from the United States, Taiwan, Ukraine, and Spanish-language communities
records.boundary: This record adds an information-governance route from platform and government retreat through attention, trust, local distribution capacity, AI-enabled influence, provenance, and public coordination. It is a symposium synthesis and expert interpretation, not a representative survey, causal evaluation, exposure estimate, or proof that any proposed accountability arrangement will work.

records.title: Norwegian citizens distinguish usable public services from weak influence, administrative trust, and confidence in automated decisions
records.source_unit: Norwegian Agency for Public and Financial Management (DFØ), Innbyggerundersøkelsen 2026 (Citizen Survey 2026)
records.geography: Norway; national citizen survey with municipal and national public-service modules, using weighted results and repeated 2010-2025 trend tables
records.boundary: This record adds a Norwegian comparative public-service, political-voice, and public-sector-AI trust route. It uses official weighted survey tables and repeated cross-sectional comparisons, not respondent-level longitudinal data, observed service outcomes, causal explanations, or evidence that AI has been deployed and evaluated in these services.

records.title: Norwegian cultural participation is stabilizing unevenly: libraries recover while cinema and theatre remain below earlier levels
records.source_unit: Statistics Norway Cultural Barometer 2025
records.geography: Norway; representative population survey of physical and digital cultural participation
records.boundary: This record adds repeated, representative cultural-participation evidence from Norway. It supports venue-specific post-pandemic stabilization, age differences, and unmet-demand barriers, not a causal pandemic effect, universal cultural recovery, price elasticity, digital substitution, or individual-level persistence.

records.title: Norway's immigrant-background cultural participation is institutionally uneven: libraries and museums are strong while concerts and theatre lag
records.source_unit: Statistics Norway, Cultural use by people with an immigrant background 2025
records.geography: Norway; immigrants and Norwegian-born people with two immigrant parents aged 9 and older
records.boundary: This record adds subgroup-specific cultural participation, unmet demand, and barrier evidence from Norway. It does not establish assimilation, discrimination, causal access barriers, cultural preference, household welfare, or individual-level persistence.

records.title: Community knowledge is frequently gathered without gaining policy power, creating capacity and evidence loops that weaken climate, nature, and social-justice delivery
records.source_unit: New Philanthropy Capital, Green Alliance, and ACEVO, Together for a fairer, greener future: Collective leadership in a time of crisis
records.geography: United Kingdom, with a focus on communities experiencing inequality, civil-society organizations, environmental and social-justice leaders, funders, policymakers, and access to nature
records.boundary: This record adds a community-power route from lived experience, local legitimacy, and unequal environmental exposure through organizational capacity, evidence standards, policy influence, shared governance, usable access to nature, and trust. It is a UK deliberative and qualitative report, not a prevalence survey, comparative causal evaluation, community-representative sample, or proof that its proposed collaboration model improves outcomes.

records.title: Young people experience digital life as both community infrastructure and an inescapable system of platform control, surveillance and harm
records.source_unit: Nuffield Foundation and Ada Lovelace Institute, I love it, but I hate it: Young people's experiences and expectations of growing up digital
records.geography: United Kingdom; peer research across Dundee, Shetland, Islington and Sandwell, spanning rural, urban and suburban contexts
records.boundary: This record adds a UK comparative lived-experience layer: digital connection is simultaneously community infrastructure and an inescapable system of platform control, surveillance, harm and unequal exposure. It is peer-led qualitative research with 49 young people, not a prevalence survey, representative estimate, behavioral trace, clinical assessment, legal finding or causal evaluation of regulation, platform design or youth governance.

records.title: Young people face a fragmented mental-health support system whose age thresholds, service silos and geography leave need ahead of access
records.source_unit: Nuffield Foundation, ‘Higgledy piggledy’: Systems of support for young people aged 14–24 with poor mental health
records.geography: United Kingdom, with prevalence and service-access analysis focused on England and youth insights from England, Scotland and Northern Ireland
records.boundary: This record adds a UK comparative system-level layer: rising reported need is not matched by seamless support, and young people navigate age thresholds, professional silos, geography, informal networks and digital front doors. It combines secondary prevalence and administrative data with youth/practitioner insight; it is not a respondent-level dataset, systematic review, clinical evaluation, representative causal study or proof that any single factor caused the prevalence trend.

records.title: Humanitarian need is becoming a system-capacity problem as conflict and climate shocks expand while funding cuts close essential services
records.source_unit: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, Global Humanitarian Overview 2026
records.geography: Global humanitarian needs and response capacity across major regions, conflict-affected communities and populations exposed to climate and disaster shocks
records.boundary: This record adds a humanitarian-system capacity layer: conflict and climate shocks create needs, but funding and delivery capacity determine whether health, food, protection, cash, water and shelter lifelines continue. It combines OCHA/UN planning estimates and system descriptions; it does not establish individual receipt, service adequacy, causal funding effects or durable recovery.

records.title: Adolescent well-being is diverging by gender and shaped across family, school, community, and digital environments
records.source_unit: OECD, Enhancing adolescent social and emotional well-being
records.geography: Cross-national OECD analysis of adolescent social and emotional well-being, gender differences, norms, and supportive environments
records.boundary: This record adds an adolescent culture and well-being route linking gender norms, identity, family communication, school engagement, community space, digital environments, mental health, and public support systems. It uses publication-level cross-national aggregate and self-report evidence, not clinical records, respondent-level causal histories, platform trace data, or claims that any single environment causes an outcome.

records.title: AI can widen the scale and accessibility of citizen participation while introducing new exclusion, civic-space, trust, and vendor-dependence risks
records.source_unit: OECD, Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Citizen Participation: Typology of Applications, Opportunities and Challenges for Democratic Innovation
records.geography: OECD member and partner countries; desk research and 50 AI citizen-participation use cases across 22 countries
records.boundary: This record adds a technology-to-democracy route across AI-assisted participation design, interpretation, translation, facilitation, scale, civic space, exclusion, trust, skills, procurement, and vendor dependence. It uses OECD desk research and 50 public use cases, not respondent-level records, representative participation estimates, individual political histories, causal estimates of AI on turnout or trust, proof of policy influence, or evidence that every AI deployment has the same effects.

records.title: AI-enabled employment support is being designed to move minimum-income beneficiaries from unstable entry jobs toward sustainable career progression
records.source_unit: OECD, AI and Digitalisation for Employment Support in Belgium and Greece: New Tools to Support Minimum Income Beneficiaries, 24 September 2026
records.geography: Belgium and Greece; Minimum Income Scheme beneficiaries, public employment services, social workers, counsellors, employers, and local/regional service institutions
records.boundary: This record adds an AI-mediated employment-service route from administrative data and job matching through career progression, job quality, agency, safeguards, and social legitimacy. It does not establish causal AI effects, universal transition rates, algorithmic fairness, realized implementation, or that recommendations create quality jobs where labour demand is weak.

records.title: AI-market dynamism coexists with concentration in hardware and data that may entrench incumbent strategic advantage
records.source_unit: OECD, Artificial Intelligence markets: Recent developments and competition issues, July 2026
records.geography: Global AI value chains and competition-policy systems, with sector and value-chain implications across economies
records.boundary: This record adds a firm-sector and market-structure route linking AI value-chain layers, concentration, competition, cost structures, strategic advantage, innovation, and public-interest oversight. It is not a firm-level market-share estimate, a consumer-price estimate, a labor-market causal study, or respondent-level microdata analysis.

records.title: AI adoption is constrained by skills while raising the premium on high-level, data and human capabilities
records.source_unit: OECD policy brief, AI and skills: What we know so far
records.geography: OECD countries and selected employer, SME and manager survey comparisons, with evidence on manufacturing, finance, algorithmic management and generative-AI use
records.boundary: This record adds an AI-workplace and skills layer linking adoption barriers to high-level, digital, data, managerial and human skills, training, algorithmic management, worker voice and job quality. It synthesizes OECD survey evidence, not respondent-level ingestion, causal training evaluation, complete labor-market measurement, wage evidence or proof of future displacement.

records.title: The social economy is becoming a market institution: inclusion depends on who controls scale, finance and impact
records.source_unit: OECD, Powering ASEAN's economy through inclusive business: From the margins to markets, OECD Local Economic and Employment Development Papers 2026/14, September 2026
records.geography: ASEAN Member States and Southeast Asia, with illustrative cases from Indonesia, Malaysia, Viet Nam, Cambodia, the Philippines and Thailand
records.boundary: This record identifies an emerging social-economy and inclusive-market subtheme. It does not establish that inclusive businesses or social enterprises reduce poverty, improve job quality, widen affordable service access, expand social protection, preserve community control, or maintain mission through scale; those require longitudinal beneficiary, worker, customer, price, quality, finance, governance and impact data.

records.title: Child-safety rules are common on paper, but systematic age assurance remains rare across online services
records.source_unit: OECD Age assurance practices of 50 online services used by children, service-level public-information benchmark
records.geography: 50 online services used by children; services operate across jurisdictions and the report compares publicly stated policies and practices rather than country populations
records.boundary: This record adds a service-level implementation and cross-border governance route to the child-digital lane. It does not establish that any service is safe or unsafe, identify individual children, evaluate age-assurance accuracy, or resolve the privacy and inclusion trade-offs of stronger verification.

records.title: Children's digital access is near-universal, while platform activity and safety risks make protection, empowerment, and child voice institutional problems
records.source_unit: OECD How's Life for Children in the Digital Age?, cross-national synthesis of PISA, HBSC, and PIRLS data
records.geography: OECD countries, with indicators using the report's specified international country subsets and survey years
records.boundary: This record adds a child digital-access, activity, exposure, and institutional-protection route distinct from the UNICEF abuse/reporting record and the broader adult social-connection and internet-wellbeing records. It does not diagnose children, estimate platform causality, or treat device time as a standalone harm measure.

records.title: Citizen participation is moving from consultation rhetoric toward a governance-capacity test: influence requires timing, institutional skill, feedback, and a place in the policy cycle
records.source_unit: OECD, Citizen Participation for Better Cohesion Policy: Insights from 11 Pilot Initiatives, OECD Public Governance Reviews, 2026
records.geography: Eleven local-authority and civil-society participation pilots across seven European Union countries: Belgium, France, Italy, Poland, Romania, the Slovak Republic, and Spain
records.boundary: This record adds a citizen-participation, cultural-access, local-governance, institutional-capacity, trust, and policy-cycle route. It uses public pilot synthesis, not respondent-level ingestion, a representative population survey, a randomized causal estimate of participation, proof of equal inclusion, or proof that recommendations were implemented and produced durable social outcomes.

records.title: Climate concern is broad but policy support depends on perceived effectiveness, economic security and fair distribution of transition burdens
records.source_unit: OECD, Taking the temperature on climate change and on just transition policies: Public sentiment in OECD countries
records.geography: Working-age adults in 27 OECD countries, using OECD Risks that Matter survey waves and reviewed international evidence
records.boundary: This record adds a climate-politics and social-legitimacy signal linking climate concern to policy support, economic security, household and worker exposure, perceived norms, communication, compensation and fair burden sharing. It is descriptive public-attitudes evidence from OECD countries and reviewed studies, not a causal evaluation, behavioral forecast, or proof that compensation produces durable support.

records.title: Digital finance is widening access while scams, wallets, payment products, and complaint routing become central consumer-protection risks
records.source_unit: OECD, Consumer Finance Risk Monitor 2026
records.geography: Financial consumer-protection authorities and financial-services markets across 60 jurisdictions, including banking, payments, credit, insurance, investment, and pensions
records.boundary: This record adds a consumer-finance market-to-protection route linking digital payments, fraud, product design, unequal exposure, complaint routing, supervision, and redress visibility. In this source, respondents are public authorities and ministries, not individual consumers; the record is not respondent-level household data, individual victimization, causal loss, completed remedy, or proof that complaint increases mean worsening harm.

records.title: Financial consumer risk is shifting from product choice toward digital exposure, scam vulnerability, and the ability to obtain remedy
records.source_unit: OECD Consumer Finance Risk Monitor 2026, based on reporting from financial authorities in 60 jurisdictions
records.geography: 60 jurisdictions worldwide, representing 107 government ministries and financial authorities; risk comparisons by income level and financial product sector
records.boundary: This record adds a global consumer-power route from macroeconomic and digital change through scams, financial exclusion, product detriment, complaints, supervisory coordination, and possible remedy. It is a jurisdiction-authority assessment synthesized by OECD, not a population prevalence study, consumer panel, transaction record, causal evaluation, or proof that regulatory responses restored losses or trust.

records.title: Critical-risk governance is shifting toward anticipatory, whole-of-society preparedness, but learning, accountability and international coordination lag
records.source_unit: OECD, Tracking Progress in the Governance of Critical Risks
records.geography: 34 OECD countries adhering to the OECD Recommendation on the Governance of Critical Risks
records.boundary: This record adds a governance and geopolitical-risk signal: states are broadening risk frameworks toward compound threats, anticipatory planning, whole-of-society participation and critical dependencies, while accountability, learning, preparedness investment and cross-border cooperation lag. It is a comparative governance review, not a causal evaluation of resilience, a forecast of a specific crisis or proof that formal arrangements translate into public safety.

records.title: Cross-border payment access can fail through cost, delay, opacity, and weak tracking even when a transfer channel exists
records.source_unit: OECD, Transparency in retail cross-border payments and remittances
records.geography: Global retail cross-border payment and remittance systems under the G20 Roadmap for Enhancing Cross-border Payments
records.boundary: This record adds a financial-consumer infrastructure route across cross-border payments, remittances, fees, currency conversion, delivery time, status tracking, terms, access, interoperability, and regulatory accountability. It uses OECD policy analysis and guidance, not individual transfer histories, household budgets, provider-level causal estimates, corridor-specific harm estimates, or proof that disclosure produces comprehension, successful delivery, or household recovery.

records.title: Online commerce is expanding while manipulative choice architecture turns consumer autonomy, privacy, and cancellation into market risks
records.source_unit: OECD consumer-policy evidence on dark commercial patterns and digital consumer vulnerability, including preliminary 2024 survey findings across 20 countries
records.geography: OECD countries; survey and prior e-commerce detriment estimates use their specified country samples
records.boundary: This record adds a consumer-choice, interface-design, privacy, time, and recourse route distinct from rental scams and financial-fraud records. It does not measure one person's purchase, prove a tactic caused loss, establish platform intent or liability, or treat online exposure as universal harm.

records.title: Generative AI can improve educational task performance without producing learning unless pedagogy, teacher agency, infrastructure, and trust keep cognitive work visible
records.source_unit: OECD, Digital Education Outlook 2026: Exploring Effective Uses of Generative AI in Education
records.geography: OECD education systems and comparative international evidence on teachers, learners, educational technology, infrastructure, and governance
records.boundary: This record adds a digital-education route across teacher use, task performance, durable learning, academic integrity, teacher agency, infrastructure, privacy, safety, and equity. It uses OECD survey indicators, emerging research synthesis, and policy framing, not respondent-level student histories, individual learning trajectories, causal AI effects, classroom observation files, or proof that any tool improves learning in every setting.

records.title: Government AI adoption is widespread, but operational accountability, procurement, evaluation, and user feedback lag
records.source_unit: OECD Digital Government Outlook 2026, chapter Adopting and governing AI in government
records.geography: 36 OECD countries in the 2025 OECD Survey on Digital Government 3.0; Germany and the United States were not available for the 2025 DGI measures
records.boundary: This record adds a government-AI adoption and accountability route connecting public-sector deployment, procurement, skills, guardrails, transparency, impact evidence, and user feedback. It does not measure individual respondents, algorithmic performance, causal effects, or the quality of any country's specific AI system.

records.title: Digital government is advancing faster than joined-up service capacity, leaving access, trust, and accountability dependent on implementation
records.source_unit: OECD Digital Government Outlook 2026
records.geography: OECD member and partner-country comparative digital-government indicators and case evidence; country coverage varies by indicator and year
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative route from digital-government infrastructure and AI adoption through service reachability, cross-agency coordination, rights access, feedback, trust, and accountability. It is a secondary comparative public-report synthesis, not respondent-level analysis, an administrative service-outcome evaluation, a causal estimate, or proof that digitalisation improves welfare or equity.

records.title: Digital-market conduct increasingly sits between competition and consumer law, making agency and coordinated redress central
records.source_unit: OECD, Competition and consumer policy in digital markets, OECD Roundtables on Competition Policy Papers No. 332
records.geography: Comparative digital-market policy and enforcement systems across OECD and partner jurisdictions
records.boundary: This record adds a digital-market consumer-agency and institutional-redress route linking personalization, interfaces, pricing, switching, competition, trust, and enforcement coordination. It is not a consumer complaint microdata analysis, individual purchase panel, platform experiment, or causal estimate of consumer harm.

records.title: Digital transformation is increasingly governed as an investment, infrastructure, and public-capability problem rather than a technology-adoption problem alone
records.source_unit: OECD, Investment Policy Framework for Digital Transformation
records.geography: OECD policy and investment context, with country examples from Morocco, Uzbekistan, and Viet Nam
records.boundary: This record adds an investment-governance and digital-capability route distinct from the OECD digital-government AI-adoption record. It is not firm-level investment data, does not estimate local infrastructure or household effects, and does not establish that foreign investment produces digital inclusion, worker power, public-service improvement, or geopolitical leverage.

records.title: Geopolitical energy disruption converts global interdependence into uneven household, business, and inflation exposure
records.source_unit: OECD Economic Outlook, Interim Report March 2026: Testing Resilience
records.geography: Global and G20 economies, with country comparisons across advanced and emerging economies and specific household-energy exposure analysis
records.boundary: This record adds an official macro-to-household pathway linking geopolitical conflict, energy and fertiliser dependence, inflation, growth, sectoral exposure, AI productivity, labour demand, and fiscal buffering. It does not provide respondent-level data, a causal household-welfare estimate, a political-opinion measure, or a forecast that remains valid if conflict and energy conditions change.

records.title: Teacher shortages expose education as a social-infrastructure and status bargain
records.source_unit: OECD, Education at a Glance 2026: OECD Indicators, 2026
records.geography: OECD countries and partner economies, with detailed teacher-shortage indicators for participating education systems
records.boundary: This record identifies teacher supply as a social-infrastructure and status problem: unequal staffing, working conditions, public recognition, demographic change and labor-market competition shape the stability of education access. It is comparative indicator and survey evidence, not causal proof that any single salary, AI, second-career or reallocation policy improves learning, retention, equity or social trust.

records.title: Headline labour resilience masks widening place-based differences in jobs, wages, skills, and bargaining conditions
records.source_unit: OECD, OECD Employment Outlook 2026: Geographic Disparities in Jobs and Incomes
records.geography: OECD countries, subnational regions, workers, households, firms, and local labour markets
records.boundary: This record adds a place-based labour-market route across headline resilience, real wages, young entry, structural shocks, skills, non-compete constraints, and employment policy. It uses OECD aggregate indicators, regional analysis, and report synthesis, not respondent-level employment histories, individual wage panels, private employer files, causal AI displacement estimates, or proof that a policy works uniformly across places.

records.title: OECD labour markets remain resilient in aggregate while regional job gaps, slowing real-wage recovery, weak mobility, and employment-control practices divide opportunity

records.boundary: This record adds an OECD labour-market and regional-opportunity lens on employment resilience, real wages, geographic gaps, mobility, skills, non-competes, and bargaining power. It uses aggregate cross-country and regional evidence, not individual job histories, causal wage estimates for every worker, household budgets, or proof that AI caused current youth or regional outcomes.

records.title: Locally rooted social-economy organizations are becoming delivery infrastructure for care, housing and community resilience as affordability gaps widen
records.source_unit: OECD and European Union, Social Economy in Europe: Contributing to Competitiveness and Prosperity

records.boundary: This record adds an institutional-delivery mechanism: housing and care affordability pressures create room for non-profit, limited-profit and cooperative organizations to function as locally rooted infrastructure, but their capacity depends on public framework conditions, finance, procurement and accountability. records.title: Agricultural productivity can expand food supply and farm income while fertilizer shocks, unequal capacity, diet change, and emissions keep food security exposed

records.boundary: This record adds a global agricultural-production, fertilizer-shock, farm-income, diet, emissions, trade, and food-security route. It uses OECD-FAO model projections and aggregate market analysis, not household food diaries, individual farm histories, causal price estimates, or proof that production growth delivers affordable healthy diets.

records.title: Aging, nonstandard work, and technology are changing who finances social protection and who is covered
records.source_unit: OECD, Financing of Social Protection, published 9 September 2026

records.boundary: This record adds an aging-and-work-to-social-protection-financing route linking care, pensions, health, long-term care, labor income, self-employment, technology, taxes, and public budgets. records.title: Strong national well-being can coexist with an intergenerational gradient in work, mental health, and social connection
records.source_unit: OECD, Well-being along the life course in Finland: Implications for forward-looking policy design

records.boundary: This record adds a comparative advanced-economy route showing how strong aggregate well-being can coexist with age-specific labor, mental-health, loneliness, gender, and fiscal pressures. records.title: Food is being used as low-stigma social infrastructure linking affordability, culture, public space, and belonging
records.source_unit: OECD, Promoting Social Connectedness Through Food

records.boundary: This record adds a food-access-to-social-infrastructure route. It is not a causal evaluation of shared meals, a representative consumer survey, a measure of household food consumption, or proof that food-based initiatives can replace income support, housing, healthcare, or durable public social infrastructure.

records.title: Preparedness is a global public good with a domestic budget problem
records.source_unit: OECD, Tracking spending on prevention, preparedness and response to global health threats, 24 September 2026

records.boundary: This record identifies a global-health-financing, preparedness and measurement subtheme. It does not establish that any particular spending level, aid reduction, tracker or domestic-financing reform will cause an outbreak, prevent one, improve health outcomes, strengthen sovereignty, or distribute protection equitably; those require named country, institution, workforce, household and outbreak episodes with observed budgets, capabilities, delivery, access and political response.

records.title: Digital transformation is becoming an economy-wide social system whose trust, well-being, and distributional effects need new measurement
records.source_unit: OECD, The OECD Going Digital Measurement Roadmap 2026

records.boundary: This record adds a measurement-and-governance route linking digital economic value, platform work, data flows, AI, well-being, digital divides, privacy, consumer protection, information integrity, trust, and statistical infrastructure. It is a policy roadmap, not respondent-level digital behavior data, a causal impact study, a platform audit, or proof of any specific online harm.

records.title: Housing exclusion is a layered pathway shaped by poverty, housing markets, institutional transitions, relationships, health and hidden forms of insecurity
records.source_unit: OECD, What is driving homelessness and housing exclusion in OECD and EU countries? A review of the literature and cross-national data

records.boundary: This record adds a housing and household-security signal linking homelessness and housing exclusion to poverty, housing affordability, eviction, institutional transitions, relationships, health, employment, social support and measurement visibility. It is a literature review and cross-national survey synthesis, not a harmonized current prevalence census, a single causal model, or a direct evaluation of any housing policy.

records.title: Employment transitions depend not only on jobs but on the public-service systems that match, train, protect, and reach people through shocks

records.boundary: This record adds a public-employment-service route across institutional variation, digital maturity, shock response, migrant transitions, social-economy partnerships, and labor-market resilience. records.title: Health-system inclusion is moving from formal coverage toward effective, equitable, and financially protected care

records.boundary: This record identifies a regional health-system transition from formal coverage toward effective, equitable, and financially protected care. records.title: City growth can coexist with concentrated opportunity gaps, making inclusion a productivity, mobility, and legitimacy problem

records.boundary: This record adds a comparative within-city opportunity and implementation layer to the urban-capacity route. records.title: Opportunity remains patterned by family background, education, gender, and place, making mobility a cumulative systems outcome

records.title: Energy shocks are being absorbed by supply substitution and reserves, but renewed inflation and depleted buffers narrow household and policy room

records.title: International student mobility is becoming a negotiated package of affordability, housing, work rights, family life, and post-study belonging
records.source_unit: OECD, International Student Mobility: Factors for Attraction and Retention, published September 11, 2026

records.boundary: This comparative record adds a cultural-mobility and institutional-capacity route from international education through affordability, housing, work rights, family life, integration, labor supply, and post-study retention. records.title: Rapid economic and human-capital gains can coexist with fragile youth transition, high work pressure, loneliness, gender barriers, and declining trust

records.boundary: This record adds a growth-to-lived-well-being and life-course-distribution route. records.title: Place identity is being operationalised as soft infrastructure for economic renewal, belonging, and local legitimacy

records.title: Paraguay's social-protection reach is tied to financing design, informality, and whether contributory and non-contributory systems can connect

records.boundary: This record adds a consumer-culture mechanism linking sentiment, household room, cost pressure, housing and job concerns, and protected festive occasions. It does not establish realized spending, household welfare, debt, social connection, or causality; several reason figures use routed subgroups without disclosed bases.

records.title: Health is becoming a continuous consumer practice spanning food, routines, data, devices, services and trusted human guidance
records.source_unit: PwC Voice of the Consumer 2026, The rise of everyday health
records.geography: 21,808 adults across 27 countries and territories, surveyed February-March 2026
records.boundary: This record adds a consumer-health and platformization route linking daily routines to wellness spending, data, devices, AI, diagnostics, coaching, pharmacies, trust and affordability. It is a commercial survey and market-insight publication, not clinical evidence, verified purchasing data, a representative population-health study, a causal evaluation or proof that consumerized health improves outcomes.

records.title: News consumption is moving toward social video and personality-led platforms while trust and verification remain contested
records.source_unit: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, Digital News Report 2025
records.geography: 48 markets across six continents, with specific United States and cross-market comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a cross-market news-platform, trust, creator, and AI-mediation route. It is based on published aggregate survey estimates, not a local respondent-level analysis; it does not establish individual persuasion, voting effects, misinformation exposure, creator influence, platform causality, or institutional legitimacy.

records.title: Platform-mediated news is becoming the default encounter while attention, trust, and civic interpretation fragment
records.source_unit: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism, Digital News Report 2026
records.geography: 48 international news markets, with age, platform, political, and trust comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a platform-mediated encounter-to-trust-and-attention route. It is not passive behavioral telemetry, an algorithmic causal study, an individual political-action panel, or a claim that news exposure caused voting, protest, polarization, or belief change.

records.title: Global publics feel the world worsening but still want cooperation that delivers security, aid and results
records.source_unit: Rockefeller Foundation and Focaldata, Seeking Security and Opportunity in a Stormy World: A 34-Country Survey
records.geography: 34 countries across wealthier and developing economies, with regional and country comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a public geopolitical-legitimacy layer: worsening world perceptions coexist with demand for cooperation, security, aid and demonstrable results, while leadership preference shifts toward coalitions and middle powers rather than automatic U.S. or Chinese primacy. It is a commissioned cross-national public-opinion survey with country medians and an information treatment, not observed foreign-policy behavior, aid allocation, institutional performance or causal geopolitical change.

records.title: Cultural institutions are being reframed as civic infrastructure whose funding, governance, and invisible labor shape social resilience and public legitimacy
records.source_unit: Salzburg Global, Creating Futures: Rethinking Cultural Institutions, Infrastructure, and Investment, September 2026
records.geography: Cultural institutions, funders, policymakers, and creative-economy actors from more than 25 countries
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural-infrastructure route from civic meaning and institutional funding through sovereignty, representation, trust, invisible labor, and public-system coordination. It is a curated international convening and prototype publication, not representative cultural-sector opinion, causal evaluation, budget data, worker panel data, or proof that proposed tools improve equity or resilience.

records.title: A more transactional international order and thinner public capacity are turning trust, foresight, and AI literacy into core state capabilities
records.source_unit: Salzburg Global, Our Key Insights: Public Institutions Responding to a New Era: Strategy in a Transformed Global Landscape, September 11, 2026
records.geography: International public-sector strategy discussion with regional perspectives from Europe, North America, and developing-country contexts
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative geopolitical-institutional route from a more transactional global order and thinner public capacity through state expertise, private dependence, AI literacy, distributed foresight, inclusion, and trust. It is a curated expert synthesis, not representative public opinion, a causal evaluation of state capacity, or proof that any proposed capability improves outcomes.

records.title: Saudi cultural participation is broad at the event level but concentrated in everyday public and commercial spaces
records.source_unit: General Authority for Statistics Household Culture and Entertainment Survey 2024
records.geography: Saudi Arabia; individuals aged 15 years and above, Saudi and non-Saudi residents
records.boundary: This record adds direct cultural-participation evidence from Saudi Arabia, distinguishing attendance, active practice, venue mix, reading, and everyday leisure. It does not establish causal effects of Vision 2030, equal access, affordability, frequency, quality, or cultural meaning; the 2024 English publication is a cross-sectional self-report survey.

records.title: Scottish democratic legitimacy combines durable voting norms with low perceived influence, weakened institutional trust, and economic insecurity gradients
records.source_unit: Scottish Government, Scottish Social Attitudes Survey 2025: Core Module
records.geography: Scotland; nationally representative survey of adults aged 16 and over
records.boundary: This record adds a Scotland-specific legitimacy route connecting economic insecurity, social trust, institutional fairness/listening, political-expression channels, perceived influence, and durable voting norms. It is a representative survey of attitudes, not an audit of government performance, a causal model of trust, a turnout estimate, or proof that participation changes policy.

records.title: High average well-being and social cohesion coexist with unequal participation, mental-health pressure, and a reliability crisis in government
records.source_unit: Sociaal en Cultureel Planbureau, Sociale en Culturele Ontwikkelingen 2026
records.geography: The Netherlands, with European comparisons using European Social Survey round 11 (2023)
records.boundary: This record adds a national public-sector social-condition route across well-being, participation, social trust, mental-health pressure, inequality, and citizen-government reliability. It uses published aggregate and subgroup survey results plus European comparisons, not raw respondent-level data, clinical diagnoses, individual political histories, causal policy evaluation, or a claim that Dutch results generalize to every country.

records.title: High average quality of life in the Netherlands coexists with stacked inequalities, participation pressure, mental-health strain, and fragile institutional trust
records.source_unit: Netherlands Institute for Social Research (SCP), Social and Cultural Developments 2026
records.geography: Netherlands; national social conditions, participation, social cohesion, and citizen-government relations, with European comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a national social-and-cultural conditions lens on quality of life, participation, stacked inequality, mental health, identity, discrimination, social cohesion, and trust in government. It uses aggregate and survey-based comparative evidence, not individual case histories, a causal model, a representative measure of every subgroup, or a claim that participation or trust has one universal cause.

records.title: Peaceful, just, and inclusive institutions are under pressure as conflict, polarization, distrust, and weak representation make development gains more fragile
records.source_unit: OHCHR, UNDP, UNICEF, and UNODC, SDG 16 Global Progress Report 2026
records.geography: Global SDG 16 indicator and country case-study frame, with examples from countries including Panama, Ghana, and Benin
records.boundary: This record adds a global public-institutions route across conflict, justice, legal identity, violence, discrimination, representation, institutional resilience, official statistics, and reform pathways. It uses a UN-produced publication synthesis and selected country case studies, not respondent-level ingestion, a causal institutional-performance model, a complete country panel, or proof that the highlighted reforms generalize everywhere.

records.title: AI is becoming a peace-and-security capability and a source of geopolitical competition faster than multilateral institutions are adapting
records.source_unit: Security Council Report, Artificial Intelligence, Geopolitics, and the UN Security Council, 15 September 2026
records.geography: International peace and security, UN Security Council agenda, states, firms, and AI supply chains
records.boundary: This record adds an AI-to-peace-and-security route from dual-use capabilities and strategic inputs through cyber, information, military, legal, and multilateral-governance consequences. It is a policy analysis, not a capability test, conflict forecast, incident attribution, legal ruling, or proof that AI causes any particular geopolitical outcome.

records.title: Social and economic rights fulfillment is measured against feasible capacity, exposing delivery gaps that GDP alone hides
records.source_unit: University of Connecticut Social and Economic Rights Empowerment Initiative, 2026 International SERF Index update
records.geography: Up to 200 countries, with separate low/middle-income and high-income assessment standards and sex-disaggregated rights indicators
records.boundary: This record adds a rights-based delivery-versus-capacity measurement layer across health, education, food, housing, and work. It does not provide respondent-level data, a causal policy evaluation, a single comparable score for all countries, or proof that benchmark attainment means universal rights enjoyment.

records.title: Workplace culture is becoming a measurable operating system of strategy, decision rights, and relationships
records.source_unit: SHRM 2026 Global Workplace Culture Report and Workplace Culture Navigator framework
records.geography: 25 countries across six continents, including the United States, United Kingdom, Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, Colombia, Egypt, France, Germany, India, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, Mexico, Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, South Africa, South Korea, Spain, Thailand, Turkey, and United Arab Emirates
records.boundary: This record adds a global organizational-culture and work-control layer. It is a publisher-produced cross-national worker study with limited public methodological detail, not respondent-level ingestion, an independent audit, a causal evaluation of culture types, proof that culture overrides labor institutions or geography, or evidence that organizational culture alone determines worker wellbeing or performance.

records.title: Singapore uses a cultural credit and multicultural funding route to convert non-attenders into arts audiences
records.source_unit: Singapore Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth SG Culture Pass and Multicultural Arts Programme statements; National Arts Council Population Survey on the Arts 2023 results
records.geography: Singapore
records.boundary: This record adds Singapore evidence on cultural credit reach, audience development, multicultural policy, and the distinction between physical attendance, digital consumption, and active practice. The Culture Pass figures are early administrative and stated-interest signals, not a causal program evaluation; the arts survey is cross-sectional and the childhood-exposure comparison is associational. The record does not establish redemption, repeat attendance, spending displacement, cultural belonging, or equal access by income, disability, migrant status, or neighborhood.

records.title: AI becomes a local-business discovery gateway, but consumer trust moves the decision into a cross-channel verification loop
records.source_unit: SOCi, 2026 Local Discovery Index
records.geography: United States; consumers researching local businesses
records.boundary: This record adds a local consumer-discovery route: AI increases discovery reach but shifts trust and conversion into a cross-channel verification loop involving search, reviews, social media, maps, and direct business information. It does not establish causal effects on sales, verify AI errors, observe individual journeys, or represent a probability sample; the research is vendor-sponsored and directional.

records.title: Global social progress is approaching a turning point as rights decline and gains in health, housing, information, and environmental quality stall or reverse
records.source_unit: Social Progress Imperative, 2026 Global Social Progress Index
records.geography: 171 countries covering more than 99% of the world’s population, with country and regional comparisons from 2011-2025
records.boundary: This record adds a global social-progress route across rights, health, safety, environmental quality, water, sanitation, housing, information, education, inclusion, opportunity, and the limits of GDP as a progress measure. It uses a composite index and publisher interpretation, not a causal political-economy model, respondent-level lived-experience data, a complete within-country distributional account, or proof that rights decline causes every other component to worsen.

records.title: South Africans value science while unequal access, trusted channels and resource costs constrain participation
records.source_unit: South African Public Relationship with Science (SAPRS) 2022 Survey Results
records.geography: South Africa; nationally representative adults aged 16 and older
records.boundary: This record adds a science-legitimacy and participation mechanism: high perceived promise and moderate trust coexist with low active information consumption and resource-sensitive engagement. It is a 2022 nationally representative survey disseminated through later reports and 2026 public discussion; it does not establish current 2026 levels, causal effects, scientific literacy, or realized institutional inclusion.

records.title: South Africa’s payments remain cash-heavy for volume while cards carry higher-value transactions across income groups
records.source_unit: South African Reserve Bank, Payments Study Report 2023, combining Survey of Consumer Payment Choice and Diary of Consumer Payment Choice
records.geography: South Africa; adults aged 18 years and older, with nationwide payment diaries, income-group, province, demographic, and payment-method dimensions
records.boundary: This record adds a South African payment-choice and transaction-diary layer to the cultural, social, and consumer atlas. It does not establish causal payment substitution, cultural spending, merchant behavior, financial welfare, or representativeness beyond the documented survey design.

records.title: South Africa's cultural and household structure is becoming more multilingual, multiracial, religiously diverse, and less formally married
records.source_unit: Statistics South Africa, Cultural Dynamics in South Africa, Census 2022 thematic report 03-01-84
records.geography: South Africa
records.boundary: This record adds South African census evidence on cultural identity, language, household composition, religion, and marriage structure. It does not measure interpersonal trust, discrimination, cultural attendance, consumer behavior, household welfare, or causal social cohesion; census categories and comparability across waves require care.

records.title: South Africa's digital access is widespread but mobile-first and sharply uneven across provinces
records.source_unit: Statistics South Africa, General Household Survey 2025
records.geography: South Africa; private households across all nine provinces and residents in workers' hostels
records.boundary: This record adds South African evidence on mobile-first digital access, provincial infrastructure inequality, household structure, food access, and social-grant coverage. It does not measure cultural participation, digital frequency, data prices, device quality, platform use, or causal household welfare effects.

records.title: South African real retail demand grows with category-specific food, clothing, and general-dealer contribution
records.source_unit: Statistics South Africa P6242.1 Retail Trade Sales, July 2026
records.geography: South Africa
records.boundary: This record adds a South African real retail and category-demand layer to the Japan household contraction, Great Britain channel shift, and U.S. aggregate-spending records. It does not measure household welfare, online behavior, cultural attendance, inequality of access, or causal category demand.

records.title: South African volunteering rises while social contribution remains mostly direct and unevenly distributed
records.source_unit: Statistics South Africa Volunteer Activities Survey, 2024
records.geography: South Africa
records.boundary: This record adds a South African unpaid-work, civic-capacity, and social-meaning layer to the cultural and consumer corpus. The official PDF was anti-bot protected during this retrieval pass; the figures were transcribed from Stats SA's indexed official publication result and the access limitation is preserved. This is not a causal volunteering, employment, social-cohesion, or household-welfare estimate.

records.title: South Korea's direct cultural attendance fell in 2025 while active participation and cultural education rose
records.source_unit: South Korea Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism / Korea Culture and Tourism Institute, 2025 National Culture and Arts Activity Survey and National Leisure Activity Survey results
records.geography: South Korea; residents aged 15 and above across 17 metropolitan and provincial areas
records.boundary: This record adds South Korean evidence on cultural attendance, active participation, cultural education, and broader leisure continuity. The sources are official self-report surveys and do not establish causal reasons for the attendance decline, actual spending, digital substitution, or equal cultural access.

records.title: South Korean online commerce expands through mobile services while clothing contracts and mobile share edges down
records.source_unit: South Korea Ministry of Data and Statistics Online Shopping Trends, July 2026
records.geography: South Korea
records.boundary: This record adds a South Korean mobile-commerce and service-category layer to Hong Kong category polarization and Japan household/channel contraction. It does not measure unique consumers, cultural attendance, household welfare, causal platform substitution, or merchant value capture.

records.title: Beverage-alcohol consumption is fragmenting across occasions, formats, price points, and moderation choices
records.source_unit: Southern Glazer's Wine & Spirits Commercial Intelligence, Raise the Bar: H2 2026 Edition, released 8 September 2026
records.geography: U.S. beverage-alcohol markets and legal-drinking-age consumers across Southern Glazer's reported commercial footprint
records.boundary: This record adds a commercial-consumption route from category reset through format, price, venue, social occasion, younger legal-drinking-age trial, and moderation choices. It is a distributor's public commercial-intelligence synthesis, not a population alcohol-use estimate, public-health evaluation, representative survey, or proof that no/low products reduce alcohol exposure.

records.title: Spanish household budgets gave recreation, sport, and culture more nominal room in 2025 while essential spending remained sharply unequal by spending quintile
records.source_unit: Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE), Household Budget Survey 2025 final results
records.geography: Spain; resident households and persons covered by the annual Household Budget Survey
records.boundary: This record adds Spanish household-budget and distributional room evidence beneath cultural-participation and transaction indicators. It does not establish real cultural consumption, attendance, causal affordability, individual welfare, or durable household trajectories.

records.title: Spain's cultural life combines high digital reach, substantial place-based participation, and gendered active practice
records.source_unit: Spanish Ministry of Culture Survey of Cultural Habits and Practices 2024-2025, provisional 2024 advance results
records.geography: Spain; people aged 15 years and above
records.boundary: This record adds provisional but official Spanish evidence spanning digital culture, place-based attendance, active creation, reading, and sex differences. It does not establish a final 2024-2025 estimate, causal post-COVID recovery, price elasticity, cultural quality, or durable identity effects; the advance is based on the first portion of a biennial sample.

records.title: Spain's cultural participation has recovered broadly, but access is now a hybrid physical-platform system
records.source_unit: Spain Ministry of Culture Survey of Cultural Habits and Practices 2024-2025
records.geography: Spain; population aged 15 years and above
records.boundary: This record adds Spain's official cultural-participation evidence with recovery, physical-digital overlap, platform subscription, and sex-differentiated practice signals. It does not estimate causal effects of platformization, household affordability, frequency intensity beyond the reported windows, or equivalence with Mexico's redesigned MODECULT population and instrument.

records.title: Consumer culture is translating ambient pressure, nostalgia, self-optimization, and spirituality into searchable and social product demand
records.source_unit: Spate, 2026 Global Culture Shifts Report
records.geography: Global consumer-culture signals observed through Google Search, TikTok, and Instagram, with emphasis on beauty, wellness, and pop culture
records.boundary: This record adds a culture, wellness, identity, platform-attention, and consumer-demand route. It uses a commercial trend-forecasting landing page, not respondent-level ingestion, raw search or social data, a representative cultural survey, clinical evidence, a causal purchase model, or proof that the six movements are durable or globally prevalent.

records.title: Gen Z audio culture is being organized through fandom, life-stage rituals, cross-format participation, and identity practices that turn listening into belonging
records.source_unit: Spotify Advertising, Culture Next 2026: The Fan Edit
records.geography: Global Gen Z Spotify audience and audio, podcast, gaming, video, and fandom culture
records.boundary: This record adds Spotify's audio-and-fandom platform signal on Gen Z rituals, fitness and gaming identity, cross-format participation, emotional media, and durable fandom. It is a platform-owned cultural synthesis, not respondent-level data, a representative Gen Z study, a clinical finding, or proof that streaming creates the identities or outcomes described.

records.title: Public fear of AI is converging with cross-partisan demand for stronger regulation, creating a legitimacy gap between use, benefit, and control
records.source_unit: CNN poll conducted by SSRS and released 24 September 2026
records.geography: United States adults age 18 and older; nationally representative SSRS Opinion Panel
records.boundary: This record adds a public-legitimacy route from AI concern through demand for federal regulation, institutional control, contestability, remedy, and trust. It does not establish AI adoption, job displacement, bias, service outcomes, regulatory effectiveness, or causal political behavior.

records.title: AI capability and adoption are accelerating faster than transparency, safety measurement, labor adjustment, and public confidence
records.source_unit: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence, 2026 AI Index Report
records.geography: Global AI ecosystem, with country, organization, labor-market, public-opinion, and model comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a technology-capability and social-consequence route across AI adoption, investment, labor adjustment, productivity, incidents, transparency, language, safety, public opinion, and institutional governance. It uses Stanford AI Index aggregate evidence and published benchmark synthesis, not respondent-level ingestion, a causal estimate of AI's aggregate employment effect, a complete incident census, a universal model-quality measure, or proof that capability gains translate into equitable welfare or trusted institutions.

records.title: Accessibility barriers can prevent travel before a trip begins for Canadians with disabilities
records.source_unit: Statistics Canada, Survey Series on Accessibility – Experiences with Accessibility and Travel, 2025
records.geography: Canada; persons aged 15 years and older with disabilities or long-term conditions, with travel, daily-activity difficulty, support, and accessibility-barrier dimensions
records.boundary: This record adds a transport-accessibility and anticipated-trip-prevention layer beneath cultural and social participation. It does not establish cultural-trip exclusion, causal disability effects, provider fault, legal non-compliance, trip counts, or outcomes after accommodation.

records.title: Canada's information ecosystem is age-stratified and misinformation-saturated, making trust and detection capacity part of civic infrastructure
records.source_unit: Statistics Canada, Canadian Social Survey and Survey Series on People and Their Communities, 2026
records.geography: Canada
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative information-ecosystem mechanism: misinformation exposure is widespread, source use is sharply age-stratified and racialized Canadians report a different source mix, while media confidence and social trust correlate with perceived detection ability. It is a Canadian cross-sectional/repeated-survey evidence base, not a causal estimate of misinformation effects, a behavioral trace of content exposure or a direct audit of truthfulness.

records.title: Publicly supported childcare is expanding economically while consolidating into fewer larger providers, leaving the space, quality, and family-stability route open
records.source_unit: Statistics Canada, The early learning and child care industry in Canada: An update to the 2021 report
records.geography: Canada; administrative and government-ledger analysis through 2022, with provincial and territorial comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a care-economy and family-continuity layer: public funding and the CWELCC system coincide with industry GDP growth, provider consolidation, changing entry/exit dynamics, and a shift from smaller home-based businesses toward larger incorporated providers. It does not establish fee reduction, space creation, quality, family access, parent employment, child outcomes, market power, or causal policy effects.

records.title: Childhood immigrants reach journeyperson certification but face persistent, trade-specific earnings gaps that narrow with institutional and employment controls
records.source_unit: Statistics Canada, Early career economic outcomes of childhood immigrant and Canadian-born journeypersons in Canada
records.geography: Canada; childhood immigrants admitted at age 17 or younger and Canadian-born journeypersons certified from 2008 to 2018
records.boundary: This record adds a migration-and-work-integration route from childhood arrival and apprenticeship through certification, trade sorting, collective employment institutions, mobility, earnings and longer-run progression. It uses linked Canadian administrative data and longitudinal certification-relative comparisons, not a causal treatment effect, a complete measure of immigrant belonging, a household-welfare estimate, or evidence that any single policy explains the observed gaps.

records.title: Digital access is a practical consumer and civic bottleneck for Canadians with disabilities
records.source_unit: Statistics Canada Barriers to Accessibility in Canada: Communication and Internet Use, 2022, with 2024 Survey Series on Accessibility technology measures
records.geography: Canada; persons aged 15 years and older with disabilities or long-term conditions
records.boundary: This record adds an accessibility-to-consumer/civic-access layer. It does not establish digital exclusion as a universal condition, transaction failure, lost income, service-remedy performance, cultural participation, or causal effects; 2022 CSD and 2024 SSA-EAICT are distinct cross-sectional frames.

records.title: Home-based child care is a constrained care infrastructure: capacity, flexibility and provider capability limit household time
records.source_unit: Statistics Canada, Characteristics of home-based child cares serving children aged 0 to 5 years in Canada, 2024
records.geography: Canada; nationally representative cross-sectional survey of licensed and unlicensed home-based child-care services, April 2024
records.boundary: This record adds a care-infrastructure route from provider capacity, licensing, training and schedule design through usable child-care access, household time, work continuity and institutional legitimacy. It is a nationally representative provider survey and descriptive 2024 snapshot, not a parent-level demand estimate, causal evaluation of CWELCC reforms, child-outcome study, or proof that licensing status alone determines quality.

records.title: Household environmental behavior is shaped by dwelling, tenure, proximity, nature contact, and region—not only environmental attitudes or income
records.source_unit: Statistics Canada, Understanding factors shaping household environmental practices and behaviours in Canada
records.geography: Canada; analysis of the 2021 Households and the Environment Survey
records.boundary: This record adds a household-environmental behavior layer: housing form, tenure, residence duration, nearby nature, settlement scale, and disposal infrastructure condition composting and hazardous-waste practices. It uses 2021 Canadian survey data published in 2026; it is not a current causal experiment, a measure of environmental attitudes alone, an audited waste-flow estimate, or proof that household behavior produces environmental outcomes.

records.title: Canadian household spending recovered unevenly: shelter and food remain concentrated while recreation, restaurants, and travel reopen through unequal household room
records.source_unit: Statistics Canada, Survey of Household Spending 2023, updated September 18, 2026 with 2021-Census-calibrated weights
records.geography: Canada; provinces and the three territorial capitals, with income-quintile, household-type, tenure, and provincial comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds an observed household-consumption and cultural-participation layer from Canada: essential spending concentration, reopening of restaurants, recreation, travel and personal care, and unequal household room by income and type.
