It uses current-dollar averages and refreshed survey weights; it is not real consumption, a panel, a causal welfare estimate, or evidence that paid spending captures all cultural participation.

records.title: Immigrant economic integration has a long wealth-building timeline: recent immigrant families can have similar incomes but substantially less accumulated wealth, homeownership, pension access, and inheritance
records.source_unit: Statistics Canada and Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada, Economic well-being among immigrant and Canadian-born families: The joint distribution of income and wealth
records.geography: Canada; recent immigrant families, established immigrant families, and Canadian-born families
records.boundary: This record adds a Canada inequality and integration signal on the joint distribution of income and wealth, homeownership, pensions, inheritance, education, and time in country. It is based on pooled Survey of Financial Security data and observational models, not respondent-level public microdata, a causal immigration evaluation, a universal immigrant-family profile, or proof that income convergence produces equal wealth or security.

records.title: Interprovincial labour mobility is a small, institutionally constrained adjustment channel whose timely measurement remains uncertain
records.source_unit: Statistics Canada, Producing timely experimental estimates of interprovincial labour mobility
records.geography: Canada; workers classified by National Occupational Classification groups and province of residence
records.boundary: This record adds a mobility-capacity and measurement-infrastructure route from regional labor imbalance through occupational recognition, relocation barriers, household costs, predicted mobility and institutional response. The rates are partly experimental model outputs based on a reference-period stability assumption; this is not a causal policy evaluation, realized migration census, household-welfare estimate, or proof that mobility resolves regional inequality.

records.title: Canadian cultural output grows while cultural jobs contract, with broadcasting up and film/video down
records.source_unit: Statistics Canada National Culture Indicators, fourth quarter 2025 and first quarter 2026, Table 36-10-0652-01
records.geography: Canada; national culture and sport sectors and selected subdomains
records.boundary: This record adds a national cultural-production and labor-market layer beneath consumer participation. It does not establish worker income, job quality, cultural access, audience demand, firm profitability, platform power, or causal effects of sporting events; the series remains revision-sensitive.

records.title: Canadian retail sales remain above year-ago levels while July volume, e-commerce, and major regional markets pull back
records.source_unit: Statistics Canada Retail trade, July 2026
records.geography: Canada
records.boundary: This record adds a Canadian retail, e-commerce, category, and regional-demand layer to the cross-country consumer-channel comparison. It does not measure unique consumers, household financial stress, cultural attendance, causal substitution, or merchant margins. The August 2026 advance estimate is excluded from the main observation because Statistics Canada labels it unofficial and subject to revision.

records.title: Hybrid friendship contact is dominant in Canada, while virtual-only connection is associated with lower satisfaction and greater loneliness
records.source_unit: Statistics Canada, Survey on Social Connections – Well-being in Canada, 2025
records.geography: Canada; residents aged 15 and over in the ten provinces, excluding territories, institutions, and First Nations reserves and settlements
records.boundary: This record adds a Canadian social-connection, hybrid/virtual contact, migration, income, racialized-group, disability, satisfaction, support, and loneliness layer. It does not establish causal effects of technology, friendship quality, social isolation, platform use, or institutional trust.

records.title: Canadian time pressure and shrinking everyday friendship contact make social connection a scarce household resource
records.source_unit: Statistics Canada, Time Use Survey: time pressure and time spent with friends over the last 30 years
records.geography: Canada; non-institutionalized persons aged 15 years and older living in the provinces
records.boundary: This record adds Canadian time-diary and perceived-time-pressure evidence on social connection, friendship contact, gendered time burden, and unmet family/friendship time. It does not measure cultural participation directly, online contact, loneliness, causal time displacement, or individual mental-health outcomes.

records.title: Finnish consumer caution is geographically and socially uneven, with weak spending intentions alongside renewed borrowing plans
records.source_unit: Statistics Finland, Consumer confidence 2026, September, released 28 September 2026
records.geography: Finland; monthly Consumer Confidence Survey, 1,157 respondents resident in Finland interviewed 1–17 September 2026
records.boundary: This record adds a household-consumption route from uneven confidence and perceived price or job risk through regional and status divergence, spending restraint, and differentiated borrowing. It does not establish realized expenditure, debt distress, causal regional effects, or household welfare from confidence balances alone.

records.title: Danish cultural participation is age- and place-shaped differently across digital games, cinema, museums, and heritage
records.source_unit: Statistics Denmark Cultural Habits Survey, Q2 2026, StatBank tables KV2HOVED and KV2URB
records.geography: Denmark; population cultural and recreational activity participation by age and degree of urbanisation
records.boundary: This record adds a current Danish cultural-behavior, age, and place layer. It does not establish frequency, spending, venue supply, affordability, travel time, cultural quality, or causal age/urbanisation effects; the 2024 questionnaire redesign limits direct historical comparison.

records.title: South African care work converts gender, household infrastructure and dependency into unequal time and labour-market room
records.source_unit: Statistics South Africa, Gender Series Volume XIII: Gender Disparities in Care Work in South Africa, 2026, with official summary and publication metadata
records.geography: South Africa; national gender, household, labour-market, education and infrastructure indicators
records.boundary: This record adds a gendered care-conversion mechanism: demographic dependency, household employment, family commitments, paid-care concentration and infrastructure effort shape who has usable time and labour-market room. Statistics South Africa states that recent time-use data are unavailable and the report uses proxy indicators; this record therefore does not estimate unpaid-care hours, causal effects, within-household bargaining, care quality or a complete care economy.

records.title: South African crime exposure, reporting and perceived safety diverge across households, gender and place
records.source_unit: Statistics South Africa, Governance, Public Safety and Justice Survey 2025/26: Victims of Crime Release
records.geography: South Africa; households and individuals aged 16 years and older as defined by GPSJS
records.boundary: This record adds a public-safety conversion mechanism: victimisation, police reporting, perceived safety and self-protection are distinct stages, with gender and place shaping usable security. The one-page official release does not establish objective crime prevalence, reporting causes, police remedy, protection effectiveness, household cost, or causal change.

records.title: Global trust deficits are becoming an operating constraint on diplomacy, technology, trade, security, and shared public goods
records.source_unit: Stimson Center, Doha Forum, and Global Institute for Strategic Research, Future of International Cooperation Report 2026: Redefining Global Trust
records.geography: Global and regional governance, with perspectives spanning diplomacy, economics, technology, security, justice, and the Global South
records.boundary: This record adds a global-governance trust route connecting information integrity, AI capacity, diplomacy, trade, security, justice, accountability and shared public goods. It is a normative policy synthesis, not a global trust prevalence estimate, a geopolitical forecast, a country implementation audit, or respondent-level data.

records.title: Payment fragmentation turns checkout into a time, liquidity, trust, and consumer-optionality system
records.source_unit: Stitch, How South Africans Shop in 2026: Consumer Payments Report
records.geography: South Africa; digitally active consumers and Stitch platform transaction data
records.boundary: This is sponsor-produced commercial trend intelligence, not a nationally representative population survey or independent causal evaluation. It is useful for identifying mechanisms at the intersection of consumer culture, payment infrastructure, liquidity, time, trust, and AI-mediated commerce; it does not establish national prevalence, realized welfare, repayment outcomes, market share, or causal effects.

records.title: Economic and social pressure is entering mental-health life through loneliness, housing, digital exposure, and help-seeking stigma
records.source_unit: St Patrick's Mental Health Services annual Stigma and Attitudes to Mental Health Survey 2026
records.geography: Ireland; nationally representative adults aged 18 and over
records.boundary: This record identifies a public-attitudes and social-pressure mechanism linking material insecurity, loneliness, housing, climate concern, digital exposure, stigma, and help-seeking. It does not establish clinical prevalence, causal effects, service capacity, treatment quality, or individual risk prediction.

records.title: Housing is becoming an integration and participation infrastructure: affordability, neighbourhoods and legal status shape who can belong and advance
records.source_unit: Expert Council on Integration and Migration, Room for Development: Housing and Participation in an Immigration Society, Annual Report 2026
records.geography: Germany, with national and urban-neighbourhood comparisons involving people with and without a migration background
records.boundary: This record adds a housing-to-participation route in an immigration society, linking affordability, tenure, migration status, neighbourhood resources, poverty, segregation, local infrastructure, labour-market access, discrimination and legal choice. It is a Germany-specific annual report and public summary, not a U.S. housing estimate, respondent-level longitudinal dataset, causal neighbourhood experiment or proof that any recommendation has been implemented.

records.title: Sweden's digital life expands and contracts at once: AI adoption rises while people seek detox, social boundaries, and safer public-service access
records.source_unit: Internet Foundation Sweden, Swedes and the Internet 2026 annual internet-use study
records.geography: Sweden; residents surveyed about internet use, AI, digital public services, social media, mobile etiquette, and digital detox
records.boundary: This record adds a Sweden-specific cultural and digital-life layer connecting AI diffusion, search substitution, verification, digital public-service usability, passive attention, detox, and mobile social norms. It does not establish actual AI performance, passive behavioral logs, clinical effects, service failure, household welfare, or causal cultural change.

records.title: Swedish inquiry frames social exclusion as an interaction among segregation, institutional distrust, discrimination, alternative systems and constrained individual rights
records.source_unit: Government of Sweden, SOU 2026:53 Parallella samhällsstrukturer – ett kunskapsunderlag för förbättrad integration och minskat utanförskap
records.geography: Sweden; national policy inquiry with attention to local areas, institutions, migrants, children, women and socially excluded communities
records.boundary: This record treats SOU 2026:53 as a government inquiry and policy knowledge base, not as a neutral prevalence census or a causal evaluation. Its politically charged term ‘parallel social structures’ has no generally accepted definition; the report itself stresses interaction among exclusion, discrimination, trust, segregation, alternative systems and rights constraints, and warns against equating all cultural, religious or migrant communities with the phenomenon.

records.title: Ireland’s AI opportunity is distributed through existing differences in work exposure, gender, skills, ownership and worker voice
records.source_unit: TASC, AI and Inequality: Spotlight on the Key Issues Affecting Ireland, part of The State We Are In: Inequality in Ireland 2026
records.geography: Ireland; workers, firms, communities and public institutions in a highly digitalised economy
records.boundary: This record adds an Ireland-specific AI-and-inequality lens: exposure, complementarity, gender, skills, algorithmic management, ownership, worker voice and global externalisation are linked as a distributional system. It is an independent think-tank synthesis and issue brief, not a representative worker panel, causal forecast, administrative inequality series or proof that the cited exposure estimates will become realized displacement or wage outcomes.

records.title: Ireland’s tax-and-transfer system reduces measured disposable-income inequality while leaving deep pre-distribution, housing and household-room pressures intact
records.source_unit: TASC, The State We Are In: Inequality in Ireland 2026
records.geography: Ireland; households, renters, workers, unemployed people, lone-parent families, people with disabilities or long-term illness, and income deciles
records.boundary: This record adds a household-material and redistribution layer to the Ireland inequality stream: market-income inequality, tax-and-transfer protection, real purchasing power, housing tenure, deprivation, emergency accommodation and essential services are connected to the report’s pre-distribution argument. It is an independent think-tank synthesis using official and secondary evidence, not a new household panel, causal poverty evaluation, complete homelessness census or proof that any proposed reform would produce a specified outcome.

records.title: Digital trust is experienced at the point of access: identity friction, understandable data practices, and AI autonomy shape abandonment and confidence
records.source_unit: Thales Digital Trust Index 2026, conducted by Vanson Bourne
records.geography: Consumers, partner users, and IT decision makers across the USA, Canada, Mexico, Brazil, UK, France, Germany, Netherlands, UAE, South Africa, Singapore, Japan, and Australia; fieldwork January–February 2026
records.boundary: This record adds a digital-trust and access-friction route across authentication, data comprehension, AI deployment, autonomous agents, sectoral confidence, abandonment, delay, switching, credential risk, and public-service dependence. It uses Thales’s sponsor-commissioned Vanson Bourne survey summary, not observed login telemetry, verified breaches, provider revenue, causal adoption estimates, individual longitudinal histories, or proof that trust ratings equal actual safety.

records.title: Media professionals are drifting away from the public they model: platform overestimation coexists with advertising distrust and shared-screen attachment
records.source_unit: thinkTV and Ipsos, Ad Nation 2026
records.geography: Canada; adults aged 18-59 and Canadian Marketing Association media/advertising professionals
records.boundary: This record adds a consumer-media translation route: professional assumptions can diverge from public behavior, while advertising trust, AI-content concern, social-ad credibility, and shared television shape cultural attention. It does not establish causal campaign performance, platform market share, purchase conversion, social cohesion, or political effects.

records.title: TikTok’s 2026 forecast points from passive scrolling toward grounded reality, curiosity-led discovery, community verification, and more intentional purchases
records.source_unit: TikTok for Business, TikTok Next 2026 Trend Report: Irreplaceable Instinct
records.geography: TikTok platform culture and global creator, search, comment, and shopping behavior
records.boundary: This record adds TikTok's platform-owned 2026 culture forecast on grounded reality, public accountability, curiosity-led discovery, evidence economies, tastemakers, intentional purchases, and community-made content. It is a platform trend synthesis, not respondent-level data, a representative population forecast, independent causal evidence, or proof that more engagement is socially beneficial.

records.title: Institutional trust is tied more strongly to perceived governance performance and integrity than to partisan identity alone
records.source_unit: Murtin et al., European Journal of Political Research 2026, What explains trust in institutions? Multi-disciplinary evidence from an international survey
records.geography: Representative samples from Germany, Italy, Japan, Slovenia, the United Kingdom, and the United States; fielded 2017–2020 in the Trustlab database
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative governance-performance-to-institutional-trust mechanism using historical six-country Trustlab data. It does not provide current 2026 trust levels, a global estimate, respondent-level ingestion into this atlas, a causal intervention test, or proof that service delivery alone resolves representation and legitimacy conflicts.

records.title: Live gaming is functioning as a global participatory culture system where communities, creators, regional scenes, and platform rewards turn watching into co-created events
records.source_unit: Twitch, State of Gaming 2026
records.geography: Global Twitch gaming viewership and creators, January 1 through September 1, 2026, with regional game rankings
records.boundary: This record adds Twitch's live-gaming signal on platform scale, genre and indie growth, regional localization, creator-led events, and reward-based participation. It is company-reported aggregate platform data, not respondent-level data, a complete gaming-market census, independent assessment of creator livelihoods, or proof that monetized participation equals community wellbeing.

records.title: Global wealth expanded rapidly while median experience, regional position, and ownership remained sharply uneven
records.source_unit: UBS Global Wealth Report 2026, seventeenth edition, using estimated personal wealth across 56 key markets
records.geography: 56 markets estimated by UBS to represent over 92% of global wealth, with regional, country, wealth-band, and high-net-worth comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a global wealth, ownership, mobility, debt, liquidity, and cultural-asset layer. It does not provide respondent-level data, a representative household panel, a causal inequality estimate, or a complete account of public wealth, informal assets, unpaid care, or lived financial security; UBS estimates and high-net-worth survey evidence carry institutional and sampling limits.

records.title: Britons value open disagreement but experience a shrinking, socially costly public space for expressing it
records.source_unit: UCL and More in Common, Disagreeing Well research, reported 22 September 2026
records.geography: Great Britain; polling of 2,000 people with follow-up focus groups
records.boundary: This record adds a civic-culture route from fear of social labelling and hostile disagreement through speech restraint, venue substitution, and the perceived usability of public forums. It does not establish actual censorship, platform causality, political withdrawal, polarization as a single metric, or that dialogue interventions produce durable institutional trust.

records.title: UK consumer enforcement is moving from investigation toward direct redress, while remedy reach and household recovery remain open
records.source_unit: UK Competition and Markets Authority Annual Report and Accounts 2025 to 2026
records.geography: United Kingdom; CMA consumer-protection, competition, and digital-markets activity, 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026
records.boundary: This record adds a UK regulator-side consumer-recourse and digital-market enforcement layer. It does not establish population-wide harm, individual refund receipt, remedy adequacy, durable compliance, affordability, switching, trust repair, or causal household welfare effects.

records.title: UK live-event ticketing shows hidden price as a cultural-access barrier that can be converted into automatic consumer remedy
records.source_unit: UK Competition and Markets Authority StubHub UK hidden-fees enforcement case
records.geography: United Kingdom; StubHub UK live-show and sports-event customers
records.boundary: This record adds a named UK cultural-consumer enforcement episode that links hidden fees, ticket checkout design, affected customers, automatic redress, firm response, and regulator authority. It does not estimate total ticketing harm, attendance exclusion, deterrence, customer refund completion, or the causal effect of transparent pricing on cultural participation.

records.title: The Ticketmaster Oasis case shows live-event pricing harm being converted into prospective disclosure and monitoring controls
records.source_unit: UK Competition and Markets Authority Ticketmaster consumer-protection case concerning Oasis Live '25 ticket sales
records.geography: United Kingdom; Ticketmaster UK live-event ticket buyers and prospective buyers
records.boundary: This record adds a named UK live-event pricing episode and contrasts prospective transparency/reporting controls with retrospective automatic refund remedy. It does not establish unlawful conduct for every dynamic price, quantify consumer losses, verify future compliance, estimate attendance exclusion, or prove that disclosure restores affordability.

records.title: Arts participation remains broad but physical engagement fell, digital substitution stalled, and deprivation and place shape access
records.source_unit: UK Department for Culture, Media and Sport, Community and Engagement Survey 2025/26: arts report
records.geography: England; representative survey of people aged 16 and over, with regional, local-authority and demographic breakdowns
records.boundary: This record adds an arts-participation route from household room, place and cultural repertoire through physical and digital engagement, local access, socioeconomic inequality and possible social connection. It is representative England survey evidence with a documented questionnaire and method discontinuity concern, not a causal explanation of participation decline, an attendance register, a spending measure, or a universal account of cultural value.

records.title: Neighbourhood belonging and cohesion remain substantial but uneven, with local trust weaker than broad intergroup coexistence
records.source_unit: UK Department for Culture, Media and Sport / Community and Engagement Survey 2025/26, neighbourhood and community report, updated 16 September 2026
records.geography: England; representative Community and Engagement Survey estimates for people aged 16 and over
records.boundary: This record adds an official aggregate outcome surface for neighbourhood belonging, neighbour interaction, collective action, local trust, intergroup coexistence, place inequality, and perceived local change. It is representative England survey reporting, not respondent-level linkage, a causal community intervention evaluation, proof that belonging causes civic action, or a universal measure of social cohesion.

records.title: Creative-industry AI adoption is being negotiated as an augmentation, trust and entry-route problem rather than simple automation
records.source_unit: UK Government, AI Adoption Plan: Creative Industries, report by the AI Champion for the Creative Industries
records.geography: United Kingdom creative industries, including businesses, freelancers, institutions and regional creative clusters
records.boundary: This record adds a creative-work and cultural-economy route linking AI adoption to firm size, subsector, operational workflow, trust, rights, cost, skills, entry-level career paths, regional infrastructure and human creative control. It is a UK government policy plan using cited business evidence and case studies, not a causal evaluation, complete creative-industry census, worker panel, consumer survey or proof that augmentation-first adoption produces equitable outcomes.

records.title: Culture and heritage are being reframed as social infrastructure whose cohesion benefits must become visible in public-investment appraisal
records.source_unit: UK Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport, Culture and Heritage Capital - Valuing social cohesion: a scoping study
records.geography: United Kingdom culture and heritage assets and services, with implications for local and national public investment appraisal
records.boundary: This record adds a culture-as-social-infrastructure and valuation-governance route from cultural assets and shared participation through belonging, networks, trust, civic engagement, and public-investment appraisal. It does not establish causal social-cohesion effects, a nationally generalisable willingness-to-pay estimate, or that monetisation captures the full political and lived meaning of culture.

records.title: Culture and heritage are being treated as social infrastructure whose cohesion value is real but difficult to isolate and monetize
records.source_unit: UK Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport / Culture and Heritage Capital Programme, Culture and heritage capital - Valuing social cohesion: a scoping study, 24 September 2026
records.geography: United Kingdom culture and heritage assets, services, communities, institutions, and social-cohesion valuation evidence
records.boundary: This record adds a culture-and-heritage-as-social-infrastructure route from public investment and access through shared identity, social ties, norms, social mixing, belonging, civic participation, and institutional legitimacy. It is a UK scoping study and evidence synthesis, not proof of causal cultural effects, a national monetized estimate, a respondent-level dataset, or evidence that all cultural assets produce cohesion equally.

records.title: Among boys and young men, loneliness is widespread but usually intermittent; family support, friendships, mental health, bullying and work or education status structure who becomes persistently disconnected
records.source_unit: UK Department for Culture, Media and Sport and National Centre for Social Research, Loneliness, isolation and social connection among boys and young men in England
records.geography: England; boys and young men aged 10–25 using Understanding Society and Mental Health of Children and Young People survey data
records.boundary: This record is the empirical companion to the UK Social Connection Framework. It uses observational national survey data, with different measures across Understanding Society and MHCYP; it is not a causal intervention evaluation, clinical diagnosis, global estimate or proof that friendship counts alone create wellbeing.

records.title: A place-based sports intervention is being used as a bridge from social connection to mental-health literacy, aspiration and re-engagement for boys and young men at risk of isolation
records.source_unit: UK Department for Culture, Media and Sport, Rugby League Cares and Edge Hill University, evaluation of Offload and Movember Ahead of the Game pilots
records.geography: Wigan and Wakefield, England; boys and young men experiencing loneliness, isolation or NEET status
records.boundary: This record adds a named intervention and evaluation route to the youth-belonging sequence. It is a local pilot with public summary findings, not a randomized trial, national programme evaluation, clinical treatment study, or proof that sport-based connection scales uniformly.

records.title: England's cultural participation is broad and mostly physical-or-hybrid, with digital access layering onto institutions
records.source_unit: UK Department for Culture, Media and Sport Participation Survey 2024/25
records.geography: England; adults aged 16 years and above
records.boundary: This record adds England's official adult cultural-participation evidence with physical-digital overlap, institution-specific digital layering, stated barriers, and Internet-capability context. It does not establish causal affordability or time constraints, platform substitution, UK-wide coverage, or individual-level cultural welfare.

records.title: Young men’s loneliness is being reframed as a social-infrastructure and participation problem, linking belonging, work, school, online risk and accessible places to connect
records.source_unit: UK Department for Culture, Media and Sport, Social Connection Framework
records.geography: England and UK policy context, focused on boys and young men aged 10–25, with implications for youth, education, local government and community provision
records.boundary: This record adds a UK comparative social-infrastructure and youth-belonging route. It is government guidance informed by mixed evidence and a small direct-engagement sample, not a representative prevalence survey, clinical evaluation, causal intervention study or proof that the referenced investment produces durable connection.

records.title: Youth wellbeing and civic confidence are tied to local third spaces, trusted adults, affordable opportunity, and whether young people feel heard
records.source_unit: UK Department for Culture, Media and Sport, Youth Matters: State of the Nation, updated 12 August 2026
records.geography: England primarily, with selected UK-wide comparisons; young people ages 10-21 and up to 25 for those with special educational needs or disabilities
records.boundary: This record adds UK public research on youth belonging, trusted adults, local third spaces, activity access, economic insecurity, and civic voice. It combines survey, cited secondary, qualitative, and youth-advisory evidence without treating them as one dataset; it is not respondent-level ingestion, a causal evaluation of youth services, a global youth estimate, or proof that any single investment reverses wellbeing or turnout patterns.

records.title: Great Britain’s mobility recovery remains mode-specific: road traffic is above baseline while public transport has not fully returned
records.source_unit: UK Department for Transport, Daily domestic transport use by mode
records.geography: Great Britain; National Rail excluding Elizabeth line, buses, Transport for London, and motor traffic
records.boundary: This record adds an observed mobility and infrastructure route from mode-specific transport operation through time, cost, access, hybrid-work change, and public-system use. It does not measure unique travelers, household transport burden, trip purpose, accessibility, social participation, emissions, or causal effects of remote work, fares, fuel, or transport policy. Mode baselines and time windows remain explicit.

records.title: Digital identity is becoming an infrastructure layer for finance, work, public services, and age assurance, while trust and access remain use-case specific
records.source_unit: UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology / Office for Digital Identities and Attributes, Digital Identity Sectoral Analysis Report 2026
records.geography: United Kingdom digital-identity sector and UK residents aged 18–66 in a weighted November 2025 consumer survey
records.boundary: This record adds a UK route from digital-identity market expansion and service embedding through consumer understanding, income-linked use, context-specific preference, public legitimacy, and exclusion risk. It preserves modeled market estimates, weighted survey, revised-baseline, self-report, and non-causal boundaries; it does not establish that digital identity improves service access, privacy, fraud outcomes, or trust.

records.title: Young people want social media redesigned and governed rather than simply removed, balancing connection and community against algorithmic pressure, AI risk, and weak trust
records.source_unit: UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology, Children's wellbeing online: What young people think about social media, safety and AI, prepared by Savanta, 15 July 2026
records.geography: United Kingdom young people ages 10-21, parents, teachers, youth practitioners, public consultation participants, and youth-led hack events
records.boundary: This record adds UK public research on young people's online connection, platform design, social-media safety, AI concerns, age verification, and youth-led policy preferences. It preserves survey, public-consultation, professional, and participatory evidence as different frames; it is not respondent-level ingestion, a clinical wellbeing study, a global youth estimate, a platform audit, or proof that a ban or feature restriction will produce the claimed outcomes.

records.title: Informal digital help is a hidden social infrastructure: proxy access solves immediate tasks while risking dependence and credential insecurity
records.source_unit: UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology commissioned mixed-method research on informal and proxy digital support, delivered by The Social Agency
records.geography: United Kingdom; adults providing or receiving informal digital support
records.boundary: This record adds a UK digital-inclusion route from service complexity and confidence or skills barriers through informal help, proxy access, financial and administrative tasks, credential risk, time burden, and possible independence. It does not establish national digital-exclusion prevalence, causal effects of service design, actual financial loss, completed service outcomes, or a representative burden on supporters.

records.title: A sharp fall in UK financial complaints partly reflects changed access to the ombudsman, not necessarily less consumer harm
records.source_unit: UK Financial Ombudsman Service, Annual complaints data and insight 2025/26
records.geography: United Kingdom; complaints referred to the Financial Ombudsman Service and Financial Ombudsman Service for Small Businesses
records.boundary: This record adds UK administrative evidence on financial complaints, uphold outcomes, professional representation, abandonment, product-level harm signals, and redress routing. It does not establish population-level financial harm, causal effects of representative fees, compensation adequacy, firm compliance, or durable consumer trust.

records.title: UK grocery-supplier compliance can remain high while retailer processes transfer forecasting, payment and exit risk downstream
records.source_unit: UK Groceries Code Adjudicator, 2026 annual supplier survey results
records.geography: United Kingdom; suppliers to the 14 designated grocery retailers
records.boundary: This record adds a firm-sector power and contestability route: retailer compliance can remain high while forecasting, payment, invoice, de-listing and reporting conditions distribute risk across suppliers. It does not measure consumer prices, supplier profitability, unlawful conduct, completed remedy, switching, investment, employment, innovation or causal retailer effects.

records.title: Supply-chain resilience is a network, climate, geopolitical, and household-affordability problem rather than a bilateral trade problem
records.source_unit: UK Government Office for Science, Global supply chains: a foresight report on risk and resilience
records.geography: Global supply networks with a UK exposure lens and comparisons to other large advanced economies, including the United States, China, Japan, France, and Italy
records.boundary: This record adds a UK-centered but globally relevant network-resilience layer to the geopolitical and household-cost map. It is a foresight study using evidence, modelling, and scenarios; it is not a disruption forecast, a realized price or shortage panel, a firm-level causal study, a household survey, or proof of strategic success.

records.title: Positive service experience does not automatically become institutional trust: the public separates delivery from whether government acts in its interests
records.source_unit: Institute for Government, More in Common and University of York Policy Engine, How does the public understand government? Assessing the perception gap between experience and trust among voters in England, September 2026
records.geography: England, with regional comparisons and focus groups in the North East and East of England; regional-mayoral areas compared with other areas
records.boundary: This record adds a political-cultural legitimacy route from everyday government experience through attribution, information, place identity, devolution, social cohesion, and institutional trust. It is a UK survey and qualitative case synthesis, not a causal evaluation of devolution, a behavioral trace, a representative U.S. estimate, or proof that better service delivery alone repairs political legitimacy.

records.title: Cost pressure and platform convenience sustain counterfeit purchasing while harm reporting and perceived seriousness remain low
records.source_unit: UK Intellectual Property Office, Counterfeit goods research (Wave 5), 2026 publication
records.geography: United Kingdom adults aged 18+; nationally representative survey with qualitative and communications-testing stages
records.boundary: This record adds a consumer-recourse and platform-mediated authenticity layer. It is based primarily on self-reported UK consumer survey and qualitative evidence; it does not estimate the counterfeit market, authenticate individual goods, establish platform liability, identify causal effects of prices or social media, or measure completed enforcement or redress.

records.title: Health-related work loss is being reframed as a workplace-system and data-intelligence problem, not only a welfare or clinical problem
records.source_unit: UK Department for Work and Pensions, Department for Business and Trade, and Department of Health and Social Care, Keep Britain Working: a national growth opportunity, September 2026 update
records.geography: United Kingdom; national policy update with regional, employer, sector, and disability-inclusion routes
records.boundary: This record adds a health-to-work conversion route from work-limiting health exposure through early support, retention, sustained return, disability inclusion, household and public-finance effects, place-based provision, and trusted intelligence. It does not establish that the proposed Workplace Health System has been implemented, that cited pathway probabilities are causal intervention effects, or that modelled economic benefits will materialize.

records.title: UK open banking has moved into routine payment scale while fraud exposure remains concentrated in authorised scams
records.source_unit: Open Banking Limited, 1 Billion Payments and Counting for UK Open Banking (21 September 2026) and Open Banking Payments Fraud Monitor, June 2026 Edition (8 July 2026)
records.geography: United Kingdom
records.boundary: This record adds UK observed digital-finance activity and fraud-risk evidence to the platform, data-portability, and consumer-choice lanes. It does not measure unique people, payment value, switching, savings, trust, reimbursement, causal safety, or distributional access. OBL is an ecosystem body and the two sources are related publisher outputs; they should not be counted as independent population corroboration.

records.title: Employment support is being redesigned as a portfolio of user-informed experiments whose legitimacy depends on learning, accessibility, and scale
records.source_unit: UK Department for Work and Pensions, Pathways to Work Innovation Fund applicant bid pack
records.geography: United Kingdom; UK-wide employment, health, skills, disability, and long-term-condition support innovation fund
records.boundary: This record adds an institutional-learning route from disability and health-related employment barriers through lived-experience design, accessible participation, cross-sector partnerships, evidence generation, and potential scale. It does not establish funded-project outcomes, causal employment effects, participant control, or successful adoption.

records.title: Consumer surveillance devices are becoming civic evidence infrastructure, but fragmented police response threatens participation and trust
records.source_unit: Police Foundation, Policing and Digital Citizen Evidence: Unleashing the potential for public participation, summarized in a report release published 16 September 2026
records.geography: United Kingdom; nationally representative YouGov survey of adults, with citizen-owned surveillance technology and evidence-sharing questions
records.boundary: This record adds a civic-technology route from household surveillance adoption through perceived safety, evidence-sharing willingness, police intake and feedback, privacy, accessibility, and institutional legitimacy. It does not establish crime reduction, actual evidence submission, case outcomes, causal trust effects, or that more surveillance is socially beneficial.

records.title: Social cohesion is being reframed as a national-resilience and security capability shaped by place, services, identity, technology, and geopolitical pressure
records.source_unit: UK Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, Protecting What Matters: Towards a more confident, cohesive, and resilient United Kingdom, Command Paper CP 1559, updated 28 April 2026
records.geography: United Kingdom social-cohesion, integration, community-resilience, online-safety, and national-security policy
records.boundary: This record adds a UK state-policy route from economic, place, demographic, technological, and geopolitical pressures through integration, identity, community infrastructure, online governance, extremism prevention, and national resilience. It is a policy diagnosis and action plan, not an independent causal evaluation, a neutral measure of public opinion, proof of extremist influence, or evidence that proposed programs have delivered cohesion.

records.title: UK APP reimbursement policy reduced measured Faster Payments fraud while shifting prevention costs and uneven implementation onto payment firms
records.source_unit: Payment Systems Regulator summary of the Frontier Economics independent evaluation of APP scam policies, published 1 July 2026
records.geography: United Kingdom; Faster Payments APP scam policy and payment service providers
records.boundary: This record adds an independent policy-effect and provider-incentive layer to the UK payment-remedy route. It is not a recipient-level panel, not open-banking-specific, and not a proof of individual adequacy, residual loss, trust, switching, or durable household recovery. Its loss and reimbursement estimates should not be mechanically pooled with the PSR dashboard because timing, scope, and denominators differ.

records.title: Before mandatory APP reimbursement, reported loss reimbursement varied sharply across UK banking groups
records.source_unit: Payment Systems Regulator 2024 APP scam performance report for transactions before the mandatory reimbursement requirement
records.geography: United Kingdom; customers of the 14 largest banking groups using Faster Payments
records.boundary: This record adds a provider-level pre-policy baseline for reported APP-scam loss reimbursement. It does not estimate causal bank effects, individual adequacy, household recovery, or a before/after policy effect; it must be kept separate from the post-October-2024 PSR reimbursement dashboard.

records.title: UK APP-fraud reimbursement converts a payment-protection rule into measured claim, speed, and returned-money outcomes
records.source_unit: Payment Systems Regulator APP scams reimbursement dashboard for Q1 2026, using Pay.UK reporting under Specific Direction 20
records.geography: United Kingdom; Faster Payments APP scams reported by consumers, including individuals, small businesses, and charities with annual income below £1 million
records.boundary: This record adds observed consumer-reimbursement and inter-firm RCA-compliance stages to the UK digital-payment and consumer-recourse lanes. It covers Faster Payments APP scams broadly, not open-banking payments specifically. It does not establish individual payment receipt, adequacy, residual loss, repeat exposure, trust, switching, non-use, or durable household recovery.

records.title: Social-security design can steer young people and households toward or away from culturally valued education and vocational pathways
records.source_unit: UK Social Security Advisory Committee, The influence of the social security system on educational and vocational decision-making at age 16, Occasional Paper 27
records.geography: England, with UK and international comparison of post-16 participation, benefits, apprenticeships, and monitoring systems
records.boundary: This record adds a social-security-to-education-choice route from household financial exposure through pathway selection, vocational participation, policy coherence, subgroup visibility, and early intervention. It does not establish a population-wide causal estimate, prove that every apprenticeship is deterred, or imply that real-time tracking alone improves outcomes.

records.title: Young people distinguish trust in elections from distrust of politicians while seeking earlier voice and better civic preparation
records.source_unit: UK Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government, Votes at 16 research: Executive summary, commissioned from Deltapoll
records.geography: United Kingdom; young people aged 14–17 across England, Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland
records.boundary: This record adds a youth political-socialization and voice layer. It combines a nationally representative survey of over 3,500 young people aged 14–17 with 32 focus groups; it is not a turnout study, causal evaluation of votes at 16, measure of future voting behavior, or proof that algorithmic exposure causes misinformation or distrust.

records.title: Youth hubs can connect open access to targeted support, but partnership time and data infrastructure determine whether reach becomes durable outcome
records.source_unit: UK Department for Culture, Media and Sport, Young Futures Hubs Early Adopters Pilot evaluation: interim report, Ecorys
records.geography: England; eight Young Futures Hubs Early Adopter sites
records.boundary: This record adds a youth-service infrastructure and evaluation-capacity layer. It covers eight Early Adopter Hubs at an interim implementation stage; it does not establish causal effects on mental health, crime, safer streets, education, employment, or wellbeing, and it cannot treat reach, attendance, qualitative accounts, soft outcomes, and linked individual outcomes as equivalent evidence.

records.title: Global policy institutions are shifting from GDP-only progress toward dashboards that measure well-being, equity, sustainability, resilience, and social cohesion
records.source_unit: United Nations Secretary-General's High-Level Expert Group on Beyond GDP, Counting What Counts: A Compass of Progress for People and Planet
records.geography: Global framework for country-owned and universally applicable progress indicators, with UNCTAD implementation and pilot context
records.boundary: This record adds a measurement-to-policy-legitimacy route: how institutions define progress, make inequality and environmental conditions visible, and potentially change decision criteria. It is not a well-being survey, respondent-level outcome, causal policy evaluation, or claim that dashboard adoption has already changed public behavior.

records.title: Care is emerging as foundational social infrastructure: it converts household vulnerability into participation, security, and dignity
records.source_unit: United Nations Commission for Social Development, Eradicating poverty and ensuring dignity through resilient care and support systems (E/CN.5/2026/4)
records.geography: Global; national experiences and international evidence reviewed for the Commission for Social Development
records.boundary: This record adds a global care-infrastructure route from life-course needs through household time, poverty, gender, work, social protection, public services, and dignity. It is a UN Secretariat policy note synthesizing evidence and good practices, not a harmonized global outcome dataset, respondent-level study, or causal evaluation of any care programme.

records.boundary: This record adds a higher-education, mobility, equity, finance, labor-market, and institutional-AI-readiness route. It uses aggregate comparative public data and report synthesis, not respondent-level ingestion, student transcripts, causal estimates of higher-education returns, a ranking of institutions, or proof that enrollment expansion translates into completion, quality, or mobility for every group.

records.title: Museums are experimenting with AI faster than they are building internal policy, training, data governance, and professional capacity
records.source_unit: UNESCO-ICOM, Global Survey on the Use of Artificial Intelligence in Museums
records.geography: Museums and cultural institutions across 90 countries, with attention to regional differences in digital infrastructure, funding, technical capacity, and expertise
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural-institutional AI signal linking museum adoption, governance, professional capacity, accuracy, copyright, data protection, digital inequality, and cultural trust. It is a public summary of a global survey, not respondent-level ingestion, a representative estimate of all museums, a causal evaluation, a visitor-outcome study, or proof that AI improves cultural access or interpretation.

records.title: Intercultural dialogue is being treated as measurable social infrastructure connecting inclusion, conflict prevention, human rights and peace
records.source_unit: UNESCO and Institute for Economics and Peace, We Need to Talk: Measuring Intercultural Dialogue for Peace and Inclusion; UNESCO public release dated March 2026
records.geography: More than 160 countries across all regions, using comparative data, regional trend analysis and case studies
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural and civic-capacity route linking intercultural dialogue to identity, inclusion, vulnerability, peace, conflict prevention, rights, resilience and policy participation. The underlying report is identified by UNESCO as 2022 and was publicly highlighted in 2026; this record is not new 2026 outcome data, a respondent-level dataset, a causal intervention evaluation, an implementation audit or proof that dialogue alone produces peace or inclusion.

records.title: AI in education is becoming a governance and human-capability question, not merely a technology-adoption question
records.source_unit: UNESCO Institute for Information Technologies in Education, 2026 GSE Annual Report: Smart Education Around the World
records.geography: Seven world regions and diverse national education systems integrating AI and digital technologies across differing social, economic, and institutional contexts
records.boundary: This record adds an education-technology governance route linking AI, pedagogy, teacher capacity, infrastructure, fragile contexts, equity, human values, sustainability, and institutional responsibility. It is a cross-regional policy synthesis, not student-level learning data, a technology-adoption census, a causal effect estimate, a school implementation audit, or proof that Smart Education improves outcomes.

records.title: Living heritage is being used as a locally grounded education, participation, and cultural-continuity resource
records.source_unit: UNESCO, Educación y patrimonio cultural inmaterial en América Latina y el Caribe, published 7 May 2026
records.geography: Latin America and the Caribbean, with educational and living-heritage practices from 15 countries
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural-education route linking living heritage, local knowledge, community participation, cultural relevance, inclusion, creativity, and policy learning. It uses a documented regional practice synthesis, not a representative census of schools or cultural practices, respondent-level learning data, causal impact evaluation, universal transferability claim, or proof of durable heritage transmission.

records.title: Education can become a form of civic and legal capability when people need to navigate justice systems that are increasingly hard to access
records.source_unit: UNESCO Global Education Monitoring Report and Namati, Education and justice: Learning to build just societies
records.geography: Global justice systems, education systems, disadvantaged populations, communities, and institutions concerned with rights, peace, democracy, and social cohesion
records.boundary: This record adds an education-to-justice route across legal capability, rights literacy, institutional trust, professional capacity, democracy, peace, crime reduction, and social cohesion. It uses UNESCO/Namati report synthesis, not respondent-level legal histories, individual case files, courtroom outcomes, causal education estimates, or proof that schooling alone produces justice.

records.title: Cultural production is becoming more digital and globally valuable while creator income, mobility, skills, and artistic freedom remain unevenly protected
records.source_unit: UNESCO, Re|Shaping Policies for Creativity 2026 and related UNESCO cultural-policy and creative-skills reporting
records.geography: More than 120 reporting countries and global cultural and creative industries, with comparisons by development status
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural-production and creative-economy route linking policy commitment, trade, digital distribution, generative-AI exposure, skills, mobility, artistic freedom, and institutional inclusion. It is not a causal estimate of individual creator income, audience preferences, cultural consumption, or AI job displacement, and it does not use respondent-level microdata.

records.title: Digital cultural access is expanding faster than creator security, local visibility, and cultural power
records.source_unit: UNESCO, Re|Shaping Policies for Creativity 2026
records.geography: Global cultural and creative sectors, with country-level policy and capacity comparisons across more than 120 countries
records.boundary: This record adds a global culture-to-platform-to-work route from formal cultural policy and trade through digital access, creator livelihoods, local visibility, gender inclusion, and artistic freedom. It uses UNESCO synthesis, country reporting, and sector statistics; it is not a creator-level panel, causal evaluation, audience-welfare estimate, or proof that cultural policy produces social cohesion or economic growth.

records.title: Digital content creators are becoming information intermediaries faster than support systems can provide verification, ethics, safety, and platform voice
records.source_unit: UNESCO, Behind the Screens in South Africa: Challenges, Opportunities, and Needs of Digital Content Creators, summarized in a UNESCO research release published 1 September 2026
records.geography: South Africa; nationwide survey of digital content creators with supporting interviews and UNESCO Social Media 4 Peace context
records.boundary: This record adds a creator-legitimacy and information-infrastructure subtheme: digital creators are increasingly intermediaries between audiences and information, while verification, ethics, AI disclosure, legal literacy, safety, and platform voice lag behind their influence. The evidence is a small self-reported survey of 48 creators, 11 interviews, and programme reporting; it is not representative audience evidence, a causal misinformation study, a platform audit, a creator-income study, or proof that training changes outcomes.

records.title: Culture is being measured as a multidimensional ecosystem linking creative work, participation, equity, infrastructure, environment, and governance
records.source_unit: UNESCO Institute for Statistics, Cultural and Creative Ecosystem Indicators Framework, Draft Report for Global Consultation
records.geography: Globally applicable framework for UNESCO Member States, national statistical offices, ministries of culture, researchers, practitioners, and civil society
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural-measurement and governance route linking creative work, participation, economic value, equity, infrastructure, environment, territory, digital platforms, AI, and public statistical capacity. It records a draft framework and contextual figures, not completed indicators, a public-opinion study, causal cultural impact evidence, or proof that countries can implement comparable measures immediately.

records.title: Cultural-heritage protection is becoming more measurable, but public investment remains sharply uneven across places
records.source_unit: UNESCO Institute for Statistics, Culture 2026 Data Release and SDG 11.4.1 heritage-expenditure indicators
records.geography: Reporting countries and SDG regions, with 2024 or latest available per-capita public expenditure on cultural and natural heritage
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural-public-finance and measurement-capacity route linking heritage spending, regional inequality, post-pandemic budget direction, data visibility, and public stewardship. It is not a complete global spending census, a measure of heritage condition or cultural participation, respondent-level cultural behavior, causal preservation evaluation, or proof that spending produces equitable access or community control.

records.title: Emergencies intensify gendered precarity in cultural work while women’s cultural labor sustains heritage, community resilience and recovery
records.source_unit: UNESCO, Voices of Courage: A Global Survey on Women, Culture and Emergencies
records.geography: More than 120 countries; women artists, cultural professionals and heritage professionals
records.boundary: This record adds a gendered cultural-emergency layer: crisis exposure moves through safety, displacement, unpaid care, funding, market access, artistic freedom and institutional recognition, while women’s cultural work helps sustain heritage, solidarity and recovery. It is a UNESCO global survey page with testimonies and case studies, not a fully documented probability sample, administrative crisis census, causal resilience evaluation or proof that cultural work replaces material protection.

records.title: Freedom of expression and information integrity are becoming public-infrastructure conditions for democratic accountability, while platforms and AI reshape who controls discourse
records.source_unit: UNESCO, World Trends in Freedom of Expression and Media Development: Global Report 2022/2025
records.geography: Global freedom of expression, journalism, media development, information integrity, digital platforms, AI, and public access to information
records.boundary: This record adds an information-as-public-good route linking press freedom, journalism, institutional checks, platforms, AI, information integrity, safety, public access, and democratic accountability. It is not individual media-use, persuasion, voting, trust, journalist respondent, or audience-level data, and it does not establish that the reported global index decline caused any particular political behavior.

records.title: Youth-led peace-building is being framed as a cultural and institutional question about participation, shared futures, and the mandate of global organizations
records.source_unit: UNESCO, Young Leaders Call for a New Culture of Peace, September 2026
records.geography: Young leaders from 135 countries engaging UNESCO and partners on the future of peace, culture, and multilateral institutions
records.boundary: This record adds a youth-led cultural and civic-participation route from peace reflection through multilateral dialogue, institutional legitimacy, shared futures, and possible agenda-setting. It is a selected participatory process, not representative youth opinion, a conflict dataset, a causal peace intervention, or proof of institutional implementation.

records.title: Climate governance is recruiting entertainment and cultural sectors as public-engagement, storytelling, and decarbonization infrastructure
records.source_unit: UN Climate Change / UNFCCC, New strategy for the Entertainment and Culture for Climate Action initiative unveiled at Climate Week NYC, 24 September 2026
records.geography: Global climate-governance initiative with sector workstreams and place-based implementation
records.boundary: This record adds a culture-to-climate-governance route from storytelling, sector organization, and place-based cultural work through public engagement and decarbonization implementation. It is a strategy announcement, not an impact evaluation, audience survey, emissions inventory, or proof that cultural action changes climate behavior.

records.title: Young adults continue to value partnership and parenthood, but housing, financial security, employment, and social uncertainty constrain the futures they can realize
records.source_unit: United Nations Population Fund, Lives, Choices and Futures: Demographic Futures Survey
records.geography: Comparative views of Internet-connected young adults aged 18–39 across 73 countries and seven regional groupings
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative youth family-formation, housing, employment-security, care, reproductive-agency, and future-expectations route. It uses the publication's aggregate survey results and preserves its non-nationally-representative Internet-connected frame; it is not raw respondent-level data, an individual fertility history, a causal fertility estimate, or a population forecast.

records.title: Maternal and newborn outcomes depend on care systems, midwifery capacity, emergency continuity, and data accountability
records.source_unit: UNFPA, Maternal and Newborn Health Fund 2025 Impact Report
records.geography: 44 UNFPA Maternal and Newborn Health Fund partner countries, including high-burden and humanitarian settings
records.boundary: This record adds a reproductive and maternal-health infrastructure route linking mortality, midwives, delivery care, emergency continuity, commodities, community health, survivor reintegration, and data accountability. It is an aggregate programme impact report, not clinical records, patient histories, respondent-level data, or a causal evaluation of every Fund-supported intervention.

records.title: Reproductive choice depends on commodity access, last-mile logistics, domestic financing, and supply-chain resilience
records.source_unit: UNFPA, UNFPA Supplies Partnership Annual Report 2025
records.geography: 54 UNFPA Supplies Partnership partner countries, including remote, rural, low-income, and humanitarian settings
records.boundary: This record adds a reproductive-commodity route linking contraceptive access, product choice, last-mile logistics, domestic financing, donor matching, health-system resilience, household agency, and modelled economic returns. It is an aggregate programme report, not individual purchase histories, clinical records, respondent-level behavior, or a causal evaluation of every estimated impact.

records.title: Central Sahel displacement is compounding insecurity, climate pressure, and strain on host-community services and infrastructure
records.source_unit: UNHCR, Salih calls for greater investment in protection and solutions in the Central Sahel, 21 September 2026
records.geography: Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger, displaced people, refugees, and host communities in the Central Sahel
records.boundary: This record adds a current Central Sahel route from insecurity and climate pressure through forced displacement, host-community capacity, local services, infrastructure, protection, and durable solutions. It is a bounded public briefing, not a full displacement database, causal conflict model, household panel, service evaluation, or proof of safe and durable return.

records.title: Protracted displacement is being managed as a long-term social and development-system problem while humanitarian funding remains structurally inadequate
records.source_unit: UNHCR, Global Appeal 2026
records.geography: Global forced displacement and statelessness across 128 countries and territories, including host communities and displacement-affected areas
records.boundary: This record adds a global displacement-and-capacity signal linking forced displacement, statelessness, humanitarian funding, host systems, legal recognition, services, work, economic inclusion, and durable solutions. It is a UNHCR planning appeal, not a realized displacement count, funding-outcome evaluation, respondent-level dataset, or proof that economic inclusion and development partnerships produce durable protection or agency.

records.title: Displacement protection is increasingly constrained by funding flexibility, operational capacity, legal access, and the ability to connect aid to work and local systems
records.source_unit: UNHCR Global Report 2025, published June 2026
records.geography: UNHCR global protection and assistance operations in 2025, including refugee, asylum-seeker, internally displaced, returnee, and stateless populations
records.boundary: This record adds a displacement-to-protection-capacity-to-access route linking humanitarian funding, earmarking, staffing, legal status, work access, national systems, and durable pathways. It is not respondent-level data, an individual service-receipt file, a causal estimate of funding effects, or proof that formal access became safe, adequate, durable, or equally distributed.

records.title: Forced displacement eased from its 2024 peak but remains a vast, concentrated, and difficult-to-reintegrate global condition
records.source_unit: UNHCR Global Trends 2025, published June 2026

records.boundary: This record adds a global forced-displacement, hosting, return, and reintegration route. It is not respondent-level migration data, does not estimate individual trajectories or causes of movement, and does not establish that a return was voluntary, safe, durable, or politically stabilizing.

records.title: Satellite monitoring is filling the time between displacement surveys, extending socioeconomic visibility while leaving verification and coverage limits open

records.title: Refugee self-reliance is constrained by the conversion gap between productive inputs, land, formal finance, documentation, and downstream markets

records.geography: Uganda refugee-hosting areas, including South Sudanese, Congolese, Sudanese, other refugee, and host-community populations
records.boundary: This record adds an operational refugee-livelihood route linking land, inputs, skills, producer organizations, market access, formalization, finance, documentation, and self-reliance. It is a partner-reporting dashboard with preliminary funding data, not a representative household panel, causal programme evaluation, or proof of sustained income, employment, food security, or durable refugee-host integration.

records.title: Children’s climate risk is increasingly a compound exposure and social-service-capacity problem
records.source_unit: UNICEF Children's Climate Risk Report 2026 and Global Child Hazard Database / Children’s Climate Risk Framework

It does not infer individual child harm, family welfare, causal service effects, or adaptation success from modeled exposure and framework indicators.

records.title: Child-survival gains depend on health, nutrition, immunization, and WASH systems whose returns extend into economic resilience and security
records.source_unit: UNICEF, The Child Survival Dividend: How saving children's lives generates compounding returns for economic prosperity, global security and our shared humanity
records.geography: Global child-survival and public-health investment evidence with attention to immunization, nutrition, health systems, WASH, financing, debt, aid, and security
records.boundary: This record adds a child-survival and public-health investment route linking mortality, immunization, nutrition, health systems, WASH, human capital, economic resilience, security, aid, debt, and political capacity. It uses publication-level aggregate evidence, not child-level medical records, household health histories, respondent-level trust measures, or causal return estimates for a specific programme.

records.title: Education systems are being asked to deliver learning, equity, and future skills while institutions built for an earlier era face technological, social, and environmental change

records.title: Education policy is being reframed as a whole-system infrastructure problem linking learning, teachers, AI, crisis continuity, and future work
records.source_unit: UNICEF Education Strategy 2026: Shaping the Future of Learning, published September 2026

records.boundary: This record adds a whole-system education route linking learning outcomes, teacher conditions, AI and EdTech, crisis continuity, disability, gender, climate, migration, household vulnerability, and future work. It records UNICEF's strategy, targets, and global evidence frame, not achieved target results, causal effects, harmonized country data, or proof that technology improves learning.

records.title: Child undernutrition is shaped by environmental exposures and public-service conditions across the first 1,000 days
records.source_unit: UNICEF, Environmental determinants of undernutrition and micronutrient deficiencies in children
records.geography: Global child nutrition and environmental-health framework focused on physical, chemical, biological, climate, and WASH exposures
records.boundary: This record adds an environmental-nutrition route linking the first 1,000 days, WASH, physical, chemical, and biological hazards, climate, public services, household buffers, and life-course capability. It uses a technical publication-level synthesis, not child-level exposure histories, clinical nutrition records, household food diaries, or causal estimates of any single hazard.

records.title: Child poverty policy is shifting toward integrated social protection systems that combine cash, public budgets, care, inclusion and crisis response
records.source_unit: UNICEF, Global Annual Results Report 2025: Goal Area 5

records.boundary: This record adds an institutional trend: child-poverty response is being organized as integrated social infrastructure linking cash, budgets, registries, payment systems, care, disability inclusion and crisis response. It is a UNICEF programme-results report, not a household panel, prevalence estimate, impact evaluation or respondent-level dataset.

records.title: Children on the move are being framed as a long-term inclusion and social-infrastructure challenge, not only a border or emergency issue
records.source_unit: UNICEF Global Programme Framework for Children on the Move, published June 2026
records.geography: Global child migration and displacement policy and programming, with implementation across regions and country offices
records.boundary: This record adds a child-mobility governance route linking root causes, protection, learning, basic services, discrimination, social cohesion, participation, integration, and durable solutions. It uses a global rights-based programme framework, not child-level migration histories, a complete needs or service-coverage census, representative attitudes of host communities, causal programme evaluation, or proof of successful integration.

records.title: Children’s changing capacities require rights-respecting support that combines development, protection, and participation
records.source_unit: UNICEF Innocenti, Growing with Rights: Understanding and supporting the evolving capacities of the child
records.geography: Global child-rights and childhood-development framework under changing social, climate, fragile-context, and digital conditions

It uses a global conceptual synthesis, not child-level developmental histories, representative participation rates, causal effects of digital or climate exposure, or proof that institutions respect or act on children’s views.

records.title: Economic inequality in wealthy countries continues to stratify children’s health, well-being, skills, and perceived opportunity

records.boundary: This record adds a wealthy-country child-inequality route linking income distribution to poverty, health, mental well-being, skills, perceived opportunity, and child participation. It uses comparative publication-level aggregate evidence and bounded child well-being measures, not household panel histories, respondent-level causal data, clinical records, or proof that income inequality alone causes any outcome.

records.title: Climate hazards are becoming an education-disruption pathway that concentrates learning and lifetime-earnings risks in lower-income countries
records.source_unit: UNICEF, Learning Interrupted: Global Snapshot on Climate-related School Disruptions in 2025

It is not student-level attendance, learning assessment, household adaptation, or individual earnings data, and the modeled economic estimate is not an observed personal loss.

records.title: Children’s futures are being shaped by interacting geopolitical, fiscal, climate, digital, and social-system pressures
records.source_unit: UNICEF Innocenti, Prospects for Children in 2026: A Global Outlook Overview, The Future for Children in a Volatile World
records.geography: Global child prospects under technological, geopolitical, public-finance, climate, environmental, and social-contract change
records.boundary: This record adds a child-centred foresight route linking geopolitics, fiscal space, AI, work, climate, public services, NGOs, and social protection. It uses a global outlook synthesis, not child-level histories, national budget estimates, causal AI or climate effects, representative forecasts, or proof that resilience tools have been implemented.

records.title: Child poverty is a multidimensional deprivation shaped by household resources, services, social protection, and converging crises
records.source_unit: UNICEF, The State of the World's Children 2025: Ending Child Poverty: Our Shared Imperative
records.geography: Global child-poverty, deprivation, social-protection, climate, conflict, service, and public-finance evidence with low-, middle-, and high-income comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a child-poverty route linking monetary resources to sanitation, housing, nutrition, education, healthcare, social protection, caregiver work, climate hazards, conflict, debt, and public budgets. It uses publication-level aggregate evidence, not child-level panel histories, household spending microdata, respondent-level deprivation interviews, or causal estimates of any single service or fiscal policy.

records.title: Digital platforms are becoming an abuse-enablement and reporting-governance layer for children
records.source_unit: UNICEF Through Children's Eyes: How Digital Technologies Enable Child Sexual Abuse and Disrupting Harm research
records.geography: 21 countries; internet-using children aged 12-17, with research conducted across two survey rounds
records.boundary: This record adds a digital child-safety and institutional-trust route connecting platform design, abuse enablement, disclosure, reporting, child protection, mental-health association, and regulation. It does not identify individual victims, perpetrators, platforms' legal liability, causal effects, or all-child prevalence beyond the source's internet-using sample.

records.title: Future-ready industrialization must connect green transition, AI, value-chain change, food systems, jobs, and social inclusion
records.source_unit: United Nations Industrial Development Organization, Industrial Development Report 2026: The Future of Industrialization
records.geography: Global industrial development, manufacturing, value chains, energy and green transition, AI, demographics, food systems, and developing economies
records.boundary: This record adds a global industrialization, green transition, AI, value-chain, demographic, food-system, and job-quality route. It uses report-level comparative analysis, not individual employment histories, firm microdata, causal industrial-policy estimates, household food diaries, or proof that industrial growth produces inclusive welfare.

records.title: Drug consumption and synthetic-market capacity are expanding while treatment access remains scarce and gendered
records.source_unit: UNODC World Drug Report 2025, global aggregate estimates and drug-market analysis
records.geography: Global; estimates cover people aged 15-64 and drug-market indicators with substance- and region-specific coverage
records.boundary: This record adds a global drug-consumption, illicit-market, treatment-access, gender, and service-capacity route. records.title: Drug markets are changing while harm, treatment access, and enforcement pathways remain uneven across regions
records.source_unit: UNODC, World Drug Report 2026 data portal
records.geography: Global drug cultivation, health-harm, treatment, and market reporting across regions and subregions
records.boundary: This record adds an aggregate drug-market, public-health, treatment-access, and institutional-response route. It is not an individual substance-use panel, clinical effectiveness study, respondent-level treatment record, or causal estimate of enforcement or drug-market policy.

records.title: AI is being debated as a transformation of human trust, culture, labor, knowledge, and responsibility rather than only as a technical capability
records.source_unit: UN Office for Partnerships, AI and Human Development: Dispatches from Cairo, Mexico City, Xi'an and Rome
records.geography: Global cross-disciplinary AI and human-development conversations held in Cairo, Mexico City, Xi'an, and Rome

records.title: Compounding geopolitical, economic, climate, food, and displacement shocks are narrowing development policy space and testing resilience systems
records.source_unit: UN Sustainable Development Group / UNDP and UN Development Coordination Office, From Shock to Resilience: Protecting Development Gains Amid Compounding Crises, September 2026

records.boundary: This record adds a development-resilience route from stacked geopolitical, energy, food, climate, conflict, and displacement shocks through fiscal space, public systems, livelihoods, and response capacity.
