records.source_unit: United Nations University Institute for Water, Environment and Health, Global Water Bankruptcy: Living Beyond Our Hydrological Means in the Post-Crisis Era
records.geography: Global river basins, aquifers, wetlands, soils, rivers, glaciers, water users, and water-governance systems
records.boundary: This record adds a hydrological-overshoot and natural-capital route across chronic water stress, aquifers, basins, ecosystems, food, health, livelihoods, governance, equity, and cooperation. It uses aggregate UNU-INWEH report analysis, not respondent-level water histories, individual consumption records, basin-level causal forecasts, household utility bills, or proof that every water system has crossed an irreversible threshold.

records.title: Youth mental health is being reframed as an ecosystem problem spanning housing, work, digital life, climate and belonging
records.source_unit: United Nations Youth Office, Youth Mental Health and Well-being Flagship Initiative; produced with the United Nations University International Institute for Global Health and launched in 2026

records.boundary: This record captures a global policy and narrative shift: youth mental health is being positioned as a systems and ecosystem issue involving housing, education, work, digital life, climate, peace, culture and youth agency. records.title: Youth mental health is being reframed as an ecosystem condition shaped by work, housing, digital life, climate, culture, and agency
records.source_unit: United Nations University Global Health and United Nations Youth Office, Youth Mental Health & Well-Being in an Uncertain World: A Global Call to Action, published 23 September 2026
records.geography: Global youth mental-health and well-being ecosystem, with attention to young people aged 15–35 and culturally adaptable local systems
records.boundary: This record adds an ecosystem and youth-agency route linking mental health to education, work, housing, peace, climate, digital spaces, community, culture, and spirituality. It uses a global framework and cited aggregate health evidence, not respondent-level mental-health histories, clinical diagnoses, representative youth participation rates, causal effects, or proof that the proposed model has been implemented.

records.title: Volunteer action is being reframed as measurable social infrastructure linking solidarity, trust, development, and public capacity
records.source_unit: United Nations Volunteers, 2026 State of the World’s Volunteerism Report: Volunteerism and its Measurements

records.boundary: This record adds a global volunteerism and social-infrastructure route linking mutual aid, trust, social cohesion, crisis response, development, measurement, inclusion, and public capacity. It uses UNV’s modelled estimates, research synthesis, case studies, and proposed GIVE framework; it is not a respondent-level atlas dataset, causal evaluation, proof that volunteering substitutes for public services, or universal measure of all solidarity and civic action.

records.title: Gen Z cultural participation is being framed as a search for control, community and visible local agency
records.source_unit: The Up and Up, Don't Tell Me What To Do: Our Fall Trend Report—Gen Z is Opting In to the Things They Can Control, September 1, 2026

records.boundary: This record identifies a youth-culture, agency, anti-algorithm, local-community and visible-political-impact subtheme. It does not establish population prevalence, representative generational change, actual time or spending behavior, platform exit, turnout, local institutional effects, or causal links between control, distrust and participation.

records.title: Rapid fertility decline and longer lives are creating older, sometimes shrinking populations that require new arrangements for care, work, technology, and disaster resilience
records.source_unit: U.S. Census Bureau, An Aging World: 2025, Report P95-26-1
records.geography: Global population aging across countries and regions, with socioeconomic and demographic coverage where data are available and projections through 2060
records.boundary: This record adds a demographic-structure route across falling fertility, longevity, population shrinkage, aging, households, care, work, age-friendly communities, AI, health systems, and humanitarian disasters. records.geography: 139 economies and global science-and-technology innovation clusters, including cross-border metropolitan regions
records.boundary: This record adds innovation-system and cluster-concentration evidence to the firm, infrastructure, work, and geopolitical map. It is not firm-level causal evidence, does not estimate local distribution or household outcomes, and does not establish that innovation concentration produces or reduces inequality, political legitimacy, or state power.

records.title: Innovation advantage depends on connected capability ecosystems, while most economies leave substantial scientific and technological potential unused
records.source_unit: World Intellectual Property Organization, Innovation Capabilities Outlook 2026
records.geography: 193-country global innovation ecosystem comparison across science, technology, entrepreneurship, and production capabilities, using data spanning 2001-2023
records.boundary: This record adds an innovation-ecosystem route across science, technology, entrepreneurship, production, complexity, diversification, regional development, and capability power. It uses aggregate WIPO and Harvard Growth Lab analysis, not respondent-level worker histories, firm case files, individual patent attribution, causal technology forecasts, or proof that capability concentration produces identical social outcomes everywhere.

records.title: Technological progress creates broad productivity only when innovation diffuses across economies through capable ecosystems
records.source_unit: World Intellectual Property Organization, World Intellectual Property Report 2026: Technology on the Move
records.geography: Global technology invention, adoption, diffusion across economies, and innovation ecosystems
records.boundary: This record adds a global technology-diffusion, adoption, innovation-ecosystem, work, consumer, and governance route. It uses report-level comparative analysis, not respondent-level technology diaries, individual employment histories, causal productivity estimates, or proof that frontier invention automatically diffuses or improves welfare.

records.title: Inequality is crossing wealth, climate responsibility, unpaid care, global finance, and political representation rather than remaining a single income gap
records.source_unit: World Inequality Lab, World Inequality Report 2026
records.geography: Global income, wealth, gender, climate, financial, regional, taxation, and political inequality across countries and regions
records.boundary: This record adds a cross-domain inequality route across income, wealth, capital-linked climate responsibility, unpaid care, human-capital access, global finance, taxation, territorial divides, and democratic coalitions. It uses World Inequality Lab aggregate distributional estimates and synthesis, not respondent-level income or political histories, household budgets, firm ownership files, individual emissions footprints, causal climate effects, or proof that any single policy produces equal outcomes everywhere.

records.title: Air pollution and climate risk are converging through wildfire smoke, heat-driven ozone, aerosols, and monitoring gaps
records.source_unit: World Meteorological Organization Air Quality and Climate Bulletin No. 6, September 2026
records.geography: Global air-quality and climate linkages, with 2025 atmospheric evidence and regional examples
records.boundary: This record adds an air-quality and climate-health route linking wildfire smoke, PM2.5, ground-level ozone, aerosols, black carbon, microplastics, atmospheric observations, and coordinated policy. It uses global and regional scientific synthesis, not personal exposure histories, clinical records, local sensor coverage, causal mortality estimates for every population, or proof that air-quality policy improved outcomes.

records.title: The global water cycle is becoming more erratic while freshwater storage and glacier buffers decline
records.source_unit: World Meteorological Organization, State of Global Water Resources 2025, published 17 September 2026
records.geography: Global hydrological cycle, river basins, groundwater, terrestrial water storage, snow, glaciers, and water-related extremes
records.boundary: This record adds a physical water-system and measurement-capacity route linking river flows, storage, groundwater, glaciers, disasters, early warning, transboundary governance, cities, food, energy, health, and household exposure. It uses global modelled, satellite, and reported hydrological evidence, not local water bills, household access histories, basin-level causal impacts, or proof that better data produced better protection.

records.title: Disaster policy faces a coverage-versus-intensity choice, with lower-income populations carrying large poverty and well-being losses
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11334, Coverage or Intensity of Support? Adaptive Social Protection to Reduce Disaster-Related Poverty
records.geography: 131 countries, with global estimates of disaster-related poverty and modeled adaptive social-protection expansion scenarios
records.boundary: This record adds an adaptive-social-protection route linking natural hazards to poverty, consumption room, well-being, coverage, benefit intensity, targeting, fiscal capacity and institutional delivery. It is modeled cross-country scenario evidence, not respondent-level data, a disaster-loss census, an implementation audit or proof that support arrives in time.

records.title: Regional integration becomes usable when trade rules are enforceable, defensive instruments disciplined, and people can move
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11449, Beneath the Surface: Deep Trade Agreements and the Potential of a Deeper AfCFTA
records.geography: African Continental Free Trade Area and worldwide trade-agreement comparison, with counterfactual estimates for African economies in the sample
records.boundary: This record adds regional-integration depth as a legal, mobility, firm, and geopolitical mechanism. It does not establish that AfCFTA implementation will produce the modeled GDP gain, that aggregate trade gains will be equally distributed, or that deep provisions automatically create household welfare, jobs, voice, or consumer affordability.

records.title: Regional integration becomes real when systems interoperate: the hidden politics of making African markets work together
records.source_unit: World Bank, Integrating Africa: From Threads to Hubs, September 2026
records.geography: Sub-Saharan Africa, the African Continental Free Trade Area, African Union, Regional Economic Communities, corridors and cross-border production networks
records.boundary: This record identifies a geopolitical-economic interoperability and regional-public-goods subtheme. It does not establish that AfCFTA implementation, interoperable systems, deeper agreements, corridors, power pools, digital networks or regional institutions will increase trade, lower prices, create jobs, reduce conflict, improve consumer welfare or distribute gains equitably; those require named corridor, firm, trader, household and institutional episodes with observed delivery, cost, access, remedy and political response.

records.title: Public-sector reform ideas diffuse faster than the institutional capacity and political conditions needed to sustain them
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11457, What Works for Public Sector Reform in Africa? Preliminary Evidence on New Public Management Reforms in World Bank Projects
records.geography: Sub-Saharan Africa; World Bank-financed public-sector reform projects implemented between 2010 and 2023, supplemented by four qualitative case studies
records.boundary: This record adds reform-design-to-state-capacity conversion as an institutional and legitimacy mechanism. It is not a representative evaluation of all African public-sector reform, not evidence that full implementation improves citizen outcomes, and not proof that New Public Management reforms are universally ineffective or that one reform family always dominates.

records.title: Global development progress is slowing unevenly as work, poverty, infrastructure, and digital access diverge by place
records.source_unit: World Bank, Atlas of Global Development 2026
records.geography: Global country comparisons across people, prosperity, planet, infrastructure, and digital transformation
records.boundary: This record adds a cross-domain global-development, gender-work, poverty-geography, infrastructure-access, and digital-divide route. It uses World Bank indicator comparisons and report-level synthesis, not respondent-level records, individual income histories, household time diaries, causal infrastructure estimates, or proof that country-level progress translates evenly into lived experience.

records.title: Economic growth is becoming less reliably job-creating as Bangladesh’s sectoral employment elasticities shift
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 111458, Structural Shift in Job Creation: Evidence from Bangladesh
records.geography: Bangladesh, with comparative Okun’s-law analysis involving six other Asian countries and sectoral employment-elasticity estimates for 2003-2024
records.boundary: This record adds a growth-to-job-quality and sectoral-conversion mechanism. It is macro time-series evidence, not a causal worker-level evaluation, a measure of realized household welfare, or proof that services are better than manufacturing or that aggregate growth has no employment benefit.

records.title: Food-tracking salience can change feeding habits and dietary diversity, but not food quantity or child nutrition status by itself
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11461, Food Accounting Salience and Dietary Diversity: A Randomized Impact Evaluation of an Intervention to Track and Improve Young Children's Food Consumption in Bihar, India
records.geography: 2,682 households with children aged 6–24 months across six districts of Bihar, India, in a cluster-randomized intervention delivered with frontline-worker support
records.boundary: This record adds a causal salience-and-tracking-to-feeding-behavior and dietary-diversity route, with explicit limits around food quantity, child MUAC, persistence, income and food availability, frontline-worker delivery, and household heterogeneity. It does not establish long-run nutrition or growth effects, food-security improvement, universal transferability, or that behavior tools can substitute for affordable diverse food and reliable care infrastructure.

records.title: Cambodia's energy, remittance, and credit shock tests whether returning workers can become a demographic dividend before the care and human-capital window closes
records.source_unit: World Bank, Cambodia Economic Update June 2026: Forever Young? Cambodia's Demographic Transition and the Road to Vision 2050
records.geography: Cambodia; national macroeconomy, households, returning migrant workers, labor market, demographic transition, human capital, care economy, and trade system
records.boundary: This comparative record adds a shock-to-demography-to-capacity route: energy and remittance disruption, household purchasing power, returning-worker reintegration, demographic timing, human capital, care infrastructure, structured migration, and fiscal or labor-market institutions. It does not infer individual worker trajectories, job quality, benefit receipt, care outcomes, causal effects of a reform, or durable household recovery.

records.title: Motherhood shifts career advancement into a flexibility trade-off inside a global organization
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11459, What Drives Child Penalties? Evidence from a Global Organization
records.geography: Headquarters-based professional staff at the World Bank Group, spanning employees from more than 190 countries; analysis period 1988-2024
records.boundary: This record adds a within-organization mechanism linking parenthood to advancement, responsibility allocation, travel, job sorting, and flexibility. It is causal evidence for the studied World Bank professional-staff setting, not proof of a universal motherhood penalty, discriminatory intent, household welfare loss, or long-run labor-market effects across populations.

records.title: China’s trade rise creates asymmetric gains and competitive pressure while deepening structural dependence for developing economies
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11467, Growing in China’s shadow
records.geography: Developing economies observed annually from 1995-2019, with extended descriptive and robustness evidence through 2023, using pre-determined 1995 trade-structure exposure to China
records.boundary: This record adds a China-centered geopolitical trade-spillover and structural-dependence mechanism. It is shift-share and panel evidence about GDP growth and trade exposure, not direct evidence about household welfare, consumer prices, employment quality, political legitimacy, or causal reform failure. The structural-transformation and reform pathways are explicitly presented as suggestive or correlational and require country, firm, worker, and household follow-through.

records.title: Cloud procurement becomes a public-capability and vendor-dependency decision
records.source_unit: World Bank, Enabling Cloud Procurement: A Guide for the Public Sector
records.geography: Public-sector ministries and agencies; comparative procurement and governance guidance drawing on public-cloud and digital-transformation cases
records.boundary: This record adds a procurement-to-public-capability mechanism linking cloud contracting to AI and data capacity, supplier market structure, lock-in, security, continuity, privacy, and public-service legitimacy. It is a World Bank implementation guide, not causal evidence that centralization, cloud adoption, or multi-cloud improves outcomes; all scenario benefits require live procurement and service audits.

records.title: Colombia’s poverty and mobility gaps are territorial: uneven public-service capacity and connectivity shape who can convert cities and growth into opportunity
records.source_unit: World Bank, Trajectories: Prosperity and Poverty Reduction in the Colombian Territory, 2026
records.geography: Colombia’s departments and municipalities, poorer territories, cities, and populations experiencing uneven poverty reduction and social mobility
records.boundary: This record adds a Colombia-specific territorial route from poverty and circumstances at birth through service access, connectivity, cities, labor markets, social mobility, and subnational institutional capacity. It is not an individual mobility prediction, causal service evaluation, household panel, or proof that city migration or decentralization produces inclusive prosperity.

records.title: Demographic divergence is redistributing labor, care, migration, and growth opportunities across countries
records.source_unit: World Bank, Global Monitoring Report 2026: Demographic Trends Are Shaping Economic Growth
records.geography: Global country and regional comparison of population growth, age structure, labor supply, migration, human capital, and old-age support
records.boundary: This record adds a demographic-structure route linking aging, youth-heavy poverty regions, labor supply, care, old-age support, migration, trade, capital, human capital, and conflict or fragility. It uses publication-level aggregate evidence, not individual fertility histories, respondent-level labor trajectories, household care diaries, or causal estimates of migration or demographic policy effects.

records.title: Digital exclusion is shifting from a network-coverage problem toward affordability, skills, safety, relevance, and gendered use barriers
records.source_unit: World Bank Gender Data Portal, Beyond Coverage: Closing Gaps in Digital Access and Use in Low- and Middle-Income Countries, published 5 May 2026
records.geography: Low- and middle-income countries, with Global Findex Digital Connectivity Tracker 2025 evidence from 123 LMICs and an 81-country usage-gap sample
records.boundary: This record adds a digital-inclusion route linking coverage, actual Internet use, affordability, skills, relevant content, safety, privacy, gender norms, and meaningful economic and civic participation. It uses aggregate cross-country data and hypothetical scenario analysis, not respondent-level digital histories, platform-use logs, causal intervention effects, a complete accessibility census, or proof that connection produces equal benefits.

records.title: Digital financial inclusion depends on competitive infrastructure, not access rules alone
records.source_unit: World Bank, Competition as a Catalyst for Digital Financial Services Usage: Chapeau Paper, September 2026
records.geography: Comparative case studies of Brazil, Ghana, India, Jamaica, Nigeria, and the Philippines, with global financial-inclusion context
records.boundary: This record adds a competition-and-interoperability-to-active-digital-use mechanism that extends the prior digital-credit and consumer-protection findings. It is a comparative case-study synthesis, not a causal evaluation, universal country ranking, or direct measure of household welfare; the next test is whether specific infrastructure and governance reforms change switching, transaction costs, fraud exposure, trust, active usage, and distributional access without creating new concentration or single-point-of-failure risks.

records.title: Digital access is expanding while infrastructure quality, data intensity, computing capacity, and skills remain sharply stratified by country income
records.source_unit: World Bank, Digital Progress and Trends Report 2025: Strengthening AI Foundations
records.geography: Global; high-income, upper-middle-income, lower-middle-income, and low-income country groups, with regional comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds infrastructure quality, data intensity, affordability, skill, and computing-capacity layers beneath digital participation and consumer behavior. It does not establish person-level access, platform outcomes, AI productivity, cultural participation, firm ownership, or household welfare.

records.title: Ecuador’s subnational infrastructure strategy routes external finance through a development bank, project preparation, and local-government capacity
records.source_unit: World Bank Group press release on Ecuador subnational infrastructure finance, published September 24, 2026
records.geography: Ecuador; local governments, provincial governments, public service providers, and national development-bank intermediary
records.boundary: This comparative record adds a subnational finance, intermediary-capacity, project-preparation, and infrastructure-target layer. It does not infer disbursement, construction, service access, affordability, local-government fiscal sustainability, private investment, job creation, climate resilience, or household benefit from the announcement.

records.title: Crisis protection is becoming a capability problem: systems must scale up temporarily and scale down credibly
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11454, Get Ready: What Lessons for Social Protection from the Recent Energy Crisis?
records.geography: Global country-response review covering the March-May 2026 energy crisis, with comparisons to responses during the 2008, 2020, and 2022 crises
records.boundary: This record adds crisis scalability and policy-instrument choice as a social-protection, household-cost, and legitimacy mechanism. It does not estimate household welfare, receipt, poverty reduction, trust, or causal protection effects, and it does not establish that subsidies are always inferior to transfers or that automatic triggers work equally across countries.

records.title: Ethiopia’s justice system shows that institutional performance, practical access, and legitimacy can diverge
records.source_unit: World Bank, Improving Justice Delivery in Ethiopia: A 2025 JUPITER Assessment, published 2026
records.geography: Ethiopia, with federal courts, regional statutory courts, and customary or cultural justice providers, including a detailed Oromia case
records.boundary: This record adds a justice-throughput-to-lived-access-and-legitimacy mechanism. It is a country assessment, not a causal evaluation of digitalization, customary-court recognition, staffing, budgets, or judicial independence; reported survey and administrative figures are bounded by geography, data quality, and institutional coverage, and the next test is whether reforms improve fair resolution, user access, time, quality, and trust across statutory and customary pathways.

records.title: Ethiopia’s first land accounts make land-cover change legible to agriculture, urban, water, and biodiversity policy
records.source_unit: World Bank, Land Accounts for Ethiopia, 2013 to 2022, 1st Edition
records.geography: Ethiopia nationally, with subnational case accounts for the Abay (Blue Nile) and Awash River Basins
records.boundary: This record adds a natural-capital-accounting-to-policy-feedback mechanism. It is a first-edition spatial account of 2013 and 2022 land cover, not causal evidence about why land changed, whether restoration is durable, whether households benefit, or whether standardized accounts alter decisions; continuous monitoring, tenure, enforcement, ecosystem, water, and livelihood outcomes remain open tests.

records.title: Fragility persists when weak institutions, repeated shocks, fiscal constraint, and human-capital loss reinforce one another
records.source_unit: World Bank, Fragile and Conflict-Affected Situations: Intertwined Crises, Multiple Vulnerabilities
records.geography: Economies classified as fragile and conflict-affected situations, with comparisons to other developing countries and global poverty, health, education, food, debt, and growth outcomes
records.boundary: This record adds a fragility-to-poverty and state-capacity route across persistent classification, overlapping shocks, conflict scarring, poverty, food insecurity, health, education, infrastructure, and debt. It uses aggregate World Bank analysis, not household respondent histories, individual health or schooling records, local case files, causal conflict forecasts, or proof that every FCS economy follows the same pathway.

records.title: Digital credit turns consumer over-indebtedness into a product-design, data, and recovery-system problem
records.source_unit: World Bank, Policy Note: Addressing Financial Consumer Over-Indebtedness, Prosperity Insight Series, July 2026
records.geography: Global policy synthesis, with examples from emerging markets and developing economies and comparative references to Australia, Brazil, Canada, Ethiopia, the European Union, India, Indonesia, the Philippines, South Africa, Tanzania, the United Kingdom, and the United States
records.boundary: This record adds a digital-credit-to-household-room and institutional-recovery mechanism. It is a global policy note, not a harmonized prevalence study, causal evaluation, or universal ranking of regulatory tools; the cited Tanzania default rate and other jurisdictional examples should not be generalized, and the key open test is whether product, data, supervision, debt-advice, and insolvency reforms reduce realized harm without driving vulnerable consumers into more dangerous informal credit.

records.title: Automation may interrupt the expected industrial relocation ladder as aging and protectionism intensify
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11468, Can the Flying Geese Fly Again? Automation and the Pattern of Industrialization
records.geography: China, nine individually reported countries, advanced economies, emerging markets, and World Bank regions in a 16-sector multi-country trade and robotization model
records.boundary: This record adds an automation-to-industrial-relocation and sectoral-task-composition mechanism. It is a calibrated multi-country model, not observed causal evidence that automation preserves manufacturing jobs, improves wages, distributes gains, or changes household consumption. The cultural and social consequences remain open: whether the expected development ladder weakens, which places lose industrial entry, and how workers and consumers experience the resulting concentration require country, firm, and worker-level follow-through.

records.title: Food security remains fragile as fertilizer costs, El Niño risk, and unequal domestic food inflation transmit shocks unevenly across income groups
records.source_unit: World Bank Food Security Update, latest update June 2026 with data as of 22 June 2026
records.geography: Global food and nutrition security, domestic food inflation across 169 countries, and income-group and regional exposure
records.boundary: This record adds an income-group and household-risk layer to the food-price route, linking domestic food inflation and real price pressure to fertilizer costs, El Niño scenarios, cereal production, and regional inequality. It uses country-level aggregate and conditional scenario evidence, not household purchase histories, diet records, individual food-security transitions, causal welfare estimates, or proof that food insecurity changed for every group.

records.title: The Gambia's growth and girls' educational gains are not yet converting into formal work, earnings, or fiscal capacity for inclusive opportunity
records.source_unit: World Bank, The Gambia Economic Update: Learning Without Earning: Women's Educational Gains and Labor Market Constraints, plus Creating Fiscal Space to Sustain Growth and Boost Job Creation, released June 9, 2026
records.geography: The Gambia; national growth, poverty, education, labor, gender, tourism, remittances, fiscal, subsidy, public-investment, and youth systems
records.boundary: This comparative record adds an education-to-employment and fiscal-capacity route linking growth, poverty, informality, youth exclusion, gendered education and work, care, land, finance, tourism, remittances, taxation, subsidies, and public investment. It does not infer individual educational trajectories, job quality, empowerment, service receipt, causal reform effects, or durable household security.

records.title: Tax and budget systems are an undercounted mechanism of gendered economic opportunity: fiscal rules can either widen care and work penalties or finance the institutions that reduce them
records.source_unit: World Bank Women, Business and the Law, Tax and Gender Budgeting thematic data and Reforming Tax and Budget Systems for Gender Equality brief
records.geography: Global fiscal-policy framework with pilot data across 81 economies for tax and 50 economies for gender-responsive budgeting
records.boundary: This record adds fiscal systems as a mechanism between formal gender rights and lived economic opportunity. It is a global pilot and policy synthesis, not a household tax-benefit incidence estimate, a causal reform evaluation, a complete measure of unpaid care or proof that gender-responsive budgeting changes outcomes.

records.title: Generative-AI use is expanding rapidly but remains sharply stratified by country income, connectivity, platform localization and digital capability
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11231, Who on Earth Is Using Generative AI? Global Trends and Shifts in 2025
records.geography: Global internet users and country income groups, using traffic to 60 consumer-facing generative-AI tools through mid-2025
records.boundary: This record adds a technology-diffusion and capability-inequality route linking generative-AI web use to platform concentration, country income, infrastructure, localization, language and potential economic participation. It is global traffic-proxy evidence through mid-2025, not respondent-level behavior, complete AI adoption, enterprise deployment, task exposure, causal productivity, labor-market or household-welfare evidence.

records.title: Demand signals can unlock small-firm digital market participation more reliably than training alone
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11460, Barriers to Market Access: Experimental Tests of Supply- and Demand-Side Strategies
records.geography: Small enterprises in Georgia participating in randomized training and demand-incentive experiments, with surveys conducted between 2018 and 2025
records.boundary: This record adds a causal demand-signal-to-digital-market-participation route for small enterprises, with null training, conditional purchase-order, payment-intensity, longer-run catch-up, and baseline-readiness evidence. It does not establish durable profits, employment, productivity, firm survival, broad consumer welfare, universal training failure, or generalization beyond the Georgian experiments.

records.title: Ghana’s preferential tariff access shifts export competition toward non-tariff compliance and traceability capacity
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11471, An Analysis of Ghana’s Good Export Market Access
records.geography: Ghanaian exports to seven major destinations: China, European Union, India, South Africa, Switzerland, United Arab Emirates, and United States
records.boundary: This record adds a tariff-preference-to-compliance-infrastructure mechanism. It is descriptive market-access and regulatory evidence, not proof that NTMs caused export exclusion, that compliance improves farmer welfare, or that digital traceability is complete, trusted, or fairly compensated. Small-firm exclusion, farmer burden, consumer benefit, and political accountability require firm-, farmer-, household-, and implementation-level follow-through.

records.title: Geopolitical energy shocks are narrowing growth and fiscal room unevenly, making debt capacity, buffers, and private investment central to social and institutional resilience
records.source_unit: World Bank Group, Global Economic Prospects, June 2026
records.geography: Global economy, emerging market and developing economies, low-income countries, commodity exporters, firms, households, and public budgets
records.boundary: This record adds a geopolitical-shock-to-growth-to-fiscal-space-to-investment route linking energy prices, inflation, debt, borrowing costs, public budgets, firms, infrastructure, AI adoption, and jobs. It is not respondent-level data, a household welfare estimate, a realized crisis outcome, or proof that fiscal or private-investment recommendations were implemented.

records.title: Mobile connectivity is widening financial access while digital safety, gender, income, and resilience gaps remain
records.source_unit: World Bank, Global Findex Database 2025: Connectivity and Financial Inclusion in the Digital Economy
records.geography: 141 economies, based on nationally representative surveys conducted in 2024
records.boundary: This record adds a global connectivity-to-financial-inclusion route linking mobile access, accounts, payments, saving, gender and income gaps, digital safety, and financial resilience. It uses aggregate publication findings from nationally representative surveys, not respondent-level analysis, personal transaction records, causal welfare estimates, or claims that digital finance automatically improves household security.

records.title: Global growth shocks scar investment announcements unevenly, making geopolitical position part of economic recovery
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11452, The Scars of Global Growth Shocks: Evidence of Uneven Recovery in FDI Announcements
records.geography: Global cross-country and cross-sector foreign-direct-investment project-announcement data, with heterogeneity by country safety, strategic sector, institutions, and geopolitical alignment
records.boundary: This record adds geopolitical positioning and investment-pipeline scarring as a firm, state-power, and household-opportunity mechanism. It is not evidence that announced projects are completed, that FDI creates local jobs or welfare, or that geopolitical alignment alone causes the observed uneven recovery.

records.title: A youth-heavy demographic wave turns jobs into an infrastructure, sector, and social-stability challenge
records.source_unit: World Bank, The Global Jobs Challenge
records.geography: Emerging market and developing economies, with global demographic, labor-market, infrastructure, and sector implications
records.boundary: This record adds a global jobs route linking youth demography, infrastructure, human and digital capital, private finance, priority sectors, technology transitions, poverty, and social stability. It is a publication-level synthesis, not individual employment histories, respondent-level labor data, a country job forecast, or proof that any single policy creates stability.

records.title: Global extreme poverty is declining only marginally while progress remains sharply uneven across regions and exposed to measurement revision
records.source_unit: World Bank September 2026 Global Poverty Update using the Poverty and Inequality Platform
records.geography: Global and regional poverty estimates through 2024 with nowcasts for 2025 and 2026
records.boundary: This record adds a material-pressure and inequality signal linking extreme-poverty measurement, household resources, regional divergence, conflict and data coverage, nowcasting, and revision. It is a World Bank modeled estimate and nowcast, not respondent-level ingestion, a current household panel, multidimensional deprivation measure, causal poverty intervention evaluation, or proof of lived welfare change.

records.title: Development redistributes working time across age and gender through schooling, pensions, social spending, and regulation
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11473, Global Working Hours
records.geography: 160 countries covering 97% of the world population in cross section, with time series spanning more than 20 years in 86 countries
records.boundary: This record adds a development-to-time-allocation mechanism. It measures paid or GDP-producing work through labor-force surveys and does not measure unpaid care, rest, subjective time pressure, job quality, household consumption, bargaining power, or causal policy effects. The gender, age, cultural, consumer, and political implications are hypotheses for follow-through, not direct outcomes established by this cross-country evidence.

records.title: Government AI adoption is broad but shallow, with institutional scaffolding often lagging use
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11466, How Is Government Using Artificial Intelligence?
records.geography: 60 economies across all income levels, surveyed through central digital agencies, sectoral ministries, and management information system leads
records.boundary: This record adds a 60-economy government-AI adoption and institutional-readiness route linking ad hoc use, data and budget constraints, income-varying barriers, governance lag, archetypes, public-worker practice, citizen exposure, and accountable service potential. It does not independently audit AI systems, measure citizen outcomes, establish causal productivity or welfare effects, or treat the four archetypes as permanent country identities.

records.title: Government AI is shifting from isolated pilots toward institutional capacity for evaluation, procurement, accountability, and sustained public-service delivery
records.source_unit: World Bank World Development Report 2026 public-service AI analysis and Policy Research Working Paper WPS11466, How Is Government Using Artificial Intelligence?
records.geography: World Bank evidence across 60 economies and developing-country public-service examples including Ghana, Bangladesh, Brazil, and Thailand
records.boundary: This record adds an institutional-conversion route: government AI moves from pilot visibility to public value only through data and infrastructure readiness, credible evaluation, local adaptation, procurement, staff capacity, auditability, portability, and correction. It does not treat adoption, model performance in demonstrations, or announced frameworks as proof of equitable service delivery, reduced waiting, improved health or education, or democratic legitimacy.

records.title: Hidden-debt revelations create a transparency shock that reprices sovereign risk and fiscal room
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11462, Sovereign Risk Repricing after Hidden-Debt Revelations
records.geography: Seven sovereign hidden-debt revelation episodes during 2005-2025: Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Mozambique, Pakistan, Senegal, Türkiye, and Zambia
records.boundary: This record adds a transparency-to-sovereign-risk repricing mechanism. It is an event-study of market spreads across seven episodes, not evidence that hidden-debt revelations directly caused household welfare loss, public-service decline, austerity, default, or political legitimacy change. Those downstream cultural, social, consumer, and political effects require named country follow-through sources.

records.title: Flood exposure and weak urban coordination can turn location advantage into spatial underperformance
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11444, Evaluating Spatial Underperformance: A Spatial Computable General Equilibrium Model Applied to Ho Chi Minh City, September 2026
records.geography: Greater Ho Chi Minh City metropolitan area, 116 spatial cells across Ho Chi Minh City and neighboring provinces; Thu Duc households, firms, commuters, land markets, and flood-exposed communities
records.boundary: This record adds a place-and-climate route linking flood exposure, productivity, amenity, transport, land use, commuting, agglomeration, and metropolitan redistribution. It is a spatial general-equilibrium simulation, not a causal estimate of completed infrastructure, and does not establish equitable household welfare, displacement outcomes, or realized net-new growth.

records.title: Future housing demand turns climate resilience into a household-wealth, fiscal-capacity, and spatial-inequality problem
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11451, Housing Requirements, Hazard Exposure, and Resilience Costs: A Global Outlook to 2100
records.geography: Global country-level and subnational housing-demand, demographic, construction, hazard-exposure, and fiscal-capacity projections to 2100
records.boundary: This record adds long-horizon housing-resilience cost and triple-burden mechanisms linking climate exposure, demographic demand, fiscal capacity, household wealth, and infrastructure. It is scenario-based projection evidence, not a realized housing shortage, actual household affordability estimate, causal adaptation evaluation, or fixed country ranking.

records.title: Safer housing follows a two-stage ladder in which poverty constrains basic robustness and institutions shape disaster learning
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11319, Why Do Some Countries Build Safer? Economic Constraints, Disaster Learning, and the Two-Stage Housing Quality Ladder
records.geography: 150 countries/economies, using national housing-robustness measures and disaster, poverty, governance and development indicators
records.boundary: This record adds a housing-and-disaster-resilience route linking household material capacity, fragile housing, poverty, building systems, governance, disaster learning and infrastructure safety. It is cross-country aggregate evidence, not a respondent-level survey, event-damage audit, household causal evaluation or proof that reforms reach informal construction.

records.title: Human-capital formation is shaped by homes, neighborhoods, and workplaces as learning progress stalls and opportunity remains place-dependent
records.source_unit: World Bank, Human Capital Report 2026: Building Human Capital Where It Matters
records.geography: Global and cross-country evidence on health, learning, skills, employment, homes, neighborhoods, and workplaces
records.boundary: This record adds a human-capital route across homes, care, neighborhoods, learning, workplaces, informal work, gender participation, and place-based opportunity. It uses World Bank aggregate comparisons and report synthesis, not respondent-level data, individual child development histories, household time diaries, individual employment panels, causal neighborhood estimates, or proof that a policy works identically across settings.

records.title: Trade facilitation is not gender-neutral when infrastructure, information and care determine who can reach the border
records.source_unit: World Bank, Bridging the Gender Gap in Trade Facilitation: Evidence and Policy Pathways from India, September 2026
records.geography: India, covering women and men traders, customs brokers, logistics facilities, border procedures and trade-related services
records.boundary: This record identifies a gendered market-access and infrastructure subtheme. It does not establish that multilingual information, care facilities, safer ports, female staffing, finance, skills or consultation will increase women's trade participation, firm profits, export volume, income, safety or political influence; those require follow-up data linking named interventions to clearance time, fees, complaints, remedy, contracts, firm survival and household outcomes.

records.title: Indonesia's poverty reduction leaves a large economic-security layer exposed to low-productivity work, care constraints, weak mobility, and climate shocks
records.source_unit: World Bank, Indonesia Poverty Assessment: Pathways Towards Economic Security, released May 2023
records.geography: Indonesia; national poverty, labor, care, urbanization, human-capital, climate-shock, and fiscal-capacity systems
records.boundary: This comparative record adds a country-level route from poverty reduction through job quality, urban mobility, unpaid care, gendered labor, climate shocks, social protection, infrastructure, and fiscal capacity. It does not infer individual household trajectories, causal effects of a named intervention, service receipt, political response, or durable recovery.

records.title: Infrastructure gaps and investment quality shape access to work, services, markets, and resilience across places
records.source_unit: World Bank, Infrastructure Foundations: From Current Assets to Future Growth
records.geography: Global infrastructure assets and investment opportunities across more than 150 countries; energy, transport, and digital infrastructure
records.boundary: This record adds a global infrastructure asset, investment-efficiency, and access-to-opportunity lens across energy, transport, and digital systems. It uses aggregate and modeled infrastructure evidence, not individual travel times, household service reliability, project-level causal evaluation, local consent, environmental impact assessment, or proof that high modeled returns produce inclusive outcomes.

records.title: International shocks are absorbed through different public, private and cross-border buffers depending on development and fiscal capacity
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11345, Who Smooths the Shock? Government and Private Saving in International Risk Sharing
records.geography: 134 countries, covering advanced economies and emerging market and developing economies, 1990-2023
records.boundary: This record adds a macro-to-household-buffer route linking international volatility to public saving, private precautionary saving, remittances, transfers, investment income, fiscal space and capital-account openness. It is aggregate accounting evidence, not respondent-level data, household causal evidence, a welfare evaluation or a forecast.

records.title: Climate adaptation is being framed as a labour-market conversion problem: resilience investment can offset job losses only through sectoral reallocation and worker protection
records.source_unit: World Bank, Jobs in a Changing Climate: Insights from Country Climate and Development Reports covering 93 economies
records.geography: Low- and middle-income economies; 93 Country Climate and Development Reports representing 64 percent of the population and 77 percent of GDP of low- and middle-income countries
records.boundary: This record adds a climate-to-work conversion route linking adaptation, low-emission development, sectoral reallocation, human capital, business investment, vulnerable households, and geopolitical/development finance. The job figures are modelled estimates and extrapolations from a 49-country quantified set and 93 CCDRs; they are not realized job counts, worker-level forecasts, wage evidence, or proof that adaptation benefits are distributed fairly.

records.title: Aid contraction is turning refugee integration into a shared labor-market and service-capacity test
records.source_unit: World Bank feature on the Kenya Longitudinal Socioeconomic Study of refugee and host households
records.geography: Kenya; refugee and host communities in Kakuma, Kalobeyei, Dadaab, Turkana, and Garissa, with urban comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative displacement, aid, labor-market, and shared-service-capacity route. It does not estimate a causal effect of aid cuts, identify individual household trajectories, establish the success or failure of Kenya's Shirika Plan, or generalize the Kenya evidence to all refugee-host settings.

records.title: Allocating scarce judicial mediation capacity turns algorithmic matching into an access-to-justice institution
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11456, SMaRT: Online Reusable Resource Assignment and an Application to Mediation in the Kenyan Judiciary
records.geography: Kenya; court-annexed mediation across 87 court stations, 13 case-type categories, and approximately 2,100 mediators
records.boundary: This record adds algorithmic public-capacity allocation as a justice and legitimacy mechanism. It is not evidence that SMaRT has improved live judicial outcomes, that mediation equals equal justice, or that optimizing resolution rates resolves the normative question of fair allocation.

records.title: Rural poverty reduction can coexist with rising urban vulnerability when better jobs, skills, and mobility routes lag behind growth
records.source_unit: World Bank Lao PDR Poverty Profile for 2026, Poverty Falls in Laos, but Quality Jobs Remain Scarce
records.geography: Lao People's Democratic Republic; expenditure and consumption surveys for 2012/13, 2018/19, and 2024/25
records.boundary: This record captures Lao PDR's descriptive poverty, urban vulnerability, labor, migration, remittance, youth, and ethnic-distribution patterns. It does not establish causal effects, individual household trajectories, migration welfare, or a universal rural-urban development model.

records.title: Urban resilience is shifting from post-disaster response toward risk-informed spatial planning that governs where growth, housing, services and infrastructure can safely occur
records.source_unit: World Bank, Handbook for Livable and Resilient Cities: Integrating Hazard and Risk Information into Urban Planning
records.geography: Global urban-planning framework with examples and guidance for national and local governments, especially in rapidly urbanizing and emerging-economy contexts
records.boundary: This record adds a place-and-governance route: housing, services, mobility, infrastructure, risk data and climate exposure are joined through spatial planning and development control. It is a World Bank planning handbook, not a city-level outcome evaluation, household mobility study, property-market estimate, engineering certification or proof that participation and enforcement occur.

records.title: A structural global growth slowdown is making productivity, investment, labor-force aging, trade, and policy space central to future social opportunity
records.source_unit: World Bank, Falling Long-Term Growth Prospects: Trends, Expectations, and Policies
records.geography: Global and regional potential growth across advanced economies and emerging market and developing economies
records.boundary: This record adds a macro-to-social trend linking potential growth, productivity, investment, labor-force aging, trade, convergence, poverty, climate action, policy space, and global cooperation. It is a World Bank structural outlook, not realized GDP or household welfare, a respondent-level dataset, a causal decomposition for every country, or proof that investment-led policy will produce equitable opportunity.

records.title: External shocks and fiscally fragile state-owned enterprises compress growth, household security, and essential-service reliability in Malawi
records.source_unit: World Bank 23rd Malawi Economic Monitor, Building Stability to Unlock Growth, published September 23, 2026
records.geography: Malawi
records.boundary: This comparative record adds an external-shock, macro-fiscal, state-owned-enterprise, and essential-service transmission layer. It does not infer individual poverty trajectories, firm-level insolvency, service interruption rates, tariff incidence, causal governance effects, political legitimacy, or successful reform implementation.

records.title: China’s export rise contains multiple provincial development paths: early divergence followed by convergence with persistent local difference
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11469, “Many Chinas”: Provincial Foundations of Chinese Export Performance
records.geography: Chinese provinces and three macro-regions from 1995 to 2023, compared with advanced and emerging economies using customs export data
records.boundary: This record adds a provincial divergence-convergence and place-mediated export-upgrading mechanism. It is descriptive evidence from provincial customs export data, not proof that export sophistication caused local wages, jobs, household consumption, migration, identity, or political trust to change. Those consequences require provincial firm, worker, household, infrastructure, and public-narrative follow-through.

records.title: Urban policy is becoming a labor-market and social-access system as MENA cities absorb youth employment pressure
records.source_unit: World Bank, Cities that Work: Realizing the Jobs Potential of MENA's Cities
records.geography: Middle East and North Africa cities, with comparison to more than 8,000 cities worldwide
records.boundary: This record adds an urban labor-market and access route linking youth employment pressure, productivity, housing, transport, childcare, safety, utilities, digital connectivity, and city governance. It is a publication-level regional synthesis, not respondent-level employment data, individual mobility histories, a city rent series, or causal proof that any recommended reform creates inclusive jobs.

records.title: Extreme heat is already reducing firm sales, productivity, and wages in MENAAP while climate trade rules and adaptation finance reshape competitiveness
records.source_unit: World Bank, Competing in the Face of Climate Risks: Evidence from Firms and Policy Priorities in MENAAP, 2026
records.geography: Middle East, North Africa, Afghanistan, and Pakistan firms, workers, sectors, trade links, and policy systems
records.boundary: This record adds a firm-climate-to-worker and trade-competitiveness route linking heat exposure, sales, productivity, wages, adaptation finance, carbon-border measures, and cooling opportunities. It is not a household heat-stress estimate, a universal causal effect, a firm census, or respondent-level microdata analysis.

records.title: Social protection is being redesigned as productive, ecological, and digital infrastructure for household autonomy in climate-exposed Mozambique
records.source_unit: World Bank feature story, Roots of Resilience: How Mozambique's Families Are Rebuilding Their Lives and Their Land, published 18 September 2026
records.geography: Mozambique; Productive Social Action Program across all 11 provinces, with reported examples in Zambezia and Sofala
records.boundary: This record adds a route from cash and social protection through skills, productive assets, ecological public work, mobile money, household room, and climate resilience. It is based on a World Bank feature story and beneficiary narratives, not a representative survey, randomized evaluation, complete programme administrative dataset, or proof of durable autonomy and ecological impact.

records.title: For adolescent girls in northern Nigeria, digital-literacy gains depend on safe-space delivery and implementation fidelity rather than technology alone
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11445, Safe Spaces to Digital Spaces: Short-Term Impacts of Life Skills and Digital Literacy Training for Adolescent Girls in Nigeria, September 2026
records.geography: Northern Nigeria, including Kaduna, Kano, and Katsina; adolescent girls in senior secondary schools, school delivery systems, families, and local communities
records.boundary: This record adds a safe-space-to-digital-participation route for adolescent girls, linking life skills, digital literacy, implementation fidelity, school retention, socio-emotional outcomes, and delivery capacity. It does not establish long-term empowerment, causal employment or health effects, universal digital access, or that technology alone changes social norms.

records.title: School-year air pollution slows primary-school learning in rural Punjab through more than attendance alone
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11463, Air Pollution and Student Learning in Pakistan
records.geography: Primary-school students in rural Punjab, Pakistan, across more than 100 villages and three districts in the LEAPS longitudinal panel
records.boundary: This record adds a causal air-pollution-to-learning and non-attendance mechanism. It is evidence for rural Punjab primary students in grades 3-5 and does not establish national Pakistan effects, lifetime earnings, household welfare, health outcomes, political response, or separately identified cognitive and instructional channels. Gender and age differences are imprecise, and generalization requires additional settings and current data.

records.title: Small reductions in the psychological cost of initiating applications can sharply increase job search
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11465, Why Don't Jobseekers Search More? Barriers and Returns to Search on a Job
records.geography: Jobseekers using a search platform in Pakistan, studied through an experiment changing the default process for initiating job applications
records.boundary: This record adds a causal application-initiation-to-search-participation route and a psychological/search-cost mechanism for jobseekers in Pakistan. It does not establish increased employment, wages, job quality, match quality, retention, employer welfare, generalization to other platforms or labor markets, or that interface defaults can substitute for decent jobs and structural access supports.

records.title: Where people live and how places connect to jobs shape welfare disparities beyond national averages
records.source_unit: World Bank, People, Jobs, And Places: A Spatial Analysis Of Welfare Disparities In Low- And Middle-Income Countries, and GeoE3 spatial-jobs evidence
records.geography: Low- and middle-income countries, cities, rural and urban places, neighborhoods, labor markets, and spatial opportunity systems
records.boundary: This record adds a spatial opportunity route linking place, transport, infrastructure, safety, hazards, job access, welfare, mobility, data, and local policy. It is not a city-specific commuting estimate, a household location panel, a causal place-effect study, or respondent-level microdata analysis.

records.title: Philippines poverty reduction is real but economically fragile as job quality, social insurance, disaster exposure, care, and local service capacity shape middle-class security
records.source_unit: World Bank, Building the Filipino Middle Class: Towards Resilient Futures and Poverty Eradication
records.geography: Philippines; national and subnational poverty, middle-class security, jobs, resilience, social protection, services, and disaster exposure
records.boundary: This record adds a country-level poverty, middle-class security, jobs, social insurance, disaster resilience, care, agriculture, and local-service lens. It uses aggregate poverty evidence and modeled scenarios, not individual household trajectories, respondent-level motivations, causal evaluation of each reform, or proof that projected 2040 outcomes will occur.

records.title: Fiscal capacity is a targeting and trust architecture, not only a spending level
records.source_unit: World Bank Group, Building on Reform: Public Finance for a Rising Philippines, announced in official press release, 28 September 2026
records.geography: Philippines; national fiscal, procurement, revenue-administration, health, education and social-protection systems
records.boundary: This record identifies a fiscal-capacity, targeting, administrative-usability and legitimacy subtheme. It does not establish that the proposed reforms will produce the stated fiscal gains, lift two million people from poverty, improve learning or health, increase tax compliance, or distribute benefits fairly; those require named implementation episodes with observed procurement, tax collection, registry coverage, transfer delivery, service outcomes, complaints, participation and political response.

records.title: August 2026 commodity prices show simultaneous energy and metals pressure with food increases and fertilizer easing, keeping geopolitical price transmission uneven
records.source_unit: World Bank Commodity Markets Price Data (Pink Sheet), September 2026 release
records.geography: Global benchmark commodity prices and price indexes, with August 2026 monthly observations
records.boundary: This record adds a commodity-price and geopolitical-economic transmission layer linking energy, food, fertilizer, metals, input costs, state exposure, firm margins, and household room. It is benchmark price and index evidence, not retail inflation, household expenditure, firm profit, trade-flow, causal policy, or welfare data.

records.title: Food-tax relief can fail to reach poorer households when informality and market segmentation block price pass-through
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11453, Who Benefits from Food Tax Exemptions in Lower-Income Settings? Evidence on Pass-Through and Incidence
records.geography: Papua New Guinea; selected food items, formal supermarkets and informal stores across central urban and rural markets, with administrative data and a nationally representative household phone panel
records.boundary: This record adds a policy-to-price pass-through and incidence route linking tax exemptions, formal and informal markets, rural-urban segmentation, competition, stores and wholesalers, household quintiles, expert prediction, cash-transfer comparison, and consumer cost-of-living politics. It is not a universal tax-incidence law, a full welfare or general-equilibrium model, or evidence that cash transfers are always administratively feasible or politically acceptable.

records.title: Climate resilience in Papua New Guinea depends on shifting adaptation authority and finance toward strained local institutions
records.source_unit: World Bank, Building Community Resilience in a Complex Setting: Opportunities for Papua New Guinea, September 2026
records.geography: Papua New Guinea; Local-Level Governments, rural and climate-sensitive communities, provinces with high climate and conflict risk, wantok networks, Indigenous and traditional knowledge systems, churches, and community organizations
records.boundary: This record adds a climate-to-local-governance route linking spatial risk, conflict sensitivity, centralized implementation, local capacity, adaptation finance, traditional support systems, community platforms, participation, and social cohesion. It does not establish causal resilience effects, equal representation, durable finance, or that community networks can replace accountable public capacity.

records.title: Extreme poverty is increasingly concentrated in fragile and conflict-affected settings where poverty and institutional fragility reinforce one another
records.source_unit: World Bank, Fragility at the Core of Global Poverty, 2026 reproducibility package
records.geography: Global countries and regions, with analysis of fragile and conflict-affected settings, poverty, institutions, conflict, displacement and development capacity
records.boundary: This record adds a poverty-fragility feedback layer: extreme poverty is increasingly concentrated in fragile and conflict-affected settings, and the report treats poverty and fragility as mutually reinforcing. The public evidence reviewed here is the World Bank abstract and reproducibility metadata; it does not claim a specific causal effect, intervention ranking, household-level pathway or complete reproduction without restricted input data.

records.title: Development legitimacy depends increasingly on how change is negotiated, especially by groups that bear its losses
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11234, Process Legitimacy and Development: Analytical Framings, Implications, and Applications
records.geography: Development-policy and institutional-reform contexts across societal, local, national and international levels
records.boundary: This record adds a process-legitimacy route linking how development change is pursued to perceived fairness, representation, contestation, negotiation, cooperation, institutional trust and implementation risk. It is a 2025 conceptual and applied World Bank working paper, not a respondent-level legitimacy dataset, causal project evaluation, current public-opinion estimate or proof that participatory processes produce equitable outcomes.

records.title: Older work in developing countries is both an economic capacity and a signal of unequal retirement security
records.source_unit: World Bank, Productive Aging: Supporting Older Workers in Developing Countries, September 2026
records.geography: Developing countries; older workers, households, firms, informal and formal labour markets, social-protection systems, and skills and health institutions
records.boundary: This record adds a productive-ageing route from older adults' market and non-market work through skills, health, work conditions, social protection, household security, and intergenerational meaning. It does not establish that working longer is desirable or voluntary, causal productivity effects, equal employer access, or a universal retirement policy.

records.title: Public-institution quality converts policy mandates into procurement prices, firm access, regulatory predictability, and private-sector outcomes
records.source_unit: World Bank, Institutions and Prosperity: Public Institutions for Enabling the Private Sector
records.geography: Public procurement and regulatory institutions, firms, markets, and government contracting across comparative country evidence and named country cases
records.boundary: This record adds a public-institution-to-firm-market route linking personnel, resources, information systems, management, independence, accountability, transparency, procurement prices, contracting ease, regulatory milestones, competition, and service quality. It is not firm respondent data, consumer-level price incidence, a universal causal estimate, proof of corruption, or evidence that institutional reform automatically creates private-sector growth or public trust.

records.title: Public-sector staffing, management, pay, and digital capacity are becoming the conversion layer between state resources and usable public outcomes
records.source_unit: World Bank, Public Workforce Performance and Prosperity
records.geography: Global public-sector employment, compensation, management practices, digital workforce capacity, and core government functions
records.boundary: This record adds a public-workforce-to-state-capacity route linking staffing, compensation, management, integrity, digital capability, service delivery, fiscal room, and institutional trust. It uses publication-level cross-national findings and frameworks rather than respondent-level data; it is not individual worker productivity, household service receipt, causal reform evaluation, or proof that public workforce reform produces trust or prosperity.

records.title: Domestic revenue mobilization is becoming a test of fiscal fairness, administrative capability, and public trust as aid and debt conditions tighten
records.source_unit: World Bank, Raising Revenue Right: A Roadmap for Domestic Resource Mobilization, 2026
records.geography: Emerging markets and developing economies, with cross-country fiscal-system comparisons and country-specific reform pathways
records.boundary: This record adds a domestic-resource-mobilization and public-finance route across fiscal pressure, tax efficiency, equity, administrative technology, transparency, trust, taxpayer compliance, and public-service capacity. It uses a World Bank policy research framework and comparative evidence, not respondent-level ingestion, a complete tax-incidence database, a causal estimate of reform effects, a country-specific implementation evaluation, or proof that more revenue becomes better services or greater legitimacy.

records.title: Remittances are a major household and development channel, while payment infrastructure still determines how much value reaches home
records.source_unit: World Bank, Cutting the cost of sending money home: Fast payment systems, digital access, and the future of remittances
records.geography: Global remittance flows, low- and middle-income countries, and remittance corridors
records.boundary: This record adds a cross-border household-transfer, remittance-cost, digital-payment, and diaspora-development route. It is not respondent-level data, does not identify individual migration histories or household spending, and does not establish causal effects of fast-payment systems on welfare, migration, or political behavior.

records.title: Social cohesion is becoming an operational development mechanism measured through bonding, bridging and linking relations rather than a single community score
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 10417, Leveraging Social Cohesion for Development Outcomes
records.geography: Global development and fragile, conflict and violence-affected contexts, with evidence and examples spanning multiple regions
records.boundary: This record adds a social-cohesion measurement and intervention route linking bonding, bridging and linking relations to trust, identity, participation, citizen-state relations, development investment and conflict or fragility outcomes. It is a 2023 World Bank working-paper synthesis, not a current global prevalence estimate, respondent-level dataset, single intervention evaluation, U.S.-specific result or proof that social-cohesion programming produces durable peace or shared prosperity.

records.title: South Africa’s offshore-wind pathway links energy security to local jobs, ports, skills, and coastal legitimacy
records.source_unit: World Bank ESMAP, A Strategic Framework for Offshore Wind Development in South Africa
records.geography: South Africa’s Exclusive Economic Zone, coastal provinces, ports, grid, supply chains, workers, fishers, maritime users, and communities
records.boundary: This record adds an energy-transition-to-jobs-and-legitimacy mechanism. It is scenario-based strategic analysis, not proof that offshore wind will be affordable, built, locally owned, job-creating, emissions-reducing, or socially accepted; technical potential, FTE years, wage contribution, and stakeholder engagement must be tested against procurement, finance, grid, environmental, labor, and community outcomes.

records.title: Gender parity in schooling is advancing across generations, but attainment, learning, and opportunity are diverging
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11455, Convergence or Reversal? The Evolution of the Gender Gap in Education in Sub-Saharan Africa
records.geography: Sub-Saharan Africa; microdata from Demographic and Health Surveys and Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys covering 35 countries, supplemented by learning assessments in 14 francophone countries
records.boundary: This record adds generational education convergence with a measurement and conversion gap between attendance, learning, work, and agency. It is descriptive cohort evidence, not a causal evaluation of schooling reform, current prevalence estimate, or proof that educational parity has already produced equal labor-market, household, health, or political outcomes.

records.title: Social protection has expanded at historic scale but coverage, benefit adequacy, and delivery infrastructure still leave billions exposed to shocks
records.source_unit: World Bank, State of Social Protection Report 2025: The 2-Billion-Person Challenge
records.geography: Low- and middle-income countries, with comparisons by income group, region, poverty status, gender, and social-protection function
records.boundary: This record adds a global social-protection route across coverage, adequacy, crisis response, delivery infrastructure, gender disparity, labor programs, and household resilience. It uses aggregate World Bank indicators and report synthesis, not respondent-level benefit histories, individual case files, causal transfer effects, household consumption panels, or proof that coverage automatically becomes adequate protection.

records.title: Thailand’s high-income path depends on whether urban concentration can become a connected multi-nodal city system rather than a Bangkok bottleneck
records.source_unit: World Bank, Thailand Cities of the Future: Urban Foundations for a High-Income Economy, September 2026
records.geography: Thailand’s 75 urban centers, Bangkok, Chiang Mai, secondary cities, and national urban-development system
records.boundary: This record adds a country-specific urban-development route from city concentration through congestion, secondary-city potential, spatial investment allocation, infrastructure, connectivity, and institutional capacity. It is not a national forecast, household welfare estimate, causal city-policy evaluation, or proof that multi-nodal investment produces inclusive growth.

records.title: Europe and Central Asia’s jobs problem is a productivity and firm-capability problem, not simply a shortage of capital or workers
records.source_unit: World Bank, TIDES of Change: Igniting Productivity Growth in Europe and Central Asia
records.geography: Europe and Central Asia; 16-country, multi-sector firm-level evidence spanning 2008–2023
records.boundary: This record adds a supply-side mobility mechanism: broad job and wage improvement depends on productivity, firm capability, competition, technology access, trade integration and skills—not merely adding capital or workers. It is regional macroeconomic and firm-level analysis with model-based estimates, not a household survey, worker-panel dataset or guarantee that productivity gains will be evenly distributed.

records.title: A transport route becomes a regional economic corridor only when operations, institutions and local links work
records.source_unit: World Bank, Integration: World-Class Trade Logistics Along the Trans-Caspian Transport Corridor, September 2026
records.geography: Trans-Caspian Transport Corridor / Middle Corridor: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyz Republic, Tajikistan, Türkiye, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan; Europe–Asia trade route
records.boundary: This record identifies a corridor-operational, regional-economic and geopolitical-resilience subtheme. It does not establish that the Trans-Caspian Transport Corridor will achieve the reported trade, travel-time, GDP or jobs scenarios, lower consumer prices, improve worker welfare, diversify geopolitical risk, or distribute gains equitably; those require named corridor projects and operating episodes with observed construction, clearance, reliability, cost, employment, local value capture, environmental exposure, remedy and political response.

records.title: Drought shocks reduce Tunisian firm revenue while resilience and labor adjustment split by firm type
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11472, Droughts and Firms in Tunisia
records.geography: Tunisia’s formal firms across 254 delegations, using a panel from approximately 2000-2019 linked to satellite and reanalysis precipitation measures
records.boundary: This record adds a drought-to-firm-performance and uneven-adaptation mechanism. It is evidence from Tunisia’s formal firm registry and does not measure informal firms, household welfare, wages, job quality, firm investment, credit, public water delivery, or causal consumer and health outcomes. The observed revenue and worker patterns support a follow-through agenda, not a universal claim about firm resilience or climate adaptation.

records.title: Tunisia’s water scarcity is a macroeconomic, labor, infrastructure, and household-security constraint rather than only an environmental risk
records.source_unit: World Bank Tunisia Economic Monitor press release, Tunisia's Water Challenge: From Scarcity to Resilience, published September 22, 2026
records.geography: Tunisia
records.boundary: This comparative record adds a water-scarcity, macroeconomic, labor-exposure, infrastructure-finance, service-provider, and household-protection layer. It does not infer realized water shortages, tariff incidence, household deprivation, job losses, project completion, provider performance, or successful climate adaptation from modeled risks and policy plans.

records.title: Women’s agency is context-specific and cannot safely be measured by one universal survey scale or current generative AI
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11464, Developing a Measure of Women's Agency in Tunisia: Machine Learning and Generative Artificial Intelligence Approaches
records.geography: Tunisia; qualitative in-depth interviews and quantitative surveys with the same sample of women, including rural and urban context comparisons, with comparison to an India-developed agency measure
records.boundary: This record adds a context-specific agency-measurement route linking qualitative grounding, survey design, machine learning, generative AI, local variation, and policy visibility. It does not provide a universal agency index, population-level agency prevalence, causal empowerment effects, proof that all generative AI fails, or a reason to discard cross-context comparison when locally validated modules are combined with a transparent core.
