records.title: Childcare delivery changes the economic and social returns of informal-sector women’s work
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11442, Childcare for Informal-Sector Workers: Delivery Models, Access, and Welfare, September 2026
records.geography: Kampala, Uganda; 883 women market vendors across six markets, their children, household caregivers, community childcare providers, and workplace-based childcare services
records.boundary: This record adds a causal childcare-to-informal-work route linking care redistribution, women’s earnings, child development, well-being, utilization, delivery model, and public value. It does not establish long-run formalisation, fertility, universal delivery superiority, provider sustainability without subsidy, or general equilibrium effects beyond the Kampala trial.

records.title: War-related disruption is associated with a more digital composition of surviving labour demand in Ukraine
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11446, Labor Demand for Digital Skills in Post-2022 Ukraine: Evidence from Online Job Vacancy Data, September 2026
records.geography: Ukraine, 2021-2025; online vacancies, employers, workers, displaced and conflict-exposed regions, digital and non-digital occupations, and reconstruction labour markets
records.boundary: This record adds a conflict-to-digital-labour-demand route linking attack exposure, occupation change, upskilling, remote work, vacancy resilience, and reconstruction planning. It does not establish individual causal skill acquisition, wages, job quality, household welfare, broad informal labour effects, or equal digital access.

records.title: Ukraine’s preschool system turns demographic shock and wartime disruption into a territorial care, labor, and recovery challenge
records.source_unit: World Bank, Spending Better on Ukraine’s Youngest Learners: A Public Expenditure and Institutional Review of Early Childhood and Preschool Education
records.geography: Ukraine nationally, with hromada, oblast, and local preschool-system variation
records.boundary: This record adds an early-childhood-care-to-territorial-inequality, female-labor-force, and recovery-capacity mechanism. It is a public expenditure and institutional review, not a causal evaluation of wartime disruption, the Preschool Law, household welfare, child development, or labor-market outcomes; the central open test is whether local implementation converts regulatory flexibility and excess capacity into equitable, safe, high-quality access.

records.title: War-related poverty and inequality in Ukraine are being transmitted through food variety, labor-market segmentation, care constraints, disability, displacement, and weakening social-assistance adequacy
records.source_unit: World Bank Monitoring Living Conditions in Ukraine: Spring 2026 Update, drawing on official pre-war surveys, UNICEF household data, and Listening to Ukraine phone surveys
records.geography: Ukraine during the fourth year of Russia’s full-scale invasion; household phone-survey and modeled national living-conditions evidence
records.boundary: This record adds a geopolitical-shock-to-household-resilience route: war conditions transmit through poverty, food variety, prices, labor-market segmentation, care, informality, disability, displacement, and social-assistance adequacy. It combines modeled estimates and repeated phone surveys, not a causal counterfactual or fully linked longitudinal household panel; it does not prove that any single policy caused the observed change.

records.title: Ukraine's proposed post-martial-law minimum-wage path is a formal-recovery bargain between earnings, jobs, and social-contribution capacity
records.source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11443, Minimum Wage Reform in a Wartime Economy: Simulating Impacts from Ukraine's Proposed Reform, September 2026
records.geography: Ukraine; formal private-sector and nonmilitary public-sector workers, employers, low-wage workers, social-insurance institutions, and post-martial-law reconstruction policy
records.boundary: This record adds a post-war wage-floor route linking formal earnings, modeled employment, social contributions, taxes, household room, and reconstruction legitimacy. It is a simulation of a proposed reform, not an observed policy effect, and does not establish informal-sector impacts, political acceptance, compliance, inflation-adjusted welfare, or universal job quality.

records.title: Rapid poverty reduction can coexist with informal job creation, spatial concentration, gendered care exclusion, and a thinner safety net
records.source_unit: World Bank Uzbekistan Poverty and Equity Assessment, Rising to Prosperity: Broadening Opportunities for All, disclosed September 18, 2026
records.geography: Uzbekistan, 2021-2025 poverty, labor-market, spatial, gender, human-capital, and social-protection analysis
records.boundary: This record captures a country-level distributional pattern in Uzbekistan: strong poverty and middle-class improvement alongside job-quality, spatial, gender, human-capital, and safety-net constraints. It does not establish causal effects, durable mobility, household-level trajectories, or a universal model of poverty reduction.

records.title: Vietnam’s trade-corridor and coastal-fisheries program links logistics, climate resilience, jobs, and livelihood upgrading
records.source_unit: World Bank Group announcement of three Vietnam projects approved September 4-14, 2026
records.geography: Viet Nam; Hai Phong, Mekong Delta, northern, central, and coastal regions
records.boundary: This comparative record adds a trade-corridor, port, climate-resilience, fisheries, and planned-employment layer. It does not infer completed infrastructure, realized jobs, lower trade costs, farmer or fisher income, equitable access, gendered control, environmental outcomes, or household security from approved loans and project targets.

records.title: Economic growth is experienced as an inaccessible ladder when jobs, networks and social norms block movement into a stable middle class
records.source_unit: World Bank, Voices of Europe and Central Asia: New Insights on Shared Prosperity and Jobs
records.geography: 43 communities in nine Europe and Central Asia countries: Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kosovo, Kyrgyz Republic, Serbia, Tajikistan and Türkiye
records.boundary: This record adds a qualitative mobility mechanism: growth does not become lived progress when stable jobs, networks, norms and perceived agency block movement into the middle class. It is a purposive community study from 2016, not a current prevalence estimate, representative regional poll or causal evaluation; its value is explanatory depth and a warning against reading macro indicators as complete social experience.

records.title: Waste is becoming a visible test of consumption growth, municipal capacity, public health, climate resilience and circular-economy opportunity
records.source_unit: World Bank Group, What a Waste 3.0: Global Snapshot of Solid Waste Management toward Circularity until 2050
records.geography: Global municipal solid-waste system analysis using publicly accessible data from 217 countries and economies and 262 cities
records.boundary: This record adds a consumption-to-public-infrastructure route: waste volumes, collection, treatment, municipal finance, public health, flooding, jobs, emissions and circularity are analyzed as one system. It is a global technical reference and scenario dataset, not household consumption microdata, a behavior-change evaluation, a city service audit or proof that circular-economy jobs are decent or equitably distributed.

records.title: Women’s lived economic opportunity can lag formal legal equality, with gendered perception gaps revealing where rights are not felt in everyday work and care
records.source_unit: World Bank Women, Business and the Law and Gallup, Women's Lived Experience (W-LEX) Data
records.geography: Bangladesh, Brazil and Nigeria; nationally representative adult surveys collected in 2024
records.boundary: This record is the lived-experience complement to the WBL 2026 legal benchmark. It uses nationally representative survey evidence from three countries, not a global survey, administrative wage records, a legal compliance audit, a causal evaluation or a measure of all women's economic experiences.

records.title: Formal gender-equality laws are advancing faster than supportive systems and enforcement
records.source_unit: World Bank Women, Business and the Law 2026
records.geography: 190 economies, with global, regional, and United States country-profile comparisons across 10 topics of women's economic opportunity
records.boundary: This record adds a gendered legal-opportunity, implementation, enforcement, work, entrepreneurship, care, and household-room route. It does not identify individual women, establish causal effects of legal reform, or substitute index scores for lived economic outcomes.

records.title: Women’s economic opportunity is constrained less by laws alone than by the weak institutions, policies and enforcement that make formal rights usable
records.source_unit: World Bank, Women, Business and the Law 2026: Benchmarking Laws for Jobs and Inclusive Growth
records.geography: 190 economies, assessed across legal frameworks, supportive frameworks and enforcement perceptions
records.boundary: This record adds a law-to-capability and gendered economic-opportunity route. It is a global legal and institutional benchmark, not respondent-level data, a measure of lived discrimination, a causal evaluation of reforms, or proof that legal equality automatically produces equal employment, income or entrepreneurial outcomes.

records.title: Energy transition is shifting from deployment to integration as AI demand, geopolitical disruption, affordability, and access collide
records.source_unit: World Energy Council, Rebalancing World Energy: Trade-Offs and Transformations, 2026 World Energy Trilemma Report, 21 September 2026
records.geography: Global energy systems; dialogue with senior energy leaders from 65 countries and regional examples
records.boundary: This record adds a global energy-systems route from AI and industrial demand, geopolitical disruption, and energy access through integration, affordability, legitimacy, and infrastructure coordination. It is a leadership-informed report, not a probability-sample public-opinion study, a demand forecast, an emissions inventory, or proof that any regional pathway is replicable.

records.title: Some social platforms create collective product traps: people use them for access while wishing the social system did not exist
records.source_unit: World Happiness Report 2026, Chapter 6: Social media, wasting time, and product traps
records.geography: United States studies summarized in the chapter, including a nationally representative adult sample, a Facebook deactivation experiment, and U.S. college-student evidence on Instagram and TikTok
records.boundary: This record adds a consumer-culture and platform-dependence route from repeated use and network effects through time valuation, wellbeing, social pressure, information access, coordination failure, and collective agency. It synthesizes studies summarized in a World Happiness Report chapter; it is not a respondent-level reanalysis, not representative evidence for all platforms or populations, and not proof that any platform should be eliminated.

records.title: Digital exposure and wellbeing vary by generation, trust, social activity, and the saturation of peers’ social-media environments
records.source_unit: World Happiness Report 2026, Chapter 8: Internet use, social media, and wellbeing
records.geography: 30 European countries in European Social Survey rounds 8-11, 2016-2024, with generational and regional comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a distinct trust, social-connection, generational, peer-saturation, and wellbeing mechanism from Chapter 8. It does not duplicate the existing platform-deactivation record, does not establish universal causal effects of internet use, and does not infer individual mental-health or political outcomes from aggregate patterns.

records.title: Public protection is shifting from reactive measurement toward AI-assisted anticipation of social risk
records.source_unit: World Bank Group Social Policy, AI for Social Risk Forecasting and Explanation
records.geography: World Bank operational settings, with proof-of-concept cases in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, the Ethiopia-Kenya-Somalia borderlands, a small island developing state, and Uganda
records.boundary: This record adds an anticipatory-public-capacity route from AI-assisted social-risk sensing to possible early action. It is not evidence that prediction is unbiased, that forecast accuracy transfers across settings, that automated triggers improve welfare, or that predictive systems should replace community voice, official statistics, or democratic accountability.

records.title: Water security is being treated as economic, public-health, and institutional infrastructure whose service failures distribute time, cost, and opportunity
records.source_unit: World Bank Group, World Bank Group Backs Water Security and the Access to Resilient Water and Sanitation Services in Brazil's Paraíba State, September 22, 2026
records.geography: Paraíba State, Northeast Brazil; João Pessoa Metropolitan Region, 85 municipalities, and rural communities
records.boundary: This record adds a named infrastructure-to-household route from drought and poverty through water security, sanitation, rural service capacity, losses, collection access, PPP governance, jobs, time, cost, and public legitimacy. It is a project announcement with estimates, not evidence of completed construction, service reliability, affordability, job quality, or causal welfare effects.

records.title: Strategic location becomes productive capacity only when energy, digital connectivity, skills, competition, and cultural assets can support locally realized opportunity
records.source_unit: World Bank Group, Country Private Sector Diagnostic for Djibouti, summarized in World Bank Group Report Identifies Significant Private Investment Potential for Djibouti, September 14, 2026
records.geography: Djibouti, a Horn of Africa maritime and digital gateway serving Ethiopia and global shipping routes
records.boundary: This record adds a geoeconomic development route from strategic location and connectivity through energy costs, renewable investment, data centers, tourism, skills, regulation, cultural assets, and potential local jobs. It is a Country Private Sector Diagnostic summary with investment and employment potentials, not evidence of realized capital, broad-based gains, affordability, or cultural and environmental sustainability.

records.title: Human capital is produced across homes, neighborhoods, and workplaces, so location, care, safety, and job quality shape lifetime opportunity
records.source_unit: World Bank Group Human Capital Report 2026, Building Human Capital Where It Matters: Homes, Neighborhoods, and Workplaces, with Human Capital Index Plus 2026 findings brief
records.geography: Global; HCI+ country and regional comparisons, with detailed evidence from low- and middle-income countries and country examples
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative human-capital route from home care and resources through neighborhood exposure, services, workplace learning, gendered labor participation, job quality, and future earnings. It synthesizes World Bank evidence and HCI+ modeled comparisons; it is not respondent-level analysis, a causal evaluation of a single program, a complete measure of wellbeing, or a claim that human capital is reducible to earnings.

records.title: Aid contraction turns refugee integration into a shared jobs, food-security, and local-capacity problem
records.source_unit: World Bank, As Aid Shrinks, Jobs Become Central to Self-reliance for Host Communities and Refugees in Kenya; based on the Kenya Longitudinal Socioeconomic Study under KAP-FD
records.geography: Kenya, with evidence from refugee and host communities in Kakuma, Kalobeyei, Dadaab, Turkana, Garissa, and urban settings; national refugee and asylum-seeker context
records.boundary: This record adds a place-based displacement-to-work-and-household-security route. It is not a universal refugee-outcome estimate, a causal evaluation of the Shirika Plan, a complete labor-market census, or proof that jobs alone resolve poverty, social cohesion, gendered care constraints, food insecurity, or public-service capacity.

records.title: Urban economic concentration can coexist with rising poverty when housing, services, finance, and climate resilience fail to scale
records.source_unit: World Bank, Madagascar Urbanization Review: Leveraging Cities as Drivers of Growth and Structural Transformation
records.geography: Madagascar, with national, capital-city, secondary-city, and urban-service comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a named-country urban realization layer to the broader urban housing and infrastructure theme. It is a World Bank country review and public summary, not respondent-level data, a longitudinal household panel, a city-by-city causal evaluation, or proof that a proposed reform has been implemented.

records.title: Climate resilience is being designed as an integrated household route from cash protection through public works, jobs, digital delivery, and institutional transparency
records.source_unit: World Bank Group, Malawi: World Bank Group Approves Grant Financing to Improve Resilience to Climate and Economic Shocks and Create Pathways to More Jobs, September 17, 2026
records.geography: Malawi; all 25 districts and four cities, with additional drought-responsive financing in 10 drought-prone districts
records.boundary: This record adds a named intervention route from climate and economic shocks through adaptive cash protection, climate-smart public works, women’s and youth employment, digital registries, payment infrastructure, targeting, transparency, and household resilience. It is a project announcement, not evidence of implementation, beneficiary outcomes, payment performance, or causal poverty reduction.

records.title: In a high-income small island economy, aging, skills shortages, high costs, and digital access determine whether growth becomes good work and intergenerational mobility
records.source_unit: World Bank Group, 2026 Seychelles Country Growth and Jobs Report: Modernize, Utilize, Digitalize: How to Raise Productivity to Deliver Growth, Good Jobs, and Social Mobility, summarized September 17, 2026
records.geography: Seychelles, a small island economy with high income per capita, geographic isolation, aging pressures, and a narrow labor market
records.boundary: This record adds a small-island growth-to-household route from aging, skills shortages, isolation, labor-market and business reform, human capital, digital access, and public services through projected jobs, wages, purchasing power, and social mobility. It is a country-report summary with modeled scenarios, not a causal evaluation, household panel, or proof of equitable gains.

records.title: Trade, climate, and conflict shocks reach households through income, food, and unequal exposure channels
records.source_unit: World Bank, Trade Policy and Natural Shocks Dashboard, with methodology reference to Crops, Conflict, and Climate Change
records.geography: Low- and middle-income countries and more than 50 countries represented in the World Bank interactive household-shock dashboard
records.boundary: This record adds a modeled household-distribution layer to the trade, climate, food, and geopolitical-shock map. It is an interactive World Bank analytical dashboard, not respondent-level longitudinal data, a realized household-income panel, a universal causal estimate, or proof that any specific trade restriction caused a measured welfare loss in a named country.

records.title: Macroeconomic stabilization can coexist with mass informality when growth does not reach productive work, infrastructure, and household earnings
records.source_unit: World Bank Group, Zimbabwe Growth and Jobs Report, summarized in Zimbabwe Must Leverage Macroeconomic Stability to Accelerate Growth and Create 230,000 New Jobs by 2040, September 4, 2026
records.geography: Zimbabwe, with national labor-market, infrastructure, macroeconomic, and household-income implications
records.boundary: This record adds a named macro-to-household route from stabilization and growth through informality, low earnings, power and transport bottlenecks, regulation, investment, formal jobs, and worker earnings. It is a country-report summary with modeled scenarios, not a causal evaluation, household panel, or proof that reforms will create evenly distributed, decent work.

records.title: Storm risk is converted into disaster through social vulnerability, infrastructure, warning reach, and protection capacity
records.source_unit: Bündnis Entwicklung hilft and Ruhr University Bochum IFHV, WorldRiskReport 2026: Storms
records.geography: 193 UN member states in the WorldRiskIndex, with a thematic focus on storms and climate-related disaster vulnerability
records.boundary: This record adds a climate-risk-to-social-capacity route. It is not a household panel, individual disaster-loss estimate, short-term forecast, causal evaluation of early-warning systems, or proof that a country ranking predicts a specific event.

records.title: Employers see the youth transition as harder, but treat employability skills as productive capability rather than a soft add-on
records.source_unit: WorldSkills UK and Public First, Ready to Work Report 2026
records.geography: United Kingdom; employers
records.boundary: This record adds an employer-side youth-transition route: perceived difficulty entering work coexists with strong employer demand for demonstrable employability skills, and competitions or practical experiences are proposed as a bridge. It does not establish actual skill deficits, hiring discrimination, productivity gains, revenue effects, or causal benefits of competitions. The research is commissioned employer polling and should be read alongside young people's own pathway preferences and observed employment outcomes.

records.title: Mental scarcity is shifting consumer value toward guidance, balance, time, and control
records.source_unit: WPP Media Trend Seminar 2026 consumer-trends whitepaper and public overview
records.geography: Nordic region; commercial consumer-trend synthesis with implications that may travel unevenly across markets
records.boundary: This record adds a Nordic commercial-foresight layer on mental scarcity, life-stage pressure, guided choice, and time/control as consumer value. It is not respondent-level data, a representative Nordic or global survey, a causal account of well-being, proof of declining luxury consumption, or evidence that algorithmic guidance preserves consumer autonomy.

records.title: Trade flexibility is becoming a governance strategy as dispersed economic power, digital services, AI, and geopolitical blocs strain multilateral rules
records.source_unit: World Trade Organization, World Trade Report 2026
records.geography: Global multilateral trade system, regional and targeted agreements, digital services, AI-enabled trade, and economies with different levels of market power
records.boundary: This record adds a trade-system-to-firm-to-economy governance route linking dispersed economic power, regional and targeted agreements, geopolitical fragmentation, digital services, AI, and institutional flexibility. It is not firm respondent data, a realized tariff or GDP estimate, a prediction of trade blocs, or proof that aggregate trade gains are broadly shared.

records.title: The future of trade cooperation is being framed as a choice between renewed multilateral rules, geopolitical fragmentation, and a thinner network of bilateral deals
records.source_unit: World Trade Organization, World Trade Report 2026: A Critical Juncture for the World Trading System, September 2026
records.geography: Global merchandise and services trade, WTO members, least-developed countries, advanced economies, and alternative trade-governance scenarios
records.boundary: This record adds a trade-governance route from multilateral rules through geopolitical fragmentation, digital and services trade, development distribution, and public bargaining space. It uses aggregate historical analysis and counterfactual scenarios, not firm-level causal estimates, household price effects, worker outcomes, or proof that reform produces inclusive gains.

records.title: AI is positioned to expand trade and productivity, but digital capability gaps and fragmented rules may concentrate the gains
records.source_unit: WTO, World Trade Report 2025: Making trade and AI work together to the benefit of all
records.geography: Global trade and AI scenarios across economies, sectors, firms, workers, and digital-trade policy environments
records.boundary: This record adds an AI-to-trade, capability-diffusion, labour, small-firm, regulatory-fragmentation, and geopolitical-dependence route. It is not firm respondent microdata, an individual employment forecast, a causal estimate of AI adoption, or proof that modeled aggregate gains will be broadly shared.

records.title: Canadians value in-person third places, but belonging remains constrained by access, cost, time and welcome
records.source_unit: YMCA Canada and YMCA of Greater Toronto, 2026 YMCA Connections Snapshot
records.geography: Canada, national survey release; subgroup and provincial comparisons reported in the public summary
records.boundary: This record adds a community-infrastructure route from desire for connection through third-place supply, affordability, welcome, social confidence, time and navigability to lived belonging. It is a sponsor-commissioned Canadian survey summary with undisclosed sample and incomplete methodology in the accessed release, not a causal evaluation, attendance register, national census of third places, or proof that YMCA provision produces durable belonging.

records.title: Consumers read financial-services AI as a cost-and-profit project unless human fallback and accountability remain visible
records.source_unit: YouGov Consumer Duty Index, Will AI help financial services companies act in consumers' best interests? The public aren't convinced
records.geography: Great Britain; adults aged 18 and over
records.boundary: This record adds a consumer-governance route: financial-services AI is judged through perceived customer benefit, human fallback, accountability, personalisation, and data protection. It does not establish actual AI deployment, firm motives, consumer harm, financial inclusion, Consumer Duty compliance, or causal trust recovery.

records.title: Mental load is an invisible household-and-work infrastructure problem: awareness, gendered strain, and help-seeking do not automatically convert into support
records.source_unit: YouGov, Empowering Minds: Closing the mental load gap across the Nordics
records.geography: Finland, Sweden, Norway, and Denmark; nationally representative online samples of adults aged 18 and older, approximately 1,000 interviews per country; fieldwork September and November 2025
records.boundary: This record adds a Nordic mental-load route across invisible planning, gendered wellbeing, financial pressure, rest, work capacity, help-seeking, service access, workplace boundaries, and public support. It uses YouGov’s public survey summary, not time-use diaries, clinical records, longitudinal couples data, observed care tasks, causal service effects, or proof that Nordic patterns generalize to the United States or other regions.

records.title: Americans are negotiating different models of the good life through childrearing values, work time, remote work, and passion versus pay
records.source_unit: Economist/YouGov Polls, summarized by YouGov in R-E-S-P-E-C-T? What Americans value in kids and work
records.geography: United States; adult citizens, with age, ideology, education, gender, parenthood, and labor-force comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a social-reproduction and work-meaning route: childrearing ideals, work time, remote-work legitimacy, and passion-versus-pay choices are patterned by age, ideology, education, parenthood, and labor-force position. It does not establish actual parenting, work hours, remote-work access, earnings, policy effects, or durable value change.

records.title: Young people are using AI companions inside a shrinking relationship field while still preferring trusted human presence
records.source_unit: Young Life Research and Practice / Pinkston, RELATE Project 2026
records.geography: 11 countries: United States, United Kingdom, Argentina, Mexico, Hong Kong, India, Ethiopia, Kenya, Liberia, Nigeria, and Zimbabwe
records.boundary: This record adds a youth relationship-and-AI companionship route from shrinking or insufficient human listening capacity through AI use, confidentiality, advice, face-to-face preference, mentorship, and offline connection. It is publisher-reported survey and qualitative evidence from a faith-based nonprofit, not independent population surveillance, platform telemetry, causal evidence, mental-health diagnosis, or proof that AI companions replace human relationships.

records.title: The mainstream is not disappearing; it is being rebuilt from niche communities through visibility, shared comprehension, and active participation
records.source_unit: YouTube Culture & Trends, In Search of Mainstream, 2026 report summary produced with NRG
records.geography: Online people aged 14-44, with published U.S. NRG survey figures and global analysis of entertainment, media, and video trends
records.boundary: This record adds YouTube's public 2026 mainstream/fandom signal: fragmentation, niche discovery, creator and meme recognition, platform legitimacy, and fandom as participatory shared achievement. It uses published aggregate survey shares and platform analysis, not raw respondent-level data, a global representative sample, independent validation of cultural importance, or proof that participation is uniformly beneficial.

records.title: Platform governance commitments and statutory remedy routes do not establish worker-level protection
records.source_unit: Malaysia Act 872 official governance route and Grab Malaysia public response page; comparative institutional layer, not worker sample
records.geography: Malaysia; comparative platform-governance case used in the US-centered atlas
records.boundary: This is a comparative Malaysia platform-governance layer, not a US worker prevalence estimate or a compliance audit. It distinguishes company commitments, official route capacity, procedural rules, actual case identification, worker uptake, appeal, payment, access restoration, durability, trust, and exit.

records.title: A reported first platform Tribunal hearing establishes institutional use without an observed worker remedy
records.source_unit: One reported GrabCar proceeding before Malaysia's Gig Workers Tribunal; case-level procedural record, not a worker sample
records.geography: Kuching, Sarawak, Malaysia; comparative case used in the US-centered atlas
records.boundary: This is one reported comparative Malaysian proceeding, not a worker prevalence estimate, compliance audit, or finding that the platform violated Act 872. It distinguishes institutional establishment, reported hearing use, evidence-stage continuation, primary case identification, award, payment, access correction, durability, trust, and exit.

records.title: A reported airspace violation can move from national interception to alliance posture without proving deterrence
records.source_unit: Official NATO and Polish government accounts of the September 2025 Polish airspace incident and Eastern Sentry response
records.geography: Poland and NATO eastern flank; September 2025 airspace incident
records.boundary: This record establishes a reported Poland/NATO incident-to-response sequence from airspace violation through interception, Article 4 consultation, Eastern Sentry, diplomacy, and information-resilience action. It does not establish independent attribution, deterrence, actual deployment effect, public legitimacy, civilian security, or later foreign-actor behavior.

records.title: Physical arrival and formal acceptance can advance a defense capability without proving readiness or strategic effect
records.source_unit: Official Polish National Security Bureau, General Command, and Ministry of National Defence F-35 Husarz program records
records.geography: Poland; Łask 32nd Tactical Air Base and Polish F-35 program
records.boundary: This record establishes public arrival, formal acceptance, first-pilot training, and a current official eight-aircraft delivery state. It does not establish full fleet realization, readiness or IOC, operational use, sustainment, affordability, or geopolitical leverage.

records.title: Benefit design can make officially equal post-16 pathways financially unequal
records.source_unit: UK Department for Work and Pensions, Social Security Advisory Committee, Occasional Paper 27
records.geography: United Kingdom, with detailed evidence on England and comparisons across the UK and selected countries
records.boundary: This record captures an institutional-incentive mechanism: benefit rules, information gaps, and weak tracking can shape post-16 choices and distribute transition costs unevenly. It does not estimate how common each mechanism is, prove that benefit rules alone cause NEET outcomes or apprenticeship dropout, or treat recommendations and international examples as evaluated interventions.

records.title: A local public-realm consultation shows voice becoming decision, then being tested through scrutiny
records.source_unit: Stockton-on-Tees Borough Council, Yarm Levelling Up Fund Cabinet decision and call-in record, May 2026
records.geography: Yarm, Stockton-on-Tees, England; local public-realm and regeneration funding decision
records.boundary: This record is a bounded local public-participation episode connecting resident feedback to a Cabinet decision, funding reallocation, scrutiny call-in, reconsideration, and published rationale. It does not establish representative public opinion, causal influence, completed regeneration, resident satisfaction, or durable trust; the council's account of engagement is kept separate from independently measured response data.

records.title: Research careers lose women after entry as caring infrastructure, work norms, assessment rules, and institutional culture compound into a pipeline penalty
records.source_unit: UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology, Women in Research Charter
records.geography: United Kingdom research system; research funders, universities, public-sector research organisations, and research businesses
records.boundary: This record adds a UK institutional-career mechanism: near-parity at entry does not persist when caring responsibilities, insecure contracts, time-intensive norms, biased productivity metrics, and inconsistent flexibility interact. The charter is a policy diagnosis and voluntary reform architecture, not evidence that signatories have implemented the commitments or that the reforms caused improved retention, promotion, or research outcomes.

records.title: Museums retain broad public legitimacy as educational, economic, informational, and civic infrastructure
records.source_unit: American Alliance of Museums, Museums & Public Opinion 2026, produced with Wilkening Consulting
records.geography: United States; national public opinion about museums and museum support
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural-institution legitimacy layer: museums are publicly framed as educational, economic, informational, and civic assets with broad support for continued public funding and limited support for censorship. The public summary does not establish attendance, access, local economic effects, learning outcomes, causal trust, or realized funding decisions.

records.title: Older Americans are converting persistent price pressure into discretionary cutbacks, delayed purchases and drawdown of financial buffers
records.source_unit: AARP Research, Price Pressures and Consumer Spending, Foresight 50+ Consumer Omnibus
records.geography: United States; adults age 50 and older, nationally representative probability-based panel
records.boundary: This record adds an age-specific U.S. consumer-pressure layer: older households are translating price perceptions into cutbacks, delayed purchases and buffer use, with differences by age and gender. It is a nationally representative cross-sectional survey of stated perceptions and intended behavior, not transaction data, a longitudinal household panel, a poverty estimate, a causal price study or evidence that respondents actually exhausted savings or took on credit.

records.title: Sandwich-generation caregiving compresses complex care, paid work, and family life into the same hours
records.source_unit: AARP Public Policy Institute and National Alliance for Caregiving, Caught in the Middle: The Crucial Role of Sandwich Generation Caregivers, part of the Caregiving in the US 2025 series
records.geography: United States; family caregivers of adults with complex medical conditions or disabilities who are also raising children
records.boundary: This record adds a life-course and household-capacity layer to the care stream: sandwich-generation caregivers are a large population that compresses complex adult care and child-rearing into overlapping time, work, health, and financial obligations. It does not establish causality, care adequacy, household trajectories, or the effects of any specific policy or employer intervention.

records.title: Mobility exposure varies sharply by household income and race in 2024 ACS PUMS
records.source_unit: 2024 ACS 1-year PUMS housing and person records joined by SERIALNO
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a descriptive 2024 PUMS cross-sectional layer. Housing measures use WGTP and person commute measures use PWGTP after a SERIALNO join. The income gradient is household past-year income; the commute universe excludes work-from-home records. The layer does not establish transport affordability, reliability, care access, missed activity, discrimination, or political/cultural response. The official 2024 PUMS data dictionary was used to correct RAC1P coding before promotion.

records.title: National ACS household vehicle scarcity and long commute exposure changed modestly across 2023–2024
records.source_unit: ACS 1-year national table estimates: B08201 household vehicle access and B08303 travel time to work
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is an annual national ACS household/worker comparison, not a longitudinal respondent panel and not a direct replication of NHTS. B08201 measures household vehicle availability; B08303 measures commute time among workers who did not work from home. The current record does not establish household income gradients, care/medical reachability, trip purpose, fares, or political/cultural response. The next test is a state or place/income ACS extension with margin-of-error handling and explicit comparison to NHTS's urban/rural and travel-day universes.

records.title: State transportation exposure is non-monotonic across median-income quartiles
records.source_unit: 2024 ACS state/DC/PR aggregate tables B08201, B08303, and B19013
records.geography: United States states, District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico
records.boundary: This is a state-context comparison, not a household-income gradient or causal estimate. B19013 ranks geographic contexts; B08201 and B08303 are aggregate tables with different universes. The result does not establish affordability, transit quality, care access, missed activity, or political response. The detailed state rows and source hashes are reproducible through the companion analysis script.

records.title: Family care operates as distributed infrastructure with uneven private costs
records.source_unit: Deliberately non-pooled comparison of GAO kinship-family and assisted-living reviews, Federal Reserve SHED, Census SIPP, and BLS ATUS
records.geography: United States; national descriptive frames with selected-community and source-specific limits
records.boundary: This is a deliberately non-pooled family-care capacity synthesis. It supports distributed care capacity and uneven private-cost mechanisms across US evidence surfaces, but does not estimate a common care burden, causal intervention effect, verified support receipt, recovery, trust, political action, or household-to-state consequence. A dated same-family care episode with alternatives and follow-up remains open.

records.title: An older America is improving some prevention measures while care capacity and behavioral-health pressures diverge
records.source_unit: America's Health Rankings 2026 Senior Report executive brief, synthesizing 56 measures from 25 data sources
records.geography: United States; adults age 65 and older, state comparisons, and selected demographic groups
records.boundary: This record adds an aging-and-capacity trend: the older US population is expanding, care workforces are growing but unevenly, behavioral-health risks are worsening in several measures, and food insecurity persists despite greater program reach. It does not establish causal mechanisms, future care adequacy, individual health trajectories, or program effectiveness.

records.title: Consumer AI choice is task-specific and trust is learned through use, while privacy action depends more on knowledge than concern
records.source_unit: June 2026 weighted survey and embedded choice experiment of US adult AI-assistant users, Jennifer Zou working paper
records.geography: United States; adult users of AI assistants
records.boundary: This record adds task-level platform choice, comparative and experiential trust, privacy knowledge/action, and hypothetical valuation of data-handling features. It does not establish actual platform telemetry, disclosure, privacy loss, durable switching, dependence, wellbeing, productivity, or causal protective behavior.

records.title: AI capability can expand while infrastructure, ownership, and public-control dependence remain unresolved
records.source_unit: Deliberately non-pooled comparison of World Bank capability framework, Romania/Malaysia infrastructure cases, OFR institutional capacity, and US physical-load governance
records.geography: United States with Romania and Malaysia comparative infrastructure cases and global/developing-country analytical context
records.boundary: This is a non-pooled capability/dependence/state-control bridge. It supports a staged interpretation in which AI access, infrastructure, public data capacity, fiscal revenue, and governance can expand simultaneously with unresolved external dependence and local incidence. It does not establish provider replaceability, public-service improvement, household benefit, state bargaining leverage, alliance behavior, or geopolitical consequence. It does not establish the general-equilibrium effect of an actual rate decision, realized household spending or portfolios for all respondents, effects on trust or voting, or a causal cultural or political response. The source is a BIS working paper and the survey is quota-based online data; preserve its draft and sampling boundaries.

records.title: Community supervision remains a large state-contact system even as its population declines

records.boundary: This record adds the scale, decline, movement categories, and continuing state-contact surface of community supervision. It does not follow the same person through conditions, services, violation or completion, housing, work, family life, safety, trust, political action, or durable inclusion.

records.title: Jail exposure can remain heavy and unequal while the aggregate jail population declines
records.source_unit: Bureau of Justice Statistics Census of Jails and Jail Inmates in 2024 statistical tables
records.geography: United States local jails; midyear 2024 custody and July 2023-June 2024 admissions, with comparison to 2014
records.boundary: This record measures local-jail custody, admissions, conviction status, stay length, racial rate differences, and decade change. It does not establish crime causation, wrongful detention, individual case outcomes, reentry success, public safety, or trust.

records.title: Aggregate jail decline can coexist with heavy and unequal pretrial exposure
records.source_unit: Bureau of Justice Statistics Census of Jails and Annual Survey of Jails estimates
records.geography: United States local jails
records.boundary: This record measures local-jail custody, admissions, conviction status, stay, and unequal exposure. It does not follow unique people through court disposition, release conditions, housing, work, health, reentry, later justice contact, or trust.

records.title: Victim surveys and police records measure overlapping but different crime worlds
records.source_unit: Bureau of Justice Statistics comparison of the National Crime Victimization Survey and FBI National Incident-Based Reporting System
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a measurement boundary between victim experience and police-recorded crime. It does not establish a universal true crime rate, a reporting percentage, police performance, case resolution, safety, trust, or political response.

records.title: Public safety can be experienced without becoming police-visible
records.source_unit: Bureau of Justice Statistics National Crime Victimization Survey; 2024 legacy-instrument estimates
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a public-safety visibility boundary: experienced victimization, reporting, police records, response, victim services, safety, trust, and collective action are separate stages. It does not establish why a person did or did not report, whether police helped, whether safety improved, or whether victimization changed political behavior.

records.title: A long-standing Black-neighborhood startup gap narrowed sharply during COVID but did not disappear evenly

records.boundary: This record adds a racialized place-level entrepreneurship pattern: a long-standing Black-neighborhood startup deficit reversed sharply in 2020 and remained relatively elevated through 2024, especially in high-deficit areas. It does not establish why the change occurred, whether firms survived, who gained income or jobs, or whether neighborhood inequality and displacement changed.

records.title: U.S. time allocation shows work, care, household maintenance, socializing, and digital leisure competing within a fixed daily budget
records.source_unit: Bureau of Labor Statistics, American Time Use Survey—2025 Results, USDL-26-1022
records.geography: United States; nationally representative American Time Use Survey estimates for people age 15 and older, with subgroup tables by sex, age, education, employment, and presence of children
records.boundary: This record adds a U.S. time-allocation route from work location and education through unpaid household activity, childcare, socializing, television, computer leisure, and household composition. It is an annual cross-sectional time-diary release, not respondent-level longitudinal analysis, causal evidence, or a complete measure of simultaneous digital, care, emotional, or relational work.

records.title: Everyday cultural and civic life has different reach and time patterns
records.source_unit: Bureau of Labor Statistics American Time Use Survey 2025 annual averages
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural-time distinction, not a trend in belonging or political participation. Socializing, religious activity, volunteering, civic obligation, informal help, organizational capacity, trust, and political action remain separate evidence surfaces.

records.title: Schedule flexibility and family-time access are widespread but uneven across U.S. workers
records.source_unit: About 6,600 wage-and-salary workers in the 2024–25 ATUS Leave and Job Flexibilities Module, with estimates weighted to the U.S. wage-and-salary worker population
records.geography: United States; workers age 15 and over at their sole or main job
records.boundary: This U.S. official-statistics record supplies a current descriptive access layer for the flexibility-to-household route. It does not show that schedule control causes family welfare, earnings, care adequacy, worker autonomy, or durable household security, and it should not be pooled numerically with the comparative Dutch structural study or the NBER experiment.

records.title: Formal leave access does not guarantee usable time when workers need it
records.source_unit: BLS American Time Use Survey 2024-25 Leave and Job Flexibilities Module; wage and salary workers' main jobs, excluding self-employed workers
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a national work-time and care-access boundary: formal leave access can coexist with unmet need because work, job-risk, and income constraints remain. It does not establish why any one worker did not take leave, whether care or illness was resolved, or whether leave policy changed later job, health, family, trust, or political outcomes.

records.title: Care and household work still divide time while socializing declines and digital leisure expands
records.source_unit: BLS American Time Use Survey respondents age 15 and over; published 2025 annual summary
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a current time-allocation and cultural-participation layer. It does not establish a causal shift in social connection, care adequacy, economic security, health, trust, or political action. The federal shutdown interrupted part of 2025 ATUS collection and BLS describes the weighting adjustment and possible effect on estimates.

records.title: Selected sector average hourly earnings rise through August 2026 while sector levels remain distinct
records.source_unit: BLS Current Employment Statistics average hourly earnings of all employees, selected private industries
records.geography: United States, selected private industries
records.boundary: This record extends the selected-industry CES earnings context through August 2026 using a partial-year series-page vintage. It does not establish worker-level wage growth, real purchasing power, job quality, bargaining power, household security, or a causal relationship with AI adoption, union membership, or quits. It must not be treated as a complete 2026 annual mean.

records.title: Consumer spending growth and housing exposure differ across income quintiles
records.source_unit: BLS Consumer Expenditure Survey consumer units; published annual 2023-to-2024 income-quintile comparisons
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a current consumer-unit composition and income-quintile distribution layer to household room and consumption. It does not show a dated price shock, a person's cash flow or adaptation, a housing payment failure, food security, borrowing, time cost, trust, political action, or causal effect of income on spending.

records.title: August 2026 consumer prices rose with a gasoline-led energy contribution
records.source_unit: Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U), U.S. city average
records.geography: United States city-average CPI-U; selected expenditure categories and national index aggregates
records.boundary: This record adds an official August 2026 CPI-U price-index checkpoint to the household-pressure atlas. It does not establish household-specific inflation, affordability, consumption response, debt or saving change, trust, political action, or a causal link from gasoline, shelter, or food prices to cultural or geopolitical outcomes. The extracted retrieval hash is for the committed release-fact summary; the official release URL remains the authoritative source.

records.title: August 2026 labor-market conditions combine steady unemployment with uneven establishment growth
records.source_unit: BLS August 2026 Employment Situation: Current Population Survey household measures and Current Employment Statistics establishment measures
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record places CPS labor-force conditions beside CES payroll, hours, earnings, and industry changes. The household and establishment surveys have different universes; the observations do not identify the same workers, a worker-level causal effect, AI exposure, bargaining power, job quality, household security, or political response. August is a current preliminary publication vintage and should be revisited after revisions.

records.title: Food-at-home prices rose sharply before annual inflation moderated
records.source_unit: monthly unadjusted CPI-U food-at-home and all-items index observations, summarized by calendar year
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a national CPI-U price-pressure series, not a household food-security estimate, a local price series, a real-income estimate, or a causal test. It is intended to be aligned with USDA food-security and household-response records while preserving separate units and timing.

records.title: National job openings and voluntary mobility cooled after 2022 while hiring remained lower
records.source_unit: BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey national total-nonfarm establishment rates
records.geography: United States, total nonfarm
records.boundary: This record establishes an aggregate establishment-based labor-market context. It does not establish worker bargaining power, job quality, pay, schedule control, household security, political meaning, or a causal effect of any labor-market condition.

records.title: National JOLTS mobility remains cool in January–July 2026, with July preliminary
records.source_unit: BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey national total-nonfarm establishment rates from public series pages
records.geography: United States, total nonfarm
records.boundary: This record extends the establishment-based JOLTS context through July 2026 using a partial-year public-page vintage. records.geography: United States, selected industries

records.source_unit: BLS JOLTS, CPS Union Members, and CES industry aggregates
records.geography: United States; selected industries
records.boundary: This record places sector-level mobility, formal representation, and average hourly earnings beside one another. It does not estimate causal union effects, worker bargaining power, job quality, schedule control, household security, or political meaning.

records.title: Sector mobility and formal union membership differ across US industries
records.source_unit: BLS JOLTS establishment rates and CPS union-affiliation industry estimates

records.boundary: This record places 2025 sector-level establishment mobility beside CPS formal union membership. It does not estimate a causal representation effect, worker bargaining power, job quality, pay, schedule control, household security, or political meaning.

records.geography: United States; national producer price indexes for final and intermediate demand
records.boundary: This record adds an official August 2026 producer-price checkpoint to the household, firm, and infrastructure atlas. records.boundary: This is a CPS representation-context trend, not a causal union-wage estimate or direct measure of worker autonomy, household security, cultural meaning, collective action, or political response. The retrieval hash covers the committed BLS analysis memo.

records.title: Workers can request changes to make work usable, but employer granting and job-level control remain uneven

records.title: Immigration policy is becoming a labor-supply and sector-growth constraint, not only a border or identity issue

records.boundary: This record adds a U.S. labor-supply route linking immigration policy, population growth, immigrant-intensive industries, education composition, fiscal incidence, and the amount of employment growth compatible with stable unemployment. It is based on a public abstract and panel-discussion summary; it does not establish causal effect sizes, sector-specific outcomes, wages, prices, fiscal balances, household welfare, or migrant-level experiences.

records.title: Providing district-specific constituent opinion made state legislators' votes track constituency preferences more closely

records.boundary: This record closes a district-opinion-information-to-legislative-vote layer under a randomized field design. It does not show that ordinary constituent contact generated the information, that the vote produced implementation or household benefit, or that the result generalizes across issues, legislatures, time, or national politics.

records.source_unit: Sensitivity screens of California ZIP-level FAIR/private-market decisions joined to ACS and CDI exposure context

records.boundary: This record qualifies the California joint insurance screen by showing sensitivity to grouping definitions. It does not establish causality, household affordability, coverage adequacy, repairs, moves, lending effects, or political response.

records.geography: California ZIP/ZCTA approximations
records.boundary: This record adds income and housing-structure place context to the California FAIR/private-market ZIP screen. It does not establish causality, household affordability, coverage adequacy, repairs, moves, or political response.

records.source_unit: California Department of Insurance ZIP-level voluntary-market policy counts crosswalked to FAIR Plan residential-structure share
records.geography: California; ZIP-code and statewide comparisons
records.boundary: This record establishes a descriptive ZIP-level association between FAIR Plan share and voluntary-market nonrenewal decisions in 2022, alongside statewide voluntary-market counts for 2020-2023. It does not establish causal private-market withdrawal, household affordability, coverage adequacy, claims, repairs, mobility, or political response.

records.title: Extended disaster assistance and mortgage bridges can lengthen the recovery clock without proving durable housing
records.source_unit: California official Los Angeles wildfire recovery updates on continued FEMA housing support and CalAssist mortgage relief

records.boundary: This record establishes a longer disaster-recovery clock, continued assistance route, mortgage and insurance bridge, aggregate insurance payment, and complaint-intervention recovery. records.title: California's immigration-status-neutral Medi-Cal expansion converted formal eligibility into initial care access, while continuity remains conditional
records.source_unit: California Department of Health Care Services and California Health Care Foundation focus-group study of newly eligible undocumented adults
records.geography: California; statewide Medi-Cal policy with a qualitative study of nearly 100 undocumented adults
records.boundary: This record follows a named state policy from formal eligibility through reported initial enrollment and care access, then into a later enrollment freeze and future premium condition. It does not establish statewide take-up, treatment completion, health improvement, employment continuity, household budget effects, verified remedy, or trust/action change.

records.title: Wildfire insurance payments and new smoke rules can advance before safe household recovery is visible
records.source_unit: California Department of Insurance wildfire claims tracker, State Farm claim investigation, and Smoke Damage Recovery Act announcement; aggregate claims, sampled regulatory review, and statewide legal response are separate units

records.boundary: This record establishes aggregate insurance payments, a sampled claim-handling investigation, and a statewide smoke-damage legal response. records.title: California wildfire risk is becoming an insurance-availability and household-exit problem before reforms can prove durable protection
records.source_unit: California Department of Insurance market data, FAIR Plan wildfire claims records, and Sustainable Insurance Strategy reforms

records.boundary: This record follows California wildfire exposure through FAIR Plan dependence, catastrophe claims, insurance-market reforms, aggregate payments, and early market-stabilization signals. records.title: A centralized privacy request can scale consumer control while leaving broker-level deletion unresolved
records.source_unit: California Privacy Protection Agency public explanation of the Delete Request and Opt-out Platform (DROP)
records.geography: California consumers and registered data brokers
records.boundary: This record establishes a large-scale centralized privacy-request route with participant volume, broker coverage, privacy-preserving intake, status categories, and response timing. It does not establish broker-level match or deletion rates, exemptions, residual data, re-collection, actual user trust, switching, wellbeing, or durable privacy. The route is an implementation and contestability stage, not a verified privacy outcome.

records.title: Parents value home libraries, but cost, time, cultural fit and work strain make household literacy uneven
records.source_unit: Capita and Book Harvest, More Books for American Families: National Children’s Book Ownership Survey, September 22, 2026
records.geography: United States; parents and guardians of children ages 0-12, with income, race, reading-routine and cultural-fit comparisons
records.boundary: This record treats home book ownership and reading routines as a household cultural-access mechanism linking cost, time, race, language, identity, work schedules and civic capacity. It does not establish that book counts cause educational or democratic outcomes, define a sufficient home library, or replace libraries, schools, digital resources and relational learning.

records.title: Care constraints move through work, time, household room, and mobility rather than one burden channel
records.source_unit: Deliberately non-pooled comparison of SIPP person-month transitions, SHED adults, ATUS diary respondents, and NHTS household/trip records
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a deliberately non-pooled care/time/material/mobility bridge. It supports a recurring pattern in which care constraints can appear as reduced work opportunity, altered time allocation, financial adaptation, household hardship, and mobility cost across different US evidence surfaces. It does not establish one care-burden index, a causal care effect, a specific institutional trigger, recovery, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence. Same-unit dated trigger, alternatives, remedy, and follow-up remain open.

records.title: Routine casework response did not vary detectably by the sender's signaled social class in four audit experiments
records.source_unit: Carnes and Holbein multiple correspondence experiments with state legislators, school principals, and mayors
records.geography: United States; North Carolina state legislators, North Carolina and Kentucky public school principals, and a national sample of mayors
records.boundary: This record provides a counterexample to treating political access inequality as uniform across every stage: routine casework response did not vary detectably by signaled social class in these experiments. It does not negate donor-based access effects, other demographic biases, unequal ability to ask, policy-level unequal responsiveness, or unequal service outcomes.

records.title: Climate and disaster risk can move homeowner losses into household and federal exposure
records.source_unit: Congressional Budget Office policy analysis, Climate Change, Disaster Risk, and Homeowner's Insurance, August 2024
records.geography: United States; national policy and modeled federal exposure frame
records.boundary: This record adds a national policy-analysis and modeled federal-exposure layer. It does not establish that climate risk caused a particular household's premium, nonrenewal, mortgage trouble, repair delay, sale, move, or political response. Those links require property- and household-level records with compatible dates and denominators.

records.title: Market income, transfers and taxes tell different stories about household security
records.source_unit: Congressional Budget Office, The Distribution of Household Income, 2023, September 2026
records.geography: United States; approximately 134 million households, income quintiles and top 1 percent, 1979–2023
records.boundary: This record identifies a U.S. distributional, transfer-tax, household-security and fiscal-legitimacy subtheme. It does not establish individual mobility, consumption, wealth, debt, material hardship, benefit adequacy, administrative access, political response or the causal effect of a specific tax or transfer; those require linked household, program, state, service and political episodes.

records.title: US growth is being reconfigured by fiscal stimulus, tariffs, immigration, aging, and AI investment
records.source_unit: Congressional Budget Office The Budget and Economic Outlook: 2026 to 2036
records.geography: United States; federal budget, macroeconomy, labor force, households, firms, trade, and global exposure
records.boundary: This record adds a macro-to-lived-conditions pathway: fiscal support, tariffs, immigration policy, aging, AI investment, trade, and debt jointly shape US growth, prices, labor supply, and household room. It is a CBO forecast under current-law and policy assumptions, not observed outcomes, a causal policy evaluation, or a distributional household panel.

records.title: Retirement security is a present social contract with a 2032 institutional deadline
records.source_unit: Congressional Budget Office, CBO's 2026 Long-Term Projections for Social Security, September 17, 2026
records.geography: United States; Social Security program, Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund, current-law 75-year projection
records.boundary: This record identifies a retirement-security, intergenerational-contract and institutional-legitimacy subtheme from a conditional CBO projection. It does not establish post-2032 benefit levels, automatic benefit reductions, reform choices, public opinion, household adequacy, saving behavior, family care, political response or causal effects; those require linked policy, survey, household and episode evidence.

records.title: County health-sector capacity and vehicle constraint occupy four distinct place cells

records.title: County growth context coincides with distinct federal trust patterns while civic action remains stable

records.geography: United States; 620 counties with at least 100,000 residents and valid 2020/2023 population estimates
records.boundary: This is a county-context comparison, not a county-representative opinion estimate or a causal local-business, capacity, migration, trust, civic-action, or voting result. records.title: Local capacity and mobility cells carry different political-context patterns without a simple trust or action gradient
