records.boundary: This record measures preliminary insurance status and coverage-type trends from NHIS. It does not establish continuity, affordability, network access, care use, medical debt, health outcomes, or causal policy effects.

records.title: County health-sector capacity and modeled social-need measures align descriptively but not as a care-adequacy estimate
records.source_unit: US county; CDC PLACES modeled county estimates joined to Census CBP health/social-assistance establishments, county population, and HRSA primary-care HPSA component presence
records.geography: United States; 3,072 matched counties and county equivalents excluding non-US territories
records.boundary: This is an ecological, cross-vintage place diagnostic. PLACES estimates are modeled, CBP measures employer stock, and HRSA measures designated components. The record does not estimate individual access, quality, wait, price, causality, health outcomes, household burden, trust, belonging, or political action.

records.title: CDC PLACES county vintages move across distinct health and social-need surfaces
records.source_unit: Same county FIPS in selected CDC PLACES 2024 and 2025 releases, with 2023 CBP health-establishment capacity quartiles
records.geography: United States; 2,885 common county FIPS with capacity context
records.boundary: This is a descriptive vintage comparison of modeled county estimates. It does not estimate change for the same residents, local intervention effects, provider adequacy, patient access, household outcomes, trust, or political action.

records.title: Youth health is improving on some emotional and dietary indicators while sleep, activity, and digital-risk constraints persist
records.source_unit: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Youth Health in Focus release; national Youth Risk Behavior Survey data for 2023–2025 and 10-year trends for 2015–2025
records.geography: United States; nationally representative high school student estimates
records.boundary: This record captures CDC-reported national changes in selected youth mental-health, dietary, activity, sleep, and digital-behavior indicators. It does not establish causal mechanisms, subgroup equity, intervention effects, or future persistence.

records.title: Headline income and official poverty improved while supplemental poverty and full-year insurance coverage stayed broadly flat
records.source_unit: U.S. Census Bureau CPS ASEC 2025 income, poverty, and health-insurance estimates released September 15, 2026
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a realized household-material and coverage layer. It does not infer household wellbeing from median income alone, estimate causal policy effects, resolve state or subgroup heterogeneity, or treat official poverty and the SPM as interchangeable measures.

records.title: Survey participation can improve through targeted design changes while broader response still declines
records.source_unit: U.S. Census Bureau 2026 ACS Research and Evaluation Report Memorandum Series #ACS26-RER-01, summarizing self-response contact-strategy research from 2005–2025
records.geography: United States American Community Survey housing-unit collection; Puerto Rico is excluded from the report's contact-strategy discussion
records.boundary: This record adds an institutional participation and measurement layer: contact design can change response rates or data-completion indicators, but repeated improvements do not eliminate broader response decline. It does not establish household trust, representativeness, equal burden, policy responsiveness, or political participation, and it does not follow the same household from contact to later outcome.

records.title: A contracting ban can leave existing minority- and women-owned firms alive while shrinking the route into the market
records.source_unit: Census Bureau Center for Economic Studies working paper using restricted Census business records on minority- and women-owned business enterprises in state contracting
records.geography: United States states that ended affirmative action in state contracting and comparison states
records.boundary: This record adds a bounded policy-to-firm-entry and firm-scale relationship in state contracting. It does not establish the legal merits of affirmative action, individual discrimination, total contracting demand, worker welfare, community prosperity, public-service quality, or the full causal mechanism behind the observed firm patterns.

records.title: AI adoption happens at separate firm, business-function, and worker-task layers
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-25 using the 2026 AI supplement to the Business Trends and Outlook Survey
records.geography: United States; firms, business functions, employment-weighted firms, and worker tasks
records.boundary: This record adds a three-layer AI diffusion map from firms to functions to tasks. It does not establish causality, worker-level wellbeing, job displacement, productivity sharing, consumer outcomes, or durable control over AI systems.

records.title: AI adoption is layered: firm use, business deployment, and worker task use do not always move together
records.source_unit: Census Center for Economic Studies Working Paper CES-26-25, The Microstructure of AI Diffusion: Evidence From Firms, Business Functions, and Worker Tasks
records.geography: United States; nationally representative 2026 Business Trends and Outlook Survey AI supplement
records.boundary: This record adds a multi-layer AI diffusion measurement: firm adoption, functional deployment, worker task use, augmentation, and employment change are separate surfaces. It does not estimate individual AI use, worker control, causal job loss, household welfare, or long-run productivity.

records.title: Early-career hiring fell in the most AI-exposed industry-state markets after ChatGPT
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-27 using matched employer-employee administrative data and Quarterly Workforce Indicators tabulations
records.geography: United States; industry-state cells, early-career workers ages 22-24, older workers, and AI-exposure quintiles
records.boundary: This record adds an entry-to-work AI-exposure pathway distinct from firm adoption and college-major exposure. It does not establish individual automation, permanent displacement, lifetime scarring, or the distribution of gains and losses across households.

records.title: AI-exposed college majors faced a weaker and lower-paid first job after ChatGPT
records.source_unit: CES-26-56 using Post-Secondary Employment Outcomes, American Community Survey occupation distributions, and Census Longitudinal Employer-Household Dynamics records
records.geography: United States; participating institutions in 24 states and 27 data partners, with LEHD outcomes excluding Alaska and Michigan
records.boundary: This record adds a bounded technology-to-labor-market-entry pathway. It does not establish a national AI displacement rate, actual individual AI use, discrimination, long-run career loss, household security, or political and cultural change.

records.title: AI-exposed college majors face a weaker and lower-paid first step into work
records.source_unit: Census Bureau Center for Economic Studies working paper using administrative records on college graduates and major-level labor-market AI exposure
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a bounded entry-to-work and early-earnings result for AI-exposed college majors. It does not establish permanent job displacement, a causal effect for every graduate, lifetime earnings, household wellbeing, political response, or whether education remains valuable over the full career.

records.title: Civic participation can rebound in reach while thinning in time
records.source_unit: Census Bureau Current Population Survey Civic Engagement and Volunteering Supplement, analyzed by Census Bureau and AmeriCorps
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record establishes a broad participation-and-time pattern, not a matched-person panel or a measure of civic efficacy, trust, belonging, policy influence, local repair, volunteer retention, or later political action. Formal volunteering and informal neighbor help are separate denominators.

records.title: Standardized web questions can lose parts of complicated household life
records.source_unit: Census/RTI Round 2 qualitative cognitive interviews for the redesigned web-administered Annual Social and Economic Supplement of the Current Population Survey
records.geography: United States; 60 remote cognitive interviews, 30 income and 30 health-insurance interviews
records.boundary: This record adds evidence that household complexity, memory, reference periods, and response-option design can shape what a public survey can see. It does not establish national prevalence, respondent intent, published-estimate bias, service eligibility, or later household and political outcomes.

records.title: Legal venue can change whether a distressed firm survives and keeps jobs
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-29 using corporate bankruptcy cases, PACER, Federal Judicial Center data, and Census administrative establishment records
records.geography: United States; Chapter 11 firms nationwide, with causal distance design focused on Maryland, New Jersey, and Pennsylvania firms filing 1990s-2021
records.boundary: This record adds a legal-institution-to-firm-survival and employment pathway. It does not establish universal bankruptcy effects, individual worker receipt or wellbeing, consumer outcomes, local tax effects, or that Delaware venue is socially optimal in every case.

records.title: The way agencies count workplaces changes the picture of firms, care services, and market concentration
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-36, New U.S. Business Establishments: Surging or Stalling?, using linked BLS-Census microdata
records.geography: United States private sector; published establishment counts through March 2023 and linked establishment-level comparison for 2004–2016
records.boundary: This record adds a measurement-to-institutional-power mechanism: the administrative frame used to count firms can change whether the economy appears concentrated or decentralized, and can change policy predictions. It does not decide which frame is universally correct, prove actual firm power, or establish care quality, worker outcomes, consumer prices, or local economic vitality.

records.title: Business AI adoption is concentrated by firm size and sector rather than spreading evenly
records.source_unit: Census Bureau Business Trends and Outlook Survey employer businesses, December 2025-May 3, 2026
records.geography: United States, with sector, state, and firm-size estimates
records.boundary: This record adds a firm-capacity and labor-exposure layer: AI adoption is stratified by size and sector. It does not show realized productivity, worker outcomes, consumer prices, local infrastructure, or political meaning.

records.title: Employer businesses report stronger input-price pressure than demand or employment expectations
records.source_unit: U.S. Census Bureau Business Trends and Outlook Survey national key performance indicators, data as of September 6, 2026
records.geography: United States employer businesses, excluding farms
records.boundary: This record adds a firm-side price-pressure and expectation layer. It does not infer realized inflation, consumer incidence, firm profitability, employment changes, or sector-specific causal effects from national BTOS indexes.

records.title: Business applications overstate entry overall while successful entrants often understate their first-year employment
records.source_unit: Census Bureau Center for Economic Studies working paper linking administrative records on 17 million U.S. business applications to realized business outcomes
records.geography: United States business applications and local economic conditions
records.boundary: This record adds a bounded expectations-to-business-entry and first-year-employment pathway. It does not establish why applicants mispredict, business quality or survival, worker outcomes, household welfare, or local economic causality.

records.title: Administrative and third-party records can help estimate who official systems miss
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-38, an evaluation of experimental capture-recapture estimation using 2020 Census administrative and third-party records
records.geography: United States; 2020 Census address canvassing and nonresponse-followup operations, administrative records, third-party data, and post-enumeration coverage estimation
records.boundary: This record adds a measurement-governance pathway from administrative records to coverage estimation. It does not establish a final population count, individual inclusion, privacy safety, equal linkage quality, representation, or downstream public protection.

records.title: Child-care difficulty converts time and money into unequal work adaptations
records.source_unit: U.S. Census Bureau 2025 CPS ASEC working paper; households with children ages 0–13, reference year 2024
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record establishes a descriptive household care-to-work adaptation surface for the 2024 reference year. It does not establish a dated provider disruption, subsidy or leave eligibility, causal child-care policy effect, wage/job loss, child outcome, later recovery, trust, political action, or longitudinal household trajectory.

records.title: Survey nonresponse can make income look higher and poverty look lower even when year-to-year direction is mostly preserved
records.source_unit: U.S. Census Bureau CPS ASEC administrative-record nonresponse-bias evaluation
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record establishes a measurement and nonresponse-bias boundary for national CPS ASEC income and poverty estimates. It does not identify each nonrespondent's experience, establish the true population values, or invalidate every year-to-year trend.

records.title: Multinational firm networks can soften how foreign disasters reach U.S. importers
records.source_unit: Census Bureau Center for Economic Studies working paper linking U.S. Bill of Lading data, geocoded natural-disaster records, and cross-border ownership data
records.geography: Foreign supplier disasters and downstream U.S. importing firms
records.boundary: This record adds a firm-network pathway from foreign natural disasters to U.S. import purchases. It does not establish national supply security, consumer-price protection, employment effects, household resilience, public legitimacy, or geopolitical leverage.

records.title: Child-tax-credit participation can be high while the dollars reaching eligible taxpayers are lower
records.source_unit: Census CES Exact Match of the 2022 CPS ASEC to IRS administrative data for CTC and ACTC-eligible taxpayers in tax year 2021
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a measurement and access boundary between eligibility, taxpayer participation, dollar participation, and household security. It does not establish benefit adequacy, timing, child wellbeing, poverty reduction, political response, or durable financial relief.

records.title: Small interface choices can change how successfully people complete public date questions
records.source_unit: Census Research Report Series methodology experiment with 1,000 participants completing near-date tasks in text-entry, dropdown, and calendar designs
records.geography: United States; survey usability experiment with study participants
records.boundary: This record adds an interface-design-to-public-task-completion pathway. It does not establish equal accessibility, population-level representation, trust, policy responsiveness, or downstream household and political outcomes.

records.title: Economic place conditions can narrow civic capacity without making community life disappear

records.geography: United States rural and urban places; individual respondents observed in CPS Volunteering Supplement 2002-2015
records.boundary: This record measures reported associations between local economic context, the Great Recession, rural/urban place, and formal volunteering in CPS Volunteering Supplement observations. records.title: Entrepreneur background can shape who gets hired and which wage opportunities persist
records.source_unit: Census Bureau and LinkedIn profile data on entrepreneurs, startup employees, wages, and social-background similarity
records.geography: United States startups and workers
records.boundary: This record adds a founder-background-to-hiring and wage-opportunity pathway. It does not establish discriminatory intent, unequal productivity, firm performance, worker wellbeing, intergenerational mobility, or a complete causal effect of entrepreneurship access.

records.title: Changing who bears environmental cleanup risk changes firms' pollution and loan terms

records.title: Lender responsibility can change both firms' environmental investment and the price of credit
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-05 using EPA and confidential Census microdata around the 1996 U.S. Lender Liability Act

records.boundary: This record adds a lender-liability-to-firm-environmental-behavior pathway. It does not establish household exposure, health effects, local cleanup, long-run employment, universal credit effects, or whether the policy's net welfare effect was positive.

records.title: Export controls can pursue national-security goals while spreading costs across U.S. firms
records.source_unit: Census Bureau Center for Economic Studies working paper using export transactions, controlled-product classifications, and firm-level outcomes

records.title: Export controls can restrict the targeted trade while spilling into firms' other markets and payroll
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-50 using export transactions, product control classifications, and firm-level outcomes
records.geography: United States exporters, controlled products, Russia-related export restriction in 2014, firms, products, and destinations
records.boundary: This record adds a geopolitical restriction-to-domestic-firm-spillover pathway. It does not measure the policy's security success, diplomatic effect, national welfare, worker-level job loss, consumer prices, or durable firm adaptation.

records.title: A local role model can alter girls' education and family trajectories decades later
records.source_unit: Census Bureau Center for Economic Studies working paper using historical U.S. Census data linked to IRS records, later censuses, and death records
records.geography: Rural United States circa 1940, with linked later-life outcomes
records.boundary: This record adds a bounded school-exposure-to-later-life pathway in historical rural America. It does not establish current school effects, universal gender effects, the exact mechanism, political behavior, individual autonomy, or a same-period estimate for present-day communities.

records.title: Federal disaster finance can change which firms and machines survive a flood

records.boundary: This record adds a disaster-shock-to-firm-reallocation and public-finance channel. It does not establish universal disaster recovery, household welfare, worker continuity, relocation, health, political trust, or that federal assistance is always fiscally self-financing.

records.title: Federal disaster spending can change which firms survive and expand after floods
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-52 using confidential plant-level Census microdata and federally declared flood event studies
records.geography: United States; plants affected by large federally declared floods, surviving and entering firms, machinery, employment, and federal disaster spending
records.boundary: This record adds a disaster-to-firm-reallocation and public-finance pathway. It does not establish household recovery, worker welfare, equal rebuilding, local service continuity, or that creative destruction is beneficial for every affected community.

records.title: Household flood exposure is shaped by property, ownership, and insurance rather than income alone

records.boundary: This record adds a household-level flood-risk distribution and protection pathway. It does not establish flood incidence, claims or repairs, causal migration, insurance adequacy, displacement, health, or durable housing security.

records.title: A proposed privacy mechanism trades some exactness for controlled public data access
records.source_unit: Census Center for Enterprise Dissemination working paper proposing a Boltzmann Machine Privacy Framework for differential privacy

records.boundary: This record adds a formal privacy-mechanism pathway between confidential data and public statistical access. records.boundary: This record adds a founder-culture and retention mechanism: a firm can depend on relationships, skills, and meaning built around a person. It does not establish that founder influence is good or bad, that turnover reflects worker harm, or that founder departure changes firm survival, worker control, household security, or broader culture.

records.title: The public sector is organized through a large and historically changing number of government units
records.source_unit: Census Bureau 2026 Annual Government Organization Table 1, Government Units by State: Years 1942 to 2026
records.geography: United States and states
records.boundary: This record adds an institutional-structure layer to the atlas. It identifies the changing number and distribution of public units, but does not infer fragmentation effects, resident trust, service quality, or political action from counts alone.

records.boundary: This record adds a bounded race- and duration-specific association between coresident grandparenting, primary caregiving, and mortality. It does not establish causality, universal caregiving burden, mechanisms, or the effect of public support and family resources.

records.title: Workers respond differently to job opportunities depending on the social makeup of the destination

records.boundary: This record adds a place-and-identity mechanism to labor mobility: the same job opportunity may be more usable when the destination offers familiar social networks or lower expected social cost. records.title: Neighborhood redevelopment can change children's opportunity without raising public-housing adults' earnings
records.source_unit: Census Bureau Center for Economic Studies working paper evaluating HOPE VI public-housing revitalization with matched difference-in-differences, anonymized tax records, movers exposure, and sibling comparisons

records.title: Hospital capacity can grow in aggregate while local geographic access shrinks

records.boundary: This record adds an infrastructure-capacity-to-geographic-access pathway. It does not establish patient-level access, quality, affordability, emergency outcomes, health inequality, hospital financial cause, telehealth substitution, or household and political response.

records.boundary: This record adds a bounded house-price-to-firm-employment pathway through credit and collateral. It does not establish one universal housing-crash mechanism, worker welfare, firm survival for all businesses, consumer effects, or household recovery.

records.title: Text-first survey access expands response speed while making voice and consent more visibly stratified

records.boundary: This record adds a measurement-infrastructure route from text-first contact and consent through response timing, demographic access differences, and the distribution of public voice. records.title: Text invitations can speed survey response, but access and consent differ across groups
records.source_unit: Census Research Report Series methodology paper using Census Household Panel paradata and survey responses from the May 2024 topical
records.geography: United States; nationally representative Census Household Panel members and approximately 10,000 May 2024 topical respondents
records.boundary: This record adds a digital-contact-to-institutional-response pathway. It does not establish household trust, equal burden, population representativeness, political participation, policy responsiveness, or a same-person route from message receipt to later civic outcome.

records.title: Housing wealth can change women's labor supply through childcare and human-capital choices
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-15 using geographically linked SIPP and housing-market data
records.geography: United States; homeowners and county housing-market exposure, with household-level labor outcomes
records.boundary: This record adds a housing-wealth-to-labor-and-care mechanism. records.title: AI at work is becoming ordinary, but its time gains and practical access are unevenly distributed

records.geography: United States; workers using AI on the job, with education, sex, and age comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a U.S. task-level AI diffusion route from workplace adoption through reported time savings and unequal access by education, sex, and age. records.title: Recent arts participation is common but unevenly distributed across age and local cultural opportunity

records.title: Arts participation is a minority routine with a larger perceived local-supply base, creating a cultural access and conversion gap

records.title: Housing-assistance entry and exit are followed by different employment and earnings trajectories
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper CES-26-31, Employment and Earnings Trajectories of HUD Program Participants
records.geography: United States; HUD program participants linked to employee-employer earnings records through Census LEHD infrastructure
records.boundary: This record adds a linked longitudinal housing-assistance-to-labor-outcome stage. It does not establish causal program effects, rent burden or housing stability for the same unit, alternatives or non-use, benefit adequacy, claim/remedy receipt, health, trust, political action, or durable household security.

records.title: Immigrant college students sort toward both very large and very small firms through different routes
records.source_unit: Census Bureau Center for Economic Studies working paper using linked Census and longitudinal employment data to trace college students' jobs and firm placement
records.geography: United States college students in 2000 followed through 2001-2020 employment records
records.boundary: This record adds a bounded immigrant-student-to-firm-placement and earnings pattern. It does not establish blocked opportunity, equal treatment, visa causality, firm productivity, household welfare, or outcomes for students who leave the United States.

records.title: Enforcement fear can reduce victim reporting while reported crime stays flat
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-23, using the Secure Communities policy and linked crime and victim-reporting evidence
records.geography: United States; immigrant communities, Hispanic victims, local law-enforcement jurisdictions, and policy rollout periods
records.boundary: This record adds a policy-climate-to-reporting-to-public-safety pathway. It does not establish universal effects, identify every reason for nonreporting, measure all victimization, or prove later trust, civic action, or durable institutional legitimacy.

records.title: Digital incentives are preferred by most people, but physical cash remains important for a smaller lower-income group
records.source_unit: Census Research Report Series nonprobability survey experiment asking preferences for $5 and $40 incentive payments
records.geography: United States; large nonprobability survey of adults
records.boundary: This record adds a stated-payment-preference and digital-access pathway. It does not establish actual payment receipt, affordability, bank or device access, privacy, incentive effectiveness, survey response, or household security.

records.title: Census 2025 income, poverty, and insurance measures move on different household-security clocks
records.source_unit: Census Current Population Survey Annual Social and Economic Supplement (CPS ASEC) national income, poverty, and health-insurance estimates
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a current national CPS ASEC release surface. It records income, official poverty, SPM poverty, and full-year uninsured estimates as separate measures. It does not establish household-specific purchasing power, a causal price or policy effect, benefit adequacy, medical access, trust, political action, or later recovery. No report PDF or microdata was acquired for this page-vintage record.

records.title: A family can count as a participating taxpayer while some eligible credit dollars remain unclaimed
records.source_unit: Census/IRS CES-26-49 Exact Match estimates linking the 2022 CPS ASEC to IRS administrative tax and advance-payment records for tax year 2021
records.geography: United States; national estimates for eligible tax units/taxpayers and eligible CTC/ACTC dollars
records.boundary: This record adds a benefit-eligibility-to-payment conversion boundary. It does not establish why an eligible taxpayer did not claim or receive a dollar, whether the credit arrived on time, what households spent it on, whether it was adequate, or whether it changed durable poverty, health, care, trust, or political action.

records.title: Who gets hired into a new firm can reflect who founded it
records.source_unit: CES-26-45 study using Census LEHD data and a complementary Crunchbase-LinkedIn/Revelio Labs startup sample to compare founder and worker backgrounds
records.geography: United States; primary LEHD analysis covers 30 states and the District of Columbia, with industry, metropolitan-area, and founding-cohort comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a founder-background-to-firm-hiring and wage-opportunity pathway. It does not establish a national employer rate, individual discrimination, worker preference, causal entrepreneurship access effects, firm culture quality, or downstream household, political, or wellbeing outcomes.

records.title: The measured shock changes the measured story of local employment and migration
records.source_unit: Census Bureau Center for Economic Studies working paper harmonizing annual commuting-zone-level local labor-demand shocks and comparing employment and migration responses
records.geography: United States commuting zones
records.boundary: This record adds a measurement-sensitive local-shock-to-employment-and-migration comparison. It does not establish one universal local-shock effect, individual migration motives, household welfare, commuting adaptation, or the causal mechanism for every shock type.

records.title: Manufacturing misallocation can rise through both margin and input-mix differences, with decline concentrated in a few industries
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper CES-26-26; U.S. manufacturing establishment data decomposing revenue-productivity dispersion into revenue-margin and input-cost-share components
records.geography: United States manufacturing industries and plants over the last several decades represented in the study's establishment data
records.boundary: This record adds a firm-allocation layer: aggregate productivity decline can reflect different internal distortions and can be concentrated in a small set of industries. It does not establish worker harm, consumer harm, causal policy mechanisms, local decline, or a direct path from measured misallocation to cultural or political change.

records.title: A redesigned ACS Medicaid question did not measure coverage better than the old version against CMS records
records.source_unit: Census SEHSD Working Paper 2026-18 using the 2022 ACS Content Test linked to CMS Medicaid enrollment records
records.geography: United States; ACS survey respondents, redesigned and control health-insurance questions, CMS enrollment records, and Medicaid measurement
records.boundary: This record adds a survey-question-to-administrative-benchmark measurement pathway. It does not establish complete Medicaid coverage measurement, actual care access, coverage continuity, health, or trust.

records.title: Military service is associated with immigrant integration, but the Vietnam draft-lottery test points mainly to self-selection
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-35, Military Service and Immigrants' Integration: Evidence from the Vietnam Draft Lotteries, also published in American Political Science Review
records.geography: United States; first-generation immigrant men present in the restricted-use 2000 long-form decennial census, born 1949–1952 and in the country before the Vietnam-era draft lotteries
records.boundary: This record adds a selection-versus-institution mechanism: military service can be correlated with immigrant integration because people who serve may already differ before service. The draft-lottery evidence supports a null or weak causal effect on the measured long-term integration outcomes for this historical complier group, while showing an education benefit. It does not establish current military integration, national identity, equal treatment, veteran wellbeing, or foreign-policy legitimacy.

records.title: A higher wage floor can change a factory's technology choice before worker outcomes are known
records.source_unit: Census Bureau Center for Economic Studies working paper using state-level robot exposure and plant-level industrial-robot imports linked to Census microdata
records.geography: United States manufacturing plants and state-border wage-floor comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a bounded policy-to-firm-technology relationship. It does not establish net employment loss, worker wage effects, household welfare, regional decline, political response, or whether automation increased or reduced practical worker control.

records.title: Starting at the minimum wage does not define one career path, and later careers do not move with policy in the same way
records.source_unit: Census Bureau Center for Economic Studies working paper merging SIPP panels from 1992-2016 into the Longitudinal Employer-Household Dynamics program
records.geography: United States workers observed in SIPP panels and linked longitudinal employment records
records.boundary: This record adds a bounded minimum-wage-worker career trajectory and policy-null result. It does not establish complete job quality, household welfare, short-run firm effects, causal reasons for young-worker growth, or the absence of distributional effects.

records.title: Modeled retail growth diverges sharply across U.S. states and consumer-facing categories
records.source_unit: U.S. Census Bureau Monthly State Retail Sales (MSRS), June 2026 experimental vintage
records.geography: United States; 50 states and District of Columbia, with national and retail-subsector comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds an experimental U.S. place-by-category retail-behavior layer. It does not establish real-volume growth, consumer welfare, cultural preference, affordability, profitability, causal substitution, or individual household behavior; all findings should be revisited after Census revisions.

records.title: Services exports can help multinational firms keep goods sales moving during a global crisis
records.source_unit: Census Bureau Center for Economic Studies working paper linking U.S. firms' foreign goods and services sales and comparing multinational exporters during the 2008-2009 global financial crisis
records.geography: United States multinational firms and foreign destinations during the 2008-2009 global financial crisis
records.boundary: This record adds a bounded services-trade-to-goods-export and firm-capacity pathway during one global crisis. It does not establish national resilience, worker welfare, consumer outcomes, causal generalization to other crises, or strategic autonomy.

records.title: Eviction can turn a housing event into residential, school, and educational disruption for children
records.source_unit: U.S. Census Bureau Center for Economic Studies Working Paper CES 25-34 / NBER Working Paper 33659 linking eviction court, public school, homelessness-service, and restricted Census records in Chicago and New York
records.geography: Cook County/Chicago and New York City; eviction court cases from roughly 2000–2019 in Cook County and 2007–2017 in New York, with linked school and administrative outcomes
records.boundary: This record adds a causal housing-to-child-outcome route in two urban settings: eviction order to movement, homelessness, school engagement, and educational outcomes. It does not establish a national eviction effect, the effect of informal displacement, household-level policy receipt, long-term adult outcomes, or which intervention prevents the harm.

records.title: Residential exit is linked to relative racial and socioeconomic status, not composition alone
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper CES-26-19; American Community Survey data and multilevel linear probability models of White residential out-mobility by tract-level racial composition and relative socioeconomic status
records.geography: United States census tracts; White residents and neighborhood composition involving Black, Hispanic, and Asian residents
records.boundary: This record adds a relative-status and residential-exit mechanism: neighborhood composition may carry different meaning depending on a person's socioeconomic position. It does not establish racial motivation, causal contact effects, forced or beneficial mobility, or a complete account of segregation, belonging, household security, or political action.

records.title: Childhood neighborhoods transmit both social opportunity and access to jobs
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper CES-26-18; Longitudinal Employer-Household Dynamics linked to the 2000 Census, with intergenerational earnings models and person-effect/establishment-premium decompositions
records.geography: United States; childhood neighborhoods and adult earnings, using linked Census and administrative employment data
records.boundary: This record adds a place-and-firm mechanism to the mobility atlas: childhood neighborhoods may transmit both human-capital conditions and access to establishments and jobs. It does not establish a universal causal effect of moving, a complete explanation of racial earnings gaps, or a direct path from neighborhood conditions to cultural belonging, political action, or durable household security.

records.title: The gig economy is a broad local service and cultural infrastructure, not one app-based labor category
records.source_unit: U.S. Census Bureau 2024 Nonemployer Statistics release and The Gig Picture visualization; administrative tax-record data for nonemployer businesses, with selected industries used as a bounded gig-economy proxy
records.geography: United States; national selected-industry totals with subnational data available in the Nonemployer Statistics program
records.boundary: This record adds a current administrative scale signal for local services, care, mobility, delivery, repair, hospitality, and cultural production. It does not establish the size of the gig workforce, platform dependence, worker earnings or control, consumer prices or quality, household income, business survival, or bargaining power. The central next test is to join a named nonemployer category or operator to work hours, fees, expenses, repeat demand, household room, service completion, and exit without treating receipts as worker welfare.

records.title: Nonprofit work supplies social infrastructure while carrying a sector-specific earnings penalty
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-33, Employees in the US Nonprofit Sector, using linked administrative tax, employer, ACS, LEHD, and IRS Form 990 data
records.geography: United States; near-universe of US workers in administrative tax data, with descriptive earnings series 2001–2022 and tax coverage through 2023
records.boundary: This record adds a firm-sector and social-infrastructure pattern: nonprofit employment is large and socially consequential while average pay is lower and highly heterogeneous. It does not show that nonprofit workers are less committed, that services are worse, that households are less secure, or that nonprofit compensation caused later community outcomes.

records.title: Software that can be reused across establishments can make larger firm scope more attractive
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-28 using confidential Annual Capital Expenditure Survey data and a calibrated firm-scope model
records.geography: United States; firms and establishments in confidential Census data, with modeled implications for long-run U.S. firm scope and concentration
records.boundary: This record adds a technology-to-firm-scope mechanism. It does not establish that custom software caused observed concentration in every industry, or that larger scope changes wages, employment, prices, privacy, service quality, political power, or consumer welfare in a particular market.

records.title: Parental homeownership correlates with adult income and ownership but does not survive causal tests in the linked study
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-54 linking American Housing Survey 1995-2002 to administrative tax data from 2016-2019
records.geography: United States; childhood households, parent-owned versus renter-occupied homes, housing quality, adult earnings, mortgage, and homeownership
records.boundary: This record adds a family-housing-to-adult-outcome association with an explicit causal counterexample. It does not establish that parental ownership causes later income, ownership, health, mobility, identity, or household security.

records.title: Public-pension funding pressure can shape private-equity matching and the productivity of financed firms
records.source_unit: Census CES working paper linking U.S. public-pension investments, private-equity funds, target firms, and confidential Census firm data
records.geography: United States public pensions, private-equity funds, and financed firms
records.boundary: This record adds a public-pension-to-private-equity-to-firm-productivity pathway. It does not establish pension solvency, beneficiary security, worker harm, firm failure, or whether a different investment policy would improve public outcomes.

records.title: U.S. e-commerce grew faster than total retail in Q2 2026 while online share reached 17.1 percent
records.source_unit: U.S. Census Bureau Quarterly Retail E-Commerce Sales Report, second quarter 2026
records.geography: United States; national retail-establishment aggregate
records.boundary: This record adds an official observed retail-channel surface linking e-commerce growth and share to possible changes in discovery, convenience, delivery, access, and platform-mediated consumption. It does not establish real consumption, household affordability, unique buyers, retailer profitability, channel substitution, or causal cultural change.

records.title: Service-sector growth is not uniformly household-facing: information demand is split between business and consumer channels
records.source_unit: Census Bureau Quarterly Services Survey employer-firm revenue by class of customer, seasonally adjusted and not price-adjusted
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record measures nominal employer-firm service revenue by customer class; it does not measure unique consumers, household spending, affordability, service completion, worker conditions, nonemployer receipts, attention, cultural meaning, or causal demand. It is a bridge between the nonemployer operator layer and payroll/service-firm revenue, not a pooled market-size estimate. Customer-class values marked S in the workbook are suppressed and are not imputed.

records.title: Hospital employment can rise while the number of local hospital establishments falls
records.source_unit: Census Bureau Center for Economic Studies working paper on U.S. hospital establishments, employment, size, and regional concentration
records.geography: United States; national, regional, and rurality comparisons over roughly three decades
records.boundary: This record adds a public-health infrastructure capacity pattern: fewer hospital establishments can coexist with more hospital-industry employment and larger establishments. It does not establish local access loss, care-quality change, patient outcomes, affordability, or household burden.

records.title: Remote work loosens the job-place tie and changes where households sort
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-34, Remote Work and Residential Sorting: IV Evidence From Expiring Office Leases
records.geography: United States; restricted-access ACS respondents, 2005–2023, linked to LODES employment flows and CompStak office leases
records.boundary: This record adds a place-and-optionality mechanism: when work no longer anchors a household near an office, some households can trade proximity for space, ownership, public schools, and tax treatment. It does not show that remote work improved wellbeing, equalized opportunity, strengthened community, caused displacement, or changed political behavior.

records.title: August 2026 retail and food-service sales rose in nominal terms while the release leaves real household consumption open
records.source_unit: Census Bureau Advance Monthly Sales for Retail and Food Services; seasonally adjusted establishment sales aggregate
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a current nominal retail and food-services activity checkpoint. It does not establish real consumption volume, household affordability, consumer confidence, firm profitability, local business survival, payment or debt response, trust, political action, or a causal link from prices or income to spending. Product, channel, geography, and household-level incidence remain open.

records.title: Rural firms' innovation gap may reflect missing complements more than rural location itself
records.source_unit: Census Bureau Center for Economic Studies working paper using confidential 2018 Annual Business Survey firm data and an Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition
records.geography: United States; firms in rural and urban counties
records.boundary: This record adds a place-based firm-innovation comparison and a possible complements mechanism. It does not establish a causal broadband, R&D, or human-capital treatment effect, firm survival, jobs, wages, regional convergence, or community wellbeing.

records.title: Family routines can stay steady while organized opportunity remains unequal
records.source_unit: U.S. Census Bureau Current Population Reports P70-212 using the 2023 Survey of Income and Program Participation weighted public-use data
records.geography: United States; children under 18, with age-specific parental-interaction and extracurricular-activity universes
records.boundary: This record adds measured family interaction, material hardship, organized activity participation, and school engagement. It does not establish causation, activity quality, belonging, later educational or adult outcomes, or a same-child journey from hardship to later life.

records.title: Monthly assistance context coexists with housing pressure, and the pooled pattern reverses by resource context
records.source_unit: 2025 SIPP public-use person-month records for January–December 2024 reference period
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a same-person descriptive bridge from monthly other assistance context to next-month housing difficulty, work, and resource movement, plus a stratified counterexample. It does not establish a causal assistance effect, HUD program receipt, benefit adequacy, alternatives, landlord or agency response, arrears, eviction, homelessness, verified recovery, trust, or political action.

records.title: A steady monthly poverty rate can hide long and unequal poverty spells
records.source_unit: U.S. Census Bureau Current Population Reports P70BR-216, using the 2025 Survey of Income and Program Participation for the 2024 reference year
records.geography: United States; nationally representative SIPP population and reported age, race/Hispanic-origin, sex, and educational-attainment groups
records.boundary: This record adds a measured distinction between a monthly poverty rate and the duration and concentration of poverty spells. It does not establish causes, assistance take-up, material hardship, household coping, trust, political action, or later recovery for the same people.

records.title: Parental leave is not one shared work-family experience
records.source_unit: Census SEHSD/SIPP Working Paper using the 2023 Survey of Income and Program Participation public-use file and first-time-parent leave histories
records.geography: United States; nationally representative SIPP source, with analysis restricted to first-time parents who worked before and after the birth of their first biological child
records.boundary: This record adds a work-family-time and unequal-optionality pattern. It does not identify the causal mechanism behind group differences, measure all parents, establish employer discrimination or legal violations, or show later child health, caregiver wellbeing, earnings, household security, trust, or political action.

records.title: Household asset ownership is common while usable financial room remains uneven
records.source_unit: U.S. Census Bureau Current Population Reports P70BR-218, using 2025 Survey of Income and Program Participation public-use data for household wealth at the end of 2024
records.geography: United States; households in housing units, with reported demographic and economic subgroup comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds measured household wealth distribution, asset ownership, unsecured debt, and subgroup differences. It does not establish immediate liquidity, realized shock absorption, causal mechanisms, later recovery, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence.

records.title: SNAP work requirements reduced participation without increasing labor supply in a five-state study
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-46 using linked administrative SNAP and employment data from five states
records.geography: United States; five states, counties and states with phased SNAP work-requirement reinstatement during the 2010s
records.boundary: This record adds a work-requirement-to-participation pathway. It does not establish a universal effect across SNAP rules, states, periods, or groups, and does not directly measure food security, health, household income, administrative burden, or political response.

records.title: Where a household stands relative to its neighborhood is linked to how far it moves
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-20 using restricted-use American Community Survey data and multinomial mobility models
records.geography: United States; census tracts, counties, households, and short- versus long-distance residential mobility
records.boundary: This record adds a relative-status-to-residential-mobility pathway. It does not establish causal status effects, household motives, housing affordability, discrimination, belonging, safety, wellbeing, or whether moving represents exit, opportunity, or displacement.

records.title: Tariffs can appear fully passed through while transaction scale changes who actually absorbs the cost
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-17 using administrative U.S. import transaction microdata for the 2018-2019 tariff episode
records.geography: United States import transactions, foreign exporters, and U.S. tariff-affected product markets
records.boundary: This record adds a tariff-to-transaction-scale and foreign-exporter-incidence pathway. It does not establish retail price pass-through, household burden, domestic firm effects, employment, welfare, strategic success, or political acceptance.

records.title: A temporary public job can keep some marginal workers attached to employment for years
records.source_unit: SEHSD-WP2026-05 using 2010 Decennial Applicant, Personnel, and Payroll System records linked to Census demographic records and 2005-2023 IRS Form W-2 records
records.geography: United States; applicants for temporary 2010 Decennial Census jobs and linked employment outcomes
records.boundary: This record adds a bounded public-hiring-to-labor-attachment pathway. It does not establish a universal job-guarantee effect, a national employment rate, equal benefit across groups, job quality, household wellbeing, or political legitimacy.

records.title: Tax-reporting thresholds make some missing tip income visible without explaining all of it
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-40 using worker and employer tax reports and restaurant revenue data
records.geography: United States; full-service single-unit restaurants, tipped workers, employers, and reporting periods 2005-2018
records.boundary: This record adds a reporting-incentive-to-hidden-income pathway. It does not identify the actor retaining unreported tips, establish wage theft, estimate current national missing income, or measure worker household security, tax enforcement, or bargaining power.

records.title: Trade welfare depends on unemployment, participation, sector switching, and where workers can live—not wages alone
records.source_unit: Census Bureau Center for Economic Studies working paper developing a local-labor-market welfare measure and applying it to China's permanent normal trade relations shock
records.geography: United States commuting zones; workers observed in 2000 with outcomes measured over 2000-2007
records.boundary: This record adds a model-based local welfare framework for trade adjustment and a China PNTR application. It does not establish a complete national welfare level, subjective wellbeing, universal causal effects, or a single remedy for trade-exposed places.

records.title: Extra unemployment-insurance search time may improve job matches less where employers have more market power
records.source_unit: Census Center for Economic Studies Working Paper CES-26-24, Unemployment Insurance Extensions, Labor Market Concentration, and Match Quality
records.geography: United States; local labor markets during the Great Recession, using matched employer-employee LEHD data
records.boundary: This record adds a firm-power boundary to unemployment insurance: extra search time may produce weaker earnings gains where local employers have more market power. It does not estimate current UI effects, household welfare, job quality, retention, or a universal concentration mechanism.

records.title: Unemployment benefits can extend the job search without equally improving jobs in concentrated labor markets
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-24 using matched employer-employee LEHD data and quasi-random UI-duration assignment during the Great Recession
records.geography: United States; local labor markets, workers, employers, and Great Recession unemployment-insurance duration rules
records.boundary: This record adds a safety-net-to-search-to-job-match pathway conditioned by local employer concentration. It does not establish a universal employer-monopsony effect, household welfare, job quality, bargaining power, or later political or cultural action.

records.title: A county can look mobile by income while remaining much less mobile by housing wealth
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-30, Lands of Opportunity: Differences in the Geography of Wealth and Income Mobility in the United States
records.geography: United States; county-level estimates for children born 1978–1986, parents observed around 2000, and adult outcomes measured mainly 2019–2021
records.boundary: This record adds a wealth-versus-income place mechanism: economic opportunity is not one ladder, and county income mobility can conceal persistent housing-wealth and ownership inheritance. The study does not establish a single cause of county differences, current causal place effects, household wellbeing, or political meaning.

records.title: WIC reach depends on how eligibility and access are measured across places and groups
records.source_unit: Census-FNS-ERS Joint Project linking restricted WIC administrative records with American Community Survey data
records.geography: United States; state, county, demographic, and socioeconomic estimates
records.boundary: This record adds a measurement and reach layer for WIC. It does not provide numeric access rates in this extraction, establish a causal access barrier, or show benefit adequacy, nutrition, child health, household security, or political response.

records.title: Wildfire destruction produces multi-year income loss and changes who returns to the community
records.source_unit: Census CES Working Paper 26-53 linking property-level damage from more than 100 U.S. wildfires to administrative tax and Census data
records.geography: United States wildfire perimeters, damaged and undamaged residents, destroyed addresses, household income, and post-fire community composition
records.boundary: This record adds a direct-property-damage-to-income-and-community-composition pathway. It does not establish why households did or did not return, insurance or aid adequacy, health, debt, displacement, or long-term place attachment.

records.title: Some college can improve women's careers and children's early-life conditions across the life cycle
records.source_unit: Census Bureau Center for Economic Studies working paper using a school-entry birthdate regression discontinuity and linked administrative records on women, jobs, and children
records.geography: United States women and their children in the study's linked administrative data
records.boundary: This record adds a local causal education-to-career and child early-life pathway. It does not establish universal returns to college, complete maternal or child wellbeing, workplace autonomy, political participation, or the same mechanism in every population.

records.title: Medical debt becomes a visible CFPB complaint category
records.source_unit: published CFPB complaint record represented in a 2025 product/sub-product aggregate snapshot
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is complaint-system visibility, not medical-debt prevalence, harm incidence, a rate among debtors, verified remedy, money recovered, care restoration, trust, switching, or exit. No CFPB record is joined to a MEPS person or household.

records.title: A financial-service transition converts technical failure into a monitored, proactive remedy
records.source_unit: CFPB-monitored Bilt transition-remediation episode
records.geography: United States consumers affected by Bilt's transition to a new bank partner
records.boundary: This record adds a named consumer-service remedy episode linking technical transition failure to fees, proactive outreach, reimbursement, technical remediation, and agency closure. It does not estimate national financial-service reliability, prove universal redress, measure customer satisfaction or retention, or establish durable trust repair.

records.title: A named consumer redress route identifies eligible victims and ongoing distribution, while successful recovery remains unobserved
records.source_unit: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau BrightSpeed case page and payments-by-case index
records.geography: United States; consumers who purchased technical-support services from BrightSpeed fraudster clients through RCCs
records.boundary: This record establishes a named aggregate compensation route, current public status, fund allocation, initial checks mailed, geographic distribution surface, and a still-unreconciled difference between CFPB amount labels. It does not establish check cashing, final delivery, amount retained, residual loss, recovery rate, trust repair, switching, continued service use, or practical exit for any consumer.

records.title: Complaint route timing, visibility, and response categories differ sharply by financial product
records.source_unit: Capped retrieval-order sample of published CFPB complaint records with case-level route fields
records.geography: United States complaint records; consumer state and ZIP are reported fields
records.boundary: This record audits a capped retrieval-order sample of public CFPB complaint cases. It adds case-level route timing and visibility fields to aggregate complaint evidence, but it does not estimate consumer harm, remedy adequacy, account-level rates, repeat contact, switching, trust, or political action.

records.title: CFPB case-route labels and API fields change across complaint vintages
records.source_unit: Capped retrieval-order sample of published CFPB complaint records with case-level route fields
records.geography: United States complaint records; consumer state and ZIP are reported fields
records.boundary: This is an API-vintage and route-field comparison, not a consumer-harm, remedy, or service-quality estimate. The 2025 response omits has_narrative in the returned sample, so it cannot be compared with 2024 narrative prevalence. Timely is not substituted for elapsed routing time, and routing is not remedy.

records.title: Cash App fraud-control failures produce a formal redress obligation while individual correction and receipt remain unobserved
records.source_unit: CFPB enforcement action, Block consent order, and CFPB payment-by-case status for Cash App fraud and dispute handling
records.geography: United States Cash App users and consumers covered by the Block enforcement order
records.boundary: This record follows Cash App fraud-related dispute exposure through CFPB enforcement, operational correction, and an ordered redress obligation, then records the public distribution-status boundary. It does not estimate user harm, payment receipt, account correction, adequacy, trust repair, continued use, switching, or exit.

records.title: Student-loan servicing errors can shift tax access, payment burden, and credit information before a regulatory remedy
records.source_unit: CFPB enforcement action and consent order against Citibank, N.A.
records.geography: United States; private student-loan servicing
records.boundary: This is a named US student-loan servicing enforcement event. It demonstrates documented administrative failures, borrower exposure mechanisms, and an ordered remedy, but does not estimate population prevalence, establish individual causal loss, verify remedy receipt or adequacy, measure durable compliance, or close household, trust, action, switching, or exit consequences.

records.title: A complaint system can improve intake integrity while reducing public narrative visibility
records.source_unit: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau official 2026 announcements about complaint-portal integrity and public complaint publication
records.geography: United States consumer-finance complaint system
records.boundary: This record establishes a dated change in complaint-portal controls and public narrative visibility. It does not establish complaint validity, consumer harm, company liability, verified correction or payment, representative public opinion, trust change, switching, or practical exit. It adds an institutional visibility boundary to the consumer-power and platform/data lanes.

records.title: Consumer credit expansion is uneven across products and credit-risk tiers, with tightness still below the 2010 index base
records.source_unit: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Consumer Credit Trends dashboard and nationally representative credit-record sample
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a market-level consumer-credit access and risk-tier route. It does not infer individual borrowing, repayment, debt distress, affordability, approval, credit-score transitions, household consumption, or causal effects from aggregate originations, inquiries, indexes, or subgroup changes.

records.title: 2026 year-to-date credit-card complaints show explanation, monetary relief, and unresolved routes in the CFPB system
records.source_unit: published CFPB credit-card complaint records received in a partial calendar-year API slice
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record is a partial-year administrative complaint-route slice.
