records.geography: United States; nationally representative time-use and labor-market estimates
records.boundary: This record estimates the time and replacement value of unpaid household work and reports selected demographic differences. It does not establish causal effects on poverty, gender inequality, health, wellbeing, labor supply, household bargaining, political action, or social welfare, and it does not follow the same household to later outcomes.

records.title: Unpaid household work makes a large hidden time-and-value layer visible while leaving care conversion open
records.source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-26-107871 using American Time Use Survey and Current Population Survey data
records.geography: United States; nationally representative ATUS and CPS-based estimates for 2021-2024, with monetary valuation for 2024
records.boundary: This record advances the hidden-price and care-visibility stage by measuring time and assigning a bounded replacement-cost range to unpaid household work. It does not establish household welfare, care quality, bargaining power, retirement security, labor-force effects, paid-care substitution, or the effect of any policy.

records.title: Unpaid household work is a large economic system that converts time into care, household maintenance, and labor-market capacity
records.source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office, Unpaid Household Work: Estimated Value and Time Spent on Domestic Tasks and Caregiving, GAO-26-107871
records.geography: United States; analysis of 2021–2024 American Time Use Survey data for individuals age 15 and older, with 2024 national valuation estimates
records.boundary: This record adds a U.S. route from unpaid domestic work and caregiving through time scarcity, household production, gender and employment exposure, economic valuation, and policy visibility. It is a secondary analysis of pooled ATUS diary data and imputed market values, not respondent-level longitudinal analysis, causal evidence, a measure of money received, or proof that paid substitution would reproduce household welfare.

records.title: Postal cost-cutting can trade financial sustainability for slower and more uneven service
records.source_unit: GAO-26-108527 review of USPS First-Class Mail service standards, cost-cutting initiatives, and customer effects
records.geography: United States; USPS market-dominant First-Class Mail, with rural and nonrural customer comparison
records.boundary: This record separates postal cost-cutting, service-standard changes, target performance, and reported rural distribution from individual delivery, household time, business continuity, affordability, complaint, trust, and political outcomes.

records.title: Accelerating a health-record rollout can outrun user readiness and operational proof
records.source_unit: GAO-26-109393 testimony summarizing GAO follow-up reports on VA Electronic Health Record Modernization
records.geography: United States Department of Veterans Affairs; VA health-care facilities and planned EHR deployments, 2017–2031 planning horizon
records.boundary: This record adds a rollout-to-usability mechanism: system deployment and acceleration can coexist with unresolved cost, schedule, user adoption, operational testing, and patient-safety controls. It does not establish patient harm, clinical effectiveness, veteran satisfaction prevalence, or the success or failure of the planned 2031 rollout.

records.title: Veteran-focused SNAP outreach can reach a recommendation and coordination stage while benefit access and food security remain open
records.source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-27-108111 review of SNAP outreach to veterans
records.geography: United States veterans and veteran households eligible for or receiving SNAP through state-administered outreach
records.boundary: This record advances a bounded veteran food-insecurity-to-outreach-and-interagency-recommendation route. It does not establish veteran-level eligibility, application, approval, benefit receipt, adequacy, food security, household recovery, trust, or completed agency action.

records.title: Federal water-infrastructure assistance can be large while local affordability, service-area visibility, and maintenance remain difficult
records.source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-25-107013 review of EPA, FEMA, and USDA assistance for drinking-water and wastewater infrastructure resilience
records.geography: United States; federal water-infrastructure assistance and selected utilities and communities, fiscal years 2014–2023
records.boundary: This record establishes a federal-assistance, local-finance, maintenance, and service-area measurement boundary for water-infrastructure resilience. It does not establish project completion, water quality, service continuity, household bills, health effects, disaster recovery, or public trust.

records.title: Water-sector digital connectivity expands remote control while legacy capacity and legal gaps constrain cybersecurity
records.source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office testimony on cybersecurity risks and federal response in the water and wastewater sector
records.geography: United States; drinking-water and wastewater systems and EPA-led federal oversight
records.boundary: This record establishes a digital-connectivity, operating-capacity, and federal-oversight risk pathway for water and wastewater systems. It does not establish a particular cyberattack, service interruption, household health effect, operator failure, compliance rate, or successful remediation.

records.title: A rapid acquisition pathway can still produce slow delivery when the technology is not mature
records.source_unit: GAO-26-108457 annual assessment of 104 of DOD's costliest weapon programs and selected rapid-acquisition efforts
records.geography: United States Department of Defense weapon-system acquisition programs; major defense acquisition and Middle Tier of Acquisition portfolios
records.boundary: This record measures DOD acquisition schedules, technology maturity, and fieldable-capability status in a selected 2026 review portfolio. It does not establish operational effectiveness, deterrence, battlefield superiority, contractor causation, or the outcome of every reform.

records.title: More health data can expand care options without settling who can trust or act on it
records.source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office technology assessment of wearable devices in clinical decision-making
records.geography: United States health-care technology and clinical settings
records.boundary: This record measures potential wearable capabilities and reported clinical-integration and governance challenges. It does not establish device use prevalence, patient benefit, privacy harm, health improvement, or inequality magnitude.

records.title: Strategic foreign assistance can continue after program transfer while oversight ownership and anti-terrorism controls remain unfinished
records.source_unit: GAO-26-107939, West Bank and Gaza: State Should Incorporate Leading Practices and Lessons Learned into Anti-Terrorism Oversight
records.geography: United States foreign assistance to the West Bank and Gaza; State Department and USAID administration, awardees, the East Jerusalem Hospital Network, and congressional oversight
records.boundary: This record adds a geopolitical assistance-control and state-capacity layer: strategic funding can be transferred and administratively reassigned while future oversight ownership, anti-terrorism procedures, audit timing, beneficiary outcomes, and partner or public response remain incomplete. It does not establish misuse, diversion, service failure, or changed geopolitical behavior.

records.title: Whistleblower information can strengthen public oversight only when trust, protection, and agency capacity make disclosure usable
records.source_unit: GAO-26-107650 review of private employment practices and selected federal agency mechanisms for receiving and protecting reports of potential wrongdoing
records.geography: United States; selected federal agencies and organizations involved in whistleblower and public-disclosure routes
records.boundary: This record measures disclosure incentives, protection mechanisms, and selected agency capacity. It does not estimate whistleblower prevalence, retaliation rates, case validity, reporter safety, enforcement effectiveness, recovered funds per reporter, or durable institutional trust.

records.title: Work and public-benefit reliance can coexist within the same labor system
records.source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-26-108703; Census estimates for 2024 labor characteristics and selected state administrative employer analysis through September 2025
records.geography: United States national estimates plus selected data from 15 state agencies across 11 states
records.boundary: This record establishes a mixed-universe labor and public-benefit interaction: work, safety-net participation, private-sector concentration, occupational composition, and selected-state employer overlap. It does not establish wages, schedule control, employer intent, benefit shifting, eligibility churn, household security, worker alternatives, remedy, trust, political action, or exit.

records.title: AI content saturation is making consumers more selective about influencers, brands, and human credibility
records.source_unit: Gartner Marketing survey and September 2026 newsroom interview on AI-generated content, influencers, and consumer trust
records.geography: United States; consumers surveyed May-June 2026
records.boundary: This record adds an AI-content trust and authenticity route: content saturation can weaken influencer and brand credibility while increasing demand for human expertise and demonstrable quality. It does not establish AI-content volume, causal trust effects, purchase conversion, or the effectiveness of recommended governance practices.

records.title: Digital infrastructure can expand capability and external dependence together
records.source_unit: documented international AI-infrastructure project case
records.geography: Romania and Malaysia; comparative cases relevant to US-linked finance, technology, and state capacity
records.boundary: This is a two-case infrastructure/state-capacity comparison, not a population trend or geopolitical leverage estimate. It records commitments, planned capacity, and an ownership milestone while leaving realized public benefit, local incidence, portability, replacement, state bargaining, and external response open. The retrieval hash covers the committed case memo.

records.title: State Auto-IRA exposure is associated with later retirement and Social Security claiming
records.source_unit: Rao, Dao, and Lee, Georgetown Center for Retirement Initiatives Working Paper CRI WP 2026-02, using Census SIPP 2014–2024; workers ages 55–75 in seven early-adopter states compared with non-adopter states; issue brief used as a companion summary
records.geography: United States; Oregon, Illinois, California, Connecticut, Colorado, Maryland, and Virginia early-adopter states compared with not-yet-adopting states
records.boundary: This record extends the Auto-IRA layer from account and debt margins to primary-paper retirement and Social Security timing estimates. It does not establish a net-welfare effect, retirement adequacy, benefit entitlement, improved health or job quality, or a causal increase in lifetime income for every exposed worker. It must not be pooled mechanically with the separate NBER balance-sheet record: the papers have different outcomes and the primary timing paper reports no statistically significant retirement-asset change, a mechanical checking-balance decline, and a small unsecured-debt decline, while the other summary reports different balance-sheet directions. That discrepancy is an open reconciliation task, not a reason to average estimates.

records.title: Georgia's large-load protections reached actual contract filings while customer incidence remains open
records.source_unit: Georgia Public Service Commission docket 44280 and related large-load filings; executed contract submissions and Commission review are distinct regulatory events
records.geography: Georgia Power service territory; Georgia Public Service Commission large-load and data-center contract oversight
records.boundary: This record advances the Georgia large-load route from rule and forecast to actual contract filings and regulatory review. It does not establish contract terms, final approval, construction, energization, payment, cost allocation, residential bills, reliability, local acceptance, or durable ratepayer protection.

records.title: Alliance capability depends on staffing and social capacity before deterrence is tested
records.source_unit: Bundeswehr account of staffing and personnel measures for Panzerbrigade 45 Lithuania
records.geography: Germany and Lithuania; German brigade stationed at NATO's eastern flank
records.boundary: This record establishes a social-capacity and workforce stage in a named alliance capability program: most positions are reportedly filled by volunteers, while mandatory measures are introduced in selected areas before the 2027 readiness target. It does not establish operational performance, deterrence, adversary adaptation, host-country consent, family burden, or durable alliance legitimacy.

records.title: U.S. teens are making AI part of learning and creativity while developing uneven habits of verification, judgment and self-limitation
records.source_unit: Google Kids & Families, U.S. Future Report 2026: Growing Up with Technology and Learning How to Shape Its Role
records.geography: United States; national teen findings with six-state context, focus groups and digital-journey evidence
records.boundary: This record captures a U.S. youth-culture and technology transition: AI is already routine in teen learning and creativity, while verification, productive friction, school norms, trusted-adult guidance and self-limitation remain uneven. The source is Google-sponsored survey and qualitative research with inconsistent public headline sample descriptions; it is not an independent behavioral-trace study, causal learning evaluation, school-policy audit, clinical assessment or proof that reported use produces better outcomes.

records.title: A search platform turns image-removal control into a trackable request and repeat-protection route
records.source_unit: Google Search product account of non-consensual explicit-image removal controls
records.geography: United States; Google Search users and people seeking removal of explicit images
records.boundary: This record adds a user-facing digital-control stage: a simpler removal request, request-status visibility, and an optional repeat-protection feature. It does not establish completed removal, removal across other services, recurrence prevention, survivor safety, wellbeing, trust, or practical exit from the search/platform ecosystem.

records.title: Financial dissatisfaction and generalized trust show a persistent but non-causal historical association
records.source_unit: GSS cumulative cross-sectional respondent with positive WTSSPS weight
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is an anchor-year descriptive screen from the cumulative GSS file. It does not establish that financial dissatisfaction causes declining trust or fairness judgments, nor does it provide a consistent unbroken annual series. Several years lack comparable field coverage; the 2024 multi-mode/design change and the use of WTSSPS rather than the 2024 nonresponse-adjusted WTSSNRPS weight require separate harmonization before formal trend inference.

records.title: Financial position coexists with distinct trust, fairness, and political orientations
records.source_unit: GSS 2024 cross-sectional respondent with nonresponse-adjusted post-stratification weight
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a weighted cross-sectional GSS 2024 comparison. It does not establish that financial satisfaction or trajectory causes trust, fairness judgments, ideology, or vote intention; it does not measure a specific bill, local exposure, institutional remedy, cultural identity formation, or geopolitical action. The 2024 file has module-specific missingness and changed multi-mode design, so it should not be treated as a direct unadjusted continuation of earlier GSS years without a separate trend audit.

records.title: Housing supply is expanding unevenly while affordability, mobility, household formation, and immigration reshape who can access place
records.source_unit: Harvard Joint Center for Housing Studies, The State of the Nation’s Housing 2026
records.geography: United States; national housing, household-formation, mobility, affordability, demographic, and regional analysis
records.boundary: This record adds a U.S. structural housing route from construction and market supply through low-cost availability, residential mobility, immigration, household formation, first-time buying, and cost burden. It is a secondary synthesis of public housing and demographic data, not a household panel, causal land-use evaluation, or proof that any single policy caused mobility or affordability changes.

records.title: Meaningful work is a strong Gen Z aspiration constrained by pay, financial security and care-work conditions
records.source_unit: Harvard Graduate School of Education Making Caring Common, in collaboration with Gallup and the Walton Family Foundation, as reported by Harvard Gazette, Gen Z puts high priority on jobs with meaning, purpose, but sees daunting hurdles, August 3, 2026
records.geography: United States; Gen Z respondents born 1997–2012, including adults ages 18–29 in work and wellbeing analyses
records.boundary: This record identifies a meaning-of-work, care-labor, financial-security and wellbeing subtheme. It does not establish causality, clinical mental-health effects, realized job choice, wage or retention effects, comparative generational altruism, employer behavior, care-sector labor supply, or the superiority of meaningful work over nonwork sources of purpose.

records.title: Hurricane Harvey firm closures produced localized consumer travel and welfare losses despite higher-value entry
records.source_unit: Hurricane Harvey case using payment-card transactions, store turnover, flood exposure, and a modeled consumer-demand panel across Houston, Corpus Christi, and Beaumont; author-hosted working paper
records.geography: United States; Texas MSAs and neighborhoods affected by Hurricane Harvey
records.boundary: This record closes a firm-turnover-to-customer-distance and modeled local-welfare arrow for Hurricane Harvey. It does not establish a general disaster effect, observed household welfare for every customer, price gouging, worker security, owner recovery, political legitimacy, or the net effect of subsidizing every damaged firm.

records.title: A year after Hurricane Harvey, recovery disruption and doubts about aid distribution remained concentrated among affected residents
records.source_unit: KFF/Episcopal Health Foundation weighted survey of adults in 24 heavily impacted Texas Gulf Coast counties, fielded late June through late July 2018; follow-up about 10–11 months after Harvey
records.geography: United States; 24 Texas Gulf Coast counties containing about 94% of the population in 41 declared disaster counties
records.boundary: This record closes a descriptive exposure-to-recovery-judgment arrow for a defined Texas Gulf Coast population after Harvey. It does not establish a causal effect of aid, firm survival, customer access, political participation, trust change, or general disaster legitimacy.

records.title: U.S. respondents accept AI assistance more readily than full replacement of human work
records.source_unit: Harvard Business School Working Paper 26-017 and HBS Working Knowledge summary; survey of 2,357 U.S. respondents evaluating 940 occupations
records.geography: United States adult population-matched survey; respondents matched the U.S. adult population on age, gender, ethnicity, and political affiliation
records.boundary: This record adds a U.S. acceptance and human-touch stage between technical capability and firm or consumer implementation. It does not establish actual adoption, worker outcomes, customer behavior, safety, fairness, productivity, or durable trust.

records.title: AI can improve customer-service speed and sentiment while failing to repair systemic complaints
records.source_unit: Randomized field experiment at an unnamed meal-delivery company; 138 customer-service agents and 256,934 online chat conversations, with separate conversation-type and chatbot-handoff comparisons
records.geography: Company customer-service operations; geography and customer demographic coverage are not fully disclosed in the public article summary
records.boundary: This record supports an experiment-based interaction result: AI suggestions can improve speed and measured sentiment, while repeat complaints and poor chatbot handoffs expose limits when the underlying problem is systemic. It does not establish durable customer recovery, refund, correction, retention, switching, household welfare, or a universal effect across firms and platforms.

records.title: Safety-net participation was associated with greater social stigma but not different government perceptions in a California low-income caregiver sample
records.source_unit: Low-income California caregivers of young children surveyed during the first COVID-19 pandemic year, with SNAP and EITC participation measures
records.geography: California, United States
records.boundary: This is a California cross-sectional association between safety-net participation and stigma/government-perception measures, not a causal trust effect, national estimate, or completed take-up-to-action pathway.

records.title: Health costs connect care choices, household adaptation, institutional response, and contested legitimacy
records.source_unit: US household, panel, institutional, and randomized evidence layers; units remain source-specific
records.geography: United States, with Oregon randomized evidence
records.boundary: This record is a layered synthesis, not a same-unit causal chain. The decisive missing link is a dated health-cost episode followed through care choice, household adaptation, institutional remedy, and later trust or action.

records.title: Health-cost burden, credit response, and confidence form linked evidence surfaces but not a same-episode causal chain
records.source_unit: Non-pooled SHED panel, CFPB credit panel/regulatory record, and Census HTOPS respondent comparison
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a non-pooled conversion hypothesis. It does not establish that a health-cost event caused a credit outcome, confidence judgment, trust change, political action, or legitimacy shift.

records.title: Skilled-nursing prior authorization can make appeal effort part of the route to covered care
records.source_unit: HHS Office of Inspector General review of Medicare Advantage skilled-nursing-facility prior authorization
records.geography: United States Medicare Advantage; 19 reviewed organizations
records.boundary: This record establishes a denial, appeal, and overturn pattern for skilled-nursing-facility prior authorization. It does not establish individual medical necessity, delay, care receipt, recovery, caregiver substitution, financial burden, trust, switching, or exit.

records.title: Household adaptation can preserve current life while consuming savings, time, health, or recourse capacity
records.source_unit: Deliberately non-pooled SHED panel paths, SHED population snapshots, and fraud/recovery conditional estimates
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a non-pooled household-adaptation and recovery architecture. It does not establish a causal price or financial shock, a single household stress score, benefit adequacy, health or care effects, verified consumer remedy, later trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence. A dated same-household event ledger with exposure, adaptation, protected/sacrificed outcomes, attribution, remedy, and recovery remains open.

records.title: Household room is layered across resources, tenure, liquidity, and credit
records.source_unit: Cross-source synthesis of SIPP person-record/month comparisons and Federal Reserve SHED adult and consent-linked credit-record measures
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: Bounded cross-source synthesis. It does not create a common-person household-room index or establish a causal tenure, price, credit, or hardship effect; it does not measure dated events, time/care substitution, recovery, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence.

records.title: Housing security has payment, coverage, hazard, and backstop layers that do not yet form a move outcome
records.source_unit: Deliberately non-pooled comparison of Federal Reserve household survey, Treasury/FIO insurance-market data, FEMA hazard context, and California FAIR Plan stocks
records.geography: United States with California residual-market case
records.boundary: This is a non-pooled housing-payment/coverage/hazard/backstop bridge. It supports a staged picture of housing security but does not establish household-level affordability, coverage adequacy, insurer causation, repairs, lending, move/stay outcomes, public legitimacy, or political response. A compatible property/household-year panel with claims, assistance, repair, and mobility outcomes remains open.

records.title: HRSA HPSA component categories condition the interpretation of modeled county social need
records.source_unit: US county with current designated primary-care HPSA component/type/population codes and 2025 CDC PLACES modeled county estimates
records.geography: United States; 2,685 matched counties with at least one designated primary-care HPSA row and selected PLACES measures
records.boundary: This is an overlapping ecological diagnostic. HRSA component and population categories are not mutually exclusive county treatments; PLACES estimates are modeled county averages. The record does not establish resident-level shortage, provider adequacy, causal effects, patient use, household burden, trust, or political action.

records.title: HRSA HPSA operational fields are unevenly populated across designation categories
records.source_unit: Current designated primary-care HRSA HPSA row; operational fields grouped by overlapping designation/type/population categories
records.geography: United States 50 states and DC; territories and Palau excluded; 20,905 rows and 2,888 counties
records.boundary: This record audits current HRSA designation fields. It does not establish active provider capacity, patient access, quality, price, travel, household outcomes, trust, or political response; overlapping component rows must not be summed into national totals.

records.title: A named primary-care site creates a public route beyond a shortage designation while booking and completed care remain unobserved
records.source_unit: HRSA primary-care HPSA and service-site records linked to Health Partners of Western Ohio patient-facing access pages
records.geography: Allen County and Lima, Ohio; North Lima Community Health Center
records.boundary: This record follows a named Ohio primary-care route from shortage designation to shared-organization identity, active service site, nominal hours, patient-facing contact, and affordability policy. It does not estimate usable access, appointment completion, wait, care continuity, health, work, household time or money, trust, switching, or exit.

records.title: Baseline expense difficulty carries a later material-pressure gradient without one universal confidence shift
records.source_unit: April-to-June 2025 Census HTOPS public-use respondent intersection linked by SCRAMID; selected linked sample, not an attrition-adjusted national panel
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record establishes a same-respondent cross-lagged descriptive association between April expense difficulty and selected June material and institutional outcomes. It does not establish a dated bill, actor, causality, attrition-adjusted population transition, remedy, recovery, trust change, political action, switching, or exit.

records.title: Retrospective fraud loss is followed by mixed material and institutional responses in a linked HTOPS panel
records.source_unit: April-to-June 2025 Census HTOPS public-use respondents linked by exact SCRAMID; same-respondent descriptive follow-up, not a representative incident sample or attrition-adjusted causal panel
records.geography: United States HTOPS/HPS public-use panel
records.boundary: This is an associative same-respondent follow-up, not a causal fraud effect or political-action estimate. It does not establish a dated incident, actor responsibility, trust change, remedy receipt, recovery, switching, or exit.

records.title: Retrospective fraud exposure is not equivalent to realized loss or restored household security
records.source_unit: April-to-June 2025 HTOPS same-respondent public-use intersection linked by SCRAMID
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a same-respondent descriptive follow-up. It does not establish a dated fraud effect, verified remedy, restored security, trust change, political action, switching, exit, or causality. Exposure and loss are retrospective, linked retention is selective, and the recovery subgroup has 11 respondents.

records.title: The linked material-to-Congress-confidence path varies by income and race/ethnicity
records.source_unit: US Census HTOPS April and June 2025 linked public-use respondents; subgroup cross-lags among retained SCRAMID matches
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record narrows a same-respondent material-to-institutional-judgment comparison by subgroup. It does not measure attributed responsibility, civic action, vote, remedy, recovery, or causality, and it must not be interpreted as an attrition-adjusted national panel estimate.

records.title: Housing-assistance exit type predicts sharply different housing, health, and wage outcomes
records.source_unit: Heads of household and individuals exiting housing assistance in the HUD HEARS linked administrative-data study
records.geography: King County, Washington; Seattle Housing Authority and King County Housing Authority
records.boundary: This record supplies a same-linked-unit regional housing-exit-to-housing-stability, health, behavioral-health, and wage-outcome bridge. It does not provide a national estimate, causal exit effects, rent burden for every linked unit, household trust, political action, or durable security beyond the one-year outcome window.

records.title: Housing assistance security can become an identity-verification and status-contestation route before household housing security is known
records.source_unit: HUD nationwide eligibility-verification announcement and PHA implementation letter; administrative policy and reported audit counts, not a household outcome sample
records.geography: United States HUD-funded public housing and Housing Choice Voucher programs
records.boundary: This record adds a housing-assistance eligibility, identity-verification, appeal, proration, and possible-termination stage. It does not independently verify HUD's reported audit counts or establish a household's eligibility, notice, appeal, payment, displacement, homelessness, housing quality, trust, or durable housing security.

records.title: A housing voucher can exist while the private-market search remains the practical gate to using it
records.source_unit: HUD summary of NYU Furman Center study using Housing Choice Voucher administrative records; search events and lease-up outcomes, not a same-household wellbeing panel
records.geography: United States Housing Choice Voucher program; national and PHA-level administrative estimates for 2018-2022
records.boundary: This record adds a concrete conversion from nominal housing assistance to private-market search, lease-up, and time burden. It does not establish why a search failed, whether the household received adequate housing, or whether the voucher changed durable housing security, mobility, trust, or political action.

records.title: Nominally affordable rental stock is much larger than affordable, available, and adequate stock
records.source_unit: HUD 2025 Worst Case Housing Needs Report to Congress using Office of Policy Development and Research tabulations of 2023 American Housing Survey data
records.geography: United States; national and Census-region rental-stock comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a national housing-stock constraint between nominal affordability and usable housing. It does not estimate a household's chance of leasing, the causal effect of scarcity on eviction or mobility, or whether a unit is safe, accessible, suitable, or durable for a particular household.

records.title: Food trust is rebounding but health judgments are moving toward ingredients, processing, labels, and perceived control over the food system
records.source_unit: International Food Information Council, 2026 IFIC Food & Health Survey: A Focus on Food & Ingredient Safety, September 8, 2026
records.geography: United States adults ages 18–80, with a first-year Canadian comparison sample
records.boundary: This record adds a U.S. food-culture and public-trust route from food-supply confidence and ingredient concerns through health heuristics, labeling awareness, federalism preferences, household preparation, and everyday risk management. It is a weighted online consumer-panel survey commissioned by IFIC, not a probability sample, behavioral trace, clinical study, or causal measure of food safety or dietary health.

records.title: AI can reduce modeled wage inequality while increasing modeled wealth inequality
records.source_unit: IMF Working Paper 2025/068 calibrated task-based model with household microdata and endogenous firm adoption choice
records.geography: Model-based distributional framework; country/household geography is defined by the paper's microdata and scenario, not a realized US panel
records.boundary: This record captures a calibrated IMF model in which AI can have different wage and wealth distributional channels. It does not establish realized US inequality, actual adoption, worker bargaining power, household security, political response, or geopolitical consequence. The scenario must be compared with observed wages, ownership, firm adoption, taxes, training, and worker outcomes before making a population claim.

records.title: US macro resilience coexists with fiscal, external, and financial-stability tail risks
records.source_unit: IMF 2026 Article IV consultation for the United States; staff estimates, projections, and Executive Board assessment
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds an IMF country-surveillance layer to the US atlas. It distinguishes retrospective aggregate conditions from conditional projections and policy assessment. It does not estimate household welfare, worker control, cultural meaning, political response, firm-level incidence, or geopolitical leverage; those arrows require compatible micro, institutional, and state-response evidence.

records.title: US formal financial access infrastructure contracted while user-reported account ownership remained high
records.source_unit: IMF Financial Access Survey annual administrative/provider-reported US series; IMF.STA:FAS(5.0.0)
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: The IMF FAS US extract establishes a provider-side contraction in commercial-bank and credit-union counts and commercial-bank branch density from 2020 to 2024, alongside falling household commercial-bank deposit and loan ratios to GDP. The World Bank Findex comparison shows high and rising adult account ownership over a partly overlapping period. The divergence is a measurement result, not proof of digital substitution, reduced welfare, exclusion, or improved access. A same-person/account event design is still needed to connect provider change to household terms, travel, payment success, remedy, trust, switching, or exit.

records.title: US provider contraction is widespread across the comparison set, but not universal
records.source_unit: IMF Financial Access Survey annual provider-reported country series; selected economy comparison
records.geography: United States, Canada, Germany, United Kingdom, China, India, Brazil, South Africa, and Mexico
records.boundary: The selected-country comparison shows that US provider contraction is widespread but not universal: Brazil and Mexico report increases in commercial-bank counts, China and India show near-flat branch density, and balance ratios move differently across countries. The result identifies heterogeneous institutional paths, not a global digital-finance mechanism or a household welfare effect. Missing country indicators remain missing, and provider aggregates are not silently converted into user outcomes.

records.title: Geopolitical shocks are modeled as growth, inflation, fiscal, and social-spending trade-offs
records.source_unit: IMF World Economic Outlook country and global projections plus cross-country defense-spending/conflict analysis
records.geography: United States and global/cross-country comparison
records.boundary: This record contributes IMF macroeconomic projections and cross-country defense/conflict trade-off estimates to the US-centered atlas. It does not establish household incidence, firm behavior, public legitimacy, social unrest, political action, alliance behavior, or geopolitical leverage for the United States. Conditional projections, country aggregates, and historical episode estimates remain separate evidence types.

records.title: Critical-infrastructure risk increasingly includes hidden ownership and organizational influence, not only technical compromise
records.source_unit: Idaho National Laboratory feature on TOPGEAR organizational-influence mapping for U.S. critical infrastructure
records.geography: United States; critical infrastructure, foreign ownership, energy, water, and military-adjacent assets
records.boundary: This record adds an organizational-ownership and socio-technical network layer to critical-infrastructure and geopolitical analysis. It does not infer foreign intent, illegal conduct, operational control, realized disruption, public harm, or policy effectiveness from ownership, board, procurement, or network relationships.

records.title: AI infrastructure is becoming a household-cost and local-consent issue while consumers compress spending and protect human service
records.source_unit: Ipsos Consumer Tracker, September 2026 U.S. wave
records.geography: United States; repeated online consumer-attitudes tracker
records.boundary: This record adds a U.S. infrastructure-legitimacy mechanism: AI expansion is being evaluated through water, grid and utility-bill exposure, while household spending compresses and consumers selectively trade brand loyalty for value. records.title: NATO infrastructure enabled a Belgian ISR deployment and named operational use without proving strategic effect
records.source_unit: NATO Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance Force account of a Belgian MQ-9B deployment at Sigonella; named national asset, NATO infrastructure, host-nation support, and operational hours
records.geography: Sigonella, Italy; Belgian MQ-9B deployment supporting NATO's Operation Sea Guardian and Operation Noble Shield
records.boundary: This record establishes a named allied capability deployment enabled by NATO infrastructure and host-nation coordination, with more than 400 reported flight hours supporting two NATO operations. It does not establish mission quality, attributed external response, deterrence, public consent, civilian burden, cost sustainability, replaceability, or durable geopolitical leverage.

records.title: An alliance can translate a hybrid incident into posture and leadership changes before deterrence is verified
records.source_unit: NATO Secretary General statement on Germany and NATO 3.0; official alliance response and posture record, not an independent incident assessment or public-opinion sample
records.geography: Germany, Lithuania, NATO eastern flank, and the North Atlantic Alliance
records.boundary: This record adds a current alliance posture and institutional-response stage, a later post-summit implementation claim, a bounded operational-readiness exercise stage, and dated German and Lithuanian public-legitimacy context layers to the geopolitical/state lane. German support for defense strengthening and European cooperation, lower trust in the United States, limited mission knowledge, and Lithuanian support for the named brigade are separate survey surfaces rather than event-specific consent for the September 2026 posture. The exercise and later NATO statement demonstrate reported training, integration, implementation, and industrial-demand stages but do not establish full operational capability, combat performance, changed adversary behavior, deterrence, local burden acceptance, or durable alliance unity. The next test is an event-country-party-year ledger joining incident verification, allied action, domestic attribution, operational performance, public response, adversary adaptation, and later policy behavior.

records.title: A host-nation rehearsal can make allied movement coordination visible without proving crisis performance
records.source_unit: NATO Rapid Deployable Corps–Italy official account of Steadfast Discovery 26
records.geography: Copenhagen and Herning, Denmark; NATO Allied Reaction Force and Danish host-nation coordination
records.boundary: This record captures an official report of a NATO host-nation rehearsal and its named coordination domains. It does not establish actual deployment performance, civilian service continuity, local consent, cost sharing, legal terms, deterrence, or strategic effect.

records.title: A security mission can adjust posture through local institutional integration before proving durable legitimacy
records.source_unit: NATO public account of KFOR posture adjustment and local security-architecture integration in Kosovo
records.geography: Kosovo; NATO-led KFOR mission and local/regional security institutions
records.boundary: This record establishes an operating and coordination stage in a NATO-led security mission: reported security improvement, gradual posture adjustment, and local institutional integration. It does not establish durable public legitimacy, reduced incidents, changed external behavior, cost distribution, or a completed geopolitical leverage outcome.

records.title: A Baltic air-policing mission moved from standing posture to a real interception while alliance unity was publicly reinforced
records.source_unit: Lithuanian Ministry of National Defence operational account and follow-up statement on NATO air-policing activity
records.geography: Lithuania, Baltic airspace, NATO Baltic air-policing mission, and Italy
records.boundary: This record adds a real operational interception, repeated follow-up alerts, and a later stated NATO posture-adaptation stage to the geopolitical/state lane. It does not establish independent attribution, deterrence, external behavioral change, civilian protection, public consent, cost sustainability, or implemented capability investment. It is distinct from the 2025 Polish airspace episode and from exercise-only records because the official account reports a named 2026 interception.

records.title: NATO moved an AI command-and-control platform from technical capability into exercise integration
records.source_unit: NATO Joint Warfare Centre / Allied Command Operations Maven Smart System implementation record
records.geography: NATO enterprise; Joint Warfare Centre, Stavanger and SHAPE, Belgium
records.boundary: This record establishes technical operational capability, classified-network authorization, and exercise integration of a NATO AI command-and-control platform. It does not establish mission effectiveness, human or public legitimacy, adversary response, deterrence, alliance durability, supplier independence, or geopolitical leverage.

records.title: A NATO ISR adaptation exercise produced flight hours and intelligence products without proving decision effect or public legitimacy
records.source_unit: NATO Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance Force account of the 2026 Adaptable Capability Exercise
records.geography: Finland, Italy, Norway, and NATO operational decision-makers
records.boundary: This record establishes NATO ISR output and alternate-location operational adaptation during a named exercise. It does not establish intelligence quality, decision effect, adversary response, deterrence, public consent, host burden, cost sustainability, or durable geopolitical leverage.

records.title: A multinational ISR capability moved from readiness toward repeated operations with host-nation support
records.source_unit: NATO Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance Force account of Agile Combat Employment 2026; named force-level operating record, not a member-state or public-opinion sample
records.geography: NATO ISR Force operations across Norway, Finland, and Italy in support of Alliance activities
records.boundary: This record adds a later geopolitical realization stage: a named multinational force operated across host nations, produced reported intelligence outputs, and integrated personnel, infrastructure, and host-nation support. It does not establish the content or adequacy of those outputs, changed adversary behavior, deterrence, public consent, host-community burden, or durable alliance leverage. The next test is an event-specific mission or host-nation follow-up with attributed external response, acceptance, cost, or reversal.

records.title: A new NATO ISR mission-operations center entered real-world use while decision quality and strategic effect remained unmeasured
records.source_unit: NATO Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance Force account of the Mission Operations Support Center during Agile Combat Employment and Ramstein Flag 2026
records.geography: Sigonella, Italy and Finland; NISRF distributed ISR operations
records.boundary: This record establishes a named NISRF support facility entering real-world mission operations during ACE/Ramstein Flag 2026. It does not establish technical reliability, product quality, decision effect, workload change, cost sustainability, host burden, adversary response, deterrence, or public legitimacy.

records.title: A NATO ISR mission entered a multinational maritime exercise and supported a surface picture without proving targeting or deterrence effect
records.source_unit: NATO Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance Force account of an RQ-4D Phoenix mission during Exercise Northern Viking 2026
records.geography: GIUK Gap and High North maritime exercise area; NISRF operating from Sigonella, Italy
records.boundary: This record establishes a named NATO ISR mission used in a multinational maritime exercise and reported support to a surface picture for over-the-horizon targeting. It does not establish targeting decisions, engagement, adversary response, deterrence, host burden, public consent, cost sustainability, or durable geopolitical leverage.

records.title: NATO makes civilian resilience part of military readiness while implementation remains open
records.source_unit: NATO 2026 Resilience Baseline Requirements official text
records.geography: NATO civil-military resilience planning and Host Nation Support requirements
records.boundary: This record captures a formal NATO policy connection between civilian resilience and military readiness. It does not establish national implementation, spending, public consent, burden distribution, essential-service performance, Host Nation Support performance, or deterrence and crisis outcomes.

records.title: A NATO technology experiment became a multinational capability commitment without proving deterrence
records.source_unit: NATO Allied Command Transformation account of Task Force X-Baltic testing, allied Phase II commitment, and follow-on procurement
records.geography: Baltic Sea; NATO Allies and critical undersea infrastructure
records.boundary: This record adds a geopolitical conversion from live autonomous-systems testing to multinational institutional commitment, national ownership, and NATO tasking. It does not establish persistent operation, independent performance, adversary response, deterrence, cost sharing, public consent, or durable legitimacy.

records.title: A multinational medical exercise can turn alliance readiness into civilian-military coordination before crisis performance is known
records.source_unit: NATO official report on Vigorous Warrior 2026, an exercise report rather than an independent evaluation of wartime medical outcomes
records.geography: Estonia, NATO member and partner countries, and the Alliance's eastern-flank medical-readiness network
records.boundary: This record adds an operational exercise and civil-military coordination stage to the geopolitical/state lane. It does not establish actual crisis medical performance, patient survival or continuity, local burden distribution, public consent, strategic deterrence, or changed adversary behavior. It is distinct from the Germany/Lithuania brigade exercise because its unit is multinational medical and civilian emergency coordination rather than brigade combat integration.

records.title: A personalized AI conversation can move political preference in an experiment before real-world voting behavior is known
records.source_unit: Peer-reviewed Nature article reporting preregistered randomized human-AI dialogue experiments in the 2024 U.S. presidential election context, the 2025 Canadian and Polish elections, and a Massachusetts ballot measure
records.geography: United States primary case: 2024 presidential election experiment and Massachusetts psychedelic-legalization ballot measure; comparative Canadian and Polish experiments are retained as context
records.boundary: This record establishes randomized evidence that human-AI political dialogues can change stated candidate or policy preferences in specified experiments. It does not establish durable belief change, verified voting, turnout, scalable campaign effects, misinformation prevalence, democratic harm, or population-wide cultural change.

records.title: Political identity is emerging as a health determinant through trust, care engagement, and mortality divergence
records.source_unit: Nature Human Behaviour article by Elizabeth Elder and Neil A. O’Brian (2026); Add Health longitudinal medical, biomarker, and death-record analysis plus an original medical-engagement survey (N=21,751)
records.geography: United States; nationally representative longitudinal cohort and a separately weighted online opinion sample
records.boundary: This record identifies a U.S. trend in which political identity may be becoming a social determinant of health through trust and medical-care engagement. It does not establish that ideology causes mortality, that one party’s beliefs determine health, or that trust is the sole explanation for the observed divergence.

records.title: 988 can improve crisis-line operations without producing a detectable short-run mortality change
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35601, difference-in-differences evaluation of the July 2022 988 implementation
records.geography: United States states with differing pre-988 crisis-line capacity gaps and national suicide-mortality and mental-health outcomes
records.boundary: This record measures an operational gain from 988 implementation and null short-run population outcomes for suicide mortality and broader mental health. It does not establish no individual benefit, no change in crisis access, or a complete test of the downstream care and social-support system.

records.title: The ACA's ban on health underwriting helped low-income, high-risk, and older applicants most
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35692, Health Insurance Underwriting and the Heterogeneous Effects of the Affordable Care Act; proprietary pre-ACA application and underwriting decisions linked to modeled reform effects
records.geography: United States; pre-ACA individual health-insurance applications and underwriting decisions, with effects estimated by age, income, and health risk
records.boundary: This record closes a previously hidden application-and-underwriting margin and shows heterogeneous ACA benefit by income, health risk, and age. It does not establish universal enrollment, continuous care, health improvement, job mobility, or household welfare, and it should not be collapsed into the separate dependent-coverage job-lock finding.

records.title: Large shocks can shape political preferences, risk attitudes, and institutional trust, especially when experienced young
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 32669 and 2025 Journal of Economic Literature review by Paola Giuliano and Antonio Spilimbergo
records.geography: Literature on recessions, inflation, trade, migration, wars, terrorism, pandemics, and natural disasters, including U.S. and cross-national evidence
records.boundary: This record preserves a review-level pattern that shocks can shape preferences, risk attitudes, and institutional trust, with stronger effects in some young-adult exposure settings. It does not estimate one U.S. effect, prove permanence, identify one mechanism, or show that changed preferences became votes, protest, policy, or durable cultural identity.

records.title: AI-driven investing grows in hedge funds while early performance advantages decay and return comovement falls
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35273 using investment-adviser regulatory disclosures, labor-market data, fund strategy descriptions, and hedge-fund performance data
records.geography: United States asset management and hedge-fund market; regulatory disclosures and USD-denominated hedge-fund assets
records.boundary: This record establishes an AI-investing adoption and performance-decay pattern in hedge funds. It does not establish household investment outcomes, market-wide productivity, causal alpha, systemic-risk reduction, worker displacement, or regulatory adequacy.

records.title: AI coding gains attenuate from task activity to shipped and used software
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35275 using GitHub developer data, AI usage telemetry, and four software marketplaces
records.geography: Software development and software marketplaces; U.S.-anchored firm and labor-market relevance with global platform evidence
records.boundary: This record establishes a production-stage gap between AI-assisted coding activity and shipped or used software. It does not establish worker displacement, wage effects, code quality, consumer welfare, firm profitability, bargaining power, or general economy-wide productivity.

records.title: US firms report early AI productivity gains alongside uneven adoption and job-mix reallocation
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34984 / Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta Working Paper 2026-4, Artificial Intelligence, Productivity, and the Workforce: Evidence from Corporate Executives
records.geography: United States; corporate executives surveyed through Federal Reserve executive/CFO survey research
records.boundary: This record adds a US firm-level AI adoption and workforce-expectation layer to the industrial/consumer program. It does not establish a causal AI productivity effect, realized employment change, worker bargaining power, pay, consumer prices, firm survival, or household welfare; executive expectations and revenue-based productivity are not the same as worker or consumer benefit.

records.title: AI forecasts differ mainly over economic consequences and produce distinct policy preferences across expert and public groups
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35046 survey of five groups forecasting the economic effects of AI
records.geography: United States; forecasts and policy preferences from academic economists, AI-company employees, AI policy researchers, highly accurate forecasters, and the general public
records.boundary: This record measures expectations, disagreement, and policy preferences about AI under stated scenarios. It does not establish realized productivity, employment, labor-force participation, GDP, retraining, job-guarantee, UBI, household welfare, or political action.

records.title: AI exposure is not the same as workers' ability to adapt
records.source_unit: occupation-level estimates of worker exposure and adaptive capacity
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This finding adds an exposure-versus-adaptation distinction to the work and technology atlas. It does not show that AI has displaced these workers, that retraining will succeed, or that adaptive capacity is equally available to people with the same occupation. It supports a broader hypothesis that technological risk depends on both the pressure imposed and the usable options available afterward.

records.title: AI exposure estimates can change when the measuring model changes
records.source_unit: large-language-model ratings of occupational AI exposure and downstream statistical estimates
records.geography: United States occupational and county-level analyses
records.boundary: This finding is a measurement-quality counterexample for the AI-work lane. It shows that some LLM-generated exposure inputs are not stable across models and that downstream estimates can change with the input. It does not invalidate every AI-exposure measure, estimate actual worker displacement, or replace substantive labor-market evidence.

records.title: AI makes measurement scalable while moving the bottleneck to construct definition and validation
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35744, a methodological review of AI-generated variables and credible inference
records.geography: Economics research and AI-enabled measurement; general methodological evidence with implications for U.S. public, firm, and institutional measurement
records.boundary: This record establishes a methodological trend: AI can lower the cost of producing structured measures while increasing the importance of construct definition, validation, and interpretive governance. It does not establish accuracy, bias, discrimination, trust, policy effects, or outcomes for any particular U.S. population or institution.

records.title: US firm AI investment is associated with recent productivity growth through organization capital
records.source_unit: US firm-level AI-skilled employment, job descriptions, organization capital, sales per worker, and productivity growth
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a firm-performance signal to the AI-work chain. It does not establish that AI caused the productivity association, that workers received the gains, that job quality or control improved, or that consumers and households benefited.

records.title: AI assistance raised patent-drafting quality, but durable expertise gains depended on seniority
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35720, Does AI Assistance Enhance or Erode Expertise? Evidence from a Three-Month Field Experiment in Patent Drafting
records.geography: United States; 133 practicing patent lawyers at 11 US intellectual-property law firms
records.boundary: This record adds a US industrial/professional-work experiment linking AI assistance, task quality, post-treatment judgment, seniority, and expertise formation. It does not establish general AI productivity, job displacement, pay, worker control, client welfare, firm profitability, legal quality, or durable career effects beyond the participating patent lawyers and study period.

records.title: Personalized AI political advice can trade perceived helpfulness for information quality
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35689; theoretical information and persuasion model of an informed AI adviser and an individual
records.geography: United States-centered AI political-advice mechanism; no empirical geographic sample
records.boundary: This record adds a theoretical AI-advice-to-belief mechanism. It does not establish deployed-system behavior, user-level political effects, polarization, radicalization, voting, trust, or a policy remedy.

records.title: Advanced AI can move the fiscal bottleneck from taxing labor and consumption toward taxing autonomous productive systems
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34873 theoretical primer on public finance under AI transformation
records.geography: General public-finance framework with implications for advanced economies and U.S.-relevant labor, consumption, and AI tax bases
records.boundary: This record adds a theoretical AI-to-tax-base and state-capacity mechanism. It does not establish realized AI displacement, a U.S. revenue loss, a feasible autonomous-system tax, ownership concentration, household incidence, or international tax coordination.

records.title: Training can improve earnings for AI-exposed workers, mainly through moving to less exposed work
records.source_unit: U.S. Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act occupational training spells and matched job-search-only service users
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This finding moves the AI-work lane from occupation-level potential toward an observed training-to-earnings route. It does not prove that training caused every gain, that training is equally reachable, or that higher quarterly earnings mean better job quality, stability, control, household security, cultural meaning, or political action.

records.title: A platform-owned product can help today's customer while changing tomorrow's choice set
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34135 field experiment and model-based counterfactuals on Amazon private labels
records.geography: United States online retail; selected Amazon product categories
records.boundary: This record separates product availability, search placement, observed substitution, search effort, cross-platform substitution, and model-based short-run consumer surplus. It does not establish long-run seller entry or exit, platform self-preferencing, data use, future prices, product quality, durable consumer dependence, or household welfare.

records.title: American Indian outcomes require disaggregated measurement of place, history, governance, and identity
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35730, a methodological and historical essay on economic, educational, health, and human-capital heterogeneity among American Indians
records.geography: United States; American Indian populations and descendants of later arrivals, with urban-rural, tribal, resource, and historical-policy distinctions
records.boundary: This record establishes a measurement and governance boundary: American Indian outcomes are heterogeneous and historically conditioned, and data definitions can obscure both disparities and improvement. It does not provide a single causal estimate, rank tribes, establish current policy effectiveness, or substitute for tribal-specific evidence and sovereignty-aware interpretation.

records.title: Automatic retirement saving expands retirement and liquid-account ownership while also increasing short-term credit-card debt
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35373 SIPP comparison of Oregon Auto-IRA exposure with similar private-sector workers in not-yet-adopting states, as summarized by the Georgetown Center for Retirement Initiatives
records.geography: United States; Oregon policy exposure compared with workers in not-yet-adopting states
records.boundary: This record shows that automatic retirement saving can move several balance-sheet margins at once: retirement ownership/assets, checking/savings ownership/balances, and credit-card debt. It does not establish a single net welfare effect, take-home-pay change, consumption response, debt cost, contribution/withdrawal mechanism, retirement adequacy, or effects by income, age, race, or job type. The public summary should not be treated as a substitute for the full NBER paper or a new independent SIPP estimate.

records.title: Automation can reduce the meaning of retained work before it eliminates jobs
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35559, a theoretical model of automation, worker contribution, compensation, and work meaning
records.geography: Conceptual mechanism with implications for workers and firms; no country-specific outcome sample
records.boundary: This record adds a mechanism between automation exposure and cultural meaning: retained employment does not guarantee retained contribution-based meaning. It does not establish observed worker harm, displacement, compensation, productivity, political action, or firm adoption rates.

records.title: Higher worker autonomy increased preventative risk-management effort in an online labor experiment
records.source_unit: 476 U.S.-located online labor-market workers randomly assigned to high- or low-autonomy transcription conditions
records.geography: United States; online labor market experiment
records.boundary: This record adds a causal task-autonomy-to-risk-management route: high autonomy increased preventative effort in a short online labor task. It does not establish durable worker control, earnings, household security, bargaining power, health, or broad gig-work effects.

records.title: Removing bank fees helps immediately, but wider recovery depends on household liquidity
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34993; individual transaction data and large-bank policy changes that eliminated NSF fees or relaxed overdraft policies from 2017-2022
records.geography: United States; customers of large banks exposed to NSF-fee and overdraft-policy changes
records.boundary: This record adds a liquidity-stratified financial-protection finding: removing a visible fee can be broadly immediate while later recovery differs by household room. It does not establish the original bill, complete household welfare, a universal overdraft effect, or whether payment success prevented or shifted harm.

records.title: Economic coercion can replace military confrontation while retaliation compounds bilateral trade losses
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35077; monthly bilateral GDELT event indicator calibrated against human-curated ground truth and estimated gravity-trade panel
records.geography: Global bilateral country pairs, with the United States-China pair highlighted in the reported trade-at-risk comparison
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative measured geopolitical-to-trade pathway and a retaliation mechanism. It does not establish a U.S.-only effect, household or firm incidence, supply substitution, public legitimacy, alliance durability, or whether economic coercion achieved a political objective. It must not be merged with the separate CRS timeline of 2025 U.S. tariff responses or with model-based claims about reserve status.

records.title: A wage floor can have modest overall employment effects while concentrating pressure on small chains
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35749, establishment-level evidence on California's AB 1228 fast-food minimum wage
records.geography: California fast-food establishments and chains covered or compared under the $20 hourly wage floor effective April 2024
records.boundary: This record adds establishment-level evidence that small-chain entry and exit can move differently from aggregate employment after a wage-floor change. It does not establish worker earnings or hours, consumer prices, service quality, firm productivity, household welfare, or the policy's total causal effect.

records.title: Local electoral accountability shapes drinking-water investment and resident-valued welfare
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35690; California municipal drinking-water systems, local political accountability, investment, pollution, and housing-based water valuations
records.geography: California municipal drinking-water systems and residents near water-system boundaries
records.boundary: This record connects local political accountability to drinking-water investment, pollution, and modeled resident-valued welfare in California. It does not establish national infrastructure performance, household bills, water access, health outcomes, maintenance durability, trust, or geopolitical leverage. Political accountability, investment, realized service, resident valuation, and durable household protection remain distinct stages.

records.title: Capital-gains tax design trades founder dilution against downside insurance in a highly concentrated startup payoff distribution
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34512 using U.S. venture-backed startup, founder, funding-round, exit, and tax-policy model data
records.geography: United States venture-backed startups; tax counterfactuals for founder equity and entrepreneurship
records.boundary: This record establishes a concentrated founder-payoff distribution and a modeled tax-design tradeoff between successful-founder dilution and downside insurance. It does not establish a realized policy effect, startup formation response, employee welfare, innovation, public revenue, or household security.

records.title: A US carbon tariff alone can shift emissions abroad without delivering the full climate result
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35307; quantitative trade and emissions model comparing US carbon tariffs with and without a domestic carbon tax
records.geography: United States and foreign trade partners in the model's carbon-intensive, trade-exposed sectors
records.boundary: This record adds a modeled distinction between domestic emissions, foreign emissions, global climate effect, US welfare, and international coordination. It does not establish real tariff incidence, emissions, firm adaptation, household bills, retaliation, partner acceptance, or durable geopolitical leverage. Model results are not observed outcomes.

records.title: Career attainment can be measured by time to reach a job level, not wages alone
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34292; database of more than 150 million resumes linked to industry, firm-size category, job titles, wages, education, and transitions
records.geography: United States labor-market resumes and public-to-private career transitions
records.boundary: This record adds a career-measurement finding: time to reach a job title contains information not captured by wages alone. It does not establish causal promotion barriers, student-debt effects, job quality, household welfare, discrimination, or that faster title attainment is always better.

records.title: Personalized school outreach increased program take-up while generic digital engagement tools produced mixed learning results
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34996, three randomized field experiments in Chicago Public Schools during remote learning
records.geography: Chicago Public Schools, United States; remote and summer learning interventions
records.boundary: This record measures randomized intervention effects on school registration, attendance, platform use, and selected later academic outcomes in Chicago Public Schools. It does not establish national effects, durable educational attainment, household burden, or a single universal digital-engagement mechanism.

records.title: Child disability benefits help more when they add household resources rather than replace parental earnings
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35725; Social Security administrative data and two quasi-experimental sources of variation in childhood SSI receipt
records.geography: United States; children receiving or near eligibility for Supplemental Security Income and adult outcomes
records.boundary: This record adds a benefit-design and family-work finding: the same child benefit can have different effects depending on whether it increases total household resources or replaces parental earnings. It does not establish a universal SSI effect, a single meaning of parental work reduction, or complete family wellbeing.

records.title: Losing the expanded Child Tax Credit reduced consumer sentiment
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35059; monthly University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Survey microdata and household-level variation in lost 2021 Child Tax Credit benefits
records.geography: United States; households covered by the study's survey and benefit-loss design
records.boundary: This record establishes a policy-to-consumer-sentiment association under the study's identification strategy. It does not establish that the same households changed their spending, trust, vote, political identity, housing security, or long-term behavior. It is one piece of a broader cross-source cultural and political pattern, not a complete household journey.

records.title: Household economic responsibility can create a route into political mobilization
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35287, The U.S. Civil War's Impact on Women's Work and Political Participation
records.geography: United States; wives and daughters of Union Army soldiers and town-level Temperance Crusade activity after the Civil War
records.boundary: This record provides historical evidence that a household economic shock can alter women's labor-market participation and that participation can become one route into collective political mobilization. It does not establish a present-day effect, a universal gender mechanism, individual persuasion, movement success, or a complete path from household burden to durable political power.

records.title: Personalized school-based supports can connect non-cognitive change to long-run educational and earnings outcomes
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35740, staggered rollout of Communities In Schools in high-poverty U.S. schools
records.geography: United States; high-poverty schools participating in Communities In Schools and linked student education and adult earnings outcomes
records.boundary: This record establishes a U.S. personalized school-support-to-long-run-outcome pathway. It does not establish that every student reached receives the same service, identify the separate causal role of each support, measure household trust or wellbeing, or prove general transfer to all schools or communities.

records.title: Competition changed consumer discrimination unevenly across historical local markets
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 33547; historical nationwide data on nondiscriminatory businesses in three industries, exogenous variation in Black-to-White consumer ratios, and more than 25,000 establishment prices
records.geography: United States local markets in the decades leading up to the Civil Rights Act of 1964
records.boundary: This record adds a historical competition-and-discrimination mechanism: market structure and consumer composition changed firm treatment and prices unevenly. It does not establish current discrimination, current consumer welfare, equal service, usable exit, or a universal relationship between competition and fair treatment.

records.title: Low-liquidity households can spend both below and above a frictionless benchmark for different reasons
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34891; administrative transaction data linked to surveyed expectations for middle-income, low-liquidity U.S. consumers
records.geography: United States; middle-income consumers with low liquid wealth in the study population
records.boundary: This record adds a low-liquidity measurement and mechanism finding: similar spending totals can conceal opposite deviations from a modeled benchmark. It does not identify each purchase's need, sacrifice, welfare effect, or later health, work, housing, debt, or political consequence.

records.title: Corporate PACs temporarily reduce visible political giving when reputational risk spikes
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35494; panel of corporate PAC contributions to US House candidates from 2000-2024
records.geography: United States; corporate PACs and US House candidate contributions
records.boundary: This record supports a temporary, selective firm response in visible corporate-PAC giving when reputational risk rises. It does not establish a change in lobbying, policy influence, consumer behavior, public legitimacy, or durable corporate political strategy. The safe-district counterexample and lack of substitution remain part of the finding.

records.title: Survey error often comes from respondents failing to report receipt, not only from nonresponse
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35680; CPS ASEC linked to administrative records for income and program receipt over more than two decades
records.geography: United States; CPS ASEC income and program-receipt variables benchmarked against linked administrative records
records.boundary: This record adds a survey-governance finding: public data can look stable in net terms while individual reporting and absolute error worsen. It does not establish the true population value for every variable, invalidate CPS trends wholesale, or identify each respondent's reason for error.

records.title: US product-market creative destruction passes asymmetric risk through to incumbent workers
records.source_unit: US administrative worker earnings, firm product-market innovation, incumbent employment, and technology-driven creative-destruction measures
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a US product-market-to-worker-risk mechanism. It does not report the abstract's omitted effect sizes, establish causal technology exposure for every worker, measure household hardship, bargaining or voice, or show whether mobility and policy responses restore earnings after job destruction.

records.title: US credit-card banking combines broad household use with unusually high lending spreads and returns
records.source_unit: US credit-card monthly account, issuer economics, and lending-return measures
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record establishes a broad US credit-card account and lender-economics layer. It does not establish the same household's APR, repayment burden, approval or denial, reward net benefit, merchant-price incidence, causal market power, or successful remedy. The account, lender, merchant, and household units remain separate.

records.title: U.S. cultural distance has widened on some political and consumer dimensions, but not everywhere
records.source_unit: Bertrand and Kamenica, NBER Working Paper 24771 and 2023 American Economic Journal: Applied Economics article
records.geography: United States; groups defined by income, education, gender, race, and political ideology; long-run cultural measures using multiple U.S. datasets
records.boundary: This finding measures cultural distance as group distinguishability across several U.S. cultural dimensions. It does not measure polarization as a whole, explain why distance changed, show reduced contact or trust, or establish that cultural distance produced political action, exclusion, or policy change.

records.title: Occupational mobility does not fully erase the long-run earnings cost of starting in a declining occupation
