records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35614; 2000 Decennial Census linked to U.S. administrative employment and earnings records through 2020
records.geography: United States; workers initially employed in occupations that later contracted and their career and family outcomes
records.boundary: This record adds a labor-transition and life-course finding: occupational mobility can be real while long-run earnings losses remain. It does not establish a universal causal effect of occupational decline, complete worker wellbeing, or equal intergenerational opportunity.

records.title: Insurance coverage can become less complete before probable dementia onset while Medicaid eligibility rises without higher take-up
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35606, retrospective Health and Retirement Study analysis of Medicare supplemental coverage around probable dementia onset
records.geography: United States; Medicare-enrolled Health and Retirement Study adults age 65 and older, 2000-2016
records.boundary: This record measures Medicare supplemental-coverage and Medicaid-eligibility differences around probable dementia onset in a historical U.S. survey panel. It does not establish causation, actual care affordability or quality, caregiver burden, financial harm, or the effect of enrollment assistance.

records.title: Dependent health coverage can keep parents in jobs
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 30200; employer-based insurance claims linked to a proxy for parental job retention, using an Affordable Care Act eligibility discontinuity
records.geography: United States parents, dependents, employers, and employer-sponsored insurance; Affordable Care Act dependent-eligibility change
records.boundary: This record adds a coverage-to-job-retention finding: dependent insurance can influence a parent's labor-market decision. It does not establish full job lock, current household welfare, treatment continuity, portability effects, or the quality of the job retained.

records.title: Unexplained digital surveillance reduces remote-worker output in a randomized online labor-market experiment
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 33348, a randomized control trial in an online labor market that separately randomizes digital surveillance and the explanation for its use
records.geography: Online labor market; remote workers and employer-management treatment arms, with no national prevalence claim
records.boundary: This record adds a randomized transparency-and-monitoring mechanism between workplace technology and worker performance. It does not establish surveillance prevalence, national worker exposure, pay, health, autonomy, appeal, remedy, job exit, household security, durable trust, or collective action.

records.title: Reserve-currency demand provides U.S. borrowing capacity whose loss would redistribute fiscal and household room
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35328 and its nontechnical summary; general-equilibrium model calibrated with Federal Reserve Flow of Funds, trade, and convenience-yield evidence
records.geography: United States and global dollar-asset holders; modeled loss of U.S. reserve-currency status
records.boundary: This record adds a reserve-demand-to-state-capacity pathway. It does not establish that the United States has lost reserve status, predict a future depreciation or rate increase, or show distributional household, firm, political, or geopolitical outcomes from such a change.

records.title: U.S. dollar safe-asset convenience remains domestically stable while its global relative advantage has fallen
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35742 measuring convenience yields on U.S. dollar safe assets and comparing domestic and global liquidity
records.geography: United States and global safe-asset markets; U.S. dollar assets, Treasurys, and repo markets
records.boundary: This record establishes a macro-financial distinction between domestic dollar liquidity convenience and global relative safe-asset advantage. It does not establish household welfare, fiscal crisis, reserve-currency loss, sanctions effectiveness, geopolitical coercion, or a causal external response.

records.title: US product-market rivalry shapes investment, markups, and industry concentration
records.source_unit: Universe of US public companies, firm investment, cost of capital, markups, product-market rivalry, mergers, and industry concentration
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a US firm-investment-to-market-structure stage. It does not establish causal consumer-price effects, worker pay or control, household room, political response, or whether any particular merger increased or reduced welfare.

records.title: Online consumer search takes repeated time and can improve price discovery
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 22302; eBay search and purchase behavior dataset
records.geography: Online eBay consumers and purchases; internet search behavior
records.boundary: This record adds an online search-and-price-discovery finding: consumers search repeatedly, incur an estimated search cost, and more search is related to lower prices in the eBay setting. It does not establish product quality, post-purchase recovery, equal consumer power, platform welfare, or the full value of time and attention.

records.title: Policy-induced employment can reduce political participation and shift political identity among lower-income mothers
records.source_unit: Lower-income U.S. mothers observed across historical EITC expansions and 1990s welfare-reform employment instruments
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a U.S. policy-induced-employment mechanism among lower-income mothers, not a universal employment effect or a household-level material-recovery ledger. It reports political participation and identity outcomes but does not establish the exact bill, time tradeoff, childcare route, responsible actor, remedy, source environment, or later switching/exit for the same person.

records.title: EITC expansions increased maternal work while reducing some time with children
records.source_unit: U.S. mothers observed in American Time Use Surveys across EITC expansions since 2003
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a U.S. policy-induced time-allocation mechanism, not a universal employment effect or a complete care ledger. It does not identify the exact household's childcare alternative, employer, remedy, civic response, source environment, or political switching/exit.

records.title: Work incentives can reduce daughters' intensive parent care without a measured replacement
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 32583, revised June 2026; Health and Retirement Study linked to a simulated EITC-benefit approach, with EITC-eligible daughters and parents age 65+ with functional limitations
records.geography: United States; adult daughters eligible for the Earned Income Tax Credit and their older parents
records.boundary: This record adds a policy-incentive-to-family-care substitution pathway and an observed replacement-care gap in the study's population. It does not show that the EITC universally reduces care, that reduced care worsens health, that paid care is unavailable for every family, or that the policy's aggregate welfare effect is negative. Preserve daughter work, parent care, replacement, care quality, health, and household security as separate stages.

records.title: Narrow election wins can direct later political investment and turn prior support into durable local advantage
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34585, revised September 2026; U.S. county presidential-election results, local officeholding, voter support, news coverage, and political-investment evidence
records.geography: United States; counties during presidential-election realignment from 1940 through 1968
records.boundary: This record adds a historical election-result-to-political-investment mechanism. It does not establish current U.S. effects, household outcomes, national policy, trust, or a universal winner/loser response.

records.title: Political office has remained socially selective across US history
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35569, Fortunate Sons: Elite Political Selection in American History, linking historical Members of Congress and family records
records.geography: United States; Members of Congress born 1830–1950 and matched historical census records
records.boundary: This record supports a historical US political-selection pattern: family origin and socioeconomic advantage are overrepresented among Members of Congress, and selected Progressive-Era reforms did not visibly alter that composition in the study's tests. It does not establish current representativeness, present-day causal mechanisms, constituent treatment, policy quality, public trust, or political action by ordinary citizens.

records.title: Well-timed emergency credit can reduce post-disaster financial collapse
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 32845; Federal Disaster Loan applications linked to pre- and post-shock credit records
records.geography: United States households with uninsured damage from federally declared natural disasters and Federal Disaster Loan applications
records.boundary: This record adds a causal emergency-liquidity finding: well-timed disaster credit reduced bankruptcy and increased later car purchases among the studied applicants. It does not establish full recovery, repayment safety, health or job continuity, equal access, or the superiority of loans over grants or other aid.

records.title: Emergency housing assistance can be followed by longer-run employment and earnings gains
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 32856, linked emergency-assistance hotline callers and federal tax records
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record supports a bounded assistance-to-labor-market outcome bridge. It does not establish that the housing crisis was prevented, that the same job was retained, that assistance was adequate, that housing remained stable, or that trust, meaning, switching, or political action changed.

records.title: Rental assistance can improve immediate rent payment and eviction anxiety without producing large measured housing-stability effects
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 32463, revised October 2025, evaluating five emergency rental-assistance programs in four U.S. cities using lottery assignment, administrative data, and surveys
records.geography: Four U.S. cities and five pandemic-era emergency rental-assistance programs distributing more than $200 million; applicant and recipient households in program-specific lottery samples
records.boundary: This record shows a bounded intervention effect: emergency rental assistance improved rent payment and reduced eviction concerns in evaluated pandemic programs, while large housing-stability or financial-distress effects were not detected. It does not establish national prevention of eviction, durable housing security, or a general failure of rental assistance.

records.title: Emergency rental aid can improve immediate payment without changing average housing stability
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 32463; five emergency-rental-assistance programs distributing more than $200 million through lottery, using administrative and survey data
records.geography: United States emergency rental assistance programs in four cities during the COVID-19 pandemic
records.boundary: This record adds a lottery-based rental-assistance finding: aid increased rent payment and reduced eviction concern, with suggestive health gains, but had little average effect on housing stability or financial distress in the pandemic setting. It does not establish lasting affordability, universal effects, or the best intervention outside that context.

records.title: A dominant local employer can turn job dependence into political influence
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35676, Firms as Electoral Monopsonies, using original worker survey evidence, a model of employer influence, and U.S. individual-level voting data with a shift-share design
records.geography: United States; local labor markets, major local employers, individual voting data, national industry concentration shocks, and predetermined local employment shares
records.boundary: This record shows a measured association and modeled mechanism linking local employer concentration to reported employer influence and Republican turnout. It does not show the same worker's message, belief change, vote, job dependence, coercion, welfare, or later willingness to act in one linked record.

records.title: Employment policy can change political participation and policy preferences among lower-income mothers
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34980; five decades of EITC expansions and 1990s welfare reform used as instruments for employment, linked to voting, registration, knowledge, civic engagement, and policy-preference outcomes
records.geography: United States; lower-income mothers represented in the study's policy-induced employment design
records.boundary: This record adds a policy-induced employment-to-political-outcome finding for lower-income mothers. It does not establish the same mother's complete work, care, income, workplace, household-security, trust, or long-term political journey, nor does it show that employment generally causes one political identity. The political endpoint is measured, but the mechanism and wider generalization remain open.

records.title: People can support strong environmental goals while rejecting a policy they think will raise their bills
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35073, comparing a probability-based representative U.S. sample with environmental economists and testing educational videos about pass-through and cost-effectiveness
records.geography: United States; probability-based American respondent sample and expert environmental-economist comparison sample
records.boundary: This record shows that cost beliefs differ between representative respondents and environmental economists, that information can move beliefs and policy support, and that a model can translate those beliefs into different policy instruments. It does not show actual household bills, distributional fairness, pollution or health results, durable belief change, or voting.

records.title: An eviction order can add homelessness, health, work, and credit damage to an earlier housing shock
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 30382; linked administrative data from Cook County and New York City with judge-assignment instrumental variables
records.geography: United States tenants in Cook County, including Chicago, and New York City housing-court systems
records.boundary: This record adds a causal housing-court cascade finding: in two urban housing-court systems, eviction orders added homelessness, hospital visits, earnings loss, reduced durable-goods consumption and credit access, with longer-run indebtedness and lower credit scores. It does not identify the full earlier shock, prove universal effects, or show that a prevented order creates durable housing security.

records.title: Family caregiving is followed by different labor-market paths for women and men
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 31450; survey responses about family caregiving linked to administrative earnings records
records.geography: United States family caregivers and matched comparison workers; long-term-care and labor-market trajectories
records.boundary: This record adds a gender-differentiated caregiving-to-labor trajectory: women show earnings and employment declines relative to a matched comparison after reported caregiving onset, while men enter caregiving after prior labor-supply disruption. It does not identify the full care burden, recipient outcome, causal mechanism, household welfare, or best policy response.

records.title: Unconditional cash transfers can raise adult children's voting propensity without changing parents' voting
records.source_unit: U.S. parent-child households followed across generations with exogenous unconditional cash-transfer exposure and voting outcomes
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a U.S. intergenerational cash-to-voting result, not a contemporaneous adult cash-transfer effect, a trust or policy-approval estimate, or a universal income-to-participation law.

records.title: Perceived Federal Reserve alignment shapes trust, expectations, and information processing
records.source_unit: US consumer survey respondent in randomized information-demand and expectation experiment
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record measures perceived Federal Reserve political alignment, trust, macroeconomic expectations, information demand, information processing, and a hypothetical election response in a 2024 online survey experiment. It does not establish that partisan perceptions reflect actual Federal Reserve bias, cause realized inflation, spending, portfolio, trust, or voting outcomes, or generalize to all US adults.

records.title: Fertility changes US mothers’ labor-force participation and remote-work patterns across the pre- and post-pandemic periods
records.source_unit: US mothers, fertility, labor-force participation, remote work, occupation teleworkability, child penalties, and period before/after 2020
records.geography: United States; American Community Survey, 2003–2024
records.boundary: This record adds a fertility, care, and remote-work arrangement layer to the US industrial/consumer program. It does not establish the size of income, care-time, housing, health, or wellbeing effects, or that remote work is uniformly available or beneficial to mothers.

records.title: People can share a goal of safety while disagreeing about the tool that provides it
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34962, The Universal Pursuit of Safety and the Demand for (Lethal, Non-Lethal or No) Guns
records.geography: United States; original survey of more than 5,400 respondents and randomized information experiments on firearm owners and non-owners
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural-political mechanism: people can share a safety objective while holding different beliefs about which tools make them safe, and information may move safer margins without dissolving identity-linked ownership choices. It does not establish actual firearm use, injury reduction, crime effects, population policy support, or durable public safety.

records.title: Firm-reported AI effects remain limited in retrospect but expand in expectation
records.source_unit: senior business executives and firms
records.geography: United States, United Kingdom, Germany, and Australia
records.boundary: This is a firm-expectations layer for the AI-at-work program. It distinguishes current adoption, low reported retrospective effects, and expected future productivity/output/employment changes. It does not establish realized employment loss, worker control, pay, household security, cultural meaning, political response, or geopolitical power, and it must not be pooled with worker-level telemetry without a common unit and period.

records.title: US financial conditions shape firm insurance and worker labor-income risk
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35781, Risk Premia, Firm Insurance, and Endogenous Labor Income Risk
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a US financial-conditions-to-firm-insurance-to-worker-risk mechanism. It does not disclose the abstract's omitted effect sizes or sample count, establish a named firm or sector outcome, measure household consumption or political response, or show that recession-contingent transfers were implemented and effective.

records.title: Fiscal news can change inflation expectations and spending before a policy is received
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35009; randomized fiscal-news information treatments linked to high-frequency spending data for approximately 11,000 Korean individuals
records.geography: South Korea; international comparison mechanism for the U.S.-centered atlas, not a U.S. household estimate
records.boundary: This record adds a cross-country mechanism test: fiscal information can move expectations and spending before a household receives a policy. The Korean result is not a U.S. estimate, and neither source alone establishes a same-household path from news through trust, liquidity, policy realization, final bill, or political action.

records.title: The financing regime of redistribution can reshape top-wealth accumulation and fiscal incidence
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35715; structurally estimated New Keynesian model with borrowers and savers, calibrated to U.S. macro-financial evidence
records.geography: United States; post-1980 fiscal-financing regime and top-income asset accumulation
records.boundary: This record adds a fiscal-financing-to-wealth-distribution mechanism. It does not directly observe a single household's transfer, tax, saving, debt, consumption, trust, political action, or durable security, and it does not rank inflationary versus debt finance as a universal welfare prescription.

records.title: Flood buyouts can reduce physical exposure while distributing compensation and relocation gains unequally
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35726; federal property acquisitions, housing sales, restricted-use Census microdata, and individual movement records
records.geography: United States; nationwide federal flood-property buyouts and post-buyout neighborhood movement
records.boundary: This record adds a climate-adaptation and unequal-mobility finding: leaving physical flood exposure can still involve unequal compensation and destination outcomes. It does not establish a universal racial mechanism, a causal effect of every buyout program, or complete household wellbeing after relocation.

records.title: Household-level flood exposure is not the same as aggregate floodplain disadvantage
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35204; confidential linked U.S. Census survey and administrative data with parcel-level flood risk and insurance coverage measures
records.geography: United States households, housing parcels, and floodplains; 1999–2023 exposure trend and household-level comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a household-level exposure and insurance comparator to the housing chain. It does not establish that flood-risk disclosure caused migration, that insurance is adequate, or that protection produced safe occupancy, repair, affordability, or durable household security.

records.title: Career information about work-life balance is distributed differently by student gender and shapes career intentions
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35750, preregistered field experiment connecting college students to 10,000 working professionals
records.geography: United States; college students seeking career information and working professionals responding to randomized messages
records.boundary: This record establishes a gendered career-information and intention pathway in a field experiment. It does not establish realized occupation, earnings, work-life balance, care burden, discrimination, household security, or universal transfer across fields and institutions.

records.title: Gender-specific labor shocks reallocate household consumption without changing total child-product spending
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35118, Gender-Specific Economic Shocks and Household Bargaining Power
records.geography: United States; heterosexual households, product-level consumption patterns, and US industrial robot and fracking shocks
records.boundary: This record adds a US industrial-shock-to-household-consumption route. It distinguishes product-composition changes, total child-product spending, and suggestive versus stronger shock evidence; it does not directly measure bargaining power, decision rights, wellbeing, parental time, prices, employment quality, or child outcomes.

records.title: Geoeconomic coercion can target foreign governments, private firms, or both
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35343; theoretical model of great-power geoeconomic coercion through trade and financial linkages
records.geography: United States/China-style hegemonic relationships with foreign governments and private firms
records.boundary: This record adds a model-based target-selection mechanism for geoeconomic coercion. It does not establish which target type is used more often, whether a target complies, who bears the cost, how domestic publics respond, whether alliances change, or whether coercion achieves a strategic objective.

records.title: A competing platform can give gig workers more leverage over the first platform
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35626, randomized pay experiments among Uber drivers paired with a natural experiment in access to a competing platform
records.geography: United States gig-economy drivers; the public abstract does not fully specify the study-area frame
records.boundary: This record measures how competitor access changes labor supply to Uber and the implied firm markdown in a gig-work setting. It does not establish durable worker control, net household income, job quality, benefits, safety, or a general result for all independent contractors or U.S. workers.

records.title: Cash paid to one person can change the work, care, and relationships of the whole household
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35589, randomized guaranteed-income experiment in which 1,000 people received $1,000 per month for three years and 2,000 controls received $50 per month
records.geography: United States; low-income experiment participants and their household members, with treatment and control groups observed over the experiment period
records.boundary: This record shows that an individual cash transfer can spill over into other household members' education, work, transfers, relationships, and reported healthcare decisions. It does not establish that every household became more secure, that lower partner earnings were harmful rather than chosen or necessary, or what happened after payments ended.

records.title: Large guaranteed-income transfers did not produce the expected political mobilization or trust shift
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 33214; randomized guaranteed-income field experiment with 1,000 low-income treatment participants and 2,000 controls, linked to political-attitude and behavior measures
records.geography: United States; low-income adults enrolled in a randomized guaranteed-income experiment
records.boundary: This record adds a causal income-to-political-attitudes/behavior test: a large three-year guaranteed-income transfer did not detectably change political participation, engagement, broad preferences, government trust, polarization, or support for democracy in the study population. It does not establish that material conditions never affect politics, that all subgroups are unaffected, or that household work, relationship, health, or meaning pathways are absent.

records.title: Extending Head Start hours increased maternal work outcomes in targeted areas
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34831; 2016 federal Head Start full-day expansion, administrative program data, geocoded centers, and household employment outcomes
records.geography: United States; Head Start grantees and mothers in treated and untreated areas
records.boundary: This record adds an experimental-policy-to-formal-care-to-maternal-work conversion. It does not establish universal childcare effects, childcare quality, child wellbeing, maternal time satisfaction, equal access, household recovery, or durable political meaning.

records.title: Health-insurer concentration links market power and adverse selection to premiums, plan design, and consumer welfare
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34928, Competition in Health Insurance Markets
records.geography: United States; commercial, Medicare Advantage, and Medicaid health-insurance markets
records.boundary: This record adds a US health-insurance competition route linking concentration, adverse selection, premiums, plan design, consumer welfare, and policy remedies across commercial, Medicare Advantage, and Medicaid markets. It does not establish a universal concentration threshold, enrollee-level welfare effect, realized remedy, provider quality, health outcome, or household recovery.

records.title: A Medicaid drug subscription model expanded hepatitis-C treatment and produced measurable health and fiscal outcomes
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35583, using Louisiana Medicaid, hepatitis-C diagnosis, spending, and health-outcome data
records.geography: Louisiana Medicaid; Louisiana Hepatitis C Elimination Plan beginning in 2019
records.boundary: This record measures a Louisiana Medicaid subscription model through treatment, diagnosis, spending, and estimated savings outcomes. It does not establish individual cure completion, equal access, household financial effects, long-run eradication, or national transferability.

records.title: Historical U.S. risk preferences shaped leverage, institutional participation, and technology adoption
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35634 using historical U.S. crop choice, agronomic, climate, bond, institutional, and mechanization data
records.geography: United States county-level risk preferences and farmer-level Kansas estimates, 1889-1929
records.boundary: This record establishes a historical U.S. risk-preference measurement and association chain from crop choice to leverage, civic-financial participation, local risk sharing, and mechanization. It does not establish contemporary cultural traits, individual psychology, causal institutional trust, present-day political action, or universal technology-adoption behavior.

records.title: Home equity can enable longer-lived and more varied entrepreneurship, but only for a small share of entry
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 21458; U.S. Census Bureau data on entrepreneurship and a 1998 Texas reform allowing home-equity lending
records.geography: United States local entrepreneurship, 1992–2007, with a Texas home-equity-lending reform case
records.boundary: This record adds a housing-collateral-to-entrepreneurship finding: home equity can enable longer-lived and more sector-balanced business entry, but the identified collateral channel is a small share of overall house-price-associated entry. It does not establish local ownership, customer benefit, job quality, durable survival, or household safety.

records.title: A homeowner's credit record can raise the price of disaster protection alongside physical risk
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34848; approximately 70 million mortgage-linked insurance policies matched to property-level disaster risk and a Washington State natural experiment
records.geography: United States homeowners insurance and mortgage-linked policies; credit-pricing natural experiment in Washington State
records.boundary: This record adds a protection-price pathway: credit and physical risk can both enter the cost of keeping a home insured. It does not establish a same-owner path from premium to escrow trouble, coverage cut, repair, sale, move, claim recovery, or complete housing security.

records.title: Temporary shelter produces public health and safety benefits without clearly reducing future homelessness
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34376, Los Angeles County homeless-services administrative records and shelter-availability variation
records.geography: Los Angeles County, California, United States
records.boundary: This record supports a temporary-shelter-to-public-health-and-safety bridge with a future-homelessness null comparison. It does not establish durable housing, individual service adequacy, resident consent, trust, political action, or a universal shelter effect.

records.title: Preserving homeownership after mortgage distress raised housing wealth without raising consumption
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 33692; mortgage-modification comparison linked to long-run housing wealth and consumption outcomes
records.geography: United States; homeowners seriously delinquent during the Great Recession and mortgage-modification eligibility
records.boundary: This record adds a housing-wealth conversion counterexample: preserving an asset can raise measured wealth without raising current consumption. It does not establish that homeownership has no security value, that every modification has the same effect, or that consumption is the complete household-welfare outcome.

records.title: Urban redevelopment can create large displacement losses while vouchers and counseling only partly offset them
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35736, The Welfare Impacts of Urban Renewal and Forced Relocation: Evidence from Chicago's HOPE VI Demolitions; administrative records of displaced public-housing residents, Census sorting and prices, and a neighborhood-choice model
records.geography: Chicago public-housing developments affected by HOPE VI demolition and redevelopment
records.boundary: This record closes a redevelopment-to-modeled-welfare and policy-offset arrow: forced relocation creates losses, vouchers and counseling partly mitigate them, and neighborhood prices and gains are redistributed toward higher-income homeowners. It does not establish universal redevelopment effects, individual housing stability, or complete resident wellbeing.

records.title: Legal representation changes the immediate housing-court path for poor tenants
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 29836; New York City Universal Access to Counsel rollout and address-level housing-court data
records.geography: New York City tenants and housing courts; address-level court data from 2016–2019
records.boundary: This record adds a court-access finding: New York City tenants who gained Universal Access legal representation had better immediate housing-court outcomes. It does not establish lasting housing stability, affordability, debt resolution, work or health recovery, or universal effects outside the program and city.

records.title: Homeowners with greater electoral participation also accumulate housing wealth more effectively
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35731; nationwide voter-property dataset, property transactions, and original survey evidence
records.geography: United States; homeowners and property transactions in a nationwide voter-property dataset
records.boundary: This record adds a politically engaged homeowner-to-housing-wealth association. It does not establish a causal effect of voting, explain renter outcomes, measure affordability or displacement, or show that wealth accumulation produces broader representation, trust, or political power.

records.title: Hurricane exposure can move a representative's climate-policy agenda and carry a later electoral cost
records.source_unit: U.S. congressional districts, representatives, federal disaster declarations, roll-call votes, and subsequent elections in the NBER study period
records.geography: United States congressional districts affected or not affected by hurricanes, 1989–2014
records.boundary: This record adds a bounded disaster exposure → representative policy response → later electoral consequence pathway. It does not establish individual household loss, attribution, trust, voter-level meaning or action, policy implementation, climate outcomes, recovery, or a universal disaster-to-political-response rule.

records.title: Immigrant earnings assimilation and return migration are separate outcomes
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35582 using longitudinal administrative earnings records for immigrant workers and native-born comparison workers, 1981-2021
records.geography: United States; immigrant arrival cohorts 1981-2010 and native-born earnings comparison
records.boundary: This record adds a migration-selection and earnings-convergence layer to the belonging and mobility themes. It does not establish a causal assimilation effect, the reasons for return, earnings parity in every subgroup, household security, legal inclusion, belonging, or political action. Stayers and return migrants must remain separate outcomes rather than being treated as one immigrant trajectory.

records.title: US minimum-wage increases reduce hours for recently arrived immigrant workers without reducing employment
records.source_unit: US immigrant and native workers, arrival status, employment, hours, turnover, and minimum-wage exposure
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a worker-subgroup and hours-adjustment signal to the US minimum-wage chain. It does not disclose effect sizes, prove the full causal mechanism, measure immigrant legal status directly, or establish effects on household income, consumption, prices, profits, automation, worker voice, or long-run mobility.

records.title: Historical immigration exposure altered local child mortality through disease-environment spillovers
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35743 using Massachusetts town-level mortality and immigration panel data, 1860-1915
records.geography: Massachusetts towns during the U.S. Age of Mass Migration, 1860-1915; historical place-level evidence rather than a contemporary national estimate
records.boundary: This record establishes a historical Massachusetts place-exposure and child-mortality mechanism during 1860-1915. It does not establish contemporary immigration effects, individual immigrant mortality, a universal disease pathway, present-day public opinion, or current policy consequences.

records.title: New residents can add workers and customers, while local housing and public capacity remain separate questions
records.source_unit: Two NBER research sources: a U.S. Census local-demand study using 1980-2000 data and a 2026 study of the 2021-2024 postpandemic immigration surge using descriptive facts and a heterogeneous-agent model
records.geography: United States; local labor markets and non-traded services in the 1980-2000 Census study, and national U.S. macroeconomic conditions in the 2021-2024 surge study
records.boundary: This record shows that immigrants can affect local labor demand through consumption and that recent national supply and demand effects may offset in an inflation model. It does not establish current local housing, service, wage-quality, public-capacity, belonging, or political outcomes, and the two source periods and units are not pooled.

records.title: People can agree inflation is harmful while disagreeing about its cause and remedy
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 32497; U.S. online survey with a conjoint experiment and an information experiment about perceived inflation causes, consequences, trade-offs, and policy responses
records.geography: United States; survey conducted March–May 2024 using the Lucid online platform, with a sample constructed to mirror the U.S. population in 2022
records.boundary: This record adds a public-belief layer between material price pressure and political judgment: people can share a negative assessment of inflation while assigning responsibility and acceptable remedies differently. It does not establish a household-to-ballot path, actual price burden, durable belief change, or which policy would improve a particular household's outcome.

records.title: Homeowners and renters translate inflation information into different spending responses
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 33595, revised July 2026; randomized inflation-information treatments among U.S. households with homeowner/renter comparison
records.geography: United States; household information experiment and homeowner/renter subgroups
records.boundary: This record adds a controlled belief-to-spending and unequal-adjustment-margin mechanism. It does not establish a political action effect, total welfare, realized inflation exposure, or a complete household event-to-recovery path.

records.title: Asymmetric import dependence can create bargaining power that changes engagement and trade adjustment
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34006; model-implied bilateral import-dependence measure combined with bilateral engagement events and a high-frequency geopolitical-relationship measure
records.geography: Global country pairs over roughly the prior 20 years, with implications for U.S.-linked trade and geopolitical dependence treated as comparative context
records.boundary: This record adds a modeled dependence-to-negotiation and anticipatory-trade-adjustment pathway. It does not establish observed coercive leverage in a named episode, a policy concession, successful deterrence, U.S.-specific incidence, firm substitution, household cost, alliance behavior, or durable geopolitical change. Keep model-implied power, engagement, trade adjustment, retaliation, and strategic outcome as separate stages.

records.title: Voluntary jail healthcare accreditation improves care standards and reduces mortality without added capital or labor inputs
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 33357, randomized offer of healthcare accreditation across 46 U.S. jails
records.geography: United States; 46 midsized jails with average daily populations between 100 and 3,000
records.boundary: This record establishes an experimental institutional-practice-to-care-and-mortality route in selected U.S. jails. It does not establish post-release health, recidivism, household outcomes, trust, fairness of detention, contractor-wide performance, or general correctional-system effects.

records.title: Randomized job-search assistance produced long-run employment gains with heterogeneous downside and housing effects
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 24422, randomized Nevada unemployment-insurance job-search assistance linked to administrative tax and housing outcomes
records.geography: Nevada, United States
records.boundary: This record supports a randomized offer-to-long-run administrative-outcome bridge. It does not establish that counseling alone caused the effects, that jobs were higher quality, that housing became adequate, that health or care improved, or that participants experienced durable trust, meaning, or political action.

records.title: Workers trade wage gains against layoff risk, and incomplete insurance can suppress mobility
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35580; representative survey of employed U.S. workers plus a general-equilibrium search model with wage and unemployment-risk job ladders
records.geography: United States; employed workers and modeled labor market
records.boundary: This record adds a measured wage-for-security trade-off and a modeled insurance-to-mobility mechanism. It does not establish actual job switching, household security, worker voice, or universal effects of unemployment insurance in observed administrative data.

records.title: K–12 AI integration is lower in more disadvantaged schools while policy, training, and guidance lag adoption
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35347 national survey of K–12 school principals
records.geography: United States; K–12 schools and school-level AI integration
records.boundary: This record measures school-level AI integration and institutional support gaps. It does not establish a causal technology-access effect, learning outcome, teacher or student wellbeing effect, privacy or safety incident, or household inequality outcome.

records.title: Worker and firm heterogeneity can explain much of the variation in wage markdowns
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35640, a model of labor supply elasticities, heterogeneous workers and firms, wage setting, and tax progressivity
records.geography: Conceptual model calibrated and discussed in relation to U.S. labor-market evidence; no single administrative sample is the observation unit
records.boundary: This record adds a firm-worker heterogeneity mechanism: market power and policy incidence depend on who sorts into which firms and how elastic labor supply is across margins. It does not establish observed worker harm, wage markdowns for a named firm, or a universal tax-policy effect.

records.title: Business applications and employer-firm formation are different local economic stages
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34881; linked administrative microdata tracking the universe of U.S. business applications and transitions into employer firms
records.geography: United States counties and local areas; business applications and employer-firm transitions
records.boundary: This record adds a local conversion finding: an application is pursuit, while an employer firm is implementation. It does not establish durable survival, job quality, local service, customer benefit, household welfare, belonging, or political participation.

records.title: Local electoral maps can be formally neutral while producing unequal racial representation
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35623; nationwide voter-file, Census, local electoral-map, and simulated-map analysis
records.geography: United States; 3,712 city council and county commission maps covering 18,521 districts
records.boundary: This record adds a local-democracy representation finding: geography, formal neutrality, enacted boundaries, legal oversight, and officeholder composition can diverge. It does not establish a single causal effect of maps on policy, welfare, trust, participation, or national political alignment.

records.title: Long-term moderate PM2.5 exposure increases circulatory disease among US soldiers
records.source_unit: US Army soldiers, annual PM2.5 exposure, duty-station assignment, circulatory disease, hypertension, respiratory disease, and duration of exposure
records.geography: United States; Army duty stations
records.boundary: This record adds a long-duration environmental-health layer to the US industrial/consumer program. It does not disclose effect sizes, establish universal civilian effects, measure household pollution, costs, worker choice, local political response, or a complete climate-health pathway in the same unit.

records.title: A randomized purpose intervention changed worker performance, retention, priorities, and parental-leave behavior
records.source_unit: 2,976 white-collar employees in a firm randomized to a worker-centered purpose intervention or comparison condition
records.geography: United States; firm-based worker experiment
records.boundary: This record adds a firm-level randomized meaning-to-work-outcome route: a purpose intervention changed performance, retention pathways, stated priorities, parental-leave behavior, and bonuses. It does not establish household welfare, durable worker control, bargaining power, broad labor-market generalization, or political action.

records.title: Managed Medicaid long-term services can spill into Medicare-financed health outcomes differently across states
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35055 using Medicare claims, Medicaid managed-LTSS rollout timing, and county-level differences-in-differences
records.geography: Florida and New York dual-eligible Medicare-Medicaid beneficiaries age 65 and older; Pennsylvania and California counties provide comparison counties
records.boundary: This record establishes a state-heterogeneous managed-LTSS-to-health route and a possible cross-payer spillover. It does not establish universal managed-care effects, individual care quality, household cost, long-term functional status, mortality, trust, or why Florida and New York differ in full.

records.title: US Medicaid nursing-home financing can reward volume over quality and shift patients toward worse providers
records.source_unit: US Medicaid nursing-home financing, federal matching grants, state creative financing, dementia admissions, facility quality, and one-year survival
records.geography: United States; 24 federal audits and Indiana administrative microdata
records.boundary: This record adds a Medicaid payment-design and patient-allocation layer to the US nursing-home chain. It does not establish that every matching grant causes harm, disclose all effect sizes, or measure worker outcomes, resident voice, prices, access, or long-run care quality in one common unit.

records.title: Navigator outreach can convert administrative help into Medicaid renewal, with uneven contact reach
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34191, Navigating Medicaid: Experimental Evidence on Administrative Burden and Coverage Loss; J-PAL evaluation summary of the Wisconsin field experiment
records.geography: United States research context; Wisconsin Medicaid fee-for-service renewal population
records.boundary: This is an experimental Wisconsin renewal-assistance result, not a national Medicaid retention rate or a complete household health outcome. It closes assignment-to-renewal and assignment-to-procedural-denial arrows while leaving contact reach, care continuity, health, cost, trust, and later security open.

records.title: Political persuasion can travel through repeated physical proximity, not only ideology or formal affiliation
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34925; randomized U.S. Senate seating assignments, recorded interactions, and legislative votes over a 30-year sample
records.geography: United States Congress
records.boundary: This record adds a causal micro-mechanism for political action: physical and repeated peer exposure can affect legislative voting. It does not establish a general solution to polarization, mass persuasion, public trust, or durable constituent realignment.

records.title: US minimum wages have adverse employment, hours, and earnings effects for low-wage workers in poor families
records.source_unit: US low-wage workers, family income-to-needs position, employment, hours, earnings, and minimum-wage policy
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a household-positioned labor-policy signal. It does not disclose effect sizes or prove that minimum wages caused the reported adverse outcomes, and it does not measure worker voice, prices, firm profits, automation, benefits, consumption, poverty transitions, or political response in the same unit.

records.title: Monetary-policy expectation estimates vary with the design used to measure the announcement response
records.source_unit: US household respondent in a two-wave survey comparison around a Federal Reserve announcement
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record promotes the author-hosted August 2026 full-paper estimates and design audit while preserving the working-paper, survey-expectation, reduced-form, exposure, and no-realized-action boundaries. It does not establish a structural monetary-policy shock, general-equilibrium effect, household spending/debt response, trust change, or political consequence.

records.title: US labor-market power cannot be read from wage markdowns alone
records.source_unit: US labor-market-power literature, firm-specific residual labor-supply elasticity, search frictions, worker preferences, employer concentration, and wage-setting practices
records.geography: United States and comparative labor-market evidence reviewed for US policy analysis
records.boundary: This record supplies a measurement framework for the US firm-power chain. It does not substitute for industry-level worker, firm, customer, or household outcome evidence and should not be used to rank firms by power without compatible elasticity, wage-setting, outside-option, and concentration measures.

records.title: Mortgage lock-in can turn higher rates into constrained staying and a more expensive housing ladder
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35237; individual-level mortgage data and spatial housing-ladder model
records.geography: United States housing market, mortgage borrowers, and modeled spatial housing ladder
records.boundary: This record establishes a mortgage-rate-to-lock-in-to-mobility pathway with modeled housing-price and rent consequences. It does not establish that every household's staying was involuntary, or measure repair, insurance, health, care, work, trust, or durable housing security after the move decision.

records.title: When voters cannot see all candidate preferences, cultural issues can become especially useful political signals
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34909, a formal model of multidimensional political signaling
records.geography: Political model with relevance to U.S. campaign communication; no U.S. respondent or election sample
records.boundary: This record adds a formal mechanism for why cultural political signals may become prominent when broader preferences are hard to observe. It does not show that current U.S. voters are uninformed, that cultural politics is replacing economic politics, that candidates caused voter beliefs, or that rhetoric produced policy change.

records.title: US multinationals concentrate foreign profits in tax-planning structures adopted by a minority of firms
records.source_unit: US multinational firms, foreign profits, tax-planning structure adoption, foreign effective tax rates, domestic and foreign investment, and global R&D
records.geography: United States multinationals with foreign operations
records.boundary: This record adds a multinational tax-planning and public-revenue layer to the US industrial program. It does not establish tax evasion, quantify realized revenue loss, or measure domestic employment, consumer prices, worker outcomes, or household welfare in the same unit.

records.title: Mixed native-immigrant founding teams show a firm-level complementarity in U.S. startup outcomes
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 33804 using linked U.S. startup, founder, employee, education, employment, funding, and exit records
records.geography: United States; startups and founders observed through linked administrative and commercial records
records.boundary: This record measures a bounded firm-level complementarity between native and immigrant founders in U.S. startups. It does not establish a universal immigrant entrepreneurship effect, worker bargaining power, wage gains, consumer welfare, community spillovers, or a complete causal account of the mechanisms behind the observed startup outcomes.

records.title: A healthy-food price wedge can exist without a detectable maternal or newborn health improvement
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35662, difference-in-differences and event-study evaluation of the Navajo Nation Healthy Diné Nation Act
records.geography: Navajo Nation; Healthy Diné Nation Act implemented in 2014-2015, with maternal and newborn outcomes from birth-certificate data
records.boundary: This record measures a place-specific fiscal food-policy design and a reported null result for maternal and newborn diet- and weight-related outcomes. It does not establish no change in purchases, no community benefit, cultural rejection, policy failure everywhere, or long-run health and household effects.

records.title: Where a child lives can shape later opportunity because housing markets do not price or finance all opportunity well
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35419, U.S.-centered review of experimental and quasi-experimental neighborhood-effects evidence and opportunity-market failures
records.geography: United States; childhood neighborhoods, residential sorting, housing mobility, and mixed-income policy
records.boundary: This review record summarizes U.S.-centered evidence that neighborhood exposure and housing-market failures can shape long-term opportunity. It does not provide one pooled causal estimate, show that every voucher or mobility service improves outcomes, or follow one family from housing search through durable adult security.

records.title: No-Surprises arbitration can strengthen provider bargaining power while narrowing networks and raising premiums
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35717, The No Surprises Act's Surprises: Arbitration, Provider Network, and Insurer Pricing; linked arbitration, provider-insurer network, and ACA marketplace plan data
records.geography: United States; national provider-insurer network panel and ACA marketplace plan data, with effects concentrated in specialties and states most affected by the No Surprises Act
records.boundary: This record closes a policy-to-provider-bargaining and provider-network arrow: formal patient liability protection can strengthen an affected provider group's outside option, coincide with narrower networks, and potentially raise premiums. It does not establish patient-level access, realized bills, care, health, or household welfare.

records.title: Predictable nursing-home inspections can make care effort rise and fall around the inspection window
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34491, revised June 2026, using U.S. nursing-home inspection records and patient outcomes; NBER Bulletin summary supplies reported model estimates
records.geography: United States Medicare- and Medicaid-certified nursing homes; inspections 2006-2019 and patient outcomes 2013-2019
records.boundary: This record measures inspection timing, facility effort, selected patient survival outcomes, and model-based inspection designs in U.S. nursing homes. It does not establish complete care quality, resident wellbeing, causal effects for every facility, or the final impact of any adopted inspection reform.

records.title: US nursing-home inspections trigger temporary quality responses while ratings still predict relative mortality
records.source_unit: US nursing homes, government inspections, facility quality responses, inspection ratings, admissions, and patient mortality
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a measurement and persistence layer to the US nursing-home regulation chain. It does not disclose effect sizes, prove that inspections cause lower mortality, establish absolute quality, or measure worker conditions, resident voice, prices, profits, or long-run access in the same unit.

records.title: US nursing-home mergers reduce deficiency citations but also reduce direct-care hours without improving resident health
records.source_unit: US nursing-home chain mergers, facility quality citations, direct-care hours, marginal cost, and resident health outcomes
records.geography: United States; nursing-home facilities observed 1999–2019
records.boundary: This record adds an ownership and compliance-versus-care comparison to the US nursing-home chain. It does not establish that mergers improve or worsen overall quality, and it does not measure worker voice, prices, profits, resident experience, access, or long-run health in the same unit.

records.title: US nursing-home profits are widely tunneled to related parties, changing the apparent return and regulatory picture
records.source_unit: US nursing-home providers, related-party real-estate and management payments, reported profits, assets, investment returns, reimbursements, and liability exposure
records.geography: United States; nursing-home providers
records.boundary: This record adds a financial-governance layer to the US nursing-home chain. It does not establish illegality, resident or worker harm, reimbursement fraud, clinical quality effects, prices, access, or causal links between tunneling and care outcomes in the same unit.

records.title: US nursing-home roommate assignment changes mortality through patient peer effects
records.source_unit: US nursing-home stays, roommate cognitive status, private-room placement, patient diagnosis, and 90-day mortality
records.geography: United States; 7,200 nursing homes
records.boundary: This record adds a patient-peer and placement layer to the US nursing-home chain. It does not establish a universal roommate policy, disclose implementation costs, or measure privacy, resident preference, worker effects, quality of life, access, or current outcomes in the same unit.

records.title: California nursing homes manipulate size thresholds to avoid staffing rules, limiting access for disadvantaged patients
records.source_unit: California nursing-home facilities, bed-count threshold, staffing requirements, facility size manipulation, and patient access
records.geography: United States; California nursing homes
records.boundary: This record adds a firm-response and consumer-access layer to the US nursing-home regulation chain. It does not disclose effect sizes or establish clinical harm, worker outcomes, price effects, ownership effects, or a universal response to staffing regulation outside California nursing homes.

records.title: Congestion pricing can make emergency medical response faster inside a city pricing zone
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35414, using New York City congestion-zone boundary, traffic and mobility measures, and emergency medical service performance
records.geography: New York City; congestion-relief zone boundary at 60th Street
records.boundary: This record adds a measured policy-to-service route: congestion pricing changed traffic conditions and EMS travel time near a New York City boundary. It does not establish patient survival, treatment quality, affordability, distributional fairness, long-run traffic adaptation, or political acceptance of the charge.

records.title: A lawyer can change an eviction case even when the rent problem remains
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 29836, Cassidy and Currie, using detailed New York City housing-court records and the staggered rollout of the Universal Access to Counsel program from 2016 through 2019
records.geography: New York City housing-court cases filed at addresses in rollout and comparison zip codes; low-income tenants targeted by the program
records.boundary: This record shows that tenant legal representation changed measured housing-court judgments, monetary judgments, and eviction-warrant outcomes in New York City. It does not show that the underlying rent problem disappeared, that every tenant remained housed, or what happened to the same tenants' later work, health, credit, schooling, or housing choices.

records.title: A coordinated office day can improve communication and retention while shifting time costs to workers
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35331; randomized trial of 248 customer-service employees assigned to fully remote work or one coordinated office day per month
records.geography: Multinational firm's customer-service workforce; trial setting and firm-specific, not a representative U.S. labor-market estimate
records.boundary: This record adds a coordinated-contact finding: one planned office day can improve measured communication, productivity, and retention in a specific team. It does not establish a universal office mandate, worker welfare, promotion, household cost, disability access, or the best schedule for other jobs.

records.title: State gun policy can respond more clearly to organized interests than to broad constituent sentiment
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34970, linking state campaign-finance records, a Gun Law Index, and estimates of constituent sentiment
records.geography: United States states; gun-policy changes and constituent sentiment, 2000-2024, with 25 years of campaign-finance records
records.boundary: This record measures state-level gun-policy responsiveness in a study linking contributions and estimated public sentiment. It does not establish that organized interests always override voters, identify individual representation, prove policy legitimacy, or measure firearm safety, violence, or public trust outcomes.

records.title: US overtime coverage expansion raised earnings without an employment decline
records.source_unit: US administrative payroll data, salaried-worker overtime thresholds, earnings, employment, and employer exemption responses
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a US policy-to-pay-and-employment comparison. It does not establish worker control over time, long-run earnings, household outcomes, firm profitability, bargaining, or whether the result generalizes beyond workers near the affected thresholds and the 2014–2021 state-policy setting.

records.title: US P-EBT disbursements increased sugary-item spending among eligible households
records.source_unit: US SNAP-eligible households with school-aged children, P-EBT disbursement timing, weekly sugary-item spending, overall food spending, and placebo households
records.geography: United States; state-level P-EBT disbursement timing
records.boundary: This record adds a direct purchase-response layer to the US safety-net program. It does not establish sugary-item consumption, nutrition, health, food security, household welfare, or a universal response to cash-like food assistance.

records.title: Party pressure can widen the gap between voter preferences and representatives' recorded votes
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34697; U.S. House roll-call votes and survey-based voter ideology estimates
records.geography: United States; U.S. House members, constituents, party pressure, and congressional roll-call voting
records.boundary: This record adds a political-institutional representation finding: party organization can shape the distance between voter preferences and members' recorded votes. It does not establish that party pressure is always harmful, that survey ideology captures all constituent demands, or that roll-call divergence produces lower trust or worse material outcomes.

records.title: Patent protection can increase agricultural innovation and local profits while raising seed costs and distorting downstream production
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35735, Flowers of Invention: The Economic Impacts of Patent Rights; crop-specific technology development, plant reproductive-structure exposure, and U.S. county outcomes
records.geography: United States agricultural crops, counties, firms, and downstream production; plant-biotechnology patent change introduced in 1985
records.boundary: This record closes a legal-rights-to-private-investment, innovation, yield, and local-profit arrow while preserving the cost and power trade-off: patent rights can raise productivity and land values alongside higher seed spending and possible downstream distortions. It does not establish consumer welfare, farm adoption, worker outcomes, or household food security.

records.title: US payment speed changes transfer behavior and deposit demand
records.source_unit: US depositor transaction, bank-transfer, county rollout, and deposit-demand measures
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record identifies a US payment-infrastructure mechanism linking transfer delay, depositor activity, deposit growth, and monetary transmission. It does not report the abstract's omitted effect sizes, establish a same-household welfare change, measure fraud or remedy, or show that faster payments improve resilience, trust, or consumer power.

records.title: A digital payment system can be widespread while cash remains a practical backup during outages
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35115, Alvarez, Argente, and Van Patten, combining U.S. electricity-outage and weather data, transaction-level expenditure data, household scanner data, surveys from the United States, Spain, and Sweden, and a NielsenIQ preparedness-information experiment
records.geography: United States as the primary atlas setting, with comparison survey and payment evidence from Spain and Sweden; county-level outage and weather variation and household/transaction observations
records.boundary: This record shows that disaster-related payment disruption can shift spending from digital methods toward cash and that cash access is associated with more completed transactions. It does not establish that households obtained essential goods, avoided health or work loss, repaid credit without strain, or experienced durable recovery.

records.title: Payment-system fees redistribute across consumers through merchant prices and rewards
records.source_unit: US merchant, transaction, payment-method, and modeled consumer-income incidence
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record promotes the underlying NBER paper beyond the prior HBS-only source note, while preserving that the central dollar figures are modeled incidence estimates. It does not establish a household-level bill, welfare effect, financial-stress outcome, or political response, and the paper remains a working paper rather than a peer-reviewed publication.

records.title: A peer self-harm death can spread risk through a youth social network while care and offending responses diverge
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35603, linked South Carolina administrative data on peer self-harm deaths and surviving students
records.geography: South Carolina students and linked administrative health, education, and criminal-justice records
records.boundary: This record measures peer-death exposure and short-run administrative self-harm, mental-health-visit, and criminal-behavior responses in South Carolina. It does not establish a national rate, individual contagion mechanism, completed suicide effect, school or family causal pathway, or later recovery outcome.

records.title: Perceived fairness of others' tax payments changes tax appeals and willingness to contribute
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 32588; U.S. property-tax information-disclosure field experiment
records.geography: United States; households subject to a local property-tax appeal process
records.boundary: This record adds a fairness-perception-to-institutional-action pathway: information about others' tax contributions changes perceived fairness and tax-appeal behavior in a property-tax setting. It does not establish payment, tax compliance, public-service trust, political participation, durable legitimacy, or household security.

records.title: AI matched some team performance while changing expertise sharing and social connection in product innovation work
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 33641, The Cybernetic Teammate: A Field Experiment on Generative AI Reshaping Teamwork and Expertise
records.geography: Procter & Gamble, a US-headquartered global consumer packaged goods company; participant geography is not fully specified in the abstract
records.boundary: This record adds a US-company consumer-goods workplace experiment linking AI access to performance, teamwork, expertise sharing, functional silos, and self-reported emotional response. It does not establish replacement of teams, durable expertise, worker control, pay, employment, product-market success, consumer welfare, or long-run social connection.

records.title: Equal platform-data access can strengthen competition while reducing the incentive to produce data
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35159; theoretical model of data-neutrality rules, affiliated and unaffiliated sellers, platform data supply, competition, and consumer welfare
records.geography: Platform-market model; used as a mechanism test for U.S.-relevant digital-market governance, not an observed U.S. firm estimate
records.boundary: This record adds a model-based platform-governance tradeoff: fairer data access can improve competition while weakening incentives to create data. It does not establish the size, direction, privacy effect, or consumer-welfare result of a neutrality rule in any particular U.S. market.

records.title: Partisan differences in workplace AI use are largely about where people work, while displacement fears may be separating
records.source_unit: Gallup Workforce Panel workers reporting workplace AI use and job-displacement risk
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This finding separates partisan composition of workplace AI exposure and use from partisan differences in perceived displacement risk. It does not establish ideological causation, actual adoption outcomes, job loss, worker control, public opinion beyond the workforce panel, or political action.

records.title: Persistent post-pandemic labor-force exit is concentrated among low-income and low-skill US workers
records.source_unit: US tax-panel workers, occupation, income, labor-force exit, self-employment income, wages, benefits, stimulus, and post-pandemic work preferences
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a post-pandemic labor-force exit and income-replacement layer to the US work/consumer program. It does not establish why workers exit, whether exit is harmful or voluntary, or how informal work, care, health, benefits, household resources, and later re-entry evolve.

records.title: Restricting mobile tracking can reduce fraud complaints through the data-resale chain
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 31692, revised May 2026; Apple App Tracking Transparency natural experiment, consumer fraud complaints, dark-web discussion, and sensitive-data prices
records.geography: United States; geographic and firm-risk variation around Apple mobile tracking restrictions
records.boundary: This record adds a platform-data-control-to-consumer-fraud-consequence pathway. It does not establish a complete household fraud-recovery episode, universal privacy benefit, causal trust change, account restoration, reimbursement, or durable exit from data-dependent services.

records.title: AI policy can distinguish worker-augmenting capability from automation and expertise commodification
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34854, Building Pro-Worker Artificial Intelligence
records.geography: United States policy and workplace examples; conceptual framework with examples spanning aviation maintenance, electrical services, custodial work, education, patent examination, and gig delivery
records.boundary: This record adds a US-oriented conceptual policy framework for distinguishing augmentation, automation, expertise leveling, capital complementarity, and new task creation. It does not estimate worker effects, adoption, productivity, pay, bargaining power, consumer prices, or the effectiveness of any policy direction; pro-worker status requires observed control and distribution, not a label.

records.title: Property-tax design reallocates housing access across generations under financial constraints
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35587, overlapping-generations model of property taxation, housing allocation, and financial constraints
records.geography: United States housing policy with a California-to-Texas property-tax counterfactual; intergenerational housing allocation
records.boundary: This record establishes a modeled intergenerational housing-allocation mechanism. It does not establish an observed California policy effect, individual displacement, rental burden, local-service change, household wealth change, or political response.

records.title: U.S. protests can create attention without usually producing broad opinion or policy change
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 32342, a database of U.S. protest waves linked to digital, survey, election, and policy measures
records.geography: United States; protest waves and local exposure, 2017-2022
records.boundary: This finding separates protest visibility and digital attention from broader opinion, electoral, legislative, and policy effects. It does not establish that protest is ineffective, that violence is necessary for influence, that the Black Lives Matter exception generalizes, or that protest participants experienced no local or personal change.

records.title: At a large public university system, high-school grades predict academic success better than standardized tests
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34975 administrative-data study of a large urban public university system
records.geography: United States; large urban public university system and first-year cohorts entering 2010–2019
records.boundary: This record compares predictive validity in one public-university system and a separate elite-institution context. It does not establish an admissions reform effect, access or inequality effect, student wellbeing, degree completion causality, earnings, or public trust.

records.title: County purchasing power and real-wage change carry distinct electoral associations
records.source_unit: US county-level changes in family-budget costs, nominal income, real wages, and presidential/Congressional election outcomes
records.geography: United States counties, with within-state cross-county comparisons
records.boundary: This is a full-paper-audited county-level political-economy record with an abstract-level companion observation. It strengthens the material-purchasing-power-to-electoral-outcome layer but does not measure individual attribution, trust formation, household adaptation, or a causal individual vote mechanism. County-level estimates and turnout changes must not be interpreted as same-person political action.

records.title: Remote work changes shopping mode, household spending, and who carries the shopping task
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34883; new survey combined with Nielsen Consumer panel and NielsenIQ marketing data
records.geography: United States households and consumers; remote-work and shopping comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a work-location-to-shopping conversion finding: remote work changes when and how households shop, what they buy, prices paid, and who handles shopping. It does not establish full household welfare, unpaid care or return work, local business survival, neighborhood change, or the experience of workers without remote-work access.

records.title: Income risk rose especially sharply at the top, increasing saving and wealth inequality in the model
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35664; digitized U.S. tax returns from 1969-2019 and a life-cycle model
records.geography: United States; tax-return income distribution, permanent and transitory income risk, saving, wealth, and financial distress
records.boundary: This record adds a distributional-finance finding: risk, saving, wealth, credit conditions, and household security can move on different levels and clocks. It does not establish that top-income saving caused any particular lower-income household's rent, loan rate, wage, distress, or political response.

records.title: US school-finance reforms raise long-run earnings per worker and GDP per capita after a long lag
records.source_unit: US state school-finance reforms, treated cohorts, earnings per worker, GDP per capita, private returns, and long-run aggregate output
records.geography: United States; staggered state-level school-finance reforms
records.boundary: This record adds a long-run public-investment-to-aggregate-output layer to the US education program. It does not establish equal distribution, student wellbeing, local access, worker voice, household consumption, or a complete causal pathway from reform dollars to GDP in every state.

records.title: Exposure to an alternative search engine can change quality beliefs and persistence beyond active choice
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 33410; randomized field experiment with U.S. desktop internet users whose default search engine was Google, combined with a demand model and search-log evidence
records.geography: United States desktop internet users; Google/Bing search market
records.boundary: This record adds a U.S. observed platform-exposure-to-use-and-belief pathway: active choice alone has a small effect, while temporary exposure to an alternative can change perceived quality and continued preference.
