It does not establish durable switching, privacy or security improvement, equal accessibility, universal consumer surplus, or political action.

records.title: Weak outside options at medical-school entry can shape physician practice and spending decades later
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35631 using U.S. medical-school application conditions, physician practice data, Medicare billing, and patient outcomes
records.geography: United States; physicians and Medicare beneficiaries observed across medical-school cohorts and later practice
records.boundary: This record measures a cohort-selection pathway from outside options to physician practice, spending, and measured patient-health outcomes. It does not establish individual physician motivation, provider fraud, universal overtreatment, household medical debt, patient trust, or a complete institutional account of health-care prices and access.

records.title: A credit-score change can help produce later default for borrowers already near trouble
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35508; credit-inquiry counting rule, score changes, and two-year default outcomes
records.geography: United States; consumers around a fourteen-day credit-inquiry scoring cutoff
records.boundary: This record adds a feedback finding: a financial signal can become part of the risk it predicts for a defined higher-risk group. It does not establish a particular lender action, monthly price, housing or job consequence, recovery path, or political response for any individual borrower.

records.title: Physical proximity and repeated peer contact can shape legislative voting
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34925, The Micro-Geography of Persuasion: Randomized Peer Exposure and Legislative Outcomes
records.geography: United States Senate; randomized seating and legislative-voting records across a 30-year study sample
records.boundary: This record adds a measured institutional mechanism: repeated physical proximity and face-to-face contact can affect legislative behavior in the U.S. Senate. It does not establish a general public persuasion effect, durable ideological change, democratic legitimacy, or a complete path from social contact to public trust and collective action.

records.title: Individual generative-AI access changes email and after-hours work patterns before detectable task redesign
records.source_unit: knowledge worker-week in a randomized field experiment across participating firms
records.geography: United States; participating firms and workers in the study
records.boundary: This record promotes a randomized worker-level time-pattern result from a defined field experiment. It does not establish firm productivity, job redesign, worker authority, pay, health, household time, political meaning, or geopolitical consequence. Access, take-up, task change, coordination, and control remain separate stages.

records.title: Remote work changes shopping mode and can raise prices paid through household shopping reallocation
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34883; Nielsen consumer-panel survey and shopping data on work-from-home households
records.geography: United States consumer households and retail purchases
records.boundary: This record adds a consumer-work mechanism: remote work reallocates shopping time and responsibility and can change prices paid. It does not establish household welfare, retailer market power, food security, or a universal remote-work effect.

records.title: Banking inertia can weaken competition while supporting deposit stability
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34267; account-opening and account-closure data at more than 900 banks with an empirical model of deposit competition and stability
records.geography: United States banks and depositors; account openings, closures, competition, and the 2023 banking turmoil
records.boundary: This record adds a banking conversion finding: account relationships can turn customer staying into both a competition effect and a stability effect. It does not establish the welfare of individual depositors, the value of branch or digital service, the causes of any customer's inertia, or equal access to safe switching.

records.title: The physical location of SNAP enrollment offices changes participation in nearby places
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34529, The Intersection of Place and Need: How Lack of Enrollment Offices Deters Participation in the Safety Net
records.geography: United States; administrative SNAP participation and geocoded enrollment offices in one state, with census-tract event-study comparisons
records.boundary: This record establishes a causal place-to-program-participation link in one state's SNAP system. It does not establish a national effect, household food security, benefit adequacy, application effort, remote-access substitution, or later political or health outcomes.

records.title: SNAP purchase restrictions can change consumption while increasing the felt stigma of receiving aid
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35659, using nationwide grocery-purchase panel data, pre/post recipient surveys, and a welfare model for 2026 SNAP sugary-drink restrictions
records.geography: United States; first 10 states implementing SNAP sugary-drink restrictions in the first half of 2026, with comparison states and a modeled national extension
records.boundary: This record measures short-run purchase changes, substitution, recipient perceptions of stigma, and a modeled national welfare scenario. It does not establish long-run health, household food security, total consumption, political response, or whether the policy is experienced as respectful or coercive by every recipient.

records.title: SNAP restrictions on sweetened beverages and candy reduced restricted spending, calories, and sugar
records.source_unit: US SNAP purchases of sweetened beverages and candy, restricted spending, calories, sugar, substitution, shelf prices, taxes, retailer SNAP intensity, online purchases, and modeled welfare
records.geography: United States; first statewide SNAP restrictions on sweetened beverages and candy
records.boundary: This record adds a restriction-response and purchase-substitution layer to the US safety-net program. It does not establish long-run consumption, nutrition, health, food security, household welfare, or that modeled nationwide benefits outweigh unequal burden for every recipient.

records.title: SNAP work requirements increase procedural denials through administrative burden
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34698, administrative SNAP data analyzed with age-based exemption and waiver-period difference-in-differences designs
records.geography: United States SNAP administrative-policy setting; study-selected jurisdictions and Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs), not a national participation rate
records.boundary: This record adds a policy-to-administrative-denial and participation-deterrence mechanism. It does not establish a national denial rate, individual notice or effort, appeal, restored benefits, food security, health, durable hardship, trust, or political action.

records.title: Economic connectedness in US Facebook friendship networks is associated with substantially greater local innovation
records.source_unit: US patenting ZIP Codes, Facebook friendship networks, economic connectedness, patents, breakthrough patents, relocation, and local social shocks
records.geography: United States; patenting ZIP Codes and Facebook friendship networks
records.boundary: This record adds a network and financing mechanism to the US innovation program. It does not establish that friendship exposure alone creates patents, measure privacy or social costs, or connect innovation to local jobs, wages, consumer welfare, or durable place capacity in the same unit.

records.title: Personalized benefit information changes the choice between Social Security Disability and early retirement applications
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35748 using Social Security statements and application behavior among older U.S. adults
records.geography: United States; people ages 62 to full retirement age, with work-limiting health conditions or low work ability
records.boundary: This record establishes an information-interface-to-benefit-application pathway for older U.S. adults with health or work limitations. It does not establish awards, receipt, benefit adequacy, health, work exit, household security, trust, or administrative cost.

records.title: Social Security support for parents changed children’s long-run migration, earnings, and neighborhood trajectories
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35456, linked parent-child administrative records and historical Social Security coverage
records.geography: United States; early Social Security program and linked later-life outcomes
records.boundary: This record links historical parental Social Security coverage to estimated long-run child migration, earnings, and neighborhood outcomes. It does not establish a contemporary national effect, observe every caregiving exchange, or prove that migration alone caused the later outcomes.

records.title: US firm wage-setting norms left many workers behind prices during 2021–2024 inflation
records.source_unit: US worker, continuing-employment relationship, employer, and administrative payroll measures
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record links firm wage-setting norms to observed worker real-wage changes during 2021–2024. It does not establish a causal employer decision, bargaining-power estimate, individual hardship, household spending response, political attribution, or durable job-switching outcome. Payroll, firm, household, and sentiment units remain separate.

records.title: US one-off transfers produced a delayed, hump-shaped consumption response
records.source_unit: US veterans, postwar transfer payments, household consumption, transfer timing, cumulative transfer multiplier, and expectations
records.geography: United States; post-World War II veteran payment natural experiment
records.boundary: This record adds a dynamic transfer-to-consumption layer to the US consumer program. It does not establish modern stimulus effects, household security, nutrition, debt, health, political trust, or equal welfare, and the one-year multiplier is not a direct measure of durable benefit.

records.title: Stimulus transfers can produce stronger electoral than consumption responses when targeting follows political responsiveness
records.source_unit: Italian municipality-level administrative recipient shares, electoral returns, income/employment distributions, and voter-panel evidence; international comparison for the US-centered program
records.geography: Italy; comparison mechanism for US fiscal-transfer and political-response analysis
records.boundary: This is an international comparison mechanism, not a US estimate. It directly strengthens the program's policy exposure → material response → attribution/electoral response architecture while leaving US transfer design, household-level causal incidence, cultural meaning, and generalization open. Consumption estimates and electoral estimates are not treated as the same respondent outcome.

records.title: Uncertain student-loan policy changed payments and spending before the policy was settled
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35319; US information experiment linked to credit-bureau, employment-verification, and nondurable-consumption records
records.geography: United States; student-loan borrowers represented in the study's survey and linked administrative records
records.boundary: This record supports a belief-to-payment-and-spending pathway under the study's design. It does not show that the expected relief was received, that borrowers changed political identity or trust, or that the same borrowers experienced a complete later housing, family, or financial-security outcome. Promise, belief, payment, spending, delinquency, and realized relief remain separate stages.

records.title: Tariff incidence reaches consumers through direct import prices and slower domestic supply-chain markups
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35561; U.S. 2025 tariff episode, consumer prices, imported inputs, and domestic producer markups
records.geography: United States goods markets and supply chains
records.boundary: This record adds a trade-to-consumer mechanism: geopolitical trade policy can redistribute costs through both rapid import prices and delayed domestic supply-chain markups. It does not show household hardship, political attribution, firm exit, or whether the policy achieved its strategic objective.

records.title: Tariffs can reach domestic prices indirectly and with a long delay
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35561; 2025 U.S. tariffs, consumer prices, imported inputs, domestic markups, and less-exposed comparison goods
records.geography: United States; consumer goods and domestic producers exposed to the 2025 tariff changes
records.boundary: This record adds a tariff-to-price pathway with separate direct and delayed indirect channels. It does not establish a particular household's total cost, quantity or quality loss, wage or job effect, political blame, or whether any later domestic production benefit offsets the consumer burden.

records.title: US tariffs pass through to consumer prices directly and later through domestic inputs and markups
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35561, The Anatomy of Tariff Pass-through into Consumer Prices
records.geography: United States; goods exposed to the 2025-2026 US tariffs
records.boundary: This record adds a US consumer-price and firm-market-power mechanism: tariffs can pass through directly to imported varieties and indirectly through domestic input costs and markups over a longer supply-chain lag. It does not establish household welfare, incidence by income, retailer behavior, firm profitability, substitution, employment, or a universal tariff effect outside the study design.

records.title: Transaction scale changes the measured incidence of US tariffs
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34901, Did Foreigners Pay America's Tariffs? Quantity Discounts, Scale Economies and Incomplete Pass-Through
records.geography: United States trade; 2018-2019 US tariffs and transaction-level imports
records.boundary: This record adds an upstream US trade-incidence counterexample: apparent one-for-one tariff pass-through can partly reflect lost transaction scale, while scale-adjusted pass-through is 60 percent and foreign exporters absorb a significant share through lower markups. It does not establish retail prices, household incidence, welfare, employment, or a universal tariff mechanism.

records.title: Worker adoption of generative AI is widespread across tasks but shallow within similar work
records.source_unit: nationally representative worker survey linked to detailed occupations and tasks
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record promotes descriptive task- and occupation-level adoption findings from NBER Working Paper 35677 and its public task indexes. It does not establish that adoption changes pay, hours, employment, discretion, monitoring, worker voice, wellbeing, household security, culture, politics, or geopolitical power. The paper is a working paper; worker-level subgroup analysis, crosswalk versioning, and workplace outcomes remain open.

records.title: Temporary work can create a second credit barrier alongside income risk
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 32858; study of temporary and permanent workers, income risk, household debt, and credit access
records.geography: United States young employees and household credit markets; temporary versus permanent work
records.boundary: This record adds a labor-status-to-credit-access finding: temporary work can raise income risk and reduce access to the credit used for housing, consumption smoothing, and durable purchases. It does not establish individual lender discrimination, household welfare, preferred work arrangement, or the long-term effect for every temporary worker.

records.title: For time-intensive platforms, attention and opportunity cost are part of the consumer price
records.source_unit: Two Facebook/Instagram field experiments and an economic model reported in NBER Working Paper 34743; platform-user experiment, not a representative welfare panel
records.geography: United States platform users and online/offline activity alternatives as described by the study
records.boundary: This record promotes a time-price mechanism for digital consumer demand. It observes experimental response and model application, but does not establish user well-being, household care/work displacement, dependence, practical exit, realized consumer surplus, or the effect of an actual platform separation. The next test is a consented time-use and substitution panel with platform exposure, ad load, content value, offline activity, work/care/sleep, switching, and later trust kept separate.

records.title: The form and timing of a transfer change how quickly households spend it
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35698; pandemic-era transfers, high-frequency household scanner data, harmonized difference-in-differences and event studies
records.geography: United States; low-income households with children receiving one-time or recurring cash or food benefits
records.boundary: This record adds a transfer-design finding: amount, label, and schedule can change the first observable spending response. It does not rank cash against food aid, establish lasting food security, or show how transfer design changes trust, political support, or durable household security.

records.title: A temporary income boost can become a durable purchase and a future loan obligation
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35026, using variation from the 2008 Economic Stimulus Act to estimate household durable-goods spending and vehicle financing responses
records.geography: United States; households and consumer expenditures exposed to the 2008 stimulus payment, with vehicle-financing response estimates
records.boundary: This record shows a large durable-spending response to a temporary income shock and substantial vehicle-loan leverage. It does not establish that the purchases improved access, protected work or care, caused later strain, or produced durable household security.

records.title: Interpersonal trust may buffer democratic political stability during economic crises
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 24187, revised August 2026, using country, subnational, and individual panels
records.geography: Democratic countries over roughly six decades, with subnational Europe, U.S. counties, and individuals in U.S. counties represented in separate analyses
records.boundary: This finding adds a trust-conditioned political-stability relationship across country, subnational, and individual analyses. It does not prove that trust alone prevents democratic turnover, identify a universal crisis mechanism, establish current U.S. national effects, or measure household recovery, institutional performance, or later public action.

records.title: Domain-specific institutional trust aligns with retirement behavior differently across groups
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35220; Health and Retirement Study trust module and older U.S. households
records.geography: United States; older households observed in the Health and Retirement Study
records.boundary: This record adds an observed trust-to-financial-behavior bridge in older U.S. households, with domain and racial/ethnic heterogeneity. It does not establish causal trust effects, current working-age behavior, retirement adequacy, institutional legitimacy, political action, or why the associations differ. Trust, financial access, behavior, wealth, and durable security remain separate stages.

records.title: Domain-specific health-care trust is associated with care seeking and care avoidance
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 32028 revised April 2026; nationally representative U.S. adult survey with trust, care-seeking, and mechanism measures
records.geography: United States; adult respondents and health-care entities including doctors, nurses, hospitals, insurers, and public-health authorities
records.boundary: This record adds a trust-to-care-seeking and care-avoidance pathway. It does not establish a causal trust shock, realized treatment, affordability, health outcome, patient-provider encounter, remedy, durable trust change, or political action.

records.title: Employer sorting and same-firm social interaction can inflate apparent heritability of U.S. earnings
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35746, linked U.S. Census twin and earnings records
records.geography: United States; twins observed as adolescents in the 2000 Census and linked to earnings about 20 years later
records.boundary: This record measures population-level earnings heritability and same-firm social-interaction sensitivity in linked U.S. twin data. It does not establish individual genetic destiny, a causal hiring-network mechanism, present-day mobility policy effects, or worker-level bargaining power.

records.title: Rideshare comparison friction can preserve platform booking volume
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 34441; audit of identical trips on Uber and Lyft with device-level app-opening data
records.geography: New York City rideshare market; Uber and Lyft identical-trip price comparison
records.boundary: This record adds a rideshare search-friction finding: identical-trip price dispersion and limited cross-app comparison can increase platform booking volume in the New York City model. It does not establish individual harm, trip-quality differences, equal access to alternatives, or universal effects outside the studied market.

records.title: Licensing changed the driver pool without showing a consistent improvement in measured ride outcomes
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35635; trip-level Uber data, driver ratings, telematics-based driving measures, a New York City/New Jersey comparison, and a Houston deregulation event
records.geography: United States; New York City/New Jersey and Houston Uber markets
records.boundary: This record adds a regulation-to-entry-and-service finding: a protective rule can change who enters without changing the measured average ride outcomes. It does not establish effects on serious incidents, ordinary ride access, fares, waits, worker income, disability service, or customer trust across all cities.

records.title: Large temporary cash transfers raised consumption and financial health without clear persistent net-worth gains
records.source_unit: U.S. low-income adults in a randomized three-year unconditional-cash-transfer experiment in two states
records.geography: United States; two states
records.boundary: This is a randomized U.S. transfer-to-consumption and balance-sheet result, not a universal cash-transfer effect or a complete household recovery, care, employment, trust, political-action, or long-run welfare estimate.

records.title: Unconditional cash transfers can shift parental investment through money or time differently across racialized groups
records.source_unit: U.S. families in a large-scale multisite randomized unconditional-cash-transfer study, analyzed by race and ethnicity
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a randomized U.S. transfer-to-parental-investment result with heterogeneous subgroup pathways, not a universal cash-transfer effect or a complete household-welfare, care-quality, labor-market, trust, or political-action estimate.

records.title: Large unconditional cash transfers improved reported parenting while increasing some reported child stress signals
records.source_unit: U.S. families in a randomized three-year unconditional-cash-transfer experiment, with child, parenting, care, and household outcomes
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a randomized U.S. transfer-to-parenting and care result, not a universal cash-transfer effect or a complete child-development, household-welfare, employment, trust, political-action, or long-run recovery estimate.

records.title: Foreign strikes can redirect domestic mobilization toward the regime they seek to weaken
records.source_unit: Geocoded Iranian protest events and U.S.–Israeli strike exposure in NBER Working Paper 35734
records.geography: Iranian counties and the 2026 U.S.–Israeli strike episode
records.boundary: This record adds a measured foreign-action-to-public-mobilization response: the abstract reports a shift from anti-government toward pro-government and anti-U.S./Israel protest after U.S.–Israeli strike exposure, with little change in total protest activity. It does not establish durable regime legitimacy, civilian protection, strategic success or failure, causal isolation from repression and propaganda, or later external behavior.

records.title: Safe-drinking-water investment can reduce pollution and older-adult mortality while household exposure remains separate
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35288; drinking-water pollution readings, water systems/areas, Safe Drinking Water Act loans, and linked administrative Medicare outcomes for older Americans
records.geography: United States; 48 states, national and place-level water-quality measures, and older-American health outcomes
records.boundary: This record adds a measured place-to-health and public-loan result: pollution declined, loans reduced pollution, and linked older-American mortality fell in the study's estimates. It does not follow the same household from exposure through bottled-water or filter spending, home value, health care, trust, political action, or durable local acceptance.

records.title: Liquid wealth changes how households absorb ordinary income shocks
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 27552; administrative banking data and an instrument based on firm-wide changes in labor income
records.geography: United States households and typical month-to-month labor-income fluctuations
records.boundary: This record adds a liquidity-and-race consumption-smoothing finding: liquid wealth changes how strongly households respond to ordinary labor-income shocks, with larger estimated sensitivity and modeled welfare costs for Black and Hispanic households in the study. It does not identify each household's first sacrifice, prove a specific causal mechanism beyond the study design, or establish political action or long-term security.

records.title: Weatherization savings can be much smaller than engineering projections
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 21331; experimental evaluation of the U.S. Weatherization Assistance Program involving more than 30,000 households
records.geography: United States residential Weatherization Assistance Program households
records.boundary: This record adds a measured infrastructure-performance finding: weatherization's realized energy savings were substantially below engineering projections in this evaluation. It does not establish the health, comfort, safety, bill, housing, or welfare outcome for each household, nor does it show that every weatherization project has the same return.

records.title: 1990s welfare reform reduced the decline in voting among exposed low-income women
records.source_unit: Low-income U.S. women observed in Current Population Survey Voting and Registration Supplements during 1990s welfare reform
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a U.S. welfare-reform policy-exposure estimate for low-income women's voting, not a universal work effect, a contemporaneous cash-transfer effect, or a complete political-trust and institutional-legitimacy pathway.

records.title: Wildfire smoke can turn intermittent school disruption into maternal employment loss
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35264, Where There's Smoke: Stochastic Caregiving Shocks and Mothers' Labor Market Outcomes
records.geography: United States; mothers and children exposed to wildfire smoke, school closures, and student absenteeism
records.boundary: This record adds a quasi-experimental material/time/care bridge: an environmental shock can intermittently remove a school-based care input, impose maternal labor-market costs, and produce accumulated employment loss, with an industry-level workplace-tolerance boundary. It does not establish a national employment effect, a household income or health path, or that male-dominated industries are the sole mechanism.

records.title: Zero-sum beliefs connect perceived group competition with U.S. political preferences and historical experience
records.source_unit: NBER Working Paper 31688, published in the 2026 American Economic Review, using a survey of 20,400 U.S. residents and ancestral information
records.geography: United States; contemporary survey respondents with individual and four-generation ancestral measures
records.boundary: This finding measures a zero-sum belief construct and its associations with policy preferences and ancestral experience in a large U.S. survey. It does not establish that zero-sum thinking is the cause of polarization, that historical experience transmits through one pathway, that scarcity is perceived incorrectly, or that beliefs became votes or policy outcomes.

records.title: Aggregate school safety can improve while some students still avoid school participation
records.source_unit: National Center for Education Statistics and Bureau of Justice Statistics Report on Indicators of School Crime and Safety: 2023; student School Crime Supplement and related indicators
records.geography: United States schools; students ages 12 to 18
records.boundary: This record adds a youth institutional-safety boundary: aggregate victimization, student fear, avoidance, attendance, school response, support, belonging, learning, and later trust are separate stages. It does not establish a same-student causal path or prove that aggregate safety improvement reached every student.

records.title: American education is being reshaped by enrollment contraction, more at-home instruction, learning loss, and a widening postsecondary value pathway
records.source_unit: National Center for Education Statistics, Report on the Condition of Education 2025, with highlights published by the Institute of Education Sciences
records.geography: United States; elementary and secondary education, postsecondary education, and young-adult economic outcomes
records.boundary: This record adds an education-capacity and opportunity layer: U.S. public enrollment is contracting in many states, at-home instruction remains above its pre-pandemic level, undergraduate and postbaccalaureate pathways are diverging, achievement indicators remain weaker than in 2019, and attainment continues to correlate with employment and earnings. It does not establish causes, institutional quality, family welfare, causal education returns, or a single national education trajectory.

records.title: Arts participation was positively associated with civic and community engagement in two national surveys, with a null overall GSS result
records.source_unit: National Endowment for the Arts, The Great Connector: How Arts Participation Renews Civic and Community Engagement
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record supplies a measured cultural-to-civic association and an explicit cross-survey counterexample. It does not establish that arts participation causes civic engagement, political mobilization, trust, belonging, or improved institutional outcomes.

records.title: Arts participation is a socially patterned cultural resource associated with connection
records.source_unit: National Endowment for the Arts analysis of Census Household Pulse Survey Phase 4.1 cycles 04-07
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural-infrastructure association: arts access and participation are distributed unevenly and correlate with reported social connection. It does not establish an arts treatment effect, durable belonging, community repair, organizational success, or political action.

records.title: Financial control can coexist with thin buffers and credit dependence
records.source_unit: NerdWallet Consumer Financial Resilience Index, September 2026 Harris Poll survey
records.geography: United States; adults age 18 and older; survey fielded September 8-10, 2026
records.boundary: This record adds a household-resilience route separating perceived control, near-term bill capacity, liquid shock buffers, expected credit use and macroeconomic expectations. It does not measure administrative wealth, realized borrowing, repayment, debt stress, consumption, health, employment, causal effects or durable financial security.

records.title: Parents broadly want more time with young children, but money, care supply, work schedules, and eldercare determine whether that ideal is reachable
records.source_unit: New America New Practice Lab, 2026 National Parent Survey
records.geography: United States; parents and primary caregivers of children ages zero through five in all 50 states and the District of Columbia
records.boundary: This record adds a family-time conversion route: parents broadly want more quality time with young children, but wages, child-care cost and supply, leave, transportation, work schedules, and eldercare determine whether that ideal is reachable. It does not establish causal policy effects, independently verified hardship, child outcomes, employer behavior, or a single preferred care model.

records.title: The New Mexico tax-credit fiscal report specified projected distribution and administrative routes, but not realized receipt
records.source_unit: New Mexico Legislative Finance Committee fiscal impact report for SB 24/CS/SFL/aHTRC/aHAFC
records.geography: New Mexico statewide personal-income-tax returns; 2008 special-session fiscal estimate
records.boundary: This record adds a planned distribution and administrative-capacity layer after statutory enactment. It does not close the realized claim/payment, timing, adequacy, household-security, or trust arrows.

records.title: The New Mexico constituency-information experiment was followed by enacted but reduced tax-credit implementation
records.source_unit: New Mexico 2008 second special-session Senate Bill 24 and Legislative Council Service implementation summary, linked to the Butler-Nickerson vote study
records.geography: New Mexico; statewide tax law and state House special-session vote
records.boundary: This record adds a vote-to-enacted-program-design arrow for the New Mexico tax-rebate episode. It does not establish that the information treatment caused enactment, that eligible households claimed or received the credit, that timing and amount were adequate, or that the episode changed later trust, political action, or material security.

records.title: A state insurance regulator makes complaint recovery and market-availability work visible without closing the household outcome chain
records.source_unit: New York State Department of Financial Services Consumer Assistance Unit 2025 annual report and property-insurance data-call instructions
records.geography: New York State regulatory and consumer-assistance system; national referrals can occur in the complaint workflow
records.boundary: This record adds a state-regulatory visibility and recourse layer. It measures complaints, closures, agency labels, reported recoveries, and insurer-reporting requirements. It does not establish insurance-market prevalence, household claim adequacy, repair completion, premium affordability, nonrenewal causation, or political meaning.

records.title: Aggregate household debt expands while delinquency remains a distinct exposure layer
records.source_unit: New York Fed Quarterly Report on Household Debt and Credit dashboard snapshot
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record establishes a current aggregate credit-market snapshot. It does not join aggregate debt to particular households, establish a causal interest-rate effect, identify who bears balances or delinquency, measure lender pricing or remedy, or infer political, cultural, or geopolitical consequences. Aggregate debt, household survey responses, and linked credit records remain separate evidence layers.

records.title: Neighborhood trust is practically resilient but socially under-connected, especially for young adults
records.source_unit: Nextdoor/The Harris Poll, Most Americans Still Rely on Their Neighbors, September 28, 2026
records.geography: United States; adults age 18+
records.boundary: This record adds a neighborhood social-infrastructure route: practical mutual aid and local recommendation trust can persist alongside an unmet desire for connection, with a sharper welcome gap among young adults. It does not establish actual assistance, completed local-service outcomes, causal app effects, or durable community recovery. The source is platform-commissioned, cross-sectional, and based on an online opt-in panel.

records.title: Mobility pressure is jointly patterned by place, household resources, and trip purpose
records.source_unit: 2022 NHTS household, person, and travel-day trip records joined by HOUSEID and grouped by URBRUR and HHFAMINC bands
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a descriptive 2022 cross-sectional screen, not a causal estimate or a complete care-access measure. Household income, vehicle count, work status, and recorded trip time are distinct variables; they do not jointly identify affordability, necessity, unmet trips, or welfare. Work and shopping trips are used as daily-life proxies, while care, medical, childcare, and social obligations require a dedicated linked calendar layer. The raw NHTS archive is externally retrieved and hash-identified; derived slices are temporary and not committed.

records.title: Urban and rural households face different transport option sets
records.source_unit: 2022 NHTS household, person, and work-trip records grouped by NHTS urban/rural category
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a descriptive 2022 NHTS urban/rural transport-option comparison. Household, person, and trip units are kept separate; urban/rural categories are not interchangeable with USDA RUCC or county capacity. The record does not establish dependence, service access, affordability, missed work/care, or a causal place effect. The official archive is externally retrieved and hash-identified; derived slices are temporary and not committed.

records.title: AI-assisted shopping is moving into mainstream product discovery and evaluation, shifting the path to purchase toward machine-mediated choice
records.source_unit: NielsenIQ Agentic Commerce Tracker press release and monthly Quick Question research
records.geography: United States, with tracker also described as covering Canada
records.boundary: This record adds a current commercial-research signal on AI-assisted shopping and machine-mediated product discovery. It does not establish representative national adoption, actual purchases, savings, consumer welfare, algorithmic accuracy, retailer dependence, or causal market-share change from the NIQ release.

records.title: Chip-card deployment can reduce future EBT theft exposure without restoring theft losses
records.source_unit: New Jersey Human Services EBT chip-card fraud-prevention rollout
records.geography: New Jersey SNAP and Work First New Jersey cardholders
records.boundary: This record establishes a named state prevention and card-access response plus a federal-policy boundary on replacement of later electronic theft. It does not establish prevented theft, restoration of stolen benefits, food security, adequacy, trust, or exit.

records.title: Municipal infrastructure pressure is becoming a local-fiscal and workforce-capacity problem
records.source_unit: National League of Cities Municipal Infrastructure Conditions 2026 Survey and report
records.geography: United States; cities, towns, and villages responding to the NLC municipal infrastructure survey
records.boundary: This record adds a municipal infrastructure and finance route linking aging assets, water and mobility priorities, local revenue, workforce capacity, federal grants, and public-service reliability. It is a self-reported municipal survey and report synthesis, not a national engineering audit, resident-outcome study, or causal evaluation of federal infrastructure policy.

records.title: Municipal infrastructure resilience depends less on project need than on local fiscal, workforce, and grant-management capacity
records.source_unit: National League of Cities, Municipal Infrastructure Conditions Report 2026 and Municipal Infrastructure Conditions Survey
records.geography: United States; responding cities, towns, and villages, with comparison to 2022 municipal infrastructure survey results
records.boundary: This record adds a U.S. local-capacity route from infrastructure condition and public need through municipal finance, staff capacity, elected priorities, federal grants, implementation, and public-system reliability. It is a municipal leader survey and advocacy-organization synthesis, not a national engineering inventory, causal evaluation, project-completion dataset, or proof of household outcomes.

records.title: Labor-process demand can be substantial while durable worker power remains unmeasured
records.source_unit: National Labor Relations Board FY 2025 Performance and Accountability Report
records.geography: United States private-sector labor-relations jurisdiction
records.boundary: This record measures demand and output on a formal labor-administration route. It does not establish the prevalence of workplace violations, individual remedy receipt, bargaining outcomes, workplace improvement, union coverage, trust, or durable worker power.

records.title: Americans use AI broadly but preserve relational and human authority for spiritual, moral, and emotionally consequential counsel
records.source_unit: NPR and Ipsos, Religion and AI Survey, August 2026
records.geography: United States; adults age 18 and older in a nationally representative KnowledgePanel probability sample
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural-meaning and relational-authority layer to AI adoption: Americans report broad instrumental use of AI but retain stronger trust in people, family, friends, written resources, and religious or human counsel for difficult personal and spiritual questions. It does not measure actual spiritual practice, advice quality, mental-health outcomes, religious-community participation, or causal substitution of AI for human relationships.

records.title: Household affordability pressure is increasingly concentrated in essential services rather than ordinary retail goods
records.source_unit: National Retail Federation, Retail Economic Perspective: Who’s to blame for higher prices?
records.geography: United States; macroeconomic and consumer-spending framing using BLS and industry data
records.boundary: This record adds a U.S. affordability mechanism: household pressure increasingly comes from essential services and fixed or difficult-to-substitute expenses, even when many retail goods are relatively affordable. The source is an NRF industry perspective using selected BLS and sector comparisons, not an independent causal price study, complete household expenditure decomposition, representative respondent survey or neutral adjudication of responsibility for inflation.

records.title: NVIDIA disclosed a February 2026 H200 license for small shipments to specific China customers, but no H200 revenue or China import was realized by filing date
records.source_unit: NVIDIA fiscal-year 2026 Form 10-K filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
records.geography: United States, China, NVIDIA, U.S. export-control authorities, and advanced-computing customers
records.boundary: This record adds a realized licensing-approval stage after BIS conditional case-by-case policy, while preserving the gap between approval and trade realization. It does not establish shipment, China import approval, revenue, Chinese capability change, U.S. supply protection, or geopolitical leverage.

records.title: NVIDIA reported a fraction of licensed H200 shipments to China, but PRC restrictions prevented full licensed sales and the market remained effectively foreclosed
records.source_unit: NVIDIA second-quarter fiscal-year 2027 Form 10-Q and Q2 fiscal-year 2027 earnings-call transcript
records.geography: United States, China, NVIDIA, U.S. export-control authorities, Chinese regulators, and advanced-computing customers
records.boundary: This record establishes partial physical shipment under the H200 licensing route and a continuing PRC restriction on full sales. It does not establish shipment quantity, customer-level import approval, H200-specific revenue, Chinese capability change, restored competition, or geopolitical leverage.

records.title: Transmission cost oversight can create a ratepayer refund route before individual bill impact is visible
records.source_unit: New York State Department of Public Service settlement announcement concerning a transmission developer's proposal and operating costs
records.geography: New York State ratepayers and transmission customers
records.boundary: This record establishes a regulatory cost-review and expected ratepayer-refund stage for a named transmission developer. It does not establish the affected customer denominator, bill posting, cash receipt, adequacy, correction of residual loss, reliability change, trust, switching, or durable household affordability. The case is a consumer-power and infrastructure-governance bridge, not a household recovery estimate.

records.title: Brooklyn bus-lane and safety works begin on a high-use, high-injury corridor while rider and safety gains remain to be measured
records.source_unit: New York City Mayor's Office and NYC Department of Transportation Bay Parkway/Cropsey Avenue bus-priority and street-safety project announcement
records.geography: Bay Parkway and Cropsey Avenue, Brooklyn, New York City
records.boundary: This record follows a named Brooklyn transportation project from a dated construction start to an affected-rider and crash/injury baseline. It does not establish completed implementation, realized travel-time or reliability improvement, rider affordability, safety reduction, traffic displacement, or durable public acceptance.

records.title: New York congestion pricing produced observed traffic and early transit changes while capital delivery and distributive legitimacy remain open
records.source_unit: Metropolitan Transportation Authority, New York City Comptroller, and New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene administrative and evaluation reporting
records.geography: New York City; Congestion Relief Zone and selected environmental-justice monitoring locations
records.boundary: This record follows a named infrastructure and pricing intervention through observed zone traffic, reported revenue, early transit indicators, an air-quality evaluation, and a visible capital portfolio. It does not establish individual household welfare, distributional incidence, long-term health, completed capital benefits, political legitimacy, or a single causal effect of congestion pricing on every outcome.

records.title: A named worker-restitution schedule can exist without public proof that payment reached the worker
records.source_unit: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection Fair Workweek restitution settlements and proposed unclaimed-restitution fund
records.geography: New York City; Salz Management LLC and Theory LLC settlements
records.boundary: This record establishes a current worker-restitution payment route and a proposed public response to unclaimed remedies. It does not establish worker receipt, adequacy, durable schedule protection, household recovery, trust, or exit.

records.title: A city can mandate measurement of algorithmic work impacts before worker outcomes are publicly visible
records.source_unit: New York City Local Law 25 of 2026 and City Council enactment record concerning a study of algorithmic tools and automated employment decision tools
records.geography: New York City municipal civil service and algorithmic employment decision context
records.boundary: This record advances the AI/work/consumer chain from rule and complaint architecture to an enacted municipal measurement mandate, reported planning-stage implementation, a citywide AI enforcement posture, proposed employee-impact reporting, and proposed consumer complaint/oversight routes. It does not establish study completion, a published report, named employer or tool implementation, worker notice or appeal, complaint investigation, decision correction, compensation, workload/pay change, trust, or exit.

records.title: New York City microhubs convert truck delivery into smaller last-mile operation
records.source_unit: New York City Department of Transportation Microhubs Pilot
records.geography: New York City, Manhattan, United States
records.boundary: This record establishes named microhub operation, alternative delivery modes, and agency-reported truck-mile and pollution reductions. It does not establish recipient-level service quality, worker or neighborhood incidence, cost savings, causal safety or air-quality effects, or durable public acceptance.

records.title: A Bronx busway converts a safety and delay problem into operating access for 39,000 daily riders without yet proving realized time savings
records.source_unit: NYC Mayor's Office and NYC DOT completion announcement for the Tremont Avenue busway
records.geography: Tremont Avenue, Bronx, New York City
records.boundary: This record establishes a completed and activated Bronx busway serving a named daily rider population in a transit-dependent corridor. It does not establish realized time savings, reliability, safety, accessibility, affordability, adjacent-neighborhood burden, or durable rider legitimacy.

records.title: Universal school meals can convert stigma-free access into participation and learning gains while leaving food quality, waste, and household spillovers contested
records.source_unit: New York City Public Schools administrative meal system, New York City Comptroller review, and longitudinal student-level evaluation of universal free meals
records.geography: New York City public schools; citywide meal operations and middle-school evaluation
records.boundary: This record follows New York City's universal school-meals route from historical student-level evaluation through current program scale, access guidance, feedback channels, and operational compliance. It does not establish current causal effects, household food-security change, nutritional adequacy, equal practical access, or durable student trust and belonging across the city.

records.title: Household spending expectations rise while credit access, financial outlook, and job-finding confidence deteriorate
records.source_unit: Federal Reserve Bank of New York Center for Microeconomic Data, August 2026 Survey of Consumer Expectations, released 8 September 2026
records.geography: United States; nationally representative internet-based rotating panel of approximately 1,300 household heads, fielded 3–31 August 2026
records.boundary: This record adds a household-finance route from category-specific price and labor expectations through income-spending divergence, credit access, missed-payment risk, and unequal financial buffers. It does not establish realized inflation, delinquency, unemployment, consumption volume, or causal effects of monetary or credit conditions.

records.title: Household inflation, earnings, and consumption diverge across US groups
records.source_unit: New York Fed Economic Heterogeneity Indicator for demographic, economic, and geographic group consumption baskets and outcomes
records.geography: United States national indicators, with metro, regional, demographic, and urban/rural groupings
records.boundary: This record measures constructed demographic inflation, employed-worker earnings ratios, and aggregate receipt-based retail-consumption directions through December/November 2025. It does not establish household-specific prices, policy causality, trust, political action, or a same-household cost-to-behavior chain. The EHI indicators are not official estimates of the Federal Reserve System or FOMC.

records.title: A gasoline shock reverses some US household inflation and spending gaps
records.source_unit: New York Fed Economic Heterogeneity Indicator for demographic, economic, geographic, and income-group outcomes
records.geography: United States national indicators, with demographic, regional, urban/rural, and income-group comparisons
records.boundary: This record measures constructed demographic inflation, employed-worker earnings ratios, and aggregate receipt-based consumer-spending directions through April 2026. It does not establish individual price payment, household-specific gasoline exposure, policy causality, trust, political action, or a same-household cost-to-behavior chain. The EHI indicators are not official estimates of the Federal Reserve System or FOMC.

records.title: Second District households and small firms absorb the 2026 shock differently from national groups
records.source_unit: New York Fed Economic Heterogeneity Indicator for the Second District and New York/New Jersey/Connecticut employer firms
records.geography: Federal Reserve Second District; firm regional analysis covers New York, New Jersey, and Connecticut
records.boundary: This record measures derived Second District inflation and spending indicators plus weighted regional employer-firm survey outcomes. It does not establish individual prices, household fuel exposure, local service access, worker household security, trust, political action, or causal policy effects. The EHI indicators are not official estimates of the Federal Reserve System or FOMC.

records.title: Small-business profitability, revenue, and employment paths diverge by firm size
records.source_unit: Federal Reserve Banks Small Business Credit Survey employer firm
records.geography: United States national small-business indicators
records.boundary: This record measures weighted employer-firm survey indicators for profitability, revenue, employment, financing, debt, pricing, and technology/supply-chain challenges. It does not establish firm survival, local service access, worker household outcomes, customer prices, market power, or political action. The SBCS is non-random and question universes vary.

records.title: A completed transmission project can make infrastructure capacity visible before household savings are verified
records.source_unit: New York Power Authority Smart Path Connect project announcement; named public transmission project and reported system-level savings, not a household billing sample
records.geography: New York North Country transmission corridor between Clinton and Massena, United States
records.boundary: This record adds a completed and energized transmission project to the infrastructure/state-capacity lane. It establishes physical realization, a reported system-level savings claim, and an official customer-facing monthly-bill-savings claim, not observed customer-level bill savings, equal ratepayer benefit, outage reduction, local acceptance, maintenance durability, or geopolitical leverage. The next test is a project or ratepayer-linked realization ledger preserving service, rate, reliability, geography, customer class, and later affordability separately.

records.title: Cross-border transmission can reach commercial operation before household affordability is visible
records.source_unit: NYSERDA and New York State announcement of commercial operation of the Champlain Hudson Power Express transmission project
records.geography: Quebec, Canada; New York State; New York City Zone J
records.boundary: This record establishes a cross-border infrastructure project reaching commercial operation and a reported route for clean electricity delivery into New York. It does not establish realized household affordability, customer-class allocation, reliability improvement, host-community acceptance, or durable geopolitical leverage. It is an infrastructure and state-dependence realization case, not a household benefit estimate.

records.title: Physical and shared brand experiences are being positioned as a counterweight to fragmented digital attention
records.source_unit: Out of Home Advertising Association of America and The Harris Poll, The Power of the Human Medium: OOH Across Experiential + Retail, released September 17, 2026
records.geography: United States; adults ages 18-64, with Gen Z comparisons
records.boundary: This record treats sponsor-funded OOH research as a directional signal about the perceived value of physical, local and shared experiences in a fragmented attention environment. It does not establish causal advertising effectiveness, representative consumer behavior, actual sales lift, long-term trust, or that physical media is universally more human or culturally relevant than digital media.

records.title: US firms report widespread algorithmic management alongside accountability and worker-protection concerns
records.source_unit: OECD employer-survey respondent reporting firm use and governance of software that instructs, monitors, or evaluates workers
records.geography: France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Spain, and the United States; US-specific rates retained where reported
records.boundary: This record measures employer-reported provision, perceived managerial effects, trustworthiness concerns, and governance measures in a six-country survey. It does not establish worker exposure, job quality, pay, autonomy, bargaining power, health effects, enforcement, remedy, or US political action. Algorithmic management is broader than generative AI.

records.title: U.S. financial infrastructure can reach a foreign firm while future sanctions compliance remains unproven
records.source_unit: U.S. Treasury Office of Foreign Assets Control settlement and enforcement release involving Adani Enterprises Limited
records.geography: Adani Enterprises Limited in India; Iran-origin LPG transactions and U.S. financial institutions
records.boundary: This record measures one OFAC enforcement case involving a foreign firm, U.S.-dollar payments, a settlement, and a future compliance commitment. It does not establish sanctions effectiveness, deterrence, strategic change, universal financial control, later compliance, recurrence, or distributional effects.

records.title: OFR reports AI-enabled efficiency alongside lower staffing and changing public financial-data infrastructure
records.source_unit: Office of Financial Research FY2025 institutional annual-report self-report
records.geography: United States federal financial-stability institution
records.boundary: This record captures OFR's FY2025 self-reported workforce, budget, AI use, analytics-platform, and financial-data-capacity changes. It does not establish that AI caused the staffing change, increased productivity by a measured amount, improved public service, reduced financial risk, or changed household or market outcomes. It is an institutional capacity and governance record.

records.title: OFR reports a changing public financial-visibility and institutional-capacity sequence
records.source_unit: Office of Financial Research annual report to Congress; institutional self-report
records.geography: United States federal financial-stability institution and financial system
records.boundary: This record captures a four-vintage OFR institutional chronology. It does not establish that AI caused staffing changes, that data collection improved financial stability, that public visibility became consumer protection, or that any household or firm experienced a linked outcome. Institutional, market, firm, account, household, and respondent units remain separate.

records.title: Randomized Medicaid access reduces financial exposure and expands care use while health and work outcomes separate
records.source_unit: Low-income uninsured Oregon adults selected or not selected by Medicaid lottery
records.geography: Oregon, United States
records.boundary: The Oregon lottery identifies selected coverage effects for a historical low-income uninsured population; it does not complete the same-person bill-to-care-choice-to-household-adaptation-to-trust chain.

records.title: Randomized Medicaid access increased one presidential-election turnout but not later turnout
records.source_unit: Low-income uninsured Oregon adults selected or not selected by the 2008 Medicaid lottery, linked to statewide voter records
records.geography: Oregon, United States
records.boundary: This record adds a randomized Medicaid-access-to-voter-participation route: coverage increased turnout in the November 2008 presidential election but not subsequent turnout through November 2010. It does not establish a causal trust effect, a universal Medicaid-to-voting effect, a specific household recovery mechanism, or durable political realignment.

records.title: A randomized two-way interaction with a Member of Congress can increase trust and later political support among participating constituents
records.source_unit: Ohio State University field experiments with Members of Congress in online deliberative town halls
records.geography: United States congressional districts; 20 online town-hall meetings with 12 Members of Congress in studies conducted in 2006 and 2008
records.boundary: This record provides causal evidence that a specific deliberative interaction can affect policy agreement, leader trust/approval, and possibly later vote behavior among selected participants. It does not estimate present-day national prevalence, prove that ordinary constituent contact receives a response, establish durable institutional legitimacy, or generalize across issues, leaders, channels, or nonparticipants.

records.title: Interest in congressional engagement coexists with contact barriers and weak perceived responsiveness
records.source_unit: Ohio State University Institute for Democratic Engagement and Accountability Constituent Engagement Survey
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record closes a descriptive contact-to-perceived-responsiveness layer for congressional engagement. It does not observe a constituent's actual office response, issue resolution, policy influence, satisfaction, remedy, later trust change, or durable political action, and it is not a verified contact log.

records.title: Telephone town-hall participation can improve evaluations of the forum and Member, while deliberative design mainly improves the forum evaluation
records.source_unit: Abernathy, Esterling, Freebourn, Kennedy, Minozzi, Neblo, and Solis field experiment with Members of Congress
records.geography: United States congressional districts; four Members of Congress and eight telephone town-hall sessions
records.boundary: This record adds a causal communication-design layer between constituent interaction and perceived forum/Member evaluation. It does not establish present-day national prevalence, actual office response, issue resolution, policy influence, durable trust, or equal access to two-way representation.

records.title: Small-business revenue losses passed only partially into linked owner-household consumption during COVID-19
records.source_unit: Linked US small-business and owner-household financial-account data; revised NBER working-paper summary, not a general household survey
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record closes a measured firm-revenue-to-linked-owner-consumption arrow for the early COVID-19 period, with persistent muted pass-through through 2021. It does not establish a natural-disaster recovery effect, business survival, worker conditions, customer welfare, household security for every owner, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence.

records.title: Panel-measured economic insecurity predicted participation and right-leaning presidential preference
records.source_unit: Understanding America Study panel respondents with repeated household-income observations and 2016 presidential preference reports
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a panel-measured economic-insecurity-to-political-preference contrast: insecurity predicted greater reported voting probability and Trump support in the 2016 U.S. presidential context, conditional on current resources. It does not establish causality, generalized distrust, ballot-validated turnout, or a universal hardship-to-mobilization mechanism.

records.title: Young people are drawing a trust boundary around family and friends while adopting AI and losing financial independence
records.source_unit: Pacsun and GlobalData, 2026 Youth Report / Drawbridge Generation
records.geography: United States; Gen Z and Gen Alpha respondents ages 11-24
records.boundary: This record adds a youth-cultural route from noisy public information and AI adoption through trust concentration, material dependence, mental-health priorities, and selective delegation. It does not establish causes of financial dependence, clinical mental-health prevalence, actual AI advice quality, or general U.S. youth behavior outside the reported survey frame.

records.title: 9/11 remains a vivid lived memory while national trauma shifts toward school, family, and generational transmission
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center, 9/11 memories remain vivid in the U.S. 25 years later, September 2026
records.geography: United States; adults nationally with age and generational comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural-memory and generational-transmission layer: 9/11 remains vividly remembered by those old enough to recall it, while younger Americans increasingly encounter it through school, family, friends, media, and inherited narratives. It does not establish memory accuracy, shared meaning, trauma prevalence, policy attitudes, national identity, or causal political effects.

records.title: Adult platform reach is broad, increasingly diversified, and patterned by age and social position
records.source_unit: US adult survey respondent, with platform-use and frequency reports
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record measures self-reported adult platform reach, frequency, change across repeated survey waves, and subgroup differences. It does not establish total attention time, content exposure, recommendation effects, political persuasion, consumer conversion, privacy loss, dependence, or causality.

records.title: AI chatbots are becoming a low-cost health-navigation layer while usefulness, privacy, and mental-health legitimacy remain unsettled
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center, From Diagnoses to Treatments, Why Americans Use AI Chatbots for Health, and companion analysis on loneliness, depression, and stress, August 25, 2026
records.geography: United States; adults nationally with health-chatbot use, age, race/ethnicity, income, education, AI-attitude, helpfulness, privacy, and mental-health judgments
records.boundary: This record adds an AI-mediated health-navigation and social-support layer: speed, cost, privacy, diagnostic interpretation, sensitive questions, and emotional support create different legitimacy conditions. It does not establish clinical accuracy, treatment efficacy, data protection, mental-health outcomes, or whether chatbot use replaces professional care.

records.title: AI concern and expected job loss have become more Democratic than Republican in 2026
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center American Trends Panel survey of US adults
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record measures public attitudes and expectations about AI, not realized AI exposure, employment displacement, productivity, wages, workplace control, firm adoption, political action, regulation, or geopolitical capability. Party differences are descriptive; a same-worker implementation-to-outcome and policy-response chain remains open.

records.title: AI optimism is giving way to a cross-generational expectation of job loss, with young adults moving sharply toward concern
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center short read, Young adults in the U.S. are increasingly wary of AI, concerned it will take jobs, August 18, 2026
records.geography: United States; adults nationally, with age comparisons and a 2021-2026 trend
records.boundary: This record treats AI skepticism as a cultural, labor-market and legitimacy signal connecting age, work expectations, social connection and technology adoption. It does not forecast actual employment, measure individual exposure, establish causal sources of concern, or imply that public expectations are correct.

records.title: AI use is becoming ordinary while control and social-impact concerns remain divided
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center survey respondent; U.S. adults, with employed-adult and age subgroup universes where specified
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a 2026 public-use, purpose, age, perceived-impact, privacy, pace, and regulatory-confidence layer. It does not establish chatbot dependence, actual privacy loss, product causation, emotional harm, changed political behavior, or unequal realized benefit. The 2024 and 2026 use measures have wording and universe changes; the age series is a descriptive brand-specific comparison.

records.title: AI health use is motivated by speed and cost while patients want disclosure and more control over provider use
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center American Trends Panel survey of U.S. adults, June 22-28, 2026; paired health-chatbot-use and healthcare-AI-transparency reports
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a practical health-information, transparency, and control layer to the AI trend. It does not evaluate medical accuracy, provider compliance, clinical outcomes, privacy harms, substitution of care, or causal patient behavior.

records.title: AI adoption is broadening while perceived control and regulatory confidence remain weak
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center American Trends Panel survey of U.S. adults, February 17-23, 2026
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record identifies a cultural and institutional pattern in which AI use is expanding faster than confidence in governance. It does not estimate productivity, labor displacement, psychological effect, privacy harm, or political realignment.

records.title: Family support networks can extend beyond legal and household ties
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center survey of U.S. adults, including 4,271 Black adults, fielded June 16-29, 2025
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural and social-network layer: family can be defined through birth, law, marriage, and choice, with reported closeness extending beyond the nuclear household. It does not establish care delivery, financial support, burden, household security, identity causation, trust, political action, or later durability.

records.title: Young-adult place retention is a work-quality, mobility and belonging bargain
records.source_unit: The Pew Charitable Trusts, Gen Z Likes Philadelphia but Feels Frustrated by Low Pay, Limited Jobs, August 12, 2026
records.geography: Philadelphia and Greater Philadelphia; residents ages 18–29, with contextual Census comparisons
records.boundary: This record identifies a place-retention, work-quality, social-capital and infrastructure subtheme. It does not establish representative Gen Z preferences, causal effects of jobs or transit, realized migration, wages, job retention, employer behavior, housing outcomes, family formation or generalization beyond Philadelphia and the report's qualitative/contextual evidence.

records.title: American views of China remain more negative than positive but have warmed since 2021
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center American Trends Panel feeling-thermometer survey of U.S. adults
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a U.S. public-attitude time trend toward China. It does not infer alliance change, threat reduction, policy support, economic dependence, or future diplomatic behavior from thermometer ratings.

records.title: U.S. public life is organized into distinct participation modes rather than a single engaged-disengaged spectrum
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center / Pew-Knight Initiative, How Americans Are Engaged With News, Politics, Religion and Civic Life, July 16, 2026
records.geography: United States; nationally representative adult survey evidence with cluster-defined engagement groups
records.boundary: This record adds a U.S. public-life route from news attention, community and religious participation, voting, volunteering, donations, and direct political action through socioeconomic position and institutional feedback. It uses aggregate survey classifications, not respondent-level files or longitudinal causal analysis; the engagement groups are descriptive and period-specific rather than fixed identities.

records.title: U.S. public concern about data centers shifts from unfamiliarity toward local infrastructure burden
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center American Trends Panel survey of U.S. adults, July 20-August 9, 2026
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a public-legitimacy and local-siting layer to the AI infrastructure trend. It does not infer actual data-center externalities, protest behavior, permitting outcomes, or a causal relationship between awareness and opposition.

records.title: Data centers are becoming a local legitimacy problem as Americans connect AI infrastructure to energy, environment, and quality of life
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center survey analysis, Americans' views of data centers have turned more negative, September 2026
records.geography: United States; adults nationally with urban, suburban, rural, party, age, education, and awareness comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a local-legitimacy and household-cost layer to AI infrastructure: rising awareness is accompanied by more negative perceptions of environmental, energy, quality-of-life, jobs, and tax effects, plus broad discomfort with local siting. It does not establish realized impacts, causal opinion change, community decisions, rate effects, emissions, water use, or durable public consent.

records.title: Americans see democracy as a diminished example and want change without equal confidence that change is possible
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center spring 2026 Global Attitudes Survey and U.S. democracy analysis
records.geography: United States, with cross-national high-income-country comparison
records.boundary: This record measures democratic evaluation and satisfaction in public-attitude surveys. It does not establish institutional performance, legal change, causal polarization, reform feasibility, turnout, protest, voting, or rejection of democratic government.

records.title: A more diverse eligible electorate does not automatically mean more political power
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center analysis of American Community Survey/IPUMS data and Census-based population projections
records.geography: United States citizens age 18 and older in the 50 states and District of Columbia
records.boundary: This record measures the changing racial and ethnic composition of the formal eligible electorate and group-specific eligibility shares. It does not measure registration, ballot access, turnout, representation, party preference, policy influence, political efficacy, or legitimacy; 2026 national values are projections and four-group displays omit other or multiple-race categories.

records.title: Family caregiving operates as unpaid social infrastructure while shifting health, work, money, and social costs onto caregivers
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center American Trends Panel survey of US adults with aging parents or spouses/partners
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record establishes family-caregiving prevalence, tasks, income/gender differences, and reported cross-domain effects. It does not establish exact hours, paid-care substitution, adequacy, household financial recovery, health causation, policy receipt, trust, political action, or caregiver exit.

records.title: Foreign-policy values cross-cut U.S. political coalitions
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center 2026 Political Typology survey of the American Trends Panel
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a cross-pressure map of U.S. foreign-policy values within domestic political coalitions. It does not follow respondents into voting, protest, defense spending, military service, alliance burden sharing, government decisions, partner consent, or external geopolitical behavior.

records.title: Trust in who should regulate AI is internationally distributed rather than aligned with one Western model
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center surveys of 13,696 adults in 12 countries conducted February 8-May 13, 2026, including separate U.S. and cross-national samples
records.geography: United States and 11 additional countries surveyed by Pew Research Center
records.boundary: This record adds a geopolitical-cultural layer to AI governance: regulatory legitimacy is contested across countries and does not map neatly onto U.S., EU, or Chinese formal capacity. It does not measure actual regulation, platform behavior, alliance alignment, or strategic influence.

records.title: U.S. global-role legitimacy separates foreign reception, domestic judgment, and partisan meaning
records.source_unit: Pew 2026 Global Attitudes Survey and U.S. American Trends Panel supplement; country publics and US respondents kept separate
records.geography: 36 non-US countries and United States
records.boundary: This is a deliberately non-pooled legitimacy synthesis. It distinguishes foreign reception, domestic judgment, and partisan meaning, but does not estimate a causal policy effect, international reputation trend, alliance response, state capability, geopolitical leverage, or political action from the survey. An event-country-party-year behavior ledger remains open.

records.title: Grandparent ties can function as social infrastructure before they become formal care
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center synthesis using Census SIPP, University of Michigan HRS, Census ACS, and Pew surveys
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record keeps grandparent status, routine contact, caregiving, shared housing, and reported closeness separate. It does not establish causal effects, support quality, burden, cultural identity, household welfare, or later durability.

records.title: Health-information pathways are racially differentiated, with social media and influencers filling different access and disclosure roles
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center, Americans' use of social media for health information differs by race and ethnicity, August 13, 2026
records.geography: United States; adults nationally with race/ethnicity, source-use, perceived-accuracy, source-criteria, and influencer-purpose comparisons
