records.boundary: This record adds a race-differentiated health-information pathway: platform use, perceived accuracy, source criteria, and influencer use for sensitive questions do not move together. It does not establish misinformation exposure, clinical substitution, provider discrimination, algorithmic causality, or health outcomes.

records.title: Americans use many health-information sources while trust and accuracy remain unsettled
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center American Trends Panel survey of U.S. adults
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds an information-legitimacy layer to the health and digital lanes: people combine institutional, peer, platform, and AI sources while many find accuracy and conflict difficult to judge. It does not estimate misinformation prevalence, medical decisions, treatment quality, or health outcomes.

records.title: Health influence online is built from credentials, coaching, business, and lived experience rather than one authority route
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center analysis of prominent health and wellness influencer profiles plus American Trends Panel surveys
records.geography: United States audience; English-language Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, and top-ranked health podcasts
records.boundary: This record adds a platform-mediated health-authority layer: online health influence mixes professional identity, coaching, business, and lived experience. It does not verify credentials, accuracy, commercial incentives, medical decisions, or health outcomes.

records.title: Hispanic identity can be central and connective while its practical meaning remains contested
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center National Survey of Latinos identity, treatment, and opportunity-meaning respondents; this is a weighted cross-sectional cultural-meaning sample, not an assimilation or mobility panel
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds identity centrality, perceived opportunity meaning, selected treatment, support, collective connection, and generation-linked national self-description to the place and migration lane. It does not establish assimilation, discrimination causality, material mobility, service access, political behavior, consumer switching, or a dated encounter-to-action pathway.

records.title: Hispanic America is growing while population counts, racial categories, ancestry, and self-identification diverge
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center, Who is Hispanic?, September 2026, using Census Bureau data, ACS/IPUMS analysis, and the National Survey of Latinos
records.geography: United States; Hispanic adults and the broader U.S. Hispanic population across generations, origins, race, and family formation
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural-demographic measurement layer: the U.S. Hispanic population is growing rapidly, but race coding, ancestry, self-identification, generation, Afro-Latino identity, and intermarriage produce multiple overlapping versions of who is counted and how identity is lived. It does not establish a unified Hispanic market, electorate, culture, or causal assimilation trajectory.

records.title: Americans use different information routes for different public and consumer topics
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center survey of U.S. adults, March 6-9, 2026
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record establishes topic-specific information-source distributions. It does not establish source accuracy, trust, political persuasion, consumer action, policy understanding, platform causality, or durable institutional legitimacy.

records.title: Latino Americans separate intergenerational progress from belief that the American dream is attainable
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center National Survey of Latinos
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record measures reported American-dream meaning, perceived intergenerational living-standard change, and nativity subgroup differences. It does not measure causal income mobility, wealth, housing purchase, legal status, voting, political action, consumer switching, or future outcomes.

records.title: Communal identity can combine high social trust with partisan alignment and internal educational divides
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center 2023-24 Religious Landscape Study; U.S. adults with current or former Latter-day Saint identity
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural-identity and trust distribution layer. It does not generalize one religious group to the country, prove that communal ties cause trust or partisan identity, or establish later political action or institutional legitimacy.

records.title: A strong communal institution can show high volunteering and trust while internal access remains unequal
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center analysis of the 2023-24 Religious Landscape Study, Tradition and Change Among Latter-day Saints in the U.S.
records.geography: United States; 2023-24 Religious Landscape Study with 36,908 randomly sampled U.S. adults, including 565 current Latter-day Saints and 316 former members
records.boundary: This record shows a descriptive association between Latter-day Saint affiliation and reported volunteering and generalized trust, with important internal differences by education and region. It does not establish that religious membership caused trust or volunteering, that service was equally distributed or non-burdensome, or that the pattern produces political influence, durable belonging, or public benefit.

records.title: A durable religious community is becoming more diverse and less institutionally retained while preserving a conservative core
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center Religious Landscape Study analysis, 2007-2023/24, published September 22, 2026
records.geography: United States; adults identifying as current or former Latter-day Saints
records.boundary: This record adds a within-community cultural-demographic change layer. It does not generalize Latter-day Saint trends to U.S. religion overall, establish causes of retention or attitude change, or infer future institutional strength, political behavior, or group cohesion from descriptive comparisons.

records.title: Dense religious community persists through demographic change while retention, family formation, trust, and political meaning shift
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center, Tradition and Change Among Latter-day Saints in the U.S., September 22, 2026
records.geography: United States; adults identifying as Latter-day Saints in the 2023-24 Religious Landscape Study (RLS)
records.boundary: This record adds a religion-as-social-infrastructure route: communal ties, family practice, volunteering, generalized trust, demographic diversification, retention, and partisan meaning interact without being collapsed into religiosity or electoral behavior. It does not establish causal effects of membership, institutional policy, family wellbeing, political action, or social cohesion.

records.title: Economic and affordability salience can coexist with divided party attribution and weak policy representation
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center July 2026 survey of economic salience, party fit, presidential attribution, and AI-policy representation
records.geography: United States; 3,554 adults including 2,779 registered voters
records.boundary: This record establishes a dated cross-sectional bridge from economic and affordability salience to political attribution and representation. It does not establish a material shock, causal vote effect, policy delivery, household recovery, trust change, or geopolitical consequence.

records.title: Muslim-American institutional presence grows while public suspicion, discrimination, and partisan polarization persist
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center data essay with FBI Uniform Crime Reporting and mosque-count context
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record measures public attitudes, reported Muslim-American experiences, reported anti-Islamic hate-crime incidents, institutional presence, and political visibility. It does not establish causal effects of 9/11, party messaging, media, migration, mosque growth, individual voting, consumer behavior, service access, or total discrimination prevalence.

records.title: Muslim belonging is a dual condition of support, discrimination and representational harm
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center, Muslims have felt both discrimination and support from other Americans, September 3, 2026
records.geography: United States; U.S. Muslims, with 2026 measures compared on the chart with selected earlier Pew and Project MAPS measures
records.boundary: This record identifies a cultural belonging, discrimination, representation and institutional-voice subtheme. It does not establish verified incident rates, causal effects of media portrayal, subgroup differences, media or consumer behavior, political participation, institutional reform effects or a harmonized longitudinal trend; those require the underlying topline, microdata or linked behavioral and episode evidence.

records.title: National dissatisfaction coexists with modestly improved long-horizon expectations and persistent partisan polarization
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center report On the Country's 250th Anniversary, the American People Are in a Sour Mood, using American Trends Panel and historical survey data
records.geography: United States; adults nationally, with party and age comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a national-mood and future-imagination layer: Americans report sustained dissatisfaction and concern about division and national decline, while long-horizon expectations have improved from 2023 on selected measures and remain strongly aligned with party and age. It does not establish causal drivers, actual future outcomes, political mobilization, institutional performance, or individual material trajectories.

records.title: NATO can remain popular while permission for U.S. leadership is divided
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center 2026 survey of adults in 37 countries, including 13 NATO member states in the alliance-favorability comparison
records.geography: United States and 36 comparison countries; U.S. partisan estimates and cross-national NATO-member comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds current public legitimacy and relational-trust measures around NATO. It does not establish alliance operation, defense burden sharing, host-country consent, strategic success, willingness to bear risk, later political action, or durable alignment.

records.title: Stated willingness to help neighbors can exceed expected reciprocity without proving delivered protection
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center American Trends Panel survey on connection to neighbors
records.geography: United States; 9,482 adults in the Pew American Trends Panel
records.boundary: This record establishes local familiarity, trust, stated mutual-aid willingness, reciprocity expectations, and a potential public-request response surface. It does not estimate delivered aid, resilience, substitution for public systems, burden, recovery, political action, or exit.

records.title: Social trust is associated with stated neighborly help and willingness to follow a public request
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center American Trends Panel survey on neighborhood connection and social trust
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record closes only a same-survey association between generalized social trust and stated neighborly/public-request willingness. It does not establish social trust as a cause, observe actual compliance or assistance, measure institutional performance, or show later political action, recovery, or durable community capacity.

records.title: Platform-mediated news and civic life divide into distinct attention, trust, and action routes
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center US adult surveys and selected public social-media news-influencer accounts
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record measures distinct population engagement styles, partisan news-source ecosystems, and social-media news-influencer exposure. It does not join respondents across studies, establish platform causation, measure actual content accuracy, or infer that attention, trust, sharing, or continued use equals informed control or political influence. The retrieval hash covers the committed Pew synthesis memo.

records.title: Party identity shifts at the edges while gender, race, and education keep the coalition lines uneven
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center National Public Opinion Reference Survey (NPORS), 2020-2026 partisan-affiliation fact sheet
records.geography: United States; adults surveyed Jan. 30-June 18, 2026
records.boundary: This record adds a current coalition-identity layer to the atlas. It shows how partisan affiliation and leaning differ across social groups and over time; it does not establish why people changed, how identity became a vote or policy demand, or whether a coalition shift will persist.

records.title: American political coalitions contain cross-pressured value groups that a two-party split hides
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center 2026 Political Typology American Trends Panel survey and linked follow-up surveys
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record maps value-based coalition differences in a cluster-derived typology. It does not establish stable identities, causes of political behavior, turnout, vote choice, switching, policy influence, or a single center-versus-extremes mechanism.

records.title: Prediction-market activity expands through sports and speculative attention more than politics
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center analysis of The Block data on Kalshi and Polymarket trading, July 2024-July 2026
records.geography: Global platform trading volume; U.S. and international platform activity
records.boundary: This record adds a platform-mediated speculative-attention and consumer-participation layer. It does not estimate user counts, gambling prevalence, legality, financial welfare, political persuasion, market accuracy, or causal effects of sports trading on civic behavior.

records.title: Americans broadly value press freedom while accepting conditional restrictions and dividing by party over current constraints
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center Pew-Knight Initiative American Trends Panel surveys and focus groups
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record measures public importance judgments, perceived press freedom, conditional restriction preferences, and party differences. It does not measure actual censorship, news accuracy, platform moderation, ownership, exposure, source switching, political participation, or causal media effects; focus groups are not representative and are not pooled with survey estimates.

records.title: Americans judge the press-government relationship as bad while disagreeing over media power and permissible criticism
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center Pew-Knight Initiative surveys and focus groups on press freedom
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record measures perceptions and norms concerning press-government relations, media power, and reciprocal criticism. It does not measure actual censorship, news accuracy, ownership, audience exposure, institutional trust as a general construct, political participation, vote choice, or causal media effects. The focus groups are not representative and are not pooled with survey estimates.

records.title: Public-life engagement forms distinct participation styles rather than one civic ladder
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center Cross-Sectional Engagement Survey and American Trends Panel assignment to engagement groups
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record describes engagement clusters and associated political, news, trust, and fairness judgments. It does not estimate a causal effect of civic participation, identify the same person's trigger-to-action path, measure objective news fairness, or establish that trust produces voting, organizing, switching, or non-use.

records.title: Public participation divides into mobilization, connection, spectatorship, and outsider patterns
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center Cross-Sectional Engagement Survey and American Trends Panel; U.S. adults, 2025 fieldwork
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a multidimensional civic-culture map. It does not measure change over time, explain why people enter a group, establish civic influence, or infer trust and political meaning from participation alone.

records.title: Public-life participation is segmented into mobilizers, connectors, spectators, and outsiders rather than one engagement scale
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center and Pew-Knight Initiative Cross-Sectional Engagement Survey and American Trends Panel analysis
records.geography: United States, adults
records.boundary: This record adds a cross-domain public-life participation typology linking news attention, political action, civic involvement, religious participation, and voting. It does not infer civic health, democratic legitimacy, political causality, stable identities, or individual-level respondent behavior beyond Pew's aggregate group estimates.

records.title: Public-life engagement is organized into distinct participation routes rather than a single engaged-disengaged spectrum
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center Pew-Knight Initiative Cross-Sectional Engagement Survey and American Trends Panel classification
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a cross-domain public-life participation typology linking news attention, civic action, religious practice, charitable behavior, and voting. It does not infer causality, durable civic identity, political efficacy, social capital, institutional trust, or exclusion from the cross-sectional clusters.

records.title: Support for political reform can coexist with low confidence that reform is achievable
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center analysis of recent U.S. public-opinion surveys and Congress.gov amendment records
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record identifies a gap between public demand for political change and confidence that change is possible. It does not establish reform action, coordination, turnout, protest, institutional performance, causal polarization, or successful constitutional change.

records.title: Religion is seen as regaining public influence while most Americans still limit direct church involvement in politics
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center American Trends Panel survey on religion's influence in government and public life
records.geography: United States; adults ages 18 and older
records.boundary: This record measures perceptions of religion's influence, normative boundaries on religious political participation, familiarity with Christian nationalism, and church-state preferences. It does not establish religious participation, institutional power, policy change, mobilization, discrimination, constitutional outcomes, vote choice, or causal partisan realignment.

records.title: Religious institutions retain a community-service legitimacy that is unevenly shared
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center 2023-24 Religious Landscape Study of U.S. adults
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a religious-institution community and legitimacy layer. It does not establish service delivery, material relief, political influence, causal participation, or durable trust, and it should not be treated as a general measure of religiosity.

records.title: Americans view U.S. global power through sharply partisan lenses, with broad agreement that it interferes abroad
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center, Most Americans Now Say U.S. Foreign Policy Ignores the Interests of Other Countries, April 2026, based on the American Trends Panel
records.geography: United States; adults nationally with party, age, and global-country comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a US-to-world legitimacy layer: Americans' perceptions of U.S. power, respect, interference, peace contribution, and attention to other countries are strongly partisan and internally multidimensional. It does not establish actual foreign-policy conduct, diplomatic influence, partner trust, geopolitical outcomes, or causal effects of public opinion on policy.

records.title: People can value smartphones while struggling to reduce their use
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center American Trends Panel survey of U.S. adults
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record identifies a perceived-usefulness, perceived-cost, and self-regulation gap. It does not establish device-logged exposure, addiction, clinical harm, platform causation, durable behavior change, political action, or successful digital exit.

records.title: Perceived smartphone excess can coexist with utility, attempted cutback, and incomplete self-regulation
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center American Trends Panel smartphone-time and self-regulation survey
records.geography: United States; 9,750 adults in the American Trends Panel
records.boundary: This record establishes a bounded self-reported chain from smartphone utility and perceived excess through attempted self-regulation and incomplete success. It does not establish addiction, logged behavior, platform causality, clinical harm, or later switching, non-use, or wellbeing recovery.

records.title: Financial well-being is associated with changes in generalized social trust across a five-year respondent follow-up
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center repeated respondents in March 2020 and February 2025 American Trends Panel surveys
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a repeated-respondent association between reported financial well-being and change in generalized social trust. It does not establish that hardship caused trust loss, identify the material event or responsible actor, measure institutional response or remedy, or observe later contact, organizing, turnout, voting, switching, non-use, or exit.

records.title: State fiscal cushions remain substantial but are beginning to lose operating capacity unevenly
records.source_unit: Pew Charitable Trusts Fiscal 50 analysis of state-reported rainy day funds and ending balances, fiscal 2025
records.geography: United States; 50-state fiscal comparison
records.boundary: Pew's Fiscal 50 analysis adds a state institutional-buffer layer. It does not establish service quality, household benefit, tax incidence, disaster recovery, political trust, or geopolitical leverage. The program use is to trace when state fiscal capacity may buffer or transmit shocks, while preserving the public-decision and household-experience steps as open.

records.title: Supplement use is a mass consumer-health practice shaped by age, income, identity, and perceived personal importance
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center, About 8 in 10 Americans take supplements, and many see them as important to their health, September 2026
records.geography: United States; adults nationally with age, gender, race/ethnicity, education, and income comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a consumer-health and belief layer: supplements are a mass household practice whose product mix and perceived importance vary by age, income, gender, identity, and likely wellness culture. It does not establish efficacy, safety, clinical need, spending, substitution for care, or causal health outcomes.

records.title: Teen summer work has partly rebounded but remains far below its historical role as a routine entry into paid work
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center analysis of U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics employment data, published August 19, 2026
records.geography: United States; teens ages 16 to 19, with summer employment, age, race/ethnicity, industry, and occupation comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a youth-work and socialization layer: teen summer employment has partly rebounded in 2026 but remains far below historical levels, varies sharply by age and race/ethnicity, and is concentrated in hospitality, retail, and logistics. It does not establish causes, earnings, job quality, school tradeoffs, household necessity, discrimination, or the long-term effect of early work exposure.

records.title: Teen AI use separates instrumental help from emerging relational support
records.source_unit: US teen respondent, age 13-17, in Pew/Ipsos KnowledgePanel survey
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record separates instrumental and relational teen chatbot use in a population survey. It does not establish emotional dependence, learning gains, mental-health effects, human-support substitution, platform manipulation, privacy loss, trust change, or practical exit.

records.title: Teen digital life combines near-constant platform use with fast-growing chatbot adoption
records.source_unit: US teen-parent dyad survey respondent, age 13-17, with platform and chatbot use reports
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record measures self-reported teen platform and chatbot use, frequency, product choice, and subgroup differences. It does not establish attention minutes, dependence, harm, learning, mental health, privacy loss, political persuasion, or causal platform effects.

records.title: Place changes the route into public life more than the overall level of engagement
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center and Pew-Knight Initiative, How urban, suburban and rural Americans engage in society
records.geography: United States; urban, suburban, and rural adults
records.boundary: This record adds a place-specific route into the existing public-life engagement typology. It does not establish an urban-rural civic divide, causality, durable belonging, institutional trust, political efficacy, or that in-person interaction is intrinsically better than online participation.

records.title: In many surveyed countries, China is now viewed more favorably or reliably than the United States
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center Spring 2026 Global Attitudes Survey comparing public views of the United States and China
records.geography: 36 surveyed countries; country publics' views of the U.S. and China
records.boundary: This record adds a comparative public-reception layer between the U.S. and China. It does not show that China has greater material influence everywhere, that public opinion changed government alignment, or that favorable views imply trust, dependence, policy compliance, or strategic success.

records.title: International confidence in the United States as a partner is weaker than formal alliance ties
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center survey of adults in 36 countries, conducted in spring 2026
records.geography: United States viewed from 36 surveyed countries
records.boundary: This record adds an external-reception layer to the geopolitical atlas. It does not establish that lower confidence changed a government decision, alliance operation, public protest, trade relationship, deterrence outcome, or adversary behavior.

records.title: Skepticism about a woman president is rising even as gender-neutral leadership becomes the dominant public frame
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center short read, Americans have grown more skeptical that a woman will be president in their lifetime, September 2, 2026
records.geography: United States; adults nationally with gender, party, and expectation/importance comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a gender-representation and institutional-expectation layer: symbolic importance, perceived likelihood, party identity, and gender identity do not move as one. It does not establish electoral behavior, candidate viability, sexism as a sole cause, policy consequences of descriptive representation, or the likelihood of any future election.

records.title: Working-class identity spans income and education groups while carrying a strong partisan and financial-stress pattern
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center American Trends Panel survey and linked occupation context
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record measures self-identified working-class status and descriptive subgroup associations. It does not measure objective class position, income mobility, occupation quality, material hardship, class consciousness, voting, policy preference, or causal political identity formation.

records.title: Working-class identity is broader than income or blue-collar work and increasingly carries partisan meaning
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center data essay, Who Sees Themselves as Working Class?, August 31, 2026
records.geography: United States; adults nationally with income, education, race/ethnicity, occupation, financial-stress, and party comparisons
records.boundary: This record treats working-class identity as a cultural and political classification layer connecting work, status, financial security, race, and party. It does not define the American working class, establish economic mobility, infer policy preferences, or turn self-identification into a respondent-level causal explanation.

records.title: Working-parent arrangements trade financial benefit against family and career experience
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center survey of 2,242 U.S. working parents, March 2-15, 2026, plus Census CPS analysis
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record adds a work-family arrangement and meaning layer. It does not establish that a particular arrangement caused financial security, child outcomes, career effects, gender inequality, or care adequacy, and it does not follow one family through a dated care episode or later recovery.

records.title: U.S. working families are reorganizing paid work around care, but flexibility and childcare access remain unequal
records.source_unit: Pew Research Center survey of U.S. working parents, March 2-15, 2026, with Census Current Population Survey analysis
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record establishes U.S. population and survey observations about family employment arrangements, employer flexibility, childcare access, and reported division of care work. It does not establish causal effects, care quality, total household time, longitudinal family transitions, or political preferences. It is a mechanism-rich U.S. observation that should be triangulated with time-use, labor-market, childcare-cost, and household-finance sources.

records.title: Perceived borrowing costs are converting household financing decisions into forgone purchases, cheaper substitutes, and unequal flexibility
records.source_unit: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia Consumer Finance Institute, Are Household Perceptions of Borrowing Costs Creating Spending Headwinds?
records.geography: United States; nationally representative survey of adults fielded July 20-23, 2026
records.boundary: This record adds a consumer-credit conversion layer: perceived borrowing costs move households from intended purchases toward forgone purchases, cheaper substitutes, saving/investment, or changed affordability thresholds, with debt and asset positions shaping flexibility. It does not establish actual transactions, causal interest-rate effects, credit denial, long-run welfare, or universal income gradients.

records.title: A large-load operating event moved data-center dependency from forecast risk into grid-response rules
records.source_unit: PJM Interconnection operating account and proposed large-load reliability standards
records.geography: Northern Virginia / PJM region, United States
records.boundary: This record establishes a dated large-load operating event, an operator response, a proposed reliability-control response, and a later regulator-directed standard-setting stage. It does not establish a household outage, bill change, environmental burden, completed rule adoption, facility compliance, durable facility behavior, local acceptance, or changed geopolitical leverage.

records.title: Local capacity, population change, belonging, trust, and civic action do not form a single place gradient
records.source_unit: Deliberately non-pooled county-context respondent cells, local-area attitude samples, and national respondent cross-tabs
records.geography: United States; county contexts nationally and Chicago, suburban Cook County, and Lake County, Illinois
records.boundary: This is a non-pooled place-to-meaning comparison. It does not establish that growth, capacity, mobility, migration, or service access caused trust, belonging, immigration judgment, civic action, or vote. A same-geography panel linking dated exposure, material/service conditions, attribution, belonging, action, and institutional response remains open.

records.title: Platform review can restore access while leaving payment, durability, and exit unobserved
records.source_unit: 27 named platform-worker case or comparative records in a non-pooled public remedy ledger across Australia, the United Kingdom, the European Union, Malaysia, Uganda, Kenya, and the Philippines
records.geography: Comparative platform-work cases; not a US population estimate
records.boundary: This comparative case layer makes institutional review, restoration, payment recognition, refusal, continued use, and missing exit visible. It does not estimate remedy probability, worker welfare, platform dependence, payment receipt, recurrence prevention, trust change, switching, or US population prevalence.

records.title: Borsuk delivery is documented for an earlier contract while SAFE lists a separate later contract scope
records.source_unit: Polish Ministry of National Defence Borsuk and SAFE program pages
records.geography: Poland; Polish Armed Forces and Polish defense industry
records.boundary: This is a stage-compatible same-product comparison, not a pooled delivery estimate. It establishes one earlier Borsuk delivery and a separate later SAFE contract scope. It does not establish delivery or acceptance of the SAFE-funded 146 vehicles, production increment, local-content share, operational use, public reception, or geopolitical leverage.

records.title: Polish public support for defense financing is positive but divided across SAFE and NBP funding routes
records.source_unit: CBOS Flash 11/2026 adult-resident survey
records.geography: Poland
records.boundary: This record measures Polish public judgment about defense-financing routes. It does not measure Barracuda-500M demand, public reception of the local-production agreement, production, delivery, trust change, political action, or geopolitical leverage. The observed support shares are judgments, not behavioral outcomes.

records.title: A Polish audit found a JASSM-ER settlement evidence gap without establishing missile delivery quantity
records.source_unit: Polish Supreme Audit Office review of 2022 defence-budget execution and FMS settlement controls
records.geography: Poland and US-origin JASSM-ER procurement/accounting relationship
records.boundary: This record establishes an audited documentation/control gap for a JASSM-ER production-cost settlement and separately reports a non-JASSM-attributed 32-unit comparator. It does not estimate production, acceptance, delivery, fielding, operational readiness, delay, or geopolitical leverage for the 2024 Polish JASSM-ER order.

records.title: The 2024 Polish JASSM-ER order remains scheduled without a public delivery or acceptance record
records.source_unit: Official Polish procurement page, schedule-vintage briefing, historical delivery comparator, and current-source non-observation audit
records.geography: Poland and US-origin JASSM-ER procurement relationship
records.boundary: This record preserves a dated public-source non-observation. It does not prove no delivery occurred; it does establish that the reviewed official sources do not support promoting the 2024 JASSM-ER order to accepted, delivered, fielded, or operational capability.

EDISABL identifies a reported work-limiting condition, not diagnosis, accommodation, discrimination, or preference. Earnings and hours direction do not establish job quality, care response, recovery, trust, political action, or institutional remedy.

records.title: Monthly resource position is followed by distinct earnings and hours movement across work-limiting status
records.source_unit: Identified 2025 SIPP person, resource band at month t to valid numeric earnings/hours change at month t+1, conditioned on EDISABL
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a same-person monthly descriptive cross-lag, not a causal or household-weighted estimate. EDISABL identifies a reported work-limiting condition, not diagnosis, accommodation, discrimination, or preference. TPEARN and TMWKHRS changes do not establish direction, job quality, desired hours, care response, trust, political action, or institutional remedy.

records.title: Safety-net transitions mark pressure without establishing recovery or work change
records.source_unit: identified SIPP person, adjacent SNAP transition followed by person-month resource, earnings, hours, job, or hardship outcome
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a descriptive same-person SIPP transition bridge. It does not estimate SNAP effectiveness, benefit adequacy, household prevalence, work quality, causality, notice, administrative remedy, recovery, trust, political action, or a cultural or geopolitical consequence. The transition and following outcomes are selected valid universes with separate denominators.

records.title: Annual child-care routes differ across stable SNAP states while adjacent transition cells are too sparse
records.source_unit: identified SIPP person with November-to-December SNAP state and December-attached annual reference-year child-care fields
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record compares annual/reference-year child-care fields among people observed in stable November-to-December SNAP states. It does not estimate SNAP effects, monthly care change, benefit adequacy, hours lost, notice, effort, remedy, or political response. The adjacent no-to-yes and yes-to-no transition cells are too sparse for promoted population estimates.

records.title: Stable SNAP households show different paid-care, assistance, and work-prevention profiles
records.source_unit: 2025 SIPP public-use person-month slice; November-to-December 2024 SNAP status pairs with annual fall child-care fields
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a weighted descriptive bridge between adjacent SNAP status and annual fall child-care measures. It does not establish a SNAP effect, identify notice or application effort, measure care quality or reliability, observe benefit adequacy, or link care constraints to later work, income, child, health, trust, political action, appeal, remedy, or recovery.

records.title: Child-care work prevention and reported time-loss type differ across stable SNAP states
records.source_unit: identified person with November-to-December adjacent-month SNAP pair and annual fall child-care fields
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a same-person timing bridge across adjacent SNAP status and annual fall child-care measures. It strengthens the material-support-to-work/care-time arrow, but it does not establish a program effect, exact event timing, hours lost, notice/effort, care quality, household outcome, trust, political action, or recovery. Entry and exit cells are too sparse for time-loss reporting.

records.title: The month after a SNAP transition, resources still move more than jobs or hours
records.source_unit: identified SIPP person, SNAP transition at month t to t+1, followed by resource/earnings/hours/job change at t+1 to t+2
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record follows selected person-level SNAP transitions one month forward. It does not estimate SNAP effects, benefit adequacy, notice, effort, remedy, care, trust, political action, or restored security. Outcome universes differ: THINCPOV is household-level, TPEARN and TMWKHRS person/job-holder-level, and RMNUMJOBS person-level.

records.title: Stable SNAP receipt coexists with different annual child-care payment, assistance, and work-constraint profiles
records.source_unit: Identified SIPP person with November-to-December adjacent SNAP status and annual fall child-care fields
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a same-person adjacent-month status comparison with annual fall child-care measures. The sparse November-to-December entry and exit cells are not promoted as reliable estimates. The result does not observe notice, route effort, benefit amount, child-care quality, exact monthly timing, trust, or political action.

records.title: SNAP receipt transitions do not map cleanly onto following-month material security
records.source_unit: SIPP identified person, adjacent reference-month pair
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a Fay-BRR weighted descriptive SIPP transition comparison, not a SNAP program-effect estimate, complete household benefit spell, notice/effort/remedy record, or measure of trust, political meaning, or later recovery. The retrieval hash covers the committed analysis memo.

records.title: SNAP transition reasons lead to distinct following-month food-security paths
records.source_unit: identified SIPP person, adjacent reference-month SNAP transition with a classified recorded reason and following-month food-security outcome
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a Fay-BRR weighted descriptive comparison of recorded SNAP transition reasons and following-month food security. It does not establish notice, effort, benefit amount, gap days, causal program protection, household recovery, remedy, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence. Classified reason and food-security universes are smaller than all transition universes.

records.title: Reported reasons for monthly SNAP entry and exit are heterogeneous
records.source_unit: identified SIPP person, adjacent reference-month SNAP transition with a classified recorded reason
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a Fay-BRR weighted descriptive distribution of respondent-recorded reasons around selected monthly SNAP transitions. It does not establish a causal event, benefit adequacy, notice or remedy failure, household benefit spell, food or housing outcome, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence. Classified reason universes are smaller than all transition universes, and the entry and exit reason taxonomies are not interchangeable.

records.title: SNAP entry and exit sit beside resource and person-earnings changes while job counts usually remain unchanged
records.source_unit: identified SIPP person, adjacent reference-month SNAP transition with monthly household resource, person-earnings, and job-count context
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a Fay-BRR weighted descriptive context comparison around selected person-level SNAP transitions. It does not estimate SNAP effects, household benefit spells, notice/effort/remedy, exact bills, food security, desired hours, pay rate, work quality, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence. Person records may represent covered members of a SNAP unit. THINCPOV is monthly household income-to-poverty ratio; TPEARN is monthly person earnings; TMWKHRS is monthly average hours among job holders; RMNUMJOBS is monthly job count. Their valid universes are separate and none alone measures restored household security.

records.title: Tenure and resources jointly shape reported household pressure
records.source_unit: SIPP person record by reference month, stratified by tenure and monthly income-to-poverty band
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: Replicate-weighted descriptive person-record comparison. It does not estimate household prevalence, tenure causation, a dated bill response, health or work displacement, recovery, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence.

records.title: Utility difficulty and child-care work prevention sit beside following-month renter insecurity
records.source_unit: identified SIPP renter reference-parent person pair with utility condition at month t, annual child-care work-prevention status and following outcomes at month t+1
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This selected renter layer places utility difficulty and tenure at month t beside annual fall child-care work prevention and following-month housing hardship, food insecurity, and resource-band movement. The care field is not newly observed in the following month; utility difficulty is not a bill or shutoff; the prevention cell is small. No causal, recovery, remedy, trust, political-action, or exit claim is made.

records.title: Utility-payment difficulty coexists with more balance carrying and less savings, but access differs by resources
records.source_unit: 2025 SIPP public-use file, 2024 reference year; person records by reference month
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a person-weighted SIPP joint diagnostic, not a household-weighted causal estimate. It shows co-occurrence of utility-payment difficulty, credit-card balance carrying, savings-account ownership, and resource bands within the selected monthly records. It does not identify a dated bill, rate, lender decision, payment outcome, remedy, trust, political action, or the same household's full trajectory.

records.title: Child-care work prevention is higher inside reported utility difficulty, with tenure-specific uncertainty
records.source_unit: 2025 SIPP public-use file, 2024 reference period; December identified reference-parent person rows with valid annual fall child-care work-prevention status, utility-payment difficulty, and tenure
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a descriptive conditional bridge between an annual fall child-care work-prevention report and a December utility/tenure condition. It does not establish a dated bill shock, tenure effect, utility causation, monthly care time, household prevalence, recovery, trust, political action, or a complete material/time/care episode.

records.title: Utility difficulty and tenure sit beside a sparse child-care time-loss endpoint
records.source_unit: positive-weight SIPP person pair with utility condition and tenure at month t, followed by conditional child-care work-prevention and time-loss fields
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a 27-pair conditional timing screen. Utility difficulty is not a dated bill, shutoff, or assistance decision; ETIMELOST is conditional on reported work prevention and a valid fall-reference-year time-loss response. No no-prevention comparison, household prevalence, causal effect, downstream hardship, recovery, remedy, trust, political action, or exit is established.

records.title: Utility and energy-assistance screens precede distinct but uncertain next-month work changes
records.source_unit: 2025 SIPP public-use file, 2024 reference year; identified person-month pairs
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a same-person, month-to-next-month descriptive SIPP transition screen. It places utility-payment difficulty and energy-assistance status beside subsequent earnings and hours movement, but it does not observe the exact bill, work shock, desired hours, care substitution, remedy, recovery, trust, political action, or a causal effect of utility conditions or assistance. Person-month rows repeat household fields and are not household prevalence estimates.

records.title: Utility difficulty sits beside different work-change surfaces for renters and owners
records.source_unit: 2025 SIPP public-use file, 2024 reference year; identified person-month pairs with utility-payment difficulty and tenure at month t, followed by earnings or hours change at month t+1
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a same-person monthly descriptive transition conditioned on utility-payment difficulty and tenure. It does not establish a dated bill shock, a tenure effect, utility causation, desired hours, job quality, care substitution, recovery, trust, political action, or household prevalence. It is a conditional work-transition layer, not a complete housing/energy episode.

records.title: Work can look stable in hours while care and housing position narrow household room
records.source_unit: Deliberately non-pooled comparison of 2025 SIPP person-month directional transitions, tenure/care distributions, and stable-SNAP child-care/hardship pairs
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a deliberately non-pooled SIPP synthesis. It connects directional work movement, tenure/care distributions, and a stable-SNAP following-hardship bridge without treating them as one household estimate. It does not establish a care, tenure, SNAP, hardship, earnings, or hours causal effect; the next conditional person-month rerun requires the raw SIPP slice and replicate archive. Recovery, trust, political action, and institutional remedy remain open.

records.title: Material pressure is jointly distributed across work limitation, children, and resources
records.source_unit: SIPP person record by reference month, stratified by released work-limiting-condition status, household members under 18, and monthly household income-to-poverty ratio
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a person-weighted, design-based intersectional distribution. It does not establish household prevalence, care hours, parenthood, causal effects, a dated bill or employer event, accommodation, recovery, trust, political action, or firm/state response.

records.title: US arms-transfer dominance can deepen allied dependence without proving political control
records.source_unit: SIPRI Arms Transfers Database and Trends in International Arms Transfers 2025 fact sheet
records.geography: International transfers of major conventional arms; United States, Europe, and European NATO members
records.boundary: This record measures international major-arms transfer volumes and supplier concentration. It does not establish financial value, delivery, operational readiness, sustainment, recipient autonomy, public consent, alliance obedience, deterrence, or strategic leverage.

records.title: Global military spending rose while US spending fell and European capacity accelerated
records.source_unit: SIPRI military-expenditure estimate by country, region, and alliance grouping
records.geography: Global, national, regional, and NATO groupings
records.boundary: This record measures SIPRI monetary estimates and shares of military expenditure through 2025. It does not establish operational capability, procurement realization, alliance behavior, state intent, household incidence, social-spending displacement, or geopolitical outcomes. The 2025 database replaces prior SIPRI military-spending data and should be treated as a new vintage.

records.title: Military-resource allocation and alliance concentration increased alongside geopolitical tension
records.source_unit: SIPRI national and alliance military-expenditure estimates
records.geography: World, United States, China, and NATO alliance
records.boundary: This record measures aggregate military-resource allocation and alliance concentration. It does not establish capability, readiness, procurement realization, household or worker incidence, legitimacy, deterrence, state leverage, alliance cohesion, or an external actor's changed behavior. The retrieval hash will cover the committed analysis memo.

records.title: Emergency recovery loans reduce small-firm exit and bankruptcy after disasters while increasing employment, revenue, and private credit
records.source_unit: Over 167,000 US firm loan applications spanning about 1,900 disasters, merged to Census records and business credit reports; published causal firm-level research, not a household or customer panel
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record establishes a causal firm-level emergency-liquidity result as summarized by the official NBER paper page, with separately labeled effect-size anchors from an earlier author version. It does not establish worker household security, customer access or prices, owner recovery, local service continuity, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequences.

records.title: Expanding small-business support eligibility toward larger firms can crowd out smaller firms' revenue, wages, exits, and innovation
records.source_unit: US administrative Census firm data around quasi-random timing of expanded small-business program eligibility; NBER Working Paper 35703, issued September 2026
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record closes an eligibility-rule-to-firm-allocation and small-firm-outcome arrow for the studied US program setting. It does not establish customer welfare, worker security beyond the reported wage direction, owner-household recovery, public legitimacy, political action, or a general rule about support scale.

records.title: SNAP administrative routes can change participation without establishing household security
records.source_unit: study-specific SNAP applicant, participant, administrative case, census tract, or recertification case
records.geography: United States; study-specific states and localities
records.boundary: This record preserves study-specific causal or reported participation/denial mechanisms from NBER-linked administrative and field studies and places them beside, but does not pool them with, the national SIPP transition-to-hardship record. It does not estimate one national administrative-burden effect, same-household food or health consequences, benefit adequacy, trust, political action, or a program effect across designs. The committed paper-scan hash covers the source-specific extraction memo.

records.title: Two public SNAP EBT cases show contrasting administrative endpoints—partial replacement with residual denial and affirmed denial—without household recovery
records.source_unit: Two deliberately non-pooled Connecticut and New Jersey SNAP EBT administrative hearing decisions
records.geography: Connecticut and New Jersey, United States; anonymized SNAP households and state administrative review systems
records.boundary: This deliberately non-pooled record advances two public SNAP EBT cases through claim, administrative review, and contrasting partial remedy endpoints. It does not estimate population rates, establish independent transaction attribution, verify household food adequacy or recovery, or measure later trust, political action, recurrence, or exit.

records.title: SNAP outreach raises take-up while changing the marginal enrollee profile
records.source_unit: Randomized Pennsylvania older-adult SNAP outreach experiment; treatment and control participants remain source-specific
records.geography: Pennsylvania, United States
records.boundary: The experiment closes information/assistance to enrollment and marginal-targeting stages. It does not close benefit adequacy, food security, household adaptation, trust, political action, or recovery.

records.title: Among urban poor respondents, hardship and formative government contact could coincide with political activism
records.source_unit: 462 low-income men and women in one of the poorest congressional districts in the United States
records.geography: United States; one poor urban congressional district
records.boundary: This record adds an observational hardship-and-government-contact-to-activism surface among low-income urban respondents. It does not establish causality, national prevalence, a specific agency remedy, generalized trust change, validated turnout, or a universal hardship-to-mobilization effect.

records.title: Contemporary welfare receipt has heterogeneous and program-specific political participation associations
records.source_unit: Young U.S. adults in nationally representative longitudinal survey data on welfare receipt and political participation
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a contemporary U.S. welfare-participation association with program and attentiveness heterogeneity, not a universal cash effect, causal benefit-to-vote estimate, or trust/legitimacy result.

records.title: SSA is adding AI-assisted contact and disability-evidence processing while outcome and oversight evidence remain open
records.source_unit: U.S. Social Security Administration FY 2025-2026 Annual Performance Plan, SSA Open Data disability-denial review documentation, and SSA Office of Inspector General ongoing-audit register
records.geography: United States Social Security Administration; national disability programs and customer-service channels
records.boundary: This record establishes named SSA AI-assisted service and disability-processing initiatives alongside an open OIG AI audit and selected denial-review infrastructure. It does not establish claimant-level AI exposure, discrimination, inaccurate denial, appeal success, benefit receipt, timely correction, household income, health, work, trust, or exit.

records.title: Public support for CEO activism is becoming more issue-specific, while executive speech increasingly enters consumer choice and corporate legitimacy
records.source_unit: Stanford Graduate School of Business, Rock Center for Corporate Governance and Hoover Institution, 2026 CEO Activism Survey, September 2026
records.geography: United States; adults nationally, with demographic, partisan, age and issue comparisons
records.boundary: This record treats CEO activism as a corporate-legitimacy and consumer-response signal. It does not establish that public speech changes actual sales, employee behavior, political outcomes or social conditions; several 2026 findings are preserved directionally because the full tables are not publicly accessible.

records.title: A neighborhood gathering place can be followed by more local startups where comparable social venues were absent
records.source_unit: U.S. census tract and business-registration comparison in NBER Working Paper 32604 using the Startup Cartography Project
records.geography: United States census tracts; neighborhoods without existing coffee shops at the comparison baseline
records.boundary: This record adds a place-linked firm-formation result and an important counterexample: a new gathering venue was associated with more startups where comparable cafés were absent, while entry did not show the same effect where cafés already existed. It does not establish firm survival, job quality, customer welfare, housing affordability, displacement, or individual social connection.

records.title: AAPI cultural visibility is rising without resolving belonging, recognition, threat perception, or everyday safety
records.source_unit: The Asian American Foundation, STAATUS Index 2026
records.geography: United States; national survey of U.S. adults with Asian American and Pacific Islander subgroup analysis
records.boundary: This record adds an AAPI cultural-politics mechanism: cultural contribution and apparent social position can coexist with weak recognition, contested belonging, geopolitical threat perception, race-based harassment, and place-specific unsafety. It is a survey and message-test summary, not a longitudinal discrimination panel, administrative incident dataset, causal evaluation of education/media, or proof that stated engagement routes become durable inclusion.

records.title: U.S. public-health protection depends on operational capacity that funding totals alone do not guarantee
records.source_unit: Trust for America’s Health, Underfunded and Under Strain: The State of America’s Public Health System, September 2026; policy analysis of federal, state, and local public-health funding, workforce, infrastructure, and operations
records.geography: United States; federal public-health system with state, local, territorial, and community implications
records.boundary: This record captures TFAH’s evidence and policy analysis of U.S. public-health funding, workforce, infrastructure, operational continuity, and proposed federal changes. It does not establish a causal national health effect, independently audit every cited estimate, measure all state or local variation, or treat proposed FY2027 policy as enacted fact.

records.title: Movement buys access but consumes a large share of household money and work time
records.source_unit: 2024 US Consumer Expenditure Survey averages and 2024 American Community Survey commuting estimates; separate national source units
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: These two official sources show the money and work-time price of movement at national scale, while preserving that transportation can also create access. They do not establish a same-household transportation burden, mode substitution, service reliability, work or care outcome, place attachment, political meaning, or later mobility. The BLS and ACS source units are not joined.

records.title: U.S. households remain cautiously optimistic while inflation, generational affordability gaps, credit restraint, AI skepticism and fraud risk reshape financial behavior
records.source_unit: TransUnion Consumer Pulse Study, U.S. Q2 2026
records.geography: United States; adults aged 18 and older across all states
records.boundary: This record adds a U.S. household-resilience layer: aggregate optimism and financial stability coexist with generational affordability pressure, discretionary pullback, lower credit intent, AI skepticism, fraud exposure and uneven protective action. It is a TransUnion/Dynata online quota survey, not a longitudinal household panel, credit-bureau outcome dataset, verified fraud ledger, causal study or respondent-level financial trajectory.

records.title: Insurance market conditions vary across matched ZIP/ZCTA socioeconomic contexts
records.source_unit: Matched Treasury FIO ZIP-code/year market rows and Census ACS 5-year ZCTA context
records.geography: United States; 2022 Treasury ZIP-code rows matched to same-text 2022 ACS ZCTA codes
records.boundary: This record creates a descriptive market/place context bridge for 2022. It does not establish that income, poverty, tenure, or any place characteristic causes premiums or nonrenewals, nor does it connect them to household coverage, repairs, lending, mobility, or political response.

records.title: Higher FEMA expected-loss ratings coincide with higher observed insurance premiums and nonrenewal exposure
records.source_unit: Treasury FIO ZIP-code insurance market rows assigned to FEMA NRI county context through Census geographic relationships
records.geography: United States; 2022 Treasury ZIP rows, primary county by largest ZCTA land-area intersection, FEMA county baseline
records.boundary: This record adds hazard context to the insurance market/place bridge. It does not establish causal hazard pricing, insurer withdrawal, household affordability, coverage adequacy, repairs, lending, mobility, or political response.

records.title: Climate-risk ZIP codes show higher homeowners-insurance cost and nonrenewal exposure
records.source_unit: Treasury Federal Insurance Office analysis of aggregated homeowners-insurance policy and ZIP-code data
records.geography: United States; ZIP codes grouped by expected annual building losses from nine climate-related perils
records.boundary: This record establishes a market-side association between climate-risk ZIP-code groupings and reported premiums, nonrenewals, and claim severity in 2018-2022. It does not establish household-level affordability, actual coverage loss, repair or move outcomes, causation, or political/geopolitical consequence. Those links remain open for matched place-time work.

records.title: Rural local trust and agency can remain strong while confidence in national politics falls
records.source_unit: Trust for Civic Life second community survey conducted through participating Civic Hub networks
records.geography: United States; rural communities represented by 24 participating Civic Hub grantee networks
records.boundary: This record adds a network-recruited rural local-civic-capacity layer. It does not estimate rural national prevalence, establish that civic organizations caused trust or agency, show delivered material support, or prove durable political action, policy influence, or cross-community generalization.

records.title: The American Dream is being renegotiated through financial strain, family dependence, digital finance, and community relevance
records.source_unit: TruStage What Matters Now Consumer Research 2026, quantitative research conducted with Ipsos and qualitative research by TruStage; 8,813 U.S. consumers in English and Spanish
records.geography: United States; national consumer study with race/ethnicity, generation, income, gender identity, and neurodivergence perspectives
records.boundary: This record captures a commissioned U.S. consumer-research study linking financial strain, identity, generation, neurodivergence, family influence, digital finance, and community relevance. It does not establish objective household finances, causal mechanisms, representative subgroup effects beyond the study design, product outcomes, institutional behavior, or durable change.

records.title: Arts participation is stable but increasingly home-based and solitary, weakening its social-health pathway
records.source_unit: University of Florida and University College London EpiArts Lab analysis of American Time Use Survey data, published in Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences and summarized by UF News in July 2026
records.geography: United States; American Time Use Survey participants and reported arts/cultural activities
records.boundary: This record adds a cultural-health mechanism: daily arts participation is low but stable, while participation has shifted toward home and solitary settings, potentially weakening the social and public-space pathway through which creative activity may support well-being. It does not establish annual participation, causal health effects, unequal access mechanisms, or the value of public versus private creation.

records.title: Platform safety controls show a gap between user action and confidence that the platform will respond
records.source_unit: Nationally representative UK adult survey of platform safety-technology awareness, use, and satisfaction; published 2026
records.geography: United Kingdom social-media users; comparative digital-culture evidence, not a US population estimate
records.boundary: This record adds a user-action and perceived-outcome stage to the platform/data lane: awareness, safety-tool use, and satisfaction are separated. It is comparative UK evidence and does not establish US prevalence, causal harm reduction, platform responsibility, mental-health improvement, or durable account exit.

records.title: Americans broadly agree corruption exists and recognize public-power abuses, while partisan identity redirects blame and judgment
records.source_unit: University of Massachusetts Amherst Poll, September 2026 national public-opinion poll on federal corruption, presidential conduct, national direction, and economic perceptions
records.geography: United States; adults nationally with party, ideology, demographic, and economic comparisons
records.boundary: This record adds a public-power and attribution layer: Americans broadly perceive federal corruption and price pressure, share some standards for public abuse, but divide sharply over which institution is responsible and how identical conduct should be judged. It does not establish actual corruption, legal violations, causal responsibility for prices, enforcement, institutional remedy, or later political behavior.

records.title: Local opposition to AI data centers crosses party lines because communities separate national technological ambition from who pays local costs
records.source_unit: University of Massachusetts Amherst Poll, September 2026 national public-opinion poll on AI data centers and presidential AI handling
records.geography: United States; national adult sample fielded August 21-26, 2026
records.boundary: This record adds a local-consent and political-accountability route: opposition to AI data centers crosses party lines because residents distinguish national technological benefits from concentrated local costs and community fit. It does not establish realized environmental harm, utility-rate causality, permitting behavior, project economics, or causal presidential approval effects.

records.title: AI use, personal control, and confidence in public or private AI are separate country-level surfaces
records.source_unit: 2025 UNDP Global Survey on AI and Human Development respondent; country-weighted descriptive comparison
records.geography: United States and selected comparison countries from a 21-country survey
records.boundary: This is a weighted descriptive comparison from the UNDP 2025 Global Survey on AI and Human Development. It establishes that AI use, perceived personal control, confidence in government use, and confidence in AI design vary separately across selected countries, not that any country causes those differences or that confidence equals actual control, benefit, service quality, worker power, or human development. The survey is cross-sectional and the raw Stata file is captured by hash but not committed to the repository.

records.title: High average human development does not settle the question of who can exercise new choices
records.source_unit: UNDP Human Development Reports country-level composite index and ranking for the United States
records.geography: United States; international comparison across 193 countries and territories
records.boundary: This is a bounded UNDP human-development context record. It establishes a high US average HDI and its reported long-run change, not equal capability, household welfare, AI access, worker control, political trust, or geopolitical power. Composite-country averages remain a comparison frame for the US-centered program, not a substitute for subgroup and same-unit evidence.

records.title: Family formation and child retention are becoming a metropolitan geography problem shaped by housing, care, schools and mobility
records.source_unit: Urban Institute research report, Where Do Families Live? Measuring Fertility and Child Migration Across Core Cities and Suburbs in the United States, June 25, 2026
records.geography: United States; 43 major metropolitan areas, comparing core cities, suburbs, exurbs and socioeconomic groups
records.boundary: This record treats fertility, child retention and family migration as linked to metropolitan housing, care, schooling, commute, amenities and socioeconomic constraint. It does not establish causal effects, define an ideal urban form, measure individual preferences, or imply that suburbanization alone explains demographic change.

records.title: Immigration concern is turning public systems into places of practical non-use for immigrant families
records.source_unit: Urban Institute, Immigrant Families Disengaged from Public Life and Essential Services Because of Immigration Concerns in 2025: Findings from the Well-Being and Basic Needs Survey
records.geography: United States; nationally representative Well-Being and Basic Needs Survey, with analysis of adults in immigrant families and mixed-status families
records.boundary: This record adds a U.S. route from immigration enforcement concern through household risk perception, practical non-use of work, health care, schools, police, community life, and safety-net programs, with disproportionate exposure in mixed-status families. It is nationally representative survey evidence for the measured 2025 round, not respondent-level longitudinal data, a causal estimate of enforcement effects, a complete account of local enforcement, or proof of durable institutional withdrawal.

records.title: Charitable food is an elevated but incomplete buffer, with access shaped by time, transport, awareness, stigma, and treatment
records.source_unit: Urban Institute December Well-Being and Basic Needs Survey: adults reporting household receipt of free groceries or meals and related access experiences
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This layer measures charitable-food receipt, access difficulty, perceived treatment, and unmet need in a weighted cross-sectional survey. It does not measure food quantity or nutritional adequacy, provider capacity directly, SNAP benefit loss, causal stigma effects, or later trust and political action. It complements the formal SNAP route and food-security layers without merging their denominators or claiming that charitable food replaces public assistance.

records.title: Food insecurity remained elevated after the pandemic support cycle, with sharper exposure among families with children and lower incomes
records.source_unit: Urban Institute December Well-Being and Basic Needs Survey: nationally representative adults, with working-age trend series for 2019–2025 and an expanded older-adult sample in 2025
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a published, weighted, respondent-level cross-sectional trend layer. It shows persistent and unequal food hardship and supplies a baseline for monitoring later policy implementation; it does not estimate the causal effect of the OBBBA, SNAP receipt, food prices, or charitable food on any household, nor does it link the same people to benefit amounts, administrative routes, health, political judgment, or later action. The working-age series also contains a 2025 methodology change and should be read as a bounded trend rather than a seamless causal time series.

records.title: Immigration concerns can turn status exposure into avoidance of work, care, community participation, and safety-net programs
records.source_unit: Urban Institute Well-Being and Basic Needs Survey immigrant-family analysis
records.geography: United States; adults ages 18 and older in immigrant families, including mixed-status families
records.boundary: This record observes reported family-level worry, avoidance, and safety-net nonparticipation associated with immigration concerns. It does not establish legal-status composition beyond source-defined family categories, enforcement exposure, agency data sharing, benefit eligibility, causal policy effects, realized health or earnings loss, or later trust, political action, migration, or recovery.

records.title: Unmet assistance among older adults coexists with food, health-cost, housing, and utility hardship
records.source_unit: Urban Institute December 2025 Well-Being and Basic Needs Survey published estimates
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a published cross-sectional 2025 WBNS age-and-care material-security layer. It does not link a respondent to a dated service request, caregiver, agency, benefit amount, care completion, remedy, food quantity, health outcome, institutional setting, trust, political action, or recovery. The 2025 older-adult sample should not be pooled mechanically with earlier working-age WBNS estimates.

records.title: Reported SNAP interruptions expose notice, time, paperwork, and interview route failures
records.source_unit: Urban Institute December 2024 Well-Being and Basic Needs Survey analysis of adults ages 18–64 in families receiving SNAP
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a respondent-reported, retrospective interruption and route-burden layer. It does not link to administrative case files, identify exact notice or benefit dates, measure benefit amounts or gap days, verify agency responsibility, observe appeals/corrections, or estimate downstream food security, health, trust, political action, or return to SNAP. It is complementary to—not interchangeable with—the USDA/FNA state route-performance layer and SIPP transition layers.

records.title: Undersea cable redundancy is a geopolitical and economic-continuity dependency, not only a bandwidth issue
