records.geography: United States, Taiwan, Japan, Philippines, Hawaii, Guam, and trans-Pacific cable networks
records.boundary: This record adds an external geopolitical-infrastructure dependency and scenario-model layer. It does not establish Chinese intent, a sabotage event, future attack probability, realized connectivity loss, consumer harm, firm loss, or U.S. strategic leverage; modeled capacity and latency effects must remain separate from observed outages and downstream outcomes.

records.title: SNAP EBT security modernization adds protection but leaves recipient usability and recovery open
records.source_unit: USDA Food and Nutrition Administration public SNAP EBT security, modernization, retailer, and card-replacement materials
records.geography: United States SNAP participants, state agencies, retailers, processors, and USDA/FNA
records.boundary: This record adds current EBT security, migration, replacement-monitoring, and recipient-usability stages. It does not establish that chip or tap technology reduced theft, that a named household received a replacement, that a replacement was timely or adequate, or that food security, trust, continued participation, or exit changed.

records.title: Taiwan's reciprocal-trade commitments convert U.S. pressure into a planned capacity and procurement response
records.source_unit: U.S. Trade Representative fact sheet on the U.S.-Taiwan Agreement on Reciprocal Trade
records.geography: United States and Taiwan bilateral trade, semiconductor, energy, and strategic-technology relationship
records.boundary: This record establishes an announced Taiwan policy and market response to a U.S.-Taiwan reciprocal-trade framework, including planned U.S. capacity investment and purchases. It does not establish implementation, delivered output, firm or household incidence, supply-chain replacement, Taiwanese dependence, changed external behavior beyond the agreement commitments, or U.S. geopolitical leverage.

records.title: Virginia moves large-load data-center governance toward explicit cost allocation and reliability controls
records.source_unit: Virginia State Corporation Commission / Dominion Energy Virginia large-load regulatory record
records.geography: Virginia, United States; Dominion Energy Virginia service territory
records.boundary: This record establishes regulatory response and reported operational stress in Virginia's large-load system. It does not establish actual Prince William facility load, household bill effects, utility cost allocation outcomes, water/environmental burden, public legitimacy, firm behavior, or geopolitical leverage. Those arrows require customer-, feeder-, place-, or docket-level evidence.

records.title: Data-center growth can produce a proposed household-relief route before bill-credit receipt is visible
records.source_unit: Dominion Energy and NextEra Energy Virginia benefits-package announcement; proposed residential customer relief and large-load cost-governance terms
records.geography: Virginia, United States
records.boundary: This record establishes a proposed residential bill-credit route alongside an approved modeled cost-allocation framework. It does not establish customer eligibility, bill posting, receipt, net savings, avoided ratepayer burden, reliability improvement, local acceptance, or durable affordability.

records.title: Aggregate insurance restitution and corrective plans can coexist with unknown individual recovery and coverage continuity
records.source_unit: Virginia State Corporation Commission public settlement summaries for Esurance, State Farm, and Anthem/Carelon

records.boundary: This record establishes three Virginia SCC insurance settlements with regulator-reported aggregate restitution, reported aggregate payment, and prospective correction. It does not claim recipient-level receipt beyond the regulator's aggregate payment statement, adequate compensation, coverage or care restoration, durable error reduction, trust change, switching, or exit.

records.title: A large retailer reports privacy-request completion and denial as separate control stages
records.source_unit: Walmart corporate California privacy-rights metrics for 2025 requests, updated June 18, 2026
records.geography: California residents submitting CCPA requests to Walmart
records.boundary: This record adds an account-holder administrative completion stage to the platform/data-control lane: requests, verification/denial, completion, and timing are visible in a named company report. It does not verify individual deletion, residual data, adequacy, trust, switching, or wellbeing, and it does not pool Walmart's request universe with California DROP or other companies.

records.title: U.S. institutional trust is being sorted by party, place, and economic security rather than disappearing uniformly
records.source_unit: Washington University in St. Louis Weidenbaum Center Survey Waves 6-8, 2025-2026; report analysis of institutional trust by partisanship, geography, and economic security
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record establishes U.S. survey associations between institutional trust and partisanship, geography, and economic security, including institution-specific partisan and urban-rural differences. It does not establish causal effects, individual-level change, institutional performance, democratic stability, political action, or the mechanism by which household economic security shapes trust.

records.title: People may feel better after leaving a platform while social dependence makes leaving hard
records.source_unit: World Happiness Report 2026 Chapter 6 synthesis of published Facebook deactivation and U.S. college-student collective-exit studies; component studies are retained as distinct populations and designs
records.geography: United States; Facebook-user experiment and U.S. college-student Instagram/TikTok coordination study
records.boundary: This record adds a platform-exit and collective-coordination mechanism. It does not establish a population-wide causal effect of social media, a durable exit rate, a complete welfare balance, a political-action effect, or a recommendation about platform policy. The two component studies use different samples, platforms, outcomes, and designs.

records.title: US firm capacity is a size-stratified bundle of training, growth, infrastructure, and constraint
records.source_unit: World Bank Enterprise Survey country profile; 2,589 US establishments interviewed May 2024–April 2025
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record establishes a bounded 2024 US firm baseline in which size is associated with different reported training, employment-growth, infrastructure, finance, and obstacle profiles. It does not estimate AI adoption, productivity causality, worker outcomes, firm survival, household incidence, or geopolitical leverage; the establishment survey size cells, indicator universes, and manager perceptions remain distinct evidence surfaces.

records.title: Financial access is broadening, but digital reach and financial room remain different surfaces
records.source_unit: World Bank Global Findex 2025 country-level and demographic indicators; nationally representative adult survey aggregates
records.geography: United States with selected country comparisons
records.boundary: The Global Findex 2025 adds a valuable cross-country demand-side layer: US account ownership rose from 88.0% in 2011 to 97.0% in 2024, and the measured gender ownership gap nearly disappeared. But access, connectivity, digital payment use, emergency resilience, formal borrowing, affordable terms, effective remedy, trust, and political action remain different surfaces. The 2024 high-income questionnaire does not return several US financial-use indicators; those missing values are not zeros. This record does not establish a causal digital-finance effect, household recovery, consumer welfare, or geopolitical leverage.

records.title: Global poverty reduction has stalled while climate and inequality risks remain geographically concentrated
records.source_unit: World Bank global poverty, prosperity, inequality, climate-risk, and data-coverage assessment
records.geography: Global, with regional and country-income-group comparisons
records.boundary: This record contributes global poverty, shared prosperity, inequality, climate-risk, and data-coverage context to a US-centered comparative atlas. It does not estimate US household poverty, causal conflict effects, climate losses, political unrest, migration, legitimacy, or geopolitical behavior. Poverty thresholds, projections, regional shares, and data-coverage findings remain separate evidence types.

records.title: AI capability depends on local complements and can expand capacity while deepening concentration risk
records.source_unit: World Bank World Development Report 2026 framework and chapter-level synthesis; developing-country perspective with US-relevant value-chain implications
records.geography: Global/developing-country analytical frame; US is a value-chain and institutional comparison case, not the report's sole population
records.boundary: This is a World Bank framework and report-evidence record, not a US AI adoption, productivity, or geopolitical-leverage estimate. It contributes a capability/dependency mechanism and identifies measurable complements, concentration, public procurement, and governance stages. Country, firm, household, and state effects require separate primary records and compatible denominators.

records.title: Music consumption is expanding for a younger cohort while discovery remains a platform-and-relationship hybrid
records.source_unit: YouGov, Music consumption trends 2026: Who's listening more—and what's driving discovery?, September 7, 2026
records.geography: United States; adults age 18+ with generational comparisons
records.boundary: This record identifies a music-consumption, generational identity and hybrid-discovery subtheme. It does not establish streaming volume, subscription or concert spending, artist income, algorithmic causality, cultural influence, genre change, platform market power, or within-generation growth rates; the public article does not state the effective rolling sample size.

records.boundary: This record establishes a reported General Dynamics-OTS subaward and a multi-facility DLA entity footprint under one parent. records.boundary: Supplier-name breadth is not replaceability, competition, production capacity, delivery, or geopolitical leverage. Reported component descriptions are not a bill of materials, output count, or proof of integration.

records.title: Real food sales grew modestly in 2025 while outlet patterns diverged between full-service and limited-service eating
records.source_unit: USDA Economic Research Service Food Expenditure Series monthly outlet sales and annual food-expenditure tables, constant 2025 dollars
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record measures real sales across all purchasers and selected outlets, not household consumption or welfare. It should be triangulated with USDA food-security prevalence, assistance spending, Census QSS customer classes, and household-level food acquisition data before interpreting a cultural or consumer trend.

records.title: Food insecurity is a graded household-security outcome with family shielding and institutional coping
records.source_unit: USDA Food Security Supplement household, child-household, poverty, and assistance measures
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This is a national descriptive USDA household-security layer. It does not identify a dated price or institutional trigger, detailed purchases, care/time displacement, health outcome, benefit adequacy, trust, political action, or causal effect. Published rounded percentages and counts are retained; where the committed memo did not preserve a full absolute denominator, the denominator is explicitly labeled as a percentage base. The retrieval hash covers the committed analysis memo.

records.title: Food access remains materially constrained while inflation-adjusted nutrition-assistance spending recedes
records.source_unit: USDA Economic Research Service national food-security prevalence and federal food-and-nutrition-assistance spending summaries
records.geography: United States
records.boundary: This record links two adjacent but non-identical institutional layers: household-reported food-access difficulty and federal assistance spending. It does not estimate causal program effects, household benefit receipt, food affordability, nutrition, food retail demand, cultural food practice, or political attribution. The record should be read with the state SNAP-participation and QSS customer-class records, not as a joined household panel.

records.title: SNAP participation is non-monotonic across state income contexts and coexists with distinct mobility exposures
records.source_unit: Matched USDA SNAP state/DC rate and 2024 ACS state/DC aggregate context
records.geography: United States; 50 states and District of Columbia
records.boundary: This is a descriptive ecological crosswalk of 51 USDA FY2025 participation rates and 2024 ACS state aggregates. It does not establish individual or household relationships, causal direction, administrative performance, eligible nonparticipation, benefit adequacy, food security, or political meaning. The state-income quartiles are recomputed over matched states/DC and the ACS mobility measures retain their distinct table universes. The retrieval hash covers the committed crosswalk layer.

records.title: SNAP remains a large, heterogeneous national support system with distinct scale and household layers

records.boundary: This is current official USDA ERS program and research-summary context, not a new national causal estimate. It keeps scale, state range, household composition, benefit distribution, and research-summary patterns separate from NBER access studies and SIPP person-month hardship estimates. It does not establish benefit adequacy, same-household route burden, downstream security, trust, political action, or geopolitical consequence. The retrieval hash covers the committed source-specific layer.

records.title: FY2025 SNAP participation varies widely across states and DC

records.boundary: This record is a descriptive transcription and summary of 51 FY2025 state/DC participation rates. It does not establish why rates differ, whether eligible nonparticipants differ, state administrative performance, benefit adequacy, food security, household outcomes, trust, political action, or causal effects. Population-weighted national estimates and state-level need/eligibility/administrative decomposition remain open. The retrieval hash covers the committed state-specific layer.

records.boundary: This layer distinguishes population participation, application-route timeliness, recertification-route timeliness, and a low-income access index. The committed layer hash covers the detailed interpretation and summary; the reproduction script preserves the full state-by-state extraction path.
